dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fift.formal:
The framework does not generate its asymmetry; it inherits it.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Sakharov.)} The Sakharov conditions are for generating an asymmetry dynamically from a symmetric state; a universe whose asymmetry is initial data does not need them. The descent supplies the reason the initial data need not be symmetric: it is irreversible (the lossy projection of the taxonomy paper's descent theorem \cite{ButlerT1}), it creates the tower charges, and it makes one orientation choice, the Witt flag, which is what particle-versus-antiparticle means (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}). Each matches a Sakharov condition in name; none is a mechanism producing a number.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The fifteenth refutation.)} A pre-descent $\theta$-term would source asymmetry through the topology of gauge bundles; but it integrates a characteristic class, of even degree, so the odd-dimensional towers carry no continuous $\theta$, and at the P3 representatives a $\theta$-term exists exactly where a flag bit does. In this tower it is excluded empirically: a $\theta$-routed asymmetry needs an angle of order one at the descent that does not relax before it acts, and the neutron dipole bound $|d_{n}| < 1.8 \times 10^{-26}\,e\,$cm \cite{Abel2020} gives $|\theta| \lesssim 10^{-10}$ today (through a hadronic matrix element with its own uncertainty). Not excluded, and not claimed: an angle that relaxes or rolls; and the mirror's angle, which equals ours only by the common ceiling coupling along the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), a premise of its own there, not P2), the copy being of the functional, not its coefficient. Internally the paper says only that the orientation is the one mechanism the framework itself supplies; that locates the mechanism and does not refute the alternative.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Confinement and universality.)} The orientation route is one bit spent once (uniqueness among all conceivable mechanisms is not claimed). A flag exists on every rung of every tower (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries}), but the flag \emph{bit} only in the even residues at their P3 representatives (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}), so the asymmetry is confined to the oriented causal towers, this one and the mirror, and the odd towers carry none by either route. The value is common to this tower and the mirror by Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v), under that clause's premises. No universality beyond the reversal pair is assumed: the former Premise P4 (democracy of the asymmetry over the oriented towers), retired as a postulate, was that theorem on the mirror, void on the odd residues, which carry no flag bit, and a premise only on the fork $r = 0$, where nothing stored uses it; the equality is not extendable to inequivalent towers, the asymmetry per mode depending on the tower's own charge structure.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The value, a stance.)} $\epsilon$ is not derived here and not classified. The trichotomy's kinematic clause runs for it as for $N$ ($\epsilon$ is continuous), at that Fact's observation level; the dynamical clause does not, since generating an asymmetry from CPT-invariant dynamics is exactly what the Sakharov mechanism does. \emph{Stance, flagged and attacked in the section “The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper”:} the framework inherits its asymmetry, and $\epsilon$ is initial data of the descent, refuted by any in-framework calculation that produces $\epsilon$ dynamically. The count uses only the equality of $\epsilon$ across the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)), not its provenance. On the stance the unexplained numbers are two, $N$ and $\epsilon$, with the orientation bit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation} a third datum of the same event. \emph{Note (register, 2026-11-01).} The value $\epsilon$ is now a registered free input of the series, Premise \claimref{synthesis.matter-asymmetry-registered-free-input}, which takes this stance as its statement and its refutation condition; the stance is unchanged.
\end{enumerate}
dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fift.technical:
The framework inherits its asymmetry rather than generating it. The descent is irreversible, creates the tower charges and makes one orientation choice, the Witt flag, which is what particle against antiparticle means; each matches a Sakharov condition in name, but none is a mechanism producing a number. A pre-descent $\theta$-term would integrate a characteristic class of even degree, so the odd-dimensional towers carry no continuous $\theta$. In this tower a $\theta$-routed asymmetry needing an unrelaxed angle of order one at the descent is excluded empirically, since the neutron dipole bound gives $|\theta| \lesssim 10^{-10}$ today; an angle that relaxes or rolls, and the mirror's angle, are not excluded.

The flag bit exists only in the even residues at their nearest-dimension representatives, so the asymmetry is confined to this tower and the mirror, and the odd towers carry none. Equality of the value across this tower and the mirror is a clause of the copy theorem, under its premises; the former democracy-of-the-asymmetry premise P4, retired as a postulate, added to it only a premise on the fork $r = 0$ that nothing stored uses. The value $\epsilon$ is not derived; the stance, flagged as refutable by any in-framework dynamical calculation of $\epsilon$, is that it is initial data of the descent, and the count uses only $\epsilon_{2} = \epsilon_{6}$. On that stance the unexplained numbers are $N$ and $\epsilon$, with the orientation bit a third datum of the same event. (Note, 2026-11-01: $\epsilon$ is now registered as a free input of the series, with this stance's refutation condition.)
dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fift.lay: In this framework the excess of matter over antimatter is not produced by any process after the start. On a stance the paper flags, and which any calculation inside the framework that produced the excess would refute, it is part of the initial conditions the descent sets. A well-known alternative source, a constant angle in the strong force, is ruled out for our world by measurements of the neutron, although an angle that changed over time is not ruled out. The excess can only live in our world and its mirror twin; that it has the same size in the two follows from the mirror being a copy, under that result's assumptions (a wider assumption of equal size in every such world, P4, is no longer carried, since nothing used it beyond the mirror), and its size is left as an unexplained input.

proofs.main: The refutation in (ii) is a degree count. A $\theta$-term integrates over the tower's space a characteristic class of the gauge bundle ($\tr F \wedge F$ in four dimensions); Chern and Pontryagin classes have even degree, so in odd dimension there is no top-degree class and no continuous $\theta$. Homotopy agrees: bundles on $S^{d}$ are classified by $\pi_{d-1}(G)$, zero in three dimensions ($\pi_{2}(G) = 0$), and in five $\pi_{4}(SU(2)) = \mathbb{Z}_{2}$ allows only a discrete angle, $0$ or $\pi$, with $\pi_{4}(SU(n)) = 0$ for $n \geq 3$; the odd-dimensional Chern-Simons term is a quantised level, not an angle. (iii) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension} with Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v), which gives the common value on the reversal pair (the former Premise P4 is not used: its only content beyond that clause was on the fork $r = 0$); (iv) is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-trichotomy-descents-data}(1) at its level, $\epsilon$ being continuous. The degree computation is recorded in the script. Clause (i) rests on Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}, which supplies the one-handed listing choice that is the particle-antiparticle orientation, read here as the descent's flag.

__notes__.note.dark-matter.setting-p1-attacked-cou:
The case against the orientation clause: a flag is defined per rung (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) and every tower has rungs, so nothing in the algebra forbids each tower its own choice; the clause is a statement about the event, not the algebra. What survives: the choice is initial data of the descent (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation}), a per-tower choice would be a second uncaused datum of one event, which P2 refuses, and the clause is used in exactly two places, neither of which fails without it: the internal statement of the fifteenth refutation (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}), and the second route to Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v), whose first route is P2's audit. Withdraw the clause and (v) stands by the audit, P4 reverts to a premise for the mirror, and the count is unchanged. Off the reversal orbit the clause cannot reach: over $\C$ there is no signature, an identification of two towers' ambients is fixed only up to a group whose two components exchange the two families, and ``the one flag'' would be defined only up to the bit at issue; hence the scoping in Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}.

The case against the rest: nothing in the transport principle forbids multiple division events, and a multi-descent history would give each tower its own $\Lambda$, expansion and asymmetry, dissolving the count, the ratio and the universality at once. What survives: the vacuum theorem derives one frozen point per metric, and there is observationally one metric, a second gravity being excluded by the equivalence-principle tests \cite{ButlerT6}; and the dating Observation locates the descent at the origin, a later descent being a second big bang inside this one's classical era, for which the record shows nothing \cite[Obs.~7.4]{ButlerT12}. P1 is supported, not proved; a pre-descent theory of the freezing (the capstone's declared open problem) would settle it. Its reading as a sourcing rule (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}) is a further choice inside P1, the one that makes the count and the audit consistent; a different rule would have to be stated and both re-run.
__notes__.note.dark-matter.setting-machine-verific:
Every computational identity asserted in this paper at its own proof level, with the exceptions listed at the end, has been verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T14.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT14}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: exact rationals and arbitrary-precision integers, no machine floating point outside the two checks of Part N, an order-of-magnitude estimate labelled as floating point in its printed messages, the irrational constants entering only through rational brackets proved by integer inequalities. Two hundred checks, all passing, in fourteen parts keyed to statement tags; five are labelled as records rather than computations in their own printed messages (the $\theta$ no-go's degrees and homotopy table, the parity identity of Part J, the one-loop coefficient formula of Part H, and the coupling-departure illustration), and every witness the script relies on internally is counted in an aggregate check. Parts H, J and K use forty-digit decimal arithmetic for logarithms, exponentials and fixed points, the inequality chain itself being exact rational algebra. The script's printed labels give every bracket; the parts, with the statements they cover:

\emph{Part A} (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}): the census over every signature of dimension at most ten, the reversal $r \mapsto -r$, the P3 representatives and the sterile set, and the window sensitivity (four windows, four answers).

\emph{Part B} (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}): the isometry witnesses in $(1,3)$ and $(2,2)$, entry by entry, and the Jacobian of the isotropy equations.

\emph{Part C} (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}): the survey ratio, its uncertainty and the remainder $4.364$.

\emph{Part D} (Propositions \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation}): the $\theta$ no-go's inputs as recorded data, and on $\Cl(1,1)$ the reflection that exchanges the null pair and preserves the form.

\emph{Part E} (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}, Propositions \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}, \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}): the dilution exponents as a function of the sourcing rule for $D = 2, 3, 4$ and the single-sheet reading; the $\Neff$ coefficients, the thresholds $0.51$, $0.46$ and $0.465$, the entropy-release factor and the joint five-dimensional channels.

\emph{Part F} (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success}): the two valuations and the ratio of the ends.

\emph{Part G} (Theorems \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}, \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}, \claimref{dark-matter.mode-counts-two-modules-which-one}): for every $\Cl(p,q)$ of dimension at most five, the centre, a primitive idempotent by exhaustive search, the division algebra by exact rank, the component count and module dimension, agreeing with the classical table on all twenty signatures; the abstract agreements across residues; the module dimensions, the Witt indices and the weightings.

\emph{Part H} (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}): the one-loop chain as exact rational algebra on a grid, the one-flavour factors at both ends of the ceiling range, and the coupling sensitivity with its ten-percent window.

\emph{Part I} (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}): the even-subalgebra isomorphisms for $(2,4)$, $(4,2)$, $(1,3)$, $(3,1)$, the matching types, the pair-count witnesses and the mirror threshold $0.448$.

\emph{Part J} (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities}, Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}, Propositions \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}, \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}): the Fock ideals on the split forms of dimensions four, six and eight (the null-pair relations, the blade and top state, the chirality eigenvalues, the exchanging versors and their determinants), $I$ central in dimensions five and seven, the parity identity to dimension ten, the odd-dimensional Fock ideal at $m = 1, 2, 3$, the reversion form on the twistor ideal; and the mirror's cosmology at the paper's inputs: $\eta$ and $\eta^{1/3}$, the species count and the floor, the gravitational yield's shortfall, the hot deposit, the weak freeze-out, the bottleneck, the reheating, the mean-mass deficit, recombination, the cross-sections, cooling times and mean free path.

__notes__.note.dark-matter.setting-thickness-conta:
R3 is a premise: it fixes the thickness at one cell radius, on one side, and nothing in the series does. This subsection gives a mechanism that returns that value. The count is made in the towers' own spaces, by asking which quanta of a tower are in contact with a world whose space is a slice of the tower's, the count being made on the nested world's space and carried to the containing world's by reciprocity. The mechanism has four clauses on how cells make contact. They were chosen with the value known, each has a stated alternative that the observation excludes (the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}), and the mechanism holds for one nesting at a time and does not compose across two (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.scope-mechanism}). So what follows explains R3's value and does not derive it, and the tier of the rule is unchanged. The one-parameter family in which the thickness is a parameter is recorded afterwards as the sensitivity analysis. Throughout, $d_{b}$ is the common spacing of R2, the Wigner-Seitz radius, lengths are in units of it, a quantum's \emph{cell} is the ball of radius one about it in its tower's space, and a count is \emph{downward} when a world counts the cells of the tower whose space contains its own.

\emph{The four clauses.} (C) Contact: a quantum sources a world whose space is a slice of its tower's exactly when its cell meets that slice. (I) Indivisibility: a quantum that sources a world counts whole, its mass $m$ and not a fraction of it set by how much of its cell the slice cuts. (S) The side: across the direction a nesting adds or lacks, sourcing runs on one side only, the side named by the sign of the central volume element $\omega$ of the odd member of the nesting, whether that member is the tower counted or the world counting; where the odd member has two modules (residues $1$ and $5$) each module names a side, and a sheet of the three-dimensional tower holds one module. (O) Reciprocity: the ratio of two nested towers' densities found by the downward count on the nested world's space is the ratio read on the containing world's space. S postulates the side; Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algebra} only says what a side is. O is the equality of R3's two thicknesses in another form (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}(iii)).
__notes__.note.dark-matter.what-s-uses-what-it-doe: S needs a side for each sourcing quantum or sheet, and the side is postulated. What the lemma supplies is that a side exists: in an odd tower $\omega$ is central, so its sign is a label a quantum carries where the centre splits and a convention for the tower where it does not, and in the even neighbour's frame that sign is the sign of the direction the nesting adds; the even towers have no such sign, their centre being $\R$. S selects no module: where $\omega^{2} = +1$, Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mode-counts-two-modules-which-one}(ii) counts both modules under P2, R2 with S then puts each at half the density on its own side, and the two slabs sum to one cell radius, exactly as if one module held the whole density. Where $\omega^{2} = -1$ the sign is a convention for the tower, every quantum sources the same side, and the count is one cell radius at full density. S uses no orientation off the reversal orbit: reversing the neighbour's $P$ exchanges every side at once and the count is unchanged, so P1's orientation clause stays where Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} keeps it. And S does not orient the odd tower's family: Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension} concerns the flag bit, and the sign of $\omega$ is a different object. What is postulated is the one-sidedness itself, and for the residue-$1$ sheets the further stipulation that a sheet holds one module; without the first both sides count and the total is $5.729$ (the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}), and without the second the residue-$1$ sheets are sourced from both sides.
__notes__.note.dark-matter.scope-mechanism: Two limits keep the mechanism an explanation of R3's value rather than a derivation of it. First, it does not compose. For the double nesting of the three-dimensional tower's plane in the five-dimensional tower's space, R3 gives $\rho_{5\mathrm{D}}/\rho_{3\mathrm{D}} = V_{2}/V_{4} = 0.637$, one cell radius for each of the two unshared directions; counting the five-dimensional cells that meet the plane directly by C and I gives $V_{2}^{2}/V_{4} = 2$ on the full transverse disc, $1$ on a half-disc and $\tfrac{1}{2}$ on a quadrant, and S is undefined there, $P^{-1}\omega$ across two directions being a bivector. So C with I holds for adjacent nestings only, which is where the rule uses it, and O is not tested there; R3, which composes, is the statement, and the mechanism is a reading of one step. Second, C restricts the homogeneous integral of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} to one cell radius, and under it the five-dimensional tower's matter further from this world sources the one metric not at all. With P1 that matter is either absent, so that the extra direction is about one cell deep (the co-expanding direction of Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.extra-direction-must-co-expand}, forced rather than allowed) and C adds nothing to the integral over it, which is R3; or present and inert to gravity, against Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.sourcing-rule-forced-not-chosen}(i), which takes the integral over the whole direction as the only covariant choice. On the first branch C is R3; on the second it contradicts a proposition the paper calls forced. On neither is it a foundation.
__notes__.note.dark-matter.setting-what-could-fix-: By Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-frozen-point-de-sitter-radius}, our world with $\Lambda > 0$ is de Sitter space of radius $\ell = \sqrt{\tfrac{3}{\Lambda}}$ at the level of the frozen point, and Euclidean de Sitter space $\dS_{4}$ is $\Sph^{4}$ of radius $\ell$, the boundary of $\B^{5}$ of radius $\ell$. The towers share one gravity, and $\Lambda$ is a parameter of the laws, so every tower has the same $\Lambda$ and its own Euclidean de Sitter sphere $\Sph^{n(r)}$ of the same radius $\ell$; the nesting of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(iii) is the nesting of these spheres by equators. So the objects of the rule's sphere form (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not}), and the common unit R2 needs, are already in the series, with the unit the de Sitter radius rather than a microscopic spacing.

__notes__.note.dark-matter.setting-introduction:
The tower paper of this series proves that the (1,1) ascent preserves the signature residue $p - q$ modulo eight, so the transport construction runs in eight parallel towers, one per residue of the real Clifford clock \cite{ButlerT3}. Applied to the matter that gravitates and does not shine, the towers give the mirror's share of it by theorem, prove that the other four shares cannot be derived from the series as it stands, and then, by one geometric rule on three premises of its own, return the whole ratio as a closed form, $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$, found by fitting. The paper's level is Tier C: nine premises and a hypothesis, each stated before use, attacked in its own section and carried with its cost, and a falsifiability section that says how each claim would be refuted.

The chain, in outline. A residue fixes no signature, so one must be chosen for each; at the dimension nearest four (Premise P3, with the census of what other choices give) a residue has a single time when the chosen signature has exactly one timelike direction, and two residues fail, $r = 0$ with two times and $r = 4$ with none, the fixed points of the mirror map. Six towers can hold matter, this one and five dark; that they do is a theorem for the mirror (indifference along the reversal orbit) and an inference from the observed remainder for the odd four, since the framework has no other dark candidate (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). The flag does not refine the sort (Witt's theorem), so the $r = 0$ exclusion rests on a two-time import alone, carried as a fork. The five are dark by superselection: the residue is an invariant of the algebra soldered to the metric, not of the algebra alone ($\Cl(1,3)$ and the sterile tower's $\Cl(0,4)$ are the same algebra, $\Mat(2, \mathbb{H})$), so no operator built from the one metric changes residue, and given the sector decomposition the towers are exactly stable, touching this one only by weight. The descent's one orientation, the flag bit, is the chirality of the pure spinor, and its two halves lie in opposite families only when the tower's dimension is a multiple of four: the odd residues cannot be oriented, the even ones can at their P3 representatives, and the asymmetric dark matter is the mirror tower's alone.

Of the five dark towers this paper derives the contribution of one, the mirror's, by theorem, and gives the other four by a rule:
\begin{gather*}
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; \underbrace{1}_{\text{mirror, derived, to half a percent}} \;+\; \underbrace{2 \cdot \frac{4}{3} + 2 \cdot \frac{8}{3\pi}}_{\text{four odd towers, the unit-ball rule, fitted}} \;=\; \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \;=\; 5.364,\\[6pt]
\text{against the survey's}\quad
\frac{\Omega_{c}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; 5.364 \pm 0.065.
\end{gather*}
The first term is a theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-assembled}). Everything the Standard-Model paper builds this tower's content from is invariant under the signature reversal that carries $(1,3)$ to the mirror's $(3,1)$, so the mirror tower is a second Standard Model, a massless mirror photon and mirror neutrinos included; with P2 its share is one to half a percent (the half percent is the mean mass per baryon of a helium mirror), at any mirror temperature, because the stored asymmetry is a charge of the descent and not a thermal number. The share is exact and fragile (one flavour's difference at the ceiling would move it by a factor between $4.89$ and $21.4$), and it is already at the edge of the record's bound on dissipative dark matter.

The second term is not derived: the odd towers carry no asymmetry (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}), and a symmetric relic's density needs a coupling rule the series does not supply (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}). What the paper offers instead is the unit-ball rule of the section “The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule”: every populated tower holds one quantum of a common mass per unit ball of its own space, in one common unit, and its matter enters the one metric per unit of our volume through one cell radius of each direction its neighbour lacks. A tower's share is then the ratio of unit-ball volumes $V_{3}/V_{D}$: $\tfrac{4}{3}$ for each three-dimensional tower, $\tfrac{8}{3\pi}$ for each five-dimensional one.

The rule rests on three premises the series does not supply, and it was found by fitting. Its one length, the thickness of the direction we cannot see, is a premise; a contact mechanism returns its value from four clauses on how cells meet a world, each with an alternative the observation excludes, and that mechanism explains the value without deriving it. With the thickness left as a parameter the total has a floor at $5.255$, the family's one prediction independent of it, and meets the observed value at one unit and at $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ units, the chord and the arc of a quarter turn of the nested spheres. The series' one length, the de Sitter radius, makes the spheres physical, but its reductions give totals of $5$, $5.67$ or $4.33$; the inverse-square law shows the thickness is not a gravitational quantity; and the three-dimensional towers' sheets, which momentum conservation displaces with the matter, respond to gravity in full, so that a Boltzmann computation returns the standard model's linear spectra for the rule's composition. All of this is at observation level with each cost stated (the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress}), and it changes nothing derived.

The rest of the paper: a projection lemma makes every tower's content dilute as this tower's does; the radiation audit closes the three-dimensional towers by theorem plus Polyakov and leaves the mirror (whose cost is a seeded temperature below $0.448$ of ours) and the five-dimensional towers as open channels; the orientation is shown to be the arrow itself (the seventeenth refutation); infall through this tower's horizons is routed through parallel boundary mode spaces at one wall; and the rung scale is valued conditionally at $3.5 \times 10^{11}$ to $6 \times 10^{14}$ GeV. The exposures are five species, gravity-only coupling, composite self-interaction in the three-dimensional towers, which the galaxy-cluster simulations exclude unless their matter is collisionless, dissipative mirror matter against the dark-disk and collisional-fraction bounds, dark neutron-star mergers with our tidal deformability and no counterpart, permanent direct-detection nulls, and a dimmed final burst for evaporating black holes; the section “The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper” collects every prediction in one table.

__notes__.note.dark-matter.halo-built-collisionles: Beyond linear order the question is what the sheets do to a halo, and the answer is an argument, not a simulation. A particle of a three-dimensional tower has two velocities: its motion within its sheet, the tower's own dynamics, and the motion of the sheet, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress} follows the normal component of gravity pointwise. The one constraint the sheets impose is that at a point of a sheet the normal velocity is single-valued, the sheet being a surface; in-plane velocities are whatever the tower's dynamics allows, and sheets may cross, nothing forbidding it and the sourcing rule already stacking them. Cold dark matter is the same object in all three directions: a single-valued velocity field on a three-dimensional Lagrangian sheet in phase space, multi-streaming only where Lagrangian patches cross. So the sheet family's phase space contains cold dark matter's, one direction treated exactly as cold dark matter treats all three and two directions treated more permissively; with cold initial conditions, which the seeding floor gives (the section “Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows”), the in-plane motion is itself a cold single-valued flow and the two phase spaces coincide. The Lagrangian map of the sheet matter is then cold dark matter's at every order in collisionless dynamics, not only at the linear order a figure of the original checks, and a simulation of sheet-labelled particles against plain ones would integrate the same equations. Halo shapes, velocity structure and the pancake, filament and halo sequence are cold dark matter's. What can differ is what the sheets add. First, in-sheet self-interaction: a quantum collides only with quanta of its own sheet, at composite strength on the reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}, so the collision rate is set by the surface density within a sheet and the galaxy-cluster bounds on $\sigma/m$ must be re-expressed for a cross-section per sheet before the fraction test of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(v) is read against them. The companion note T14b does this: per unit of the mass gravity sees, the cross-section is $10^{8}$ to $10^{13}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$, so at composite strength the sheet matter is a fluid within its sheets, not collisionless, and in simulated galaxy clusters it forms a cored component rounder than cold dark matter (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-composition-simulated}). The conclusion of this remark therefore holds only if the three-dimensional towers' matter is collisionless. Second, on the deposit branch, an in-plane thermal velocity $\sigma_{v}$: free streaming then damps small scales within the plane only, and averaged over orientations the damping is $\langle\exp(-k^{2}\sigma_{v}^{2}\tau^{2}\sin^{2}\theta)\rangle$, milder than isotropic warm dark matter at the same dispersion by the missing normal direction; at the seeding floor $\sigma_{v}$ is of order $10^{-4}$ of our matter's thermal velocity and the cutoff lies far below any observed scale. Structural level: the argument rests on cold initial conditions, on the sheets carrying no stress and on the sheet matter being collisionless.

__notes__.note.dark-matter.setting-dark-stable-cou:
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Discussion of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}: the interval, and the mirror's nucleosynthesis.} The paper's own mechanism favours the hot end (the tower charges are created at the freezing in quanta of order the reheating temperature), but the nucleosynthesis is computed at the floor, the one value the framework fixes, the hot end being the trivial case; the interval straddles the crossover of $\eta'$ at one, charge-dominated below it, and statements that hold only at the charge-dominated end are labelled ``at the floor''.

\smallskip\noindent\emph{Weak freeze-out and the burning branch.} The mirror's expansion rate is set by the visible plasma at $T = T'/\xi$, so its weak rate over the Hubble rate scales as $T'^{3}$: at the floor it crosses one at $T' \approx 0.43$ to $0.45$ GeV, above the mirror's QCD crossover at $155$ MeV. At the floor the mirror's weak interactions froze out with its quarks free and the up-down ratio thermal (at the hot end the crossing falls below $100$ MeV, under the crossover but still where $n/p \approx 1$), so the neutron-to-proton ratio at hadronisation is near one and burning is the framework's expectation. A proton-only mirror would need a mirror lepton asymmetry large enough to bias that ratio, a datum the framework does not fix; it is carried as the alternative branch.

\smallskip\noindent\emph{The bottleneck and the reheat, at the floor.} The deuterium bottleneck opens near $T' = 0.23$ to $0.24$ MeV, not at our $0.062$, at a baryon density of $0.8$ to $1.2 \times 10^{31}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and a cosmic time of microseconds, so mirror neutrons cannot decay first and whatever can burn, burns (by then $T'/T$ has risen by about $2.6$ from its seeded value through the two sectors' separate entropy conservation, leaving $\eta'$ within ten percent). The released $7.07$ MeV per nucleon enters a plasma carrying $25$ to $33$ keV of photon energy per baryon and $2.75$ times that with pairs (thermal pairs at zero chemical potential, a lower bound on the budget, so the reheating factor below is an upper bound), so complete burning would reheat the mirror by $3.0$ to $3.2$, to $T' \approx 0.70$ to $0.78$ MeV and $\eta' \approx 0.72$ to $0.81$. Photodisintegration makes the endpoint a nuclear-statistical-equilibrium problem that completes only as expansion cools it; the figures are the completion limit. At the hot end burning does not reheat the mirror appreciably.

\smallskip\noindent\emph{Recombination, and the caveat on imported bounds.} On the burning branch the mirror is helium. It recombines earlier than we do because its photons are fewer, at $T'$ between about $0.55$ eV at the hot end and $0.68$ eV at the floor after its burning ($0.85$ eV on the proton-only branch, and higher still for helium), at a visible temperature between $0.1$ and $0.8$ keV across the interval. So bounds derived for a mirror sector with our $\eta$ assume a baryon-to-photon ratio, and on the burning branch a composition, nothing like the mirror's; the mirror-galaxy analysis of refutation item 6 rescales $\eta'$ and includes a helium mirror, but only at the hot end of the interval.

In the \emph{diffuse phase} mirror gas accreted into a halo is shock-heated to the virial temperature and ionised, a fluid with a mean free path of order ten parsecs ($\sigma/m \sim 10^{8}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$); this is what the Bullet Cluster's bound on the subcluster's mass loss, about $23$ percent and inferred from the mass-to-light ratios, tests \cite{Randall2008}; read as a bound on the dark matter, $18.6$ percent passes, and simulated, a merger in which only the mirror collides gives a mass-to-light change of $0.82$, consistent with the observed $0.84 \pm 0.07$, as cold dark matter's is (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-composition-simulated}(ii)). Its radiative cooling time is of order ten gigayears at the virial radius and a gigayear or less inside the cooling radius, where $n \gtrsim 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, so, as with our baryons, the inner gas radiates its support within a Hubble time and the outer gas does not. In the \emph{settled phase} what cools forms a mirror disk or compact objects of total mass up to $\Omega_{b'} \approx \Omega_{b}$; a thin disk of the visible disk's mass, about $50\ M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ locally, exceeds the Gaia thin-dark-disk bounds of a few $M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ \cite{Schutz2018, Widmark2021} by an order of magnitude, so the settled phase must not be a thin disk. A thick or fragmented component, or mirror feedback holding gas in the diffuse phase, avoids the bound; fragmentation into compact objects is closed by the microlensing limits (compact objects at most $1$ percent of the halo from $1.8 \times 10^{-4}$ to $6.3\ M_{\odot}$ and $10$ percent up to $860\ M_{\odot}$ \cite{Mroz2024}) unless the objects form outside that window. The phase split, the star-formation efficiency, the settled gas's fate and whether helium composition delays settling are the model; the record's mirror-galaxy analysis \cite{RouxCline2020} models them with a rescaled $\eta'$ and a helium mirror at the hot end of the interval, not at its floor; Randall et al.'s mass-to-light ratios \cite{Randall2008} are the observation behind the mass-loss bound, and Clowe et al.'s offset \cite{Clowe2006} behind the lensing test. Model-dependent, so on the burning branch a tension and not an exclusion: this is the framework's one theorem-level dark-matter prediction, and it is at the edge of the record already. The companion note T14b models the settled phase in the Milky Way (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-composition-simulated}(iv)): the proton-only branch is excluded at the Sun, and the burning branch's helium mirror, cooling slowly and with helium-star feedback, is open at the Sun under some normalisations of its gas and in the bulge only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass, so that either of two measurements not yet made would decide it. Neither measurement can yet be made from published results. The tightest Gaia bound on a thin dark disk, about $5\ M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at $95$ percent \cite{Widmark2021}, holds only for scale heights of $50$ pc or less, and at the $100$ to $500$ pc the test needs the bound is weaker; the dynamical models of the bulge \cite{Portail2017} measure its dark mass, about $3.1 \times 10^{9}\ M_{\odot}$, as halo-like, and do not separate a disk-like part from the stars' mass-to-light ratio. The test therefore needs two analyses not yet made: a vertical-dynamics or phase-space-spiral analysis of Gaia data with a dark disk of that thickness, and a bulge model with a disk-like dark component. Until then the Galaxy test is registered, not run.
\item \emph{Dark neutron-star mergers.} The copy theorem makes the mirror sector baryonic, dissipative and at the proton mass, so it forms stars, and its neutron stars have our equation of state: the same maximum mass and the same tidal deformability $\Lambda(M)$. The prediction is a class of compact-binary mergers in the ground-based gravitational-wave band with component masses of one to two solar masses, $\Lambda$ in the range of ordinary neutron stars, and no electromagnetic counterpart at any depth or distance. Nothing in the standard model produces that class, and primordial black holes in the mass range have $\Lambda = 0$. GW190425, with no counterpart and its deformability unconstrained, is the class's example event. __notes__.note.dark-matter.r1-against-series-mass-:
The odd-dimensional mass formulas can be written in a Pfaffian form or in the determinant form of this world's two-constituent formula \cite[Prop.~4.1]{ButlerT11}, and the two are normalised differently; compared across normalisations they make five-dimensional quanta appear at most half as heavy as ours, which would break R1 before it starts. In one normalisation the comparison is even. Let the tower have signature $(1, n-1)$, $n = 3, 4, 5$, with $\gamma^{0}$ Hermitian, $(\gamma^{0})^{2} = 1$, each spatial $\gamma^{k}$ anti-Hermitian, and define $j^{\mu} = \psi^{\dagger}\gamma^{0}\gamma^{\mu}\psi$ and $m^{2} = j_{\mu}j^{\mu}$. Then
\[
m^{2} \;=\; (\psi^{\dagger}\psi)^{2} - \sum_{k}(j^{k})^{2} \;\le\; (\psi^{\dagger}\psi)^{2},
\]
with equality exactly on the eigenvectors of $\gamma^{0}$, where every spatial current vanishes because $\gamma^{k}$ anticommutes with $\gamma^{0}$ and so maps each eigenspace to the other. So the heaviest quantum of unit norm has $m = 1$ in three, four and five dimensions alike (script: the three sets of matrices built exactly, the relations, the bound and its attainment in Gaussian-rational arithmetic). The five-dimensional spinor space is the four-dimensional Dirac space and the first four components of its current are the four-dimensional current, so one five-dimensional constituent is the same object as a four-dimensional Weyl pair, which is why mass begins at one in five dimensions and at two in four: the counts differ, the object does not.
