__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.abstract: The dark-matter paper T14 fixes how much matter each of five dark towers holds, not what that matter is. This note builds it with the Standard-Model paper's construction, in geometric algebra. A constituent is an element of the spin-irreducible even ideal of the tower's conformal algebra, and its scalars are the commutant of the spin action there. We prove that this field is the division algebra of the next residue: the reals in the three-dimensional towers, the complex numbers in this tower and the mirror, the quaternions in the five-dimensional towers. One identity of the reversion pairing then says where mass begins (two constituents in three and four dimensions, one in five); the momentum-preserving mixings are the field's unitary groups; and, under the series' identification premise and one transposition rule, the gauge algebras follow. The mirror carries the Standard Model again. Both three-dimensional towers carry the abelian $\so(2) \oplus \so(2)$: two copies of single-flavour electrodynamics in $2+1$ dimensions. Both five-dimensional towers carry $\uu(3)$, dark colour and one abelian charge, with vector-like quarks, leptons and a neutral singlet; with an external imaginary unit both would carry the Standard-Model algebra instead. The towers of each odd dimension differ only in discrete structure. Three consequences follow. The equal-mass premise of the unit-ball rule has no mechanism in any odd tower. A cold mirror is an unstated exception to T14's indifference premise. (Status now, 7 November 2026: it is an exception to P2 at its version-1 reach; P2 as scoped, version 2, leaves $\xi$ free, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}, and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent, Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}.) No configuration of the towers as built passes the cluster, radiation and mirror bounds together. The algebraic results are verified in exact arithmetic.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.setting-introduct:
The dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} derives eight parallel towers, one per residue $r = p - q \bmod 8$ of the real Clifford algebras, and finds that six can hold matter: this one ($r = 6$, signature $(1,3)$), its mirror ($r = 2$, $(3,1)$), two three-dimensional towers ($r = 1, 7$) and two five-dimensional towers ($r = 3, 5$). The towers touch only through the one shared metric. By its unit-ball rule the five dark towers hold, relative to our baryons, the shares $1$, $4/3$, $4/3$, $8/(3\pi)$ and $8/(3\pi)$, whose sum $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$ is the observed ratio of dark to visible matter. T14 proves the mirror a copy of this tower; for the four odd towers it says how much matter each holds and leaves open what that matter is.

This note answers that question by doing in each tower what the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} does in ours. T12's chain is: a constituent; the number of constituents at which mass begins; the mixings that preserve total momentum; the automorphisms of the smallest massive composite, identified with the gauge algebra; the content and its charges; then, with imported physics, hadrons, atoms and a stable relic. Every link is transposed here, and where the transposition meets an obstacle the resolution is taken from the way our tower resolves the same obstacle.

Everything is written in geometric algebra. A constituent is an element of a minimal left ideal of an even Clifford algebra; its momentum is the vector part of $\psi e_{t} \rev{\psi}$; its field of scalars is the corner algebra $f \Cl^{0} f$ with the adjoint $x^{\dagger} = e_{t}\rev{x}e_{t}^{-1}$. The mass laws are identities of the reversion pairing $\rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}$.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.setting-prior-art: The real Clifford algebras, their periodicity and their spinor modules are classical (Cartan, Chevalley \cite{Chevalley1954}, Lounesto \cite{Lounesto2001}); the even-subalgebra isomorphisms $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \cong \Cl(p,q-1)$ and $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \cong \Cl^{0}(q,p)$ are standard \cite{Porteous1995, Lounesto2001}, and the division algebra of each even algebra can be read off the periodicity table. The spacetime-algebra current $j = \psi\gamma_{0}\rev{\psi}$ and its square $j^{2} = |\psi\rev{\psi}|^{2}$ are Hestenes's \cite{Hestenes1966, DoranLasenby2003}. Mirror matter and its cosmology have a long literature \cite{FootMirror2004, RouxCline2020}; the parity anomaly and topologically massive gauge fields in $2+1$ dimensions are Redlich's and Deser, Jackiw and Templeton's \cite{Redlich1984, DJT1982}; Polyakov confinement \cite{Polyakov1977}; five-dimensional gauge theory, its Chern-Simons terms and its strong-coupling scale are standard \cite{IMS1997, CLP2000}. The identification of a gauge algebra with the automorphisms of the minimal massive composite is T12's, and its global form and content are classical structure theory once that identification is made.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.setting-setting-i:
Throughout, a tower is $V = \R^{p,q}$ with an orthonormal basis $\{e_{a}\}$, $Q(e_{a}) = e_{a}^{2} = \pm 1$, and $\Cl(V) = \Cl(p,q)$ its Clifford algebra, with even subalgebra $\Cl^{0}(V)$, reversion $x \mapsto \rev{x}$, grade involution $x \mapsto \hat{x}$ and grade projection $\ip{\cdot}_{k}$. In a causal signature ($\min(p,q) = 1$) the \emph{time direction} $e_{t}$ is the one basis vector of the minority sign, as in T14's convention \cite[Prop.~3.1]{ButlerT14}, and $Q(e_{t}) = \pm 1$ accordingly. The tower's conformal algebra is $\Cl(\hatV)$ with $\hatV = V \oplus \R^{1,1}$, that is $\Cl(p+1, q+1)$. The pseudoscalar of an algebra of dimension $n$ is $\omega = e_{1}e_{2}\cdots e_{n}$, central when $n$ is odd, with $Q(\omega) = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}(-1)^{q}$.

The objects that the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} and T12 describe in twistor language are, here, the even ideals of the conformal algebra and their elements; this note uses only the latter.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.two-readings-unit: Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.third-pairs-unit-five-dimensions} is where the two five-dimensional towers part. At $r = 3$ the unit that builds the pairs is fixed by the algebra, and the quaternionic unit group of a single constituent, which preserves its momentum (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.ladder}), does not preserve the pair structure. At $r = 5$ every choice of unit is equivalent, and each choice cuts the quaternionic group to the circle it generates. Under U3 both towers therefore build their pairs with one complex unit; they differ in whether the algebra names it. With an external unit, which commutes with the whole quaternionic group, the group survives in both towers alike (Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.branches-break-u-what-they-give}).
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.setting-ladder-pa: A \emph{ladder pair} is a pair $w, v$ of null vectors of the conformal space, $Q(w) = Q(v) = 0$, or of vectors dressed by a complex unit with $w^{2} = v^{2} = 0$, such that $wv + vw = 1$: the canonical anticommutation relations, one fermionic mode per pair \cite[Prop.~4.1]{ButlerT3}. Pairs built from real hyperbolic planes of $\hatV$ need no unit; their number is the real Witt index $\min(p,q) + 1$. The constituent's pair count is the complex Witt index $\lfloor (n+2)/2 \rfloor$ (T12's Lemma 2.12 in even dimension \cite[Lem.~2.12]{ButlerT12}; in odd dimension the same bound, with one generator left over).
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.setting-paired-to: T14's indifference premise P2 equates the data of the two members of each reversal pair, $\{2, 6\}$, $\{1, 7\}$ and $\{3, 5\}$ \cite[Prem.~2.2]{ButlerT14}. This section compares the members of the odd pairs as algebras.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.setting-sterile-t: Both sterile towers are empty under T14's Premise P3, which is what the unit-ball rule's agreement with the observed ratio assumes: a populated $r = 0$ at share one would move the total to $6.36$, fifteen standard deviations from the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$ \cite{Planck2018}.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.setting-content: T12's lesson is that fermions are generators of the composite, not its states \cite[Rem.~5.2, Prop.~5.3]{ButlerT12}. The generators of a hierarchy $\F^{m} \otimes \F^{k}$ are its single slot-pair cells; Hypothesis (S) adds the constituent-level states.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.setting-content-m: This section uses imported physics, stated as such, and decimal estimates, labelled; every number is reproduced by Part K of the script or by the named supplementary check.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.setting-position-: This paper is T14c of the series, a companion to the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14}, downstream of its Theorem 3.4 (types by residue), Proposition 4.1 (superselection), Theorem 4.3 (the mirror copy), Theorem 3.10 (no orientation bit in odd dimension) and its unit-ball rule (Section 7). It runs the construction of the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} in each tower, using the mass formula of the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11}, the rungs and canonical relations of the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3}, and, for comparison only, the families of T13 \cite{ButlerT13} and the neutrino sector of T15 \cite{ButlerT15}. Its physical tests take the simulations of the companion note T14b \cite{ButlerT14b} as given; the companion note T14a \cite{ButlerT14a} is upstream of nothing here. The cone fact for signature $(2,2)$ is the foundations paper T16's \cite{ButlerT16}. The capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} records T14's predictions; the section “What this note depends on, and what would refute it” lists what this note adds to them.
__notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.four-dimensional-: In this tower $x = \rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}$ lies in the two-dimensional space $(1-f)\Cl^{0}f$, a copy of $\C$, and Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(i) is T11's two-constituent mass formula \cite[Prop.~4.1]{ButlerT11} written in the even algebra, the pairing $x$ playing the role of the bracket. In five dimensions the law is the Fierz identity $j^{2} = (\bar{\psi}\psi)^{2}$ of a single Dirac spinor; the geometric statement is that the four-vector part of $\rev{\phi}\phi$ survives the idempotent.
__notes__.note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what: Every tower has rungs, the $(1,1)$ ascent adjoining a hyperbolic plane at each floor (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), so at tower level every residue is flaggable (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) and flaggability selects nothing. The flag counts no towers; it orients them (the section “The arrow counted”), and it equips them: a flag on $H_{k}$ is equivalently the complex structure $J_{k}$ on the complexification $H_{k} \oplus I_4H_{k}$ (the plane $H_{k} \otimes \C$, with the field theory's imaginary unit $I_4$, which commutes with every vector of the plane) whose $-I_4$ eigenline is the annihilated half (it lives in the complexification, since no real endomorphism squaring to $-1$ has the two real null lines as eigenlines), and the ladder pair's number operator generates a $U(1)$ commuting with the rest of the rung. So every flagged tower carries rung-level abelian charges, one per rung, whatever its ground type, as this tower's derived content acquires its $U(1)$ from three ladder pairs \cite{ButlerT12}.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.holographic-coincide: Writing, as here, $\Cl(2,4)$ for the Clifford algebra of the flat space in which $\mathrm{AdS}_{5}$ is the hyperboloid, and likewise for the other hyperboloids: the rung is the algebra of $\mathrm{AdS}_{5}$, whose isometry group $SO(2,4)$ is the conformal group of this world; the intermediate $\Cl(2,3)$ is the algebra of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}$ and, by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-odd-towers}, the conformal ambient of the three-dimensional residue-$7$ shadow, the group theory of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}/\mathrm{CFT}_{3}$; the de Sitter intermediate $\Cl(1,4)$ is the ambient of the Euclidean three-dimensional shadow $(0,3)$, also of residue $5$, the group theory of $\mathrm{dS}/\mathrm{CFT}$. All of this is the standard fact that the isometry group of $\mathrm{AdS}_{d+1}$ is the conformal group in $d$ dimensions, which any conformal field theory in $d$ dimensions shares whether or not a bulk exists; the note adds only the residues. The coincidence does expose a difference in what two frameworks say about one pair of algebras. Holography takes the bulk and its boundary to be one physics in two descriptions. The series takes the residue of a sector to be the signature of its soldered space (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower}), which a conformal class carries as well as a metric, so the boundary of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}$ has residue $7$ and lies, by Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock}, in a tower distinct from the bulk's; whether a conformal class with no chosen scale is also a superselected sector, Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue} speaking of the one metric, is a separate question and is not settled here; and the series' superselection is a statement about operators soldered to one metric, which a holographic dictionary is not. Whether that last difference means the two frameworks are speaking about different things, or that one of them is wrong about this pair, is not argued anywhere in the series and is not argued here; the remark records the question and claims nothing about the dynamical content of holography, to which the series has no counterpart.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.what-copies-are: the section “What a single generator does” to the section “The rung's even subalgebra is the anti-de Sitter algebra” are about this world's own ascent. The copy of the mirror's algebra that Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point}(ii) finds on the translation bivectors for $\Lambda < 0$ is not the mirror tower, whose vectors are soldered; it is the reason the two oriented towers' intermediate algebras are non-isomorphic (Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.copy-theorems-blind-spot}), and that non-isomorphism is a statement about the two towers' own ascents under their own solderings, unaffected by this section. Likewise the odd towers' algebras that Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-odd-towers} finds among the four extensions are their abstract algebras only.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.what-says-what-it-do: The de Sitter algebra of this world is two copies of this world, and the anti-de Sitter algebra of this world is this world merged with its mirror, with the mirror sitting on the momenta. This is a statement about the fibrewise Clifford algebra of $I^{\perp}$, which Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} supplies; it is not a statement that a negative cosmological constant would turn matter into mirror matter. The tower charge is soldered and superselected (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}), and Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.every-path-mirror-crosses-two-time} below shows that no path of sign changes at fixed dimension four connects the two oriented towers without passing through a sterile signature. What the proposition does establish is that the sign of $\Lambda$ selects which of two non-isomorphic algebras the frozen point's translation generators live in, and that only one of them contains the mirror. The observed cosmological constant is positive \cite{Planck2018}, so the algebra realised in this universe is the doubled $\Cl(1,4)$ with no copy of the mirror in it; the mirror on the momenta is a statement about the other sign. The same source gives the present Hubble rate as exceeding the asymptotic rate $\sqrt{\Lambda/3}$ of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-residue-completion-both-sides}(ii) by the factor $\Omega_{\Lambda}^{-1/2}$.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.no-mechanism: Together with Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue} this closes the question of a physical passage between the oriented towers within the series: the tower charge is superselected by the one metric, the only algebra in which both towers are present identifies them by the complex unit and not by any automorphism (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.mirror-inside-complexified-extension-absent-doubled}(iv)), and the only continuous route through signatures at dimension four runs through a signature with no causal structure. The two towers share gravity, and by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} the sign of $\Lambda$; that is the whole of the shared channel.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.what-adds-dark-energ: The dark-energy paper proves the parabolic-to-reductive rotation of the stabiliser at $\Lambda \neq 0$ at the level of groups. Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} is the same rotation at the level of the Clifford algebra: the null direction of the parabolic case is the nilpotent generator of a degenerate algebra, and the reductive case is that generator given a sign. That the tangent image keeps signature $(1,3)$ whatever $\Lambda$ does is Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(iv) read through Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-machine-veri:
Every computational identity asserted in this note has been verified in exact rational arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T14a.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT14ext}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py} and uses its basis-blade engine; no floating point anywhere. The script indexes generators from zero, so its $e_{0}, \ldots, e_{5}$ are the text's $e_{1}, \ldots, e_{6}$. Eighty-six checks, all passing, in nine parts.

\emph{Part A: the volume element.} Centrality and the sign $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2+q}$ on every diagonal signature of dimensions one, three, five and seven; the four signs of Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}; commutation of $\omega$ with the added generator; Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(iii) and the identities behind (i) and (ii), with the specific sign assignment of (i), over every odd signature of dimensions three and five; and the dimension of the centre, two over every odd signature of dimension at most five and one over every even signature of dimension at most six.

\emph{Part B: doubling and complexification.} For the two doubled extensions, the central idempotents $(1 \pm \omega)/2$, the two ideals of dimension sixteen, the action of $e_{5}$ as $+s\,\omega'$ and $-s\,\omega'$ on them with $s = e_{5}^{2}$, and the shadow meeting the even subalgebra exactly in its even part; for the two complexified extensions, the spanning of all thirty-two dimensions by $\Cl(p,q) + \omega\,\Cl(p,q)$ and $\omega^{2} = -1$ central.

\emph{Part C: where the mirror sits.} For all four extensions, the pairwise anticommutation and the squares of the bivectors $e_{\mu}e_{5}$, the generated subalgebra equal to the even subalgebra, the shadow of dimension sixteen meeting it in dimension eight, and the squares of $\omega e_{\mu}$ (reversed in the complexified cases, unchanged in the doubled ones); for $\Cl(2,3)$, the intersection equal to $\Cl^{0}(1,3)$.

\emph{Part D: the rung.} In $\Cl(2,4)$, the signatures $(2,3)$ and $(4,1)$ generated by $e_{i}e_{6}$ and $e_{i}e_{1}$, both generating the even subalgebra of dimension thirty-two; $\omega_{6}$ even, $\omega_{6}^{2} = -1$, commuting with every even element and anticommuting with every vector; the copies of $\Cl(1,3)$ and $\Cl(3,1)$ inside the even subalgebra.

\emph{Part E: the clock and the paths.} The residues of the four extensions, of the oriented pair and of the odd towers' representatives; the residue preserved by conformal completion; the centres of the four extensions of dimension two with the signs that separate the reversed pairs, and the centre of the rung of dimension one; the enumeration of sign-change walks from $(1,3)$ to $(3,1)$, exactly one, with $(0,4)$ a dead end.

\emph{Part F: the frozen point and the ascent's pair.} On exact rational instances of $I = a\,e_{+} + b\,e_{-}$ with $Q(I) = 3$, $-3$ and $0$: the orthogonality of the Lorentz frame and $w$ to $I$, $Q(w) = -Q(I)$; the signatures $(1,4)$, $(2,3)$ and $(1,3;1)$ of $I^{\perp}$ by exact congruence; $w = I$ and $I^{2} = 0$ in the null case; the opposite signs and anticommutation of $I$ and $w$; the generation of all sixty-four dimensions by $I^{\perp}$ with $I$ when $Q(I) \neq 0$; in $\Cl(1,3;1)$ the nilpotent generator, its anticommutation with the Lorentz frame, the sixteen-dimensional ideal and its vanishing square; and the signature $(1,3)$ of the Lorentz frame in all three cases.

\emph{Part G: the transport on the wall.} In the projective-to-conformal paper's model of the completion of $(1,3;1)$: the signature $(2,4)$ by exact congruence; the rank-five linear system for the image of the partner and its unique null solution $c = 0$; the norm $2ab$ of $aI + b\varphi$ on instances of both signs and zero; the invariance of the norm under rational boosts and the swap, the image staying orthogonal to the Lorentz frame; the centres of the two intermediate algebras; and the null pair $v, v^{*}$ in the root paper's normalisation, its identification with the canonical frame, and the norms $\pm\alpha\beta$ and orthogonality of $\alpha v \pm \beta v^{*}$.

\emph{Part H: the two negative results.} The canonical null frame in the rung's diagonal basis; $B = I \wedge \varphi = -e_{+}e_{-}$ with $B^{2} = 1$, commuting with the Lorentz bivectors and vectors and anticommuting with $e_{\pm}$; the rational rotor $5/4 + (3/4)B$ unit, fixing the Lorentz frame, scaling $I$ by $4$ and $\varphi$ by $1/4$, moving a frozen point along its hyperbola; the mirror's $I^{\perp}$ signatures $(4,1)$ and $(3,2)$ on the same instances; the two-by-two rule; the common presentation of $\Cl^{0}(1,4)$ and $\Cl^{0}(4,1)$; and the squares and factorisations of the bare fifth generator.

\emph{Part I: the wall in the cosmological constant.} In four dilation gauges and at seven rational values of $\Lambda$ including zero: the Gram $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1,-\Lambda/3)$ of $I_{\Lambda}^{\perp}$ and its corank at $\Lambda = 0$ only; the gauge independence of the dying eigenvalue; the exact crossing slope $-1/3$ in the parametrisation by $\Lambda$; the signatures $(2,3)$ and $(1,4)$ on the two sides; the rescaled dying entries $\pm 1/3$ and the exceptional signatures; $\Lambda\,(G^{-1})_{ww} = -3$ in every gauge with $w_{0} = a\,I_{0}$; the total signature $(2,4)$ on both sides with the complement's sign switching; the five-dimensional span at the wall and the signature of the Lorentz frame with $I_{0}$ and $\varphi$; and the general hyperplane model of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-residue-completion-both-sides}(iii) for five signatures $(p,q)$ and five values of $t$.

What the script does not check: the isomorphism types $\Mat(2,\HH)$ and $\Mat(4,\R)$ of the two oriented shadows (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}, imported; the note uses that they differ and, in Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.copy-theorems-blind-spot}, which type belongs to which tower), the frozen-point geometry (Facts \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} and \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-degenerate-algebras}, imported; the script checks the algebra of a vector of each norm sign in the rung, not that the parallel tractor is that vector), the algebra-map properties of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(i) and (ii) (argued in the text; the script checks the identities they rest on and the four extensions in detail), the identification of the MacDowell-Mansouri translation part with the bivectors $e_{\mu}e_{5}$ beyond the signs of their squares, the reversal of the tractor norm under $g \mapsto -g$ (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}(i), argued in the text; Part H checks its consequences from the reversed signature declared as input), and the transitivity of the boosts on each level set of the norm (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iii), argued in the text; Part G checks invariance under particular boosts).
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-introduction-4: \textbf{Levels.} Proposition \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter}, Corollary \claimref{simulations.confinement-scale-does-not-matter} and Lemma \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator} are proved here; Computation \claimref{simulations.cluster-bound-two-dimensions} is a numerical evaluation of an imported result. Everything that rests on simulation or on a galaxy-formation model is at observation level: it compares models with one another and with published measurements, and its costs are listed in the section “What the tests decide, and what they cost”. The runs are idealised (about $80{,}000$ particles per merger and $32{,}000$ per assembled cluster, one merger geometry run once per composition, no cosmological surroundings), and they are suited to comparing compositions, not to precision prediction.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-simulation-code: The code \file{tpsim.c} \cite{ButlerSuppT14b} was written for these tests, in C with OpenMP. It solves gravity for every particle and smoothed-particle hydrodynamics separately for each fluid species, so that each fluid interacts hydrodynamically only with itself (Premise S1).
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-gravity:
Gravity is computed with a Barnes-Hut octree \cite{BarnesHut1986}. A node of side $\ell$ at distance $r$ from its centre of mass is opened if $\ell^{2} > \theta^{2}r^{2}$ or if the particle lies inside it, with $\theta = 0.7$. Forces use Plummer softening,
\[
\mathbf{a}_{i} \;=\; \sum_{j} G\,m_{j}\,\frac{\mathbf{r}_{j} - \mathbf{r}_{i}}{\bigl(|\mathbf{r}_{j} - \mathbf{r}_{i}|^{2} + \epsilon^{2}\bigr)^{3/2}},
\qquad \epsilon = 15\ \kpc ,
\]
with nodes standing in for the particles they contain.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-smoothed-partic:
Each fluid species has its own tree. The kernel is the cubic spline of support $2h$ \cite{MonaghanLattanzio1985},
\[
W(r, h) = \frac{1}{\pi h^{3}}
\begin{cases}
1 - \tfrac{3}{2}q^{2} + \tfrac{3}{4}q^{3}, & 0 \le q < 1,\\[2pt]
\tfrac{1}{4}(2 - q)^{3}, & 1 \le q < 2,\\[2pt]
0, & q \ge 2,
\end{cases}
\qquad q = r/h ,
\]
normalised so that $\int W\,d^{3}r = 1$. Density is gathered at each particle's own smoothing length, $\rho_{i} = \sum_{j} m_{j}W(r_{ij}, h_{i})$; pressure and sound speed are $P_{i} = (\gamma - 1)\rho_{i}u_{i}$ and $c_{i} = \sqrt{\gamma(\gamma - 1)u_{i}}$. The next smoothing length is
\[
h_{i} = \tfrac{1}{2}\Bigl(\frac{3N_{\mathrm{ngb}}m_{i}}{4\pi\rho_{i}}\Bigr)^{1/3}, \qquad N_{\mathrm{ngb}} = 40,
\]
limited to a change between $0.8$ and $1.25$ per step, floored at $h_{\min} = 10\ \kpc$, and cut to $0.7h_{i}$ if a particle's neighbour list reaches its cap of $2000$.

The equations of motion are the symmetric form \cite{Monaghan1992},
\begin{align*}
\frac{d\mathbf{v}_{i}}{dt} &= -\sum_{j} m_{j}\Bigl(\frac{P_{i}}{\rho_{i}^{2}} + \frac{P_{j}}{\rho_{j}^{2}} + \Pi_{ij}\Bigr)\,\mathbf{g}_{ij},
\\
\frac{du_{i}}{dt} &= \sum_{j} m_{j}\Bigl(\frac{P_{i}}{\rho_{i}^{2}} + \tfrac{1}{2}\Pi_{ij}\Bigr)\,\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{g}_{ij},
\end{align*}
with the kernel gradient averaged over the two smoothing lengths, $\mathbf{g}_{ij} = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\nabla_{i}W(r_{ij}, h_{i}) + \nabla_{i}W(r_{ij}, h_{j})\bigr)$, and $\mathbf{v}_{ij} = \mathbf{v}_{i} - \mathbf{v}_{j}$. The artificial viscosity acts on approaching pairs \cite{MonaghanGingold1983}:
\[
\Pi_{ij} = \frac{-\alpha\,\bar{c}_{ij}\mu_{ij} + \beta\mu_{ij}^{2}}{\bar{\rho}_{ij}}, \qquad
\mu_{ij} = \frac{\bar{h}_{ij}\,\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{r}_{ij}}{r_{ij}^{2} + 0.01\bar{h}_{ij}^{2}} \quad (\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{r}_{ij} < 0),
\]
with $\alpha = 1$, $\beta = 2$ and bars denoting pair means. Internal energy is floored at $u_{\mathrm{floor}} = u(10^{4}\ \mathrm{K})$ for mean particle mass $0.6\,m_{p}$.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-sheet-fluid:
Premise S2 is implemented by contracting both the kernel gradient and the separation vector of every pair of sheet-fluid particles with an averaged pair operator before they enter the equations above. With $\mathbf{n}_{i}$ and $\mathbf{n}_{j}$ the unit normals of the two particles' sheets,
\begin{equation}
P_{ij}(\mathbf{v}) \;=\; \mathbf{v} - \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl((\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}_{i})\mathbf{n}_{i} + (\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}_{j})\mathbf{n}_{j}\bigr),
\qquad
\mathbf{g}_{ij} \mapsto P_{ij}\mathbf{g}_{ij}, \quad \mathbf{r}_{ij} \mapsto P_{ij}\mathbf{r}_{ij}.
\end{equation}
$P_{ij}$ is the mean of the two in-plane projectors, the rejections $\mathbf{v} \mapsto (\mathbf{v}\wedge\mathbf{n}_{i})\,\mathbf{n}_{i}$ and $\mathbf{v} \mapsto (\mathbf{v}\wedge\mathbf{n}_{j})\,\mathbf{n}_{j}$ (Lemma \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}(ii)). When all normals are parallel it is the projection onto the common sheet, nothing acts along the normal except gravity, and motion along it is ballistic; for differently oriented normals it is not a projection and keeps part of each normal component (Lemma \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}(iii)). Each particle's normal is fixed at its initial value, random per particle or common to all (the section “Initial conditions”).
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-sheet-fluid-2: The averaging in the relation displayed with \claimref{simulations.confinement-scale-does-not-matter} is an approximation: it stands in for the interaction of quanta on differently oriented sheets, which T14 does not specify (Premise S2). The runs with all sheets parallel (the section “Initial conditions”) do not use the average. With the normals along the line of sight (\texttt{rule\_perp}) the subcluster fails as with random sheets; with the normals along the merger axis (\texttt{rule\_par}) the fluid slides through along the axis and the subcluster keeps a lensing peak but half its mass (the section “Results: mergers and halos”).
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-machine-verific:
\textbf{The script.} \file{verify\_T14b.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT14b} imports the series' shared library \file{GA.py} and checks the note's computational identities and derived numbers: $60$ checks, all passing, in eight parts. A few are arithmetic restatements of a quoted number rather than tests of a claim (D4, F3, R4, R7). Algebraic identities are checked in exact rational arithmetic; evaluations with physical constants, transcendental functions and integrals in double precision, with the tolerance stated beside each check.

\emph{Part A: composition.} $T(1) = (11\pi + 16)/(3\pi)$ between rational bounds; $T(\pi/2) = T(1)$; the three shares and their sum; the baryon, galaxy and gas fractions of every halo; the three colliding shares and their order against the bounds.

\emph{Part B: self-interaction.} Proposition \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter} as an exact identity; $n_{b}$ and $d_{b}$; the ratio $V_{3}/V_{2} = 4/3$ from the unit-ball volumes; the range of the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter}; the bound on $\lambda$; Computation \claimref{simulations.cluster-bound-two-dimensions}, with Bessel functions by their series; the five-dimensional range; the mean free path.

\emph{Part C: the code's algebra.} The kernel's normalisation, derivative and continuity, exactly; Lemma \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}(ii) in the blade engine of $\Cl(3,0)$, (iii) in exact rationals, including $P_{ij}^{2} \ne P_{ij}$ for orthogonal normals, and (i) on a rational instance with distinct normals and viscosity; the cooling update as a polynomial identity; the units; the settling threshold at $\mu = 0.6$ and its temperature for the helium plasma, from the code's $u(T)$ formula and constants; the algebra of the bremsstrahlung coefficient (the electron and ion densities and $T(u)$ for He$^{++}$) against $du/dt = -\varepsilon/\rho$, with the code's constants.

\emph{Part D: initial conditions.} The Hernquist matching and $r_{200}$, exactly; the Jeans equation for $\sigma_{r}^{2}$ at three radii; the truncation fraction; the merger geometry, exactly.

\emph{Part E: the mirror's composition.} Freeze-out temperatures, $Y'$, $\eta'$, the recombination temperature and $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}}$.

\emph{Part F: cooling.} The metal-free $\Lambda_{N}$ at three temperatures; the cooling-time ratios of helium to our gas; the Tozzi-Norman conversion.

\emph{Part G: supernova energy.} The continuity of the IMF; our energy per unit mass; $F$ for our IMF's shape and the best shifted IMF.

\emph{Part R: recorded outputs.} Selected simulation and model outputs, carried as constants from the run summaries, and the comparisons the text draws from them: the mass-to-light change, ratio and sampling error; the merger separations; the halo ratios, with their seed-paired values; the Galaxy floors against the decisive limits and the three readings of the bulge room. The outputs themselves are reproduced by the deposited scripts, not by this one: Part R does not read \file{outputs/}, so a change to a deposited output would not fail the script.

\emph{What the script does not check:} the simulations and the Galaxy model themselves, which the section “Running the code” shows how to rerun, and the imported Facts and published bounds.
__notes__.note.simulations.what-premise-c-needs: Premise C is not derived, and it is not T14's reading. What it needs is a statement about the three-dimensional towers' couplings: whether their abelian charges are gauge charges, as the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} makes the charges of the four-dimensional minimal massive composite, and with what strength their lightest stable state interacts. The series fixes neither \cite[Prop.~A.4]{ButlerT14}. The note tests reading (C) as stated and records this as its main cost (the section “What the tests decide, and what they cost”).
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-confinement-sca: \textbf{How it is computed.} (i) is Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-low-energy-scattering-two-dimensions} evaluated at $ka = 0.0050$ and $ka = 2.4 \times 10^{-13}$, with $\mu = m/2$; the script computes the Bessel functions by their series and the partial-wave sum to $m = \pm 1$. (ii) is Proposition \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter} with $s = 3.5$ cm solved for $\lambda$. (iii) With the s-wave alone $\lambda = 4\sin^{2}\delta_{0}/k$, so $\lambda < 4.8 \times 10^{-12}$ fm gives $\delta_{0} < 1.7 \times 10^{-7}$; in the logarithmic form $\lambda \approx \pi^{2}/\bigl(k(\ln(ka/2) + \gamma_{E})^{2}\bigr)$, so the bound requires $|\ln(ka/2) + \gamma_{E}| > 9.3 \times 10^{6}$, that is $a < 10^{-4.0 \times 10^{6}}$ fm. These are floating-point evaluations, checked in the script (the section “Machine verification”); nothing below depends on their digits beyond the first.

\textbf{The five-dimensional towers and the mirror.} A five-dimensional tower's matter counts through one cell radius $L$ of its extra direction, so its effective cross-section is $\sigma_{4}/L$ with $\sigma_{4} \sim \lambda^{3}$; in general $\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sigma_{D}\,d_{b}^{\,3-D}$. For $\lambda = 0.21$ to $2$ fm and $L = d_{b}/(1+z)$ this is $7 \times 10^{-20}$ to $6 \times 10^{-17}\ \cmg$: collisionless by geometry. The mirror's figure is that of Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-mirror}, $5 \times 10^{7}$ to $2 \times 10^{8}\ \cmg$: a fluid like our gas. a figure of the original shows the three.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-effective-cross: A quantum of a three-dimensional tower lives in a two-dimensional sheet. It collides only with quanta of its own sheet, and its cross-section is a length $\lambda$. Gravity sees the tower's matter per unit of shared three-volume \cite[Lem.~6.1]{ButlerT14}.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-what-tests-deci:
\textbf{Statements of T14 the tests bear on.} T14 records the outcome in its Section 7.7 and at each place cited below \cite[Fact~7.32]{ButlerT14}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item At composite strength the three-dimensional towers' self-interaction is $10^{8}$ to $10^{13}\ \cmg$ (Proposition \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter}), far above the cluster bounds \cite[Prop.~6.2]{ButlerT14}.
\item ``A halo built from collisionless sheets is a cold-dark-matter halo'' \cite[Rem.~7.30]{ButlerT14} needs the sheet matter collisionless; as a fluid it is cored, rounder and less concentrated than collisionless matter (Observation \claimref{simulations.halo-shapes}).
\item The self-interacting fraction, counted as all colliding dark matter, is $68$ percent in reading (W) and $19$ percent in reading (C); T14's Proposition 7.15(v) counts the three-dimensional towers alone (about half); for the merger bound its Section 7.7 adds the mirror, as here \cite[Prop.~7.15(v), \S7.7]{ButlerT14}. The Bullet bound on mass loss is about $23$ percent \cite{Randall2008}, inferred from the mass-to-light ratio.
\item The mirror analysis T14 cites \cite[\S 8, refutation item 6]{ButlerT14} rescales $\eta$ and includes a helium mirror down to $T'/T = 10^{-3}$ \cite{RouxCline2020}; it covers the hot end of T14's interval, not its floor.
\item For the helium branch with stars the excess over the Galaxy's room at the Sun is a factor of $1.5$ to $2.8$ over the $2\sigma$ room of $15\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at equal feedback, and at the helium-star feedback it falls within the $2\sigma$ room at the Sun in most set-ups in total normalisation (all of them at the best-shifted IMF) and persists in the bulge unless the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass (Observation \claimref{simulations.mirror-galaxy}). The order-of-magnitude excess holds for the proton-only branch and for a mirror that forms no stars \cite[\S 8, refutation item 6]{ButlerT14}.
\item The current bounds on the settled phase are the thin-disk bound of Widmark et al.\ \cite{Widmark2021} and the microlensing bound of Mr\'oz et al.\ (compact objects at most $1$ percent of the halo from $1.8 \times 10^{-4}$ to $6.3\ \Msun$ and $10$ percent up to $860\ \Msun$ \cite{Mroz2024}), which T14's refutation item 6 uses. The thin-disk bound, about $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at $95$ percent, holds for scale heights of $50$ pc or less; it does not reach the $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at $100$ to $500$ pc that would decide the helium branch, and the bulge models \cite{Portail2017} do not separate a disk-like part of the bulge's dark mass, so the Galaxy test is not yet decidable.
\end{enumerate}

__notes__.note.simulations.setting-colliding-share:
If collisional dark matter were held back in a merger as completely as the gas is, the share of the dark matter that collides would bound the subcluster's mass loss, whatever its cross-section. As a heuristic, then, by the relation displayed with \claimref{simulations.imported-mirror}:
\[
\text{(W): } f_{\mathrm{mirror}} + f_{3\mathrm{D}} = 68.3\%, \qquad
\text{(C): } f_{\mathrm{mirror}} = 18.6\%, \qquad
\text{mixed count: } 50.3\%,
\]
against a mass loss of at most $23$ percent (Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-bullet-cluster}). These are shares of the dark matter, as T14 counts them, so the bound is read as a bound on the subcluster's dark matter, its gas having been stripped in any case. Counted with the subcluster's own gas ($13.7$ percent of its mass: the baryon fraction $0.157$ less the $2$ percent in galaxies), the colliding fraction of its mass is $0.137 + 0.843\,f$, with $f$ the colliding share of the dark matter above: $71$ percent in (W), $29$ in (C) and $56$ in the mixed count, and on that count reading (C) is above the bound as well. T14 \cite[Rem.~7.10, Prop.~7.15(v)]{ButlerT14} counts the self-interacting fraction as the three-dimensional towers alone (about half) and tests the mirror's $18.6$ percent separately; for a bound on mass loss the two add. The simulations of the section “Results: mergers and halos” test the heuristic, and it holds only roughly in either direction: colliding matter that partly passes through is held back less than its share (\texttt{rule\_par}), while a halo that puffs loses more than its share from a fixed aperture (Observation \claimref{simulations.merger}). a figure of the original shows the comparison.

__notes__.note.simulations.setting-measurements-4: \textbf{Halo shapes.} The assembled cluster's centre is found by shrinking spheres on all mass. Its three-dimensional axis ratios come from the iterative reduced inertia tensor, $I_{ab} = \sum m\,x_{a}x_{b}/r_{\mathrm{ell}}^{2}$ over the ellipsoid of the current shape, inside $300$ and $1000$ kpc. The projected ellipticity $1 - b/a$ is the same construction in two dimensions inside a projected $500$ kpc, averaged over the three coordinate projections; this is the quantity of Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-cluster-shapes}.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-result:
So with the consistent yield the Galaxy test would be decided by either of two measurements not yet made: a $2\sigma$ limit below $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ on extra disk-like mass at the Sun with scale height $100$ to $500$ pc (the room is $4.6 \pm 5$, the dynamical stellar surface density less the counted one, Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-milky-ways-mass-budget}), or a limit below $1.7 \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$ on disk-like dark mass in the bulge volume, which would bound the mirror's mass there directly, whatever reading of the room is taken. Either excludes the helium branch under every choice tried with yield $yF$; with the yield held at ours the limits would need to reach $4.2\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ and $1.3 \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$. The thin-gas bound is not used to decide, because the mirror's gas at high $F$ sits at the star-formation threshold of the model, which is its least certain part.

Roux and Cline find $\Omega_{b'} \lesssim 0.8\,\Omega_{b}$ at low mirror temperature \cite{RouxCline2020}. Their analysis includes a helium mirror with $\eta' = \eta\,\beta/x^{3}$, down to $x = T'/T = 10^{-3}$, which covers T14's hot end; what it does not include is the floor of T14's interval and the helium-star supernova factor.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-imported-dark-m:
Throughout, the dark composition at $c = 1$ is
\begin{equation}
f_{\mathrm{mirror}} = \frac{3\pi}{11\pi + 16} = 0.1864,\qquad
f_{3\mathrm{D}} = \frac{8\pi}{11\pi + 16} = 0.4971,\qquad
f_{5\mathrm{D}} = \frac{16}{11\pi + 16} = 0.3165,
\end{equation}
and the baryon fraction of every halo is $1/(1 + T) = 0.1571$. Each tower's matter makes up these fractions of the dark matter in every halo; the cosmic baryon fraction is taken as the rule's $1/(1 + T) = 0.1571$ in the simulations and as Planck's $\Omega_{b}/\Omega_{m} = 0.1565$ in the Galaxy model (whose $H_{0}$ is $67.4$ km/s/Mpc; the simulations use $70$ in $r_{200}$). The mixed count of T14 \cite[Rem.~7.10]{ButlerT14} exchanges $f_{3\mathrm{D}}$ and $f_{5\mathrm{D}}$ and has the same total, since $T(\pi/2) = T(1)$. T14 records it as an assignment that is not consistent; it is run alongside as a comparison.
__notes__.note.simulations.abstract: The dark-matter paper T14 fixes how much matter each dark tower holds. By its unit-ball rule the mirror carries 18.6 percent of the dark matter, the three-dimensional towers 49.7 percent and the five-dimensional towers 31.6 percent. This note sets out the assumptions, equations, code and results of the tests of those amounts. Quanta confined to a sheet scatter in two dimensions; per unit of the mass gravity sees, their cross-section is a length times the sheet spacing. At composite strength the three-dimensional towers' matter is a fluid, eight to thirteen orders of magnitude above the cluster bound, whatever its confinement scale. A tree-gravity, multi-species smoothed-particle code, with the sheet fluid's pressure confined to its planes, follows a Bullet-like merger and a cluster's assembly. As T14 writes it, the composition fails both tests: 68 percent of the dark matter collides, with randomly oriented sheets the subcluster dissolves from the lensing map, and halos reach about 0.4 of the cold-dark-matter ellipticity. If the odd towers' matter is collisionless, only the mirror collides; the subcluster keeps a lensing peak on its galaxies, its gas trailing, at the cost of a puffier subcluster and halos about 0.8 as elliptical. A semi-analytic Milky Way model with helium-star feedback excludes the mirror's proton-only branch; its helium branch fits at the Sun under some normalisations, and in the bulge only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass. Two films, the code and a verification script accompany the note.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-introduction:
The dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} derives eight towers of the Clifford clock, proves that matter in the five populated dark towers gravitates on our metric and does nothing else, and by one geometric rule, the unit-ball rule, returns the ratio of dark to visible matter as $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$. The Clifford clock is the mod-$8$ periodicity of the real Clifford algebras, read as a ladder of spacetimes of different dimension, ours among them. The rule was found by fitting one length, so the total is not a test of it. What the rule also fixes, and what can be tested, is the composition: which towers hold how much, and therefore what that matter does when halos collide, when clusters assemble and when gas settles into a galaxy.

Tower dimensions count time. A three-dimensional tower has two space dimensions, so its matter lives on sheets, one direction short of ours; a five-dimensional tower has four, one more. There are two of each, and these four are the odd towers; with the mirror, a copy of ours, they are the five populated dark towers. The share of a tower is the ratio of unit-ball volumes, $V_{3}/V_{D}$ for a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions, which gives $V_{3}/V_{2} = 4/3$ for each three-dimensional tower (Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-unit-ball-rule-family}).

This note collects everything that was done to test the composition. It is a methods note: each section states its premises, the equations it uses, how the code implements them, and what came out. Nothing here changes a derived result of T14. Where the tests disagree with a physical statement of T14, the note says which statement and what was found, and T14 records the outcome in its Section 7.7.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-introduction-5: \textbf{Films.} Two films accompany the note \cite{ButlerSuppT14b}. \file{merger\_three\_ways.mp4} shows the merger in three compositions side by side (a figure of the original); \file{bullet\_moment.mp4} builds up the Bullet-like moment of reading (C) layer by layer against the observed numbers (a figure of the original). Both are also on YouTube, as ``Galaxy clusters in collision'' and ``The Bullet moment''. the section “The films” describes what each shows and how it was made.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-mirrors-cooling:
Bremsstrahlung from a fully ionised helium plasma, with Gaunt factor $1.2$ and $Z^{2} = 4$, gives $du/dt = -A\rho\sqrt{u}$ for a constant $A$. At fixed density this has the exact solution
\[
\sqrt{u(t + \Delta t)} \;=\; \sqrt{u(t)} - \tfrac{1}{2}A\rho\,\Delta t ,
\]
which the code applies after each step. When $u$ falls below $3u_{\mathrm{floor}}$ (for the helium plasma, $\mu = 4/3$, about $6.7 \times 10^{4}$ K) the particle becomes type $5$ and is collisionless from then on (Premise S3).
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-time-integratio:
All particles share one time step,
\[
\Delta t = \min\Bigl(\Delta t_{\max},\ \min_{i}\tfrac{1}{4}\sqrt{\epsilon/|\mathbf{a}_{i}|},\ \min_{i\in\text{fluid}}\tfrac{1}{4}h_{i}/v_{\mathrm{sig},i}\Bigr),\qquad
v_{\mathrm{sig},i} = \max\Bigl(2c_{i},\ \max_{j}\bigl(c_{i} + c_{j} - 3w_{ij}\bigr)\Bigr),
\]
with $\Delta t_{\max} = 0.002$, the inner maximum over approaching pairs, and $w_{ij} = \mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{r}_{ij}/r_{ij}$, negative on approach. The integrator is kick-drift-kick leapfrog, with the step shortened to land on each output time. Snapshots record positions, velocities, masses, internal energies, densities, smoothing lengths, types and halo labels. A merger run takes $15$ to $60$ minutes on two cores.

\textbf{Tests.} Two tests (\file{tpsim\_tests.py}, output deposited) check the sheet fluid and the code's stability. A uniform sphere of hot sheet fluid ($2000$ particles) with every normal along $z$ grows in rms extent by factors $1.49$ and $1.47$ in $x$ and $y$ over $0.1$ time units and stays at $1.00$ in $z$; with random normals it grows by $1.33$ to $1.35$ along all three axes. An isolated main-cluster halo with the unit-ball composition as written ($20{,}000$ particles, every species) keeps its $10$ and $50$ percent mass radii within $1.3$ percent over $1$ time unit ($0.98$ Gyr).
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-halos:
A halo of mass $M_{200}$ and concentration $c$ is a Hernquist sphere of the same mass inside $r_{200}$, with the scale length that matches the Navarro-Frenk-White inner profile \cite{Hernquist1990, NFW1997, SpringelDiMatteoHernquist2005}:
\[
r_{200} = \Bigl(\frac{GM_{200}}{100H_{0}^{2}}\Bigr)^{1/3},\qquad
a = \frac{r_{200}}{c}\sqrt{2\Bigl[\ln(1 + c) - \frac{c}{1 + c}\Bigr]},\qquad
M_{H} = M_{200}\Bigl(1 + \frac{a}{r_{200}}\Bigr)^{2},
\]
with $H_{0} = 70$ km/s/Mpc; the first is the radius inside which the mean density is $200$ times critical, and the last makes the Hernquist enclosed mass $M_{H}r^{2}/(r + a)^{2}$ equal $M_{200}$ at $r_{200}$. The sphere is truncated at $15a$, keeping $225/256$ of $M_{H}$. Positions are drawn from the enclosed-mass profile; each particle is then assigned a species at random in proportion to the species' mass fraction (Premise S5).

Collisionless particles take speeds from the isotropic Hernquist distribution function $f(E)$ \cite{Hernquist1990} by rejection sampling up to the escape speed, with random directions. Fluid particles start at rest with $u = \sigma_{r}^{2}/(\gamma - 1)$, so that $P = \rho\sigma_{r}^{2}$ and the gas is in hydrostatic equilibrium with the isotropic Jeans dispersion
\[
\sigma_{r}^{2}(r) = \frac{GM_{H}}{12a}\Bigl[12x(1 + x)^{3}\ln\frac{1 + x}{x} - \frac{x}{1 + x}\bigl(25 + 52x + 42x^{2} + 12x^{3}\bigr)\Bigr], \qquad x = r/a ,
\]
which solves $d(\rho\sigma_{r}^{2})/dr = -\rho\,GM(r)/r^{2}$ for the Hernquist density. The sheet fluid has no pressure along its normal, so it also carries a Gaussian velocity of dispersion $\sigma_{r}$ along the normal.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-merger:
Modelled on the Bullet Cluster: a main cluster with $M_{200} = 1.5 \times 10^{15}\ \Msun$ and $c = 4$ ($60{,}000$ particles), and a subcluster with $1.5 \times 10^{14}\ \Msun$ and $c = 7$ ($20{,}000$ particles), separated by $2500$ kpc along $x$ with impact parameter $150$ kpc along $y$, closing at $1800$ km/s, in the centre-of-mass frame. The random-number seed is $7$ for every merger. The truncated masses are $2.29 \times 10^{15}$ and $1.97 \times 10^{14}\ \Msun$, so main-cluster particles carry $3.8 \times 10^{10}\ \Msun$ and subcluster particles $9.8 \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$. Every halo has baryons $0.1571$ of its mass (galaxies $0.020$, our gas $0.1371$) and dark matter $0.8429$, split by composition as in the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}. The line of sight is $z$, perpendicular to the orbit.

The orientation codes describe the sheets' normals: \texttt{random} (a random normal per particle), \texttt{perp} (all normals along the line of sight, perpendicular to the merger axis, so the axis lies in the sheets) and \texttt{par} (all normals along the merger axis). Suffix \texttt{nm}: the mirror collisionless from the start; suffix \texttt{lo}: half resolution.}

The variants isolate one effect each. \texttt{mixed} is T14's mixed count with the mirror as gas. \texttt{mixednm} and \texttt{rule1nm} make the mirror collisionless from the start, so that only the sheet fluid collides and its effect is seen apart from the mirror gas's; \texttt{rule1} and \texttt{rule1nm} let only one of the two three-dimensional towers collide, halving the sheet fluid.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-cluster-assembl: Eight progenitors with $M_{200} = 2 \times 10^{14}\ \Msun$ and $c = 5$, $4000$ particles each, are placed at random inside $1.5$ Mpc, at least $700$ kpc apart, with random velocities of dispersion $150$ km/s, and the whole is set at rest at the origin. They collapse and merge into one cluster, $2.3 \times 10^{15}\ \Msun$ in all with $M_{200} \approx 2.0 \times 10^{15}\ \Msun$ at the end, followed to $t = 2.0$ ($1.96$ Gyr). Each composition in the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.merger} is run with two random seeds, $11$ and $23$; \texttt{rule1} is run once, with seed $11$ (projected ellipticity $0.17$, $0.72$ of CDM's with the same seed), and is not tabulated.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-measurements: \textbf{Centres.} Each cluster's centre is found by shrinking spheres on its own collisionless members (dark matter, galaxies and settled mirror matter): the centre of mass within a sphere, the sphere shrunk by $10$ percent, repeated down to $40$ kpc. The search at each snapshot starts from the previous one.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-measurements-2: \textbf{The Bullet-like moment.} The Bullet-like moment is the nearer of the two snapshots after closest approach that bracket the observed $720$ kpc separation, or the last snapshot ($t = 1.3$) if that separation is never reached.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-merger-3: The half-resolution runs agree with the full ones (contrast $0.90$ against $0.95$ for \texttt{rule\_random}, $7.13$ against $7.50$ for CDM). a figure of the original follows the subcluster's own mass through the merger in the three main compositions.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-films:
Both films are rendered from simulation snapshots by \file{render\_lib.py} \cite{ButlerSuppT14b}. Each layer is a projected map along the line of sight on a grid of $300$ cells across the field, smoothed by a Gaussian of $18$ kpc (gas) or $25$ kpc (total mass), placed on a log scale, and added in its own colour onto a dark ground: galaxies as individual points, our gas weighted by $m\rho\sqrt{u}$ (a bremsstrahlung proxy for the X-ray map), mirror gas, and total projected mass as contours (what lensing measures). In Film 1 the sheet fluid is drawn as solid green contours rather than a fill, since a green fill screen-blended over the pink gas reads as white. The colour scales are fixed from one snapshot and shared by every panel, so brightness can be compared across panels.

The films use the same initial conditions as the runs of the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}, re-run with snapshots every $0.01$ time units ($9.8$ Myr). They reproduce the Bullet-moment measurements of the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator} within run-to-run noise (contrast $4.48$ against $4.74$ for (C), $0.92$ against $0.95$ for (W), $7.27$ against $7.50$ for CDM; mass-to-light change $0.79$ against $0.82$ for (C)), the differences coming from the shifted time steps.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-films-2:
\textbf{Film 1: the merger, three ways.} \file{merger\_three\_ways.mp4} ($16$ s, $1920 \times 1080$), titled for a general audience ``Galaxy clusters in collision: testing three ideas about dark matter'', shows CDM, reading (W) with random normals and reading (C) side by side from approach to $1.27$ Gyr, labelled ``Standard cold dark matter: none of it collides'', ``Unit-ball rule: mirror and 3D-tower matter collide'' and ``Unit-ball rule: only mirror matter collides''.

The subtitle states that collisions are within a tower's own matter and that different towers interact only through gravity (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}). Collisionless matter appears only in the total-mass contours, so the CDM panel has no orange or green layer and the right-hand panel no green one; the film's legend calls the sheet fluid ``colliding 3D-tower matter''. A panel beside the chart explains the Bullet-like separation.

Below the maps a chart, with its own legend, follows the subcluster's own mass (a figure of the original), with a cursor at the current time. The film runs without pauses; reading (C)'s Bullet-like separation, $1.17$ Gyr, falls at $15$ s. The camera is centred between the two clusters of the CDM run and its width follows their separation; positions are interpolated linearly between snapshots at three frames per interval.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-mirror-galaxy: The mirror's share is the same in both readings, so the merger cannot separate them. Its standing test in T14 is the Galaxy \cite[\S 8, refutation item 6]{ButlerT14}: dissipative mirror matter, $18.6$ percent of the dark matter, must not settle into structures the Milky Way's dynamics excludes.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-composition-rec: With $\xi$ in T14's interval the mirror's weak interactions freeze out at $T' = 274$, $117$ and $47$ MeV for $\xi = 2.8 \times 10^{-4}$, $10^{-3}$ and $4 \times 10^{-3}$ (rate normalised to our freeze-out at $0.80$ MeV, expansion set by our $g_{*} = 106.75$). T14 gives $0.43$ to $0.45$ GeV at the floor; both lie above the hadronisation temperature, so the helium fraction is the same. Near the floor the neutron-to-proton ratio is set at hadronisation, so $Y' = 0.996$, $0.995$ and $0.986$: helium, with $0.4$ to $1.4$ percent residual hydrogen. Saha recombination of helium at $\eta'$, with $\xi$ raised by T14's entropy factor of about $2.6$ after burning (and by its burning reheat, a further factor of about $3.1$, at the floor), puts it at a visible temperature of $0.08$ to $1.6$ keV, redshift $3 \times 10^{5}$ to $7 \times 10^{6}$, overlapping T14's $0.1$ to $0.8$ keV \cite[Prop.~4.6]{ButlerT14}; the ends differ by the recombination criterion and the reheating bracket, which does not affect what follows. The extra radiation is $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} \le 10^{-7}$. After recombination the mirror gas has a Jeans mass of $2 \times 10^{-6}$ to $2 \times 10^{-4}\ \Msun$ at $z = 100$: for the cosmic microwave background and large-scale structure it is cold dark matter, and the Galaxy is where it can be tested.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-model:
One Milky Way halo is shared by both sectors: the same growth, potential and spin. Its growth follows the Fakhouri-Ma-Boylan-Kolchin rate \cite{Fakhouri2010},
\[
\frac{dM}{dt} = A\Bigl(\frac{M}{10^{12}\Msun}\Bigr)^{1.1}(1 + bz)\sqrt{\Omega_{m}(1+z)^{3} + \Omega_{\Lambda}},
\]
with $(A, b) = (46.1\ \Msun/\mathrm{yr}, 1.11)$ (mean) or $(25.3, 1.65)$ (median). Each sector accretes its baryon share $f_{b}\,dM$ ($f_{b} = \Omega_{b}/\Omega_{m} = 0.1565$) into a hot halo, an isothermal sphere $\rho_{g}(r) = m_{\mathrm{hot}}/(4\pi Rr^{2})$ at the virial temperature $T = \mu m_{p}V^{2}/2k$ of its own composition. Following Croton et al.\ \cite{Croton2006}, with their parameter values, and with $R$ and $V$ the halo's virial radius and circular velocity, $m_{\mathrm{hot}}$ and $m_{\mathrm{cold}}$ the hot and cold gas masses, $r_{\mathrm{cool}}$ the radius at which the cooling time equals the reference time, and $\lambda$ the spin parameter:
\begin{align*}
t_{\mathrm{cool}}(r_{\mathrm{cool}}) &= t_{\mathrm{dyn}} = R/V \quad (\text{or the cosmic time}),\\
\dot m_{\mathrm{cool}} &= \tfrac{1}{2}m_{\mathrm{hot}}\frac{r_{\mathrm{cool}}}{R}\frac{V}{R} \quad (\text{all hot gas per } t_{\mathrm{dyn}} \text{ if } r_{\mathrm{cool}} > R),\\
\dot m_{*} &= \alpha\,\frac{m_{\mathrm{cold}} - m_{\mathrm{crit}}}{t_{\mathrm{disk}}}, \qquad
m_{\mathrm{crit}} = 3.8 \times 10^{9}\Msun\,\frac{V}{200\ \mathrm{km/s}}\,\frac{3R_{d}}{10\ \kpc},\\
\Delta m_{\mathrm{reheat}} &= \epsilon_{\mathrm{disk}}F\,\Delta m_{*}, \qquad
\Delta E = \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_{\mathrm{halo}}F\,\Delta m_{*}V_{\mathrm{SN}}^{2},\\
\Delta m_{\mathrm{eject}} &= \frac{\Delta E - \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta m_{\mathrm{reheat}}V^{2}}{\tfrac{1}{2}V^{2}}, \qquad
\dot m_{\mathrm{return}} = \gamma_{\mathrm{ej}}\,m_{\mathrm{ej}}/t_{\mathrm{dyn}},
\end{align*}
with $\alpha = 0.07$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{disk}} = 3.5$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{halo}} = 0.35$, $V_{\mathrm{SN}} = 630$ km/s, $\gamma_{\mathrm{ej}} = 0.5$, recycled fraction $0.43$, $R_{d} = \lambda R/\sqrt{2}$ and $t_{\mathrm{disk}} = 3R_{d}/V$. Metals are followed in each sector from a metal-free start: a yield $y = 0.03$ per unit of stars formed enters the cold gas and is carried by every flow, and each hot halo cools at its own metallicity. The feedback factor $F$ multiplies the supernova energy and mass loading per unit stellar mass; for our sector it is a calibrated number $F_{\mathrm{cal}}$, and the mirror's is $F$ times that.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-model-2:
\textbf{Calibration and normalisation.} In each set-up our sector's $F_{\mathrm{cal}}$ is tuned so that its settled mass, stars plus cold gas, is the observed $6.0 \times 10^{10}\ \Msun$. The mirror, at $\Omega_{b'} = 0.995\,\Omega_{b}$, then runs in the same halo with feedback $F\,F_{\mathrm{cal}}$ and with yield $yF$ (its extra feedback comes from extra supernovae, which also make metals; the consistent choice) or, for comparison, $y$. Its surface density at the Sun is normalised to ours, either in total,
\[
\Sigma'_{x} = 47.1\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}\times\frac{m'_{x}}{6.0 \times 10^{10}\ \Msun},
\]
or with gas and stars scaled separately to our observed $13.7$ and $33.4$ (component normalisation). The mass the mirror puts in the bulge volume is taken as a quarter of its settled mass, the fraction of ours the bulge volume holds. There are $24$ set-ups: $M_{200} = 1.0$, $1.2$ and $1.5 \times 10^{12}\ \Msun$; mean or median growth; $t_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ or cosmic time as cooling reference; and a star-formation-threshold disk of $5.6$ kpc ($\lambda = 0.035$) or $2.6$ kpc ($\lambda = 0.0163$, the Milky Way's). Points with $F\,F_{\mathrm{cal}}$ above $12$ are dropped as not converged.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-how-much-feedba:
A pure-helium star is a bare helium core. Helium stars collapse to iron cores from about $2.5\ \Msun$ \cite{Woosley2019}, form black holes above final masses of about $10$ to $12\ \Msun$ \cite{Woosley2019, Ertl2020}, and explode by pair instability from $64$ to $133\ \Msun$ \cite{HegerWoosley2002}. Taking $10^{50}$ erg from $2.5$ to $3\ \Msun$, $10^{51}$ erg from $3\ \Msun$ to the black-hole cut, none above it to $64\ \Msun$, and pair-instability energies rising from $10^{51}$ to $10^{53}$ erg, the energy per unit mass formed relative to ours ($1.08 \times 10^{49}$ erg/$\Msun$ for a Chabrier IMF \cite{Chabrier2003}, one core collapse per $93\ \Msun$) is given in the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.halo-shapes}.

\emph{The tests at a glance.}

\textbf{What the tests decide.} Read as T14 writes it, the composition fails the merger and the halo shapes, and it fails them because of the three-dimensional towers' self-interaction, not because of the amounts. Read with the odd towers collisionless, the same amounts keep a lensing peak on the subcluster's galaxies with its gas behind and a mass-to-light change consistent with the observed ratio (as CDM's is; the measure does not discriminate), and come within a quarter of CDM on halo shapes. The remaining exposure is the mirror in the Galaxy, the same in both readings: its helium branch is open at the Sun, at the $2\sigma$ room, under some normalisations of the mirror's gas and, in the bulge, only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-position-series: This paper is T14b of the series, a companion to the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14}. It is downstream of T14's Proposition 4.1 (superselection), Theorem 4.3 and Proposition 4.6 (the mirror), Proposition 6.2 (the radiation audit and its self-interaction statement) and Section 7 (the unit-ball rule, its premises R1 to R3, the thickness family and the moving sheets), and it tests the composition T14's Section 7 fixes against the record. Remark \claimref{note.simulations.what-premise-c-needs} refers to the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the gauge charges of the four-dimensional minimal massive composite. It proves nothing about the series' algebra and changes no derived result of T14; it says which of T14's physical statements the simulations and the Galaxy model support and which they do not (the section “What the tests decide, and what they cost”). The capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} should carry the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.mirror-galaxy} beside T14's ledger entry, Premise C as the condition under which the rule's composition meets the cluster record, and the two measurements of the section “The mirror in the Galaxy” that would decide the mirror's helium branch.

Two rules follow from how the scripts are written. First, every file in \file{code/} must stay in that one folder: the scripts import one another by module name (\file{ics}, \file{render\_lib}, \file{sam2} and so on), and Python finds them because they sit beside the script being run. Second, the working directory matters. The simulation and measurement scripts read and write paths relative to the folder they are run from (\file{runs/}, \file{halos/}, \file{./tpsim}), so they must be run from \file{work/sims} (mergers, assembly, measurements) or \file{work/films} (film re-runs), never from \file{code/}. \file{reproduce.py} sets the working directory for each stage and copies \file{tpsim} into place, so the simplest course is to run everything through it.

\textbf{In an IDE.} In Visual Studio Code, open \file{T14b\_supplement} with \emph{File, Open Folder} (on Windows, from inside WSL with the WSL extension's \emph{Open Folder in WSL}). Create a virtual environment in that folder, select it as the Python interpreter, and run the stages from the integrated terminal at the top folder. To run or debug one script inside the IDE, give its launch configuration the stage folder as working directory, for example \texttt{"cwd": "\$\{workspaceFolder\}/work/sims"}. In PyCharm, mark \file{code/} as a sources root and set each run configuration's working directory to \file{work/sims}, \file{work/films} or \file{work/galaxy}. No C tooling in the IDE is needed: \file{tpsim} is built once from the terminal.
__notes__.note.simulations.setting-running:
From the top folder:
{ \begin{verbatim}
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python code/reproduce.py figures --deposited   # the note's figures from outputs/
python code/reproduce.py all --quick           # check the whole chain on small runs
python code/reproduce.py all                   # the note's runs, half a day to a day
python code/reproduce.py compare               # regenerated against deposited
\end{verbatim}}
The first run of \file{reproduce.py} redraws the eight figures from the deposited results in a few seconds; with the library versions above and the Computer Modern font they are identical, pixel for pixel, to the note's, and with other versions the data are the same and the typography may differ. The \texttt{--quick} option runs three small mergers ($4000$ particles), two small cluster assemblies and coarse films, and one disk scale of the Galaxy model, so that every stage can be checked in about half an hour; its numbers are not the note's, and it works in \file{work\_quick/}, so it never occupies the folders of the full runs. The \texttt{figures} stage draws from \file{work/outputs/}, takes any result not regenerated there from the deposited \file{outputs/}, and says which it used for each file. Stages can be run one at a time, in the order of the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.mirror-galaxy}; each needs only the ones before it, and \texttt{--threads} sets the number of OpenMP threads for \file{tpsim} (default $2$, as in the note). A merger run that has finished is skipped if the stage is started again.

__notes__.note.simulations.setting-running-2:
\textbf{Single runs by hand.} Compile \file{tpsim} and copy it into the stage folder, then run from there:
{ \begin{verbatim}
mkdir -p work/bin work/sims
gcc -O3 -fopenmp -o work/bin/tpsim code/tpsim.c -lm
cp work/bin/tpsim work/sims/
cd work/sims
python ../../code/merger.py mirror random mirror_only
python ../../code/halo.py rule random rule_random_s2 4000 2.0 23
python ../../code/analyze3.py cdm mirror_only
\end{verbatim}}
\file{merger.py} takes a model, a sheet orientation and a run name, then optionally the particle numbers of the two clusters (default $60{,}000$ and $20{,}000$) and an end time (capped at $1.3$). The models are \texttt{cdm}, \texttt{rule}, \texttt{mixed}, \texttt{mixednm}, \texttt{rule1}, \texttt{rule1nm} and \texttt{mirror} (the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}); the orientations are \texttt{random}, \texttt{perp} and \texttt{par}. \file{halo.py} takes a model, \texttt{random}, a run name, then particles per progenitor, end time and seed; the note's runs used $4000$, $2.0$ and seeds $11$ and $23$ (the defaults are $5000$, $2.5$ and $11$). \file{analyze3.py} measures the named merger runs and should be given \texttt{cdm} first, since own mass is relative to it. \file{tpsim} itself takes the initial-conditions file, an output prefix, the end time, the snapshot interval, the softening, the opening angle $\theta$, the cooling coefficient $A$, the energy floor, and optionally $\Delta t_{\max}$ and $h_{\min}$; the scripts pass $0.02$ (mergers) or $0.5$ (assembly), $15$, $0.7$, \texttt{ics.cooling\_A()}, \texttt{ics.u\_of\_T(1e4)}, $0.002$ and $10$.

__notes__.note.standard-model.what-settled-what-gr: Two consequences. First, the routing question is settled: Proposition \claimref{standard-model.spectrum-run} asks whether the pair and tower structure, ``eight towers derived'', supplies the demanded content, and the dark-matter paper carries the same as its successor problem (5). The towers do not. The answer does not depend on the odd towers' content, on their coupling rule, which the dark-matter paper shows not to be derivable \cite[Prop.~A.4]{ButlerT14}, or on their scales: it depends only on superselection, and it holds for any content whatever in the other seven sectors. What remains of the routing is the pair structure of this tower, taken up in the section “What is left in this tower”. Second, the one coupling the towers do share, the metric, contributes to the running of a gauge coupling only through graviton loops, which are suppressed by $(\mu/M_{P})^{2}$ and are not part of the one-loop gauge $\beta$-function at all; at the meeting scales of the section “The exact criterion at one threshold”, some two to five orders below $M_{P}$, this is at most a part in $10^{4}$, below the record's precision. The gravitational channel is therefore not an exception to Proposition \claimref{standard-model.no-tower-but-one-contributes-towers}; it is quoted at assembly level, as the framework's gravitational sector is not quantised in this series.

dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-giv.formal:
(i) For a five-dimensional tower whose light content is the nine vectors of its $\mathfrak{u}(3)$, eight gluons and the abelian photon, $c = 9 \times 2.3 \times 10^{-3} = 0.021$, $g_{d} = 18$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} = 3.5 \times 10^{-4}$ at the ceiling reheating; whether those are its light species is part of the coupling question of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}, and the value is the floor for that content, not for the tower.

(ii) For the mirror tower, whose content is the Standard Model's (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), the species sum over four real scalars, forty-five Weyl fermions and twelve vectors gives $c = 0.053$ counting the fermions as $22.5$ Dirac species and $0.078$ counting them singly, with $g_{d} = 4 + 45 \times \tfrac{7}{4} + 24 = 106.75$, hence $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}}$ between $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ and, with the charge reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, $\eta'$ between $19$ and $26$ at the floor; the bracket is the counting ambiguity and is carried as such, and $\eta'$ would fall below one at the floor only for a coefficient above about $4$.

(iii) The produced yield at the ceiling, $Y = 1.8$ to $2.7 \times 10^{-15}$ per unit entropy for the mirror, falls short of the $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy our baryon number requires by a factor of $3$ to $5 \times 10^{4}$; closing the gap would need $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ between $1.9$ and $2.2 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, $31.9$ to $36.2$ times the ceiling, where the floor itself would be $4 \times 10^{-3}$, above the charge-domination crossover and equal to the hot-deposit value of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, as it must be (the same energy per unit of baryon number either way). Gravity heats the dark towers; it does not populate them with charge, which is the descent's.

(iv) The mirror's contribution to $\Neff$, $7.447\,\xi^{4}$, is below $10^{-13}$ at the floor and below $10^{-8}$ at the hot deposit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}; a nine-vector tower's, $2.202 \times 18\,\xi^{4}$ for eighteen light polarisations, the coefficient being half the two-polarisation $\Delta\Neff$ bracketed in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}, is below $10^{-12}$ at its floor.
