dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3.technical:
Assume equal mass per quantum, one quantum per unit ball, and four clauses: contact (a quantum sources a world when its cell meets that world's space), indivisibility (it then counts whole), side (it sources on one side only, the side named by the sign of $\omega$) and reciprocity. For a five-dimensional tower with our space the hyperplane $x_{4} = 0$, the quanta at height $h$ that source our world are those with $0 \le h \le 1$ on their side, giving $\int_{0}^{1} dh/V_{4} = 1/V_{4}$ per unit three-volume, so $f_{5\mathrm{D}} = V_{3}/V_{4}$. For a three-dimensional tower the count runs downward on its own plane, giving $\rho_{\mathrm{us}}/\rho_{3\mathrm{D}} = V_{2}/V_{3}$, and reciprocity forces its sheets to be one cell radius apart, so $f_{3\mathrm{D}} = V_{3}/V_{2}$.

So the mechanism returns the one-cell-per-unshared-direction rule: its unit is the cell radius of the unit-ball premise, the side clause supplies the factor one half against two-sided contact, and reciprocity is the equality of the two thicknesses. The spacing $d_{b}$ cancels and the total is the unit-ball rule's.
dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3.lay: The rule for how much a hidden world's matter weighs on ours contained a free choice: how thick a slice of the hidden direction counts. This result shows that a simple contact picture fixes it, assuming equal mass per particle (R1) and one particle per unit ball (R2): a hidden particle counts if its small cell touches our space, it counts in full, it acts from one side only, and the counting works the same way in both directions (reciprocity). Under those assumptions the thickness comes out as exactly one cell, the value the rule had assumed (R3).
dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3.typing_note: Added R1 and R2 as assumptions since the statement is under them; the clauses C, I, S and O are not store entities and stay unedged; the unit-ball rule is not edged because its total is the comparison the mechanism reproduces and that rule itself rests on R3, which the mechanism replaces. Levels pass: lay now names R1 and R2 and the reciprocity clause O, which it had dropped.

proofs.main:
(i) Take coordinates on the five-dimensional tower's space $\R^{4}$ with our space the hyperplane $x_{4} = 0$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(ii)). By R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}) the quanta's centres have density $1/V_{4}$ per unit four-volume. A cell, the unit ball about a centre at height $x_{4} = h$, meets the hyperplane exactly when $|h| \leq 1$ (C); each such quantum counts whole (I); and each sources on one side only (S), the side its sign of $\omega$ names through Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algebra}(i). Which side is immaterial to the number: the quanta of one sign source our world from the slab $0 \leq h \leq 1$ and those of the other from $-1 \leq h \leq 0$, and whether the tower holds both signs at half the density each or one sign at the whole density, the quanta sourcing our world per unit of our three-volume number
\[
\int_{0}^{1}\frac{dh}{V_{4}} \;=\; \frac{1}{V_{4}},
\]
one cell radius of the extra direction; with R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}) the density is $m/V_{4}$ against ours, $m/V_{3}$.

(ii) The contact count runs downward only. A cell of the containing tower is a solid region meeting the nested world's space in a region of positive measure, whereas the cells of a tower nested in this world are discs in a sheet, and no count of discs per unit of our three-volume is defined until the sheets' spacing is. So count on the three-dimensional tower's own space, the plane $x_{3} = 0$ in ours (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(ii)), where our quanta are the containing tower's: their centres have density $1/V_{3}$ per unit three-volume, a cell meets the plane when $|x_{3}| \leq 1$, it counts whole, and each sheet is sourced from one side, the side named by the sheet's own $\omega$ across the direction it lacks (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algebra}(iii) or (iv); at residue $1$ each module names a side, and S takes each sheet to hold one module, so a sheet of either kind is sourced from one side; a sheet holding both would be sourced from both, at $2/V_{3}$). Per unit area of the plane our quanta number $1/V_{3}$ and the tower's own $1/V_{2}$, so on that world
\[
\frac{\rho_{\mathrm{us}}}{\rho_{3\mathrm{D}}} \;=\; \frac{V_{2}}{V_{3}} .
\]
By O the same ratio holds read on our space, $\rho_{3\mathrm{D}}/\rho_{\mathrm{us}} = V_{3}/V_{2}$. A family of sheets $s$ apart, each of density $m/V_{2}$ per unit area, has density $m/(V_{2}s)$ per unit three-volume, so $s = 1$: the sheets are one cell radius apart, which is the sheet clause of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} with its unit named. The nestings over the mirror (residues $3$ and $1$) are not reached by the count, since the residue-$3$ tower's space contains the mirror's and not ours; $f_{3} = f_{5}$ and $f_{1} = f_{7}$ are P2's audit along the reversal orbit, as in the relation displayed with \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

(iii) (i) and (ii) are R3's two clauses with the value one cell radius. The unit is R2's: with any other cell convention the contact slab has another width (the mean spacing is $n^{-1/3} = 1.61\,d_{b}$, and cubic cells give the $5.000$ of the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress}). Two-sided contact gives $2/V_{4}$, so S is the factor one half. In (ii) the downward count fixes $\rho_{\mathrm{us}}/\rho_{3\mathrm{D}}$ on the sheet, and for sheets $s$ apart the ratio read on our space is $V_{3}/(sV_{2})$; O sets the two equal, which is $s = 1$, so O is the equality of the sheet spacing and the extra length. Every count is a number of quanta per unit region of radius $d_{b}$, so $d_{b}$ cancels in each ratio as $m$ does by R1. The script recomputes the slab count as an integral, the downward count, the total, the alternatives of the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}, and the non-composition of Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.scope-mechanism}.

dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass.formal:
Every populated tower carries the same total mass $M_{\mathrm{tot}}$ on its de Sitter sphere. This is a democracy of mass, distinct from an equality of the asymmetry per mode (the former Premise P4, retired as a postulate; the asymmetry is equal in this tower and the mirror by Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)), which the odd towers do not carry.

\emph{Note (where D belongs).} D is the premise of the de Sitter reading of the count (Propositions \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}, \claimref{dark-matter.two-reductions}) and is not counted with R1 to R3: no stored statement of the fitted total with the cell radius as unit has D in its past cone, with one exception, the audit \claimref{synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r2-and-d-only-as-mass-per-unit-ball}, which sets the two readings side by side (its clause (ii) is under D, its clause (i) under R1 to R3) and so has both among its conditions, and Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(iv) has the de Sitter reading replace R2 by D. The two readings cannot be held together with more than one quantum per tower (argued): D with R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}) gives every populated tower the same number of quanta on its de Sitter sphere, and R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}) gives a tower of dimension $D$ one quantum per ball of the common cell radius $a$, so by the equality of the ball and sphere forms the number is $(\ell/a)^{D}$ for $D = 2, 3, 4$, and $x^{2} = x^{3} = x^{4}$ holds for $x > 0$ only at $x = 1$: the cell radius is the de Sitter radius and each tower holds one quantum per de Sitter ball. D is also the one postulate of the dark-matter subject that names the de Sitter radius, so it is the one whose content depends on that radius being a constant of the laws: it shares the exposure of $w = -1$. If $w$ differed from $-1$ the unit of D would change with time and the two results under D would go with it; the fitted total, which does not use D, would not.
dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass.technical:
This premise states that every populated tower carries the same total mass $M_{\mathrm{tot}}$ on its own de Sitter sphere. It is a democracy of mass, distinct from an equality of the asymmetry per mode, which holds for this tower and the mirror and which the odd towers do not carry. It is the premise under which the shares can be read at the de Sitter radius rather than at a microscopic spacing.

Note: D belongs to the de Sitter reading and is not counted with R1 to R3. Held together with R1 and R2 it forces the cell radius to be the de Sitter radius, one quantum per de Sitter ball (argued), so the two readings are alternatives. It is the one dark-matter postulate that names the de Sitter radius, and so shares the exposure of $w = -1$.
dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass.lay: This is an assumption, not a result: every populated hidden world holds the same total amount of mass, spread over its own version of the cosmic sphere. It is separate from the statement that the matter excess is the same in our world and its mirror, which the odd-dimensional worlds cannot carry. It belongs to one of two alternative ways of counting, the one that uses the size of the cosmic horizon as its unit, and it cannot be combined with the other way (one particle per ball of a small fixed size) unless each world holds a single particle. Because it uses the horizon size, it depends on dark energy being a true constant.

dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-u.technical:
Assume every populated tower carries the same total mass $M_{\mathrm{tot}}$ on its de Sitter sphere of radius $\ell$, and take the thickness rule with $\ell$ as its unit. A tower of dimension $n$ then has density $M_{\mathrm{tot}}/(|\Sph^{n}|\,\ell^{n})$ on its sphere; counting one thickness $\ell$ of the direction we cannot see, or sheets $\ell$ apart, turns this into a density per unit of our four-measure, and the share is
$f = |\Sph^{4}|/|\Sph^{n}|$. These are the sphere form of the shares, and their total is the unit-ball rule's. Here $\ell$ is the counting unit of the thickness rule, not the extent of a metric fifth direction: a metric fifth direction of that extent is excluded by short-range tests of Newton's law (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity}).
dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-u.lay: Suppose every hidden world holds the same total mass, spread over a sphere whose size is set by the cosmological constant, and the counted slice is one such radius thick. Then the share each world contributes here depends only on ratios of sphere sizes. Those ratios give the same total amount of dark matter as the unit-ball rule, with a cosmic rather than a microscopic unit of length.

dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algeb.formal:
Write $P$ for the even world's pseudoscalar, the ordered product of its generators, and $\omega$ for the central volume element of the odd tower. In the four nestings of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(i):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (Residue $5$, $\Cl(1,4) \supset \Cl(1,3)$.) $\omega = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}$ is central with $\omega^{2} = +1$, $P = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$ has $P^{2} = -1$, and the fifth direction is
\[
e_{4} \;=\; P^{-1}\omega .
\]
Reversing our orientation, $P \mapsto -P$ with $\omega$ fixed, reverses $e_{4}$. The central idempotents $\tfrac{1}{2}(1 \pm \omega)$ cut out the two simple components on which the two irreducible modules live (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(iv)), and $e_{4}$ acts on them as $\pm P^{-1}$. The reflection through our world, $x_{4} \mapsto -x_{4}$, fixes $P$ and sends $\omega \mapsto -\omega$: it exchanges the two components.
\item[(ii)] (Residue $3$, $\Cl(4,1) \supset \Cl(3,1)$.) The mirror's algebra is the slice $\{e_{0}, e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{4}\}$ with $P = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{4}$, $P^{2} = -1$; $\omega^{2} = -1$, one module; the added direction is $e_{3} = -P^{-1}\omega$, reversed by $P \mapsto -P$.
\item[(iii)] (Residue $7$, $\Cl(1,2) \subset \Cl(1,3)$.) $\omega = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}$ is central in the slice with $\omega^{2} = -1$, and the direction the three-dimensional tower lacks is $e_{3} = \omega^{-1}P$.
\item[(iv)] (Residue $1$, $\Cl(2,1) \subset \Cl(3,1)$.) The slice is $\{e_{0}, e_{1}, e_{3}\}$, $\omega = e_{0}e_{1}e_{3}$ is central in it with $\omega^{2} = +1$, two modules, and the lacking direction is $e_{2} = -\omega^{-1}P$.
\end{enumerate}
These are identities: $\omega$ is the ordered product $P e_{4}$ (or $\omega_{3}e_{3}$), so each equation restates the ordering, and its sign under $P \mapsto -P$ is immediate. What they fix is the meaning of a side: given the even world's orientation, the sign of $\omega$ is the sign of the direction the nesting adds or removes. Where $\omega^{2} = +1$ (residues $5$ and $1$) that sign is a label a quantum carries, its simple component; where $\omega^{2} = -1$ (residues $3$ and $7$) $-\omega$ is the conjugate complex structure on the same real module, and the sign is a convention for the tower as a whole. The lemma supplies no half-space: that a quantum sources on the side its sign names is clause S.
dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algeb.technical:
In each nesting of an odd tower's algebra with an even world's, write $P$ for the even world's pseudoscalar and $\omega$ for the odd algebra's central volume element. For the five-dimensional tower over ours, $\Cl(1,4) \supset \Cl(1,3)$, $\omega = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}$ with $\omega^{2} = +1$, $P^{2} = -1$, and the fifth direction is $e_{4} = P^{-1}\omega$. It reverses when our orientation does, acts as $\pm P^{-1}$ on the two simple components cut out by $\tfrac{1}{2}(1 \pm \omega)$, and the reflection through our world exchanges those components. The other nestings give $e_{3} = -P^{-1}\omega$ over the mirror ($\omega^{2} = -1$), $e_{3} = \omega^{-1}P$ for the three-dimensional tower in ours ($\omega^{2} = -1$) and $e_{2} = -\omega^{-1}P$ in the mirror ($\omega^{2} = +1$).

These are identities restating the order of the generators. What they fix is the meaning of a side: given the even world's orientation, the sign of $\omega$ is the sign of the direction the nesting adds or removes. Where $\omega^{2} = +1$ that sign is a label each quantum carries, its simple component; where $\omega^{2} = -1$ it is a convention for the tower as a whole. The lemma supplies no half-space; sourcing on the named side is a separate clause.
dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algeb.lay: When a world with one more or one fewer dimension is nested against ours, the extra direction can be written in the algebra as a product of our volume element and the other world's. Reversing our orientation reverses that direction, so the sign of the other world's volume element names a side of our world. Whether a particle actually acts from the side its sign names is a separate clause (clause S), not part of this result. In some nestings each particle carries the sign; in others it is only a convention for the whole hidden world.

dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-towe.formal: Let a tower have dimension $n$ and conformal completion with ambient $V$ of dimension $n + 2$, and let $W, W' \subset V_{\C}$ be a Witt pair, the two halves of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag} taken coherently across the pairs, with pure spinors the null blade $f$ and the top state (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.null-blades-fock-ideal-chirality}). Then the choice between $W$ and $W'$ is a discrete invariant of the connected conformal spin group, a \emph{bit}, if and only if $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ (ambient dimension $2m$ with $m$ odd), and the bit is the chirality of the pure spinor, that is, the parity of the Fock grade of the complementary half's pure spinor ($0$ for $f$, $m$ for the top state). (i) The odd residues are odd-dimensional for every signature in the class, so the ambient is odd-dimensional, the pseudoscalar central, an even versor carries $W$ to $W'$, and the spin algebra mixes the Fock grades: no bit, on any window. (ii) The even residues carry the bit exactly at tower dimension $0 \bmod 4$: under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} all four are at dimension four and carry it; the causal representatives of the alternative windows of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(iii), $(1,1)$ of $r = 0$ and $(1,5)$ of $r = 4$, do not. So the towers that can be oriented are the even residues $\{0, 2, 4, 6\}$ given P3, and the odd residues cannot be, given nothing.
dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-towe.technical:
Take a tower of dimension $n$ with conformal ambient $V$ of dimension $n + 2$, and a Witt pair $W, W' \subset V_{\C}$ with pure spinors the null blade $f$ and the top state. The choice between $W$ and $W'$ is a discrete invariant of the connected conformal spin group, a bit, exactly when $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$, that is ambient dimension $2m$ with $m$ odd, and the bit is the chirality of the pure spinor: Fock grade $0$ for $f$ against $m$ for the top state. Odd residues are odd-dimensional in every signature of the class, so the ambient is odd-dimensional, the pseudoscalar is central and an even versor carries $W$ to $W'$: no bit on any window.

Among even residues, under the nearest-dimension premise all four representatives are four-dimensional and carry the bit, while the alternative causal representatives $(1,1)$ and $(1,5)$ do not. So given that premise the towers that can be oriented are the even residues, and the odd residues cannot be oriented on any premise.
dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-towe.lay: At the descent a choice is made between two complementary halves of a geometric structure. This result shows that the choice is a genuine two-way switch, one the world's continuous symmetries cannot undo, only when the world's dimension is a multiple of four. Four-dimensional worlds like ours and the mirror have the switch, and if the other even hidden worlds take their nearest-dimension forms (Premise P3) they are four-dimensional and have it too; odd-dimensional hidden worlds never do, whatever is assumed.
dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-towe.typing_note: Removed the chirality proposition of the Standard-Model paper: the proof cites it only to say that its listing choice is this flag choice, a remark rather than a premise; the residue proposition is used only to name the alternative windows, whose representatives are listed explicitly, so it is not edged. proofs.main:
By Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities}(iii) the Witt pair lies in opposite families exactly when $\dim V_{\C} = 2m$ with $m$ odd, and a choice between $W$ and $W'$ that the connected group cannot undo is exactly a difference of family, since the connected group is transitive within a family (Witt together with Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities}(ii)): so the bit exists if and only if $m$ is odd, and it is the chirality $\epsilon(-1)^{m}$ against $\epsilon$ of the two pure spinors, the Fock-grade parity of the top state $v_{1}\cdots v_{m}f$. With $2m = n + 2$, $m$ is odd if and only if $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$. For this tower and the mirror (at dimension four, by \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives}), $\dim V_{\C} = 6$, $m = 3$: opposite families, the choice a bit; in ambient dimensions four and eight ($m = 2, 4$: $(1,1)$ and $(1,5)$) the top state has even grade, the same chirality as $f$, and there is no bit.

For odd $n$, $\dim V_{\C}$ is odd and Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities}'s odd case applies: one family, the exchanging even versor exhibited in dimensions five and seven. The script corroborates with the exchanging isometry's determinant, $(-1)^{m}$ in even dimension and $+1$ in odd.

The listing choice of \cite[Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT12} is the choice of which half of each pair annihilates, $f$ against the top state (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.null-blades-fock-ideal-chirality}). That odd residues are odd-dimensional only is $p - q \equiv p + q \pmod 2$, script-checked to dimension ten; a split real form suffices because every statement concerns $V_{\C}$, $S$ and $I$, shared by all real forms with the same complexification.

dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-.formal: The sterile towers are not the unflaggable ones, and no flag-level strengthening of the count exists: in every nondefinite representative the isometry group acts transitively on hyperbolic planes and on the null lines within them (Witt's theorem), so no representative offers a distinguished plane or half of one, and the descent's flag is as uncaused in $(1,3)$ as in $(2,2)$. The definite representatives of $r = 4$ contain no hyperbolic plane, so no \emph{rung-level} flag can be chosen in them, but the descent's flag, a maximal isotropic of the complexified ambient, exists there as for every even residue (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}); the sterility of $r = 4$ is the single-clock filter restated. So the exclusion of $r = 0$ rests on the two-time instability import alone, and a stabilisation of two-time dynamics is an open fork: six causal towers, the $r = 0$ tower an \emph{oriented} one (Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-can-carry-arrow}), a Kleinian copy of the Standard Model with an asymmetric share of one, costed in the section “The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper”.
dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-.technical:
In every nondefinite representative the isometry group acts transitively on hyperbolic planes and on the null lines within them, by Witt's theorem, so no representative offers a distinguished plane or half of one: the descent's flag is as uncaused in $(1,3)$ as in $(2,2)$. The definite representatives of residue $4$ contain no hyperbolic plane, so no rung-level flag can be chosen in them, but the descent's flag, a maximal isotropic subspace of the complexified ambient, exists there as in every even residue; the sterility of residue $4$ is the single-clock filter restated.

Hence the sterile towers are not the unflaggable ones and no flag-level strengthening of the count exists. The exclusion of residue $0$ rests on the imported two-time instability alone, and a stabilisation of two-time dynamics is an open fork: six causal towers, with the residue-$0$ tower an oriented one, a Kleinian copy of the Standard Model with an asymmetric share of one.
dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-.lay: One might hope to rule out some hidden worlds more firmly by showing they cannot support the orientation choice made at the descent. This result shows that hope fails: symmetry treats every candidate choice alike in every relevant world, ours included. So the hidden world with two time directions is excluded only because two-time physics is unstable, and if that instability were ever cured it would return as an oriented copy of the Standard Model.
dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-.typing_note: The statement's clauses quoting the flag-bit theorem and the which-towers corollary are real dependencies, but neither edge was added because both would close a cycle through the two-families proposition, which uses this claim only for Witt's theorem (an edge for its owner to review).

proofs.main: A hyperbolic plane requires one plus and one minus among the representative's directions, and a definite signature has none. Otherwise Witt's theorem (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-extension}) extends any isometry between nondegenerate subspaces to the whole space; two hyperbolic planes are isometric, so the isometry group is transitive on them, and composing with the isometry of a plane that exchanges its null lines gives transitivity on null lines. In $(1,3)$ the rotation $e_{1} \mapsto e_{2}$, $e_{2} \mapsto -e_{1}$ fixes $e_{0}$ and its orientation and carries $\mathrm{span}(e_{0}, e_{1})$ onto $\mathrm{span}(e_{0}, e_{2})$ and $\R(e_{0} + e_{1})$ onto $\R(e_{0} + e_{2})$: the time orientation distinguishes a time direction, not a plane or a null line, the candidate flags through a time axis forming the celestial sphere. In $(2,2)$ the totally isotropic planes form a one-parameter family per component and the hyperbolic planes a four-parameter family, likewise permuted transitively. The script checks the witnesses and the Jacobian rank exactly. The obstruction is the same in every nondefinite residue, so it cannot sterilise $r = 0$ while leaving $r = 6$ causal.

dark-matter.imported-composition-simulat.formal:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Quanta confined to a sheet scatter in two dimensions. Per unit of the mass gravity sees, the three-dimensional towers' matter at composite strength has a cross-section of $10^{8}$ to $10^{13}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$ in galaxy clusters, eight to thirteen orders of magnitude above the galaxy-cluster bounds, whatever its confinement scale: it is a fluid whose pressure acts within its sheets.
\item[(ii)] In the merger, with the three-dimensional towers' matter colliding, the subcluster's sheet fluid and mirror gas are held back with its gas, and with randomly oriented sheets the subcluster has no separate lensing peak. With the odd towers' matter collisionless, the subcluster keeps a lensing peak on its galaxies with its gas $355$ kpc behind, and its mass-to-light change, $0.82$, is consistent with the observed ratio $0.84 \pm 0.07$ \cite{Randall2008}, as cold dark matter's is; the cost is a puffier subcluster, with lensing contrast $4.7$ against cold dark matter's $7.5$.
\item[(ii$'$)] The exchanged assignment of Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not}, with the three-dimensional towers' matter colliding, fails in the same way: lensing contrast $1.1$, the subcluster's own mass $0.27$ of cold dark matter's, and galaxy-cluster ellipticity $0.49$ of cold dark matter's. With the mirror settled it is marginal, contrast $2.7$ and mass $0.44$.
\item[(iii)] In the assembled galaxy clusters, two seeds each, the projected ellipticity is $0.43$ of cold dark matter's with the three-dimensional towers colliding, both seeds below cold dark matter's, the sheet fluid forming a cored component rounder than the collisionless dark matter; with the odd towers' matter collisionless it is $0.77$, rounder, with one seed inside the range of the cold-dark-matter seeds, so not excluded.
\item[(iv)] In the Milky Way, the proton-only branch is excluded at the Sun. On the burning branch a helium mirror, cooling slowly and with helium-star supernovae giving $3.6$ to $7.3$ times our feedback per unit mass formed, fits the $2\sigma$ room for extra disk-like mass at the Sun under some normalisations of its gas, and fits the bulge only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass. With the consistent yield, extra disk-like mass at the Sun below $5\ M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$, or disk-like dark mass in the bulge volume below $1.7 \times 10^{9}\ M_{\odot}$, would exclude it. Neither has yet been made (the dark-matter paper's own refutation condition 6, the section “The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper”, not the series' sixth refutation).
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~3.1, Cor.~3.4, Obs.~7.1, 7.2, 9.1, Tables~3, 4]{ButlerT14b}; the observations compared are those of \cite{Clowe2006, Randall2008}.
dark-matter.imported-composition-simulat.technical:
This collects the simulation results for the dark towers' matter. Quanta confined to a sheet scatter in two dimensions, and per unit of the mass gravity sees the three-dimensional towers' matter at composite strength has a cross-section of $10^{8}$ to $10^{13}\ \cmg$ in galaxy clusters, eight to thirteen orders of magnitude above the cluster bounds whatever its confinement scale: it is a fluid whose pressure acts within its sheets. In the merging cluster, if that matter collides the subcluster has no separate lensing peak (and the exchanged assignment fails likewise, marginally with the mirror settled); if the odd towers' matter is collisionless the subcluster keeps a lensing peak with its gas $355$ kpc behind and a mass-to-light change of $0.82$, consistent with the observed $0.84 \pm 0.07$, at the cost of lensing contrast $4.7$ against cold dark matter's $7.5$.

In assembled clusters the projected ellipticity is $0.43$ of cold dark matter's with colliding sheet matter and $0.77$, not excluded, with the odd towers' matter collisionless. In the Milky Way the proton-only mirror branch is excluded at the Sun; on the burning branch a helium mirror fits the room for extra disk-like mass at the Sun under some gas normalisations and the bulge only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass. With the consistent yield, a bound below $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ on extra disk-like mass at the Sun, or below $1.7 \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$ on disk-like dark mass in the bulge, would exclude it.
dark-matter.imported-composition-simulat.lay: Computer simulations test how the hidden worlds' matter would behave in colliding galaxy clusters and in our own galaxy. Matter confined to flat sheets, interacting at the strength the framework's composites would have, collides far too strongly to match what is seen, while collisionless matter from the odd-dimensional worlds reproduces the observed separation of mass and gas, at the cost of a somewhat puffier cluster. A mirror world made mostly of helium is still allowed in our galaxy, but only for some assumptions about its gas, and in the central bulge only if the mirror's matter there exceeds twice its proportional share of the dark mass; a somewhat sharper measurement of hidden disk-like mass near the Sun could rule it out.

dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupli.formal: Under the entropy paper's Indifference premise (for the sphere step of the four-dimensional lift) and, wherever the thermal state is used, the singularity paper's premise (Q), and with the other hypotheses the acoustic chain carries: within the s-wave current algebra and its assembled four-dimensional lift, every gauge-charged or charge-conjugation-odd probe has zero linear overlap with the graviton mode, so at first order only the charge-conjugation-even neutral sector couples; in the conformal vacuum its overlap is carried by $T$ alone, and Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.conclusion-does-not-depend-ontology-level} reads it as the one coupling sector, stress-energy (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip}, Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised}). Hence matter that gravitates on this metric and carries no gauge charge shared with us acts on us, through the metric-forming correlations, by its stress-energy alone, at first order. With Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}, read operationally as the sector decomposition of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators}, which makes these correlations its only contact with us, it does nothing else observable at first order. \emph{Provenance:} the series' acoustic no-go \cite[\S5]{ButlerT10} restated, at its mixed level.
dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupli.technical: Under the Indifference premise (sphere step of the lift) and premise (Q) (the induced thermal state), and with the further hypotheses of the acoustic chain: in the s-wave current algebra and its assembled four-dimensional lift, every gauge-charged or charge-conjugation-odd probe has zero linear overlap with the graviton mode, so at first order only the charge-conjugation-even neutral sector couples. In the conformal vacuum that overlap is carried by the stress tensor alone, and the ontology proposition reads it as the one coupling sector, stress-energy. Matter that gravitates on this metric and shares no gauge charge with us therefore acts on us through the metric-forming correlations by its stress-energy alone, at first order; with Premise P1, which makes these correlations its only contact with us, it does nothing else observable at first order. This is the series' acoustic no-go restated at its mixed level.
dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupli.lay: In the framework's spherically averaged (s-wave) description of fields near horizons, with an assembled four-dimensional lift, and under two assumptions of earlier papers in the series (one about how the horizon's spherical structure is built, one about the joint state of the near-horizon modes), the series showed that the structure from which spacetime's geometry is made can be gripped, at first order, only by probes that carry no charge and do not change sign under charge conjugation, which the series reads as energy and momentum. So matter that feels gravity but shares none of our other forces can affect us through that structure only by its weight, to first order. If, as the dark-matter paper's single-frozen-point premise says, that structure is its only contact with us, it has no other effect we could observe at that order.

proofs.main:
Restatement of the series' own result; no new step. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} shows, for any state invariant under the gauge group, charge conjugation and the modular flow, that a gauge-charged or charge-conjugation-odd probe $O$ has $\varphi(T\,O) = 0$ for the graviton mode $T$ and all its modes $T_{n}$; the induced thermal state has the three invariances under premise (Q), and the conformal vacuum has them without it. At first order, therefore, only the charge-conjugation-even neutral subalgebra couples. In the conformal vacuum the orthogonality of quasi-primaries of unequal dimension leaves $T$ as the only quasi-primary with nonzero overlap, so the coupling is carried by $T$ alone; in the thermal state the first-order coupling sector is the whole charge-conjugation-even neutral subalgebra, generated by the current bilinears and strictly larger than the conformal family of $T$, as that proposition states. Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised} carries the orthogonality to the four-dimensional lift, its sphere step conditional on the Indifference premise and its near-horizon reduction at assembly level. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.conclusion-does-not-depend-ontology-level} reads the result as one coupling sector, stress-energy, with no selective coupling, no enhanced source and no enhanced detector, at first order; the statement adopts that reading at the source's mixed level.

Matter of a sector that shares no gauge charge with ours enters our sector's observables through the metric-forming correlations by the linear overlap of its operators with ours on those correlations; by the three results the first-order overlap with the graviton mode is that of the sector just described, so this matter acts on us through these correlations by its stress-energy alone, at first order. Whether the sector touches ours by any other route is not decided by the acoustic chain: "carries no gauge charge shared with us" does not by itself exclude, for example, a gauge-singlet portal. That the metric-forming correlations are its only contact is the sector decomposition of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators}, the operational reading of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}, assumed here, and the closing clause of the statement is conditional on it; P1 also enters the dark-matter paper's superselection theorem as an assumption there. Every premise of the three cited results is a premise of this one, and reaches its dependants through them.

dark-matter.imported-induced-equations-h.formal:
Let a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat $\R^{4,1}$, in the signature $(-,+,+,+,+)$ of the source (the $d$-dimensional clause of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}, $d = 5$, with the product of that signature) obey the five-dimensional field equations, which in the source's sign read $a \cdot G(b) = \kappa_{5}^{2}\, a \cdot T(b)$ for physical vectors $a, b$, with $G$ the Einstein map of the derived metric and $T$ the stress-energy map, and let $\Sigma$ be a timelike hypersurface of the flat background with unit physical normal $n$ (a physical vector, $Q(n) = +1$, orthogonal to $\hb^{-1}$ of the tangent directions of $\Sigma$). Then the Einstein map of the metric that $\hb^{-1}$ induces on $\Sigma$, as a bilinear form on the physical tangent vectors $a, b$ of $\Sigma$, contains, from the bulk stress-energy, the term
\[
\frac{2\kappa_{5}^{2}}{3}\Bigl[\,a \cdot T(b) + \bigl(n \cdot T(n) - \tfrac{1}{4}T\bigr)\, a \cdot b\Bigr],
\]
with $T = \partial_a \cdot T(a)$ the trace (in components: $\tfrac{2\kappa_{5}^{2}}{3}[T_{\mu\nu} + (T_{ab}n^{a}n^{b} - \tfrac14 T)g_{\mu\nu}]$), together with terms quadratic in the hypersurface's own extrinsic curvature, the projected $D$-derivative of $n$, and the projected bulk Weyl curvature $\mathcal{W}$, the trace-free part of the five-dimensional field strength. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[eq.~(15)]{SMS2000}, read in five-dimensional Gauge Theory Gravity through the frame formalism, which holds in every dimension.
dark-matter.imported-induced-equations-h.technical: Let a five-dimensional gravitational field on flat $\R^{4,1}$, in the signature $(-,+,+,+,+)$ of the source, obey the field equations $a \cdot G(b) = \kappa_{5}^{2}\, a \cdot T(b)$ (source's sign) for its derived metric, and take a timelike hypersurface of the flat background with unit physical normal $n$. The Einstein map induced on the hypersurface, as a bilinear form on its physical tangent vectors $a, b$, contains, from the bulk stress-energy, the term $\tfrac{2\kappa_{5}^{2}}{3}\bigl[a \cdot T(b) + \bigl(n \cdot T(n) - \tfrac{1}{4}T\bigr)\, a \cdot b\bigr]$, with $T = \partial_a \cdot T(a)$ the bulk trace. The remaining terms are quadratic in the hypersurface's own extrinsic curvature or come from the projected bulk Weyl curvature. This is the Shiromizu-Maeda-Sasaki form of the induced equations, read in five-dimensional Gauge Theory Gravity.
dark-matter.imported-induced-equations-h.lay: If our world is a thin slice inside a five-dimensional space, gravity there can still be described as fields on a flat five-dimensional background. Einstein's equations for those fields imply modified equations on the slice. This imported result says how matter spread through the larger space shows up as a source of gravity on the slice, alongside extra terms from the slice's own bending and from the tidal part of the five-dimensional field.

imported_from.citation: T. Shiromizu, K. Maeda and M. Sasaki, The Einstein equations on the 3-brane world, Phys. Rev. D 62, 024012 (2000).

dark-matter.imported-inverse-square-law-.formal: Newton's inverse-square law holds down to separations of about $50$ micrometres, and a single extra spatial dimension of size larger than about $40$ micrometres is excluded. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Lee2020}.
dark-matter.imported-inverse-square-law-.technical: Laboratory tests of gravity confirm Newton's $1/r^{2}$ law down to separations of about $50$ micrometres. A single extra spatial dimension changes the force law at separations below its size, so the same data exclude one extra dimension larger than about $40$ micrometres.
dark-matter.imported-inverse-square-law-.lay: Gravity has been measured in the laboratory between objects only a twentieth of a millimetre apart, and it still follows Newton's inverse-square law. That rules out a single hidden extra dimension of space bigger than about four hundredths of a millimetre.

dark-matter.imported-linear-momentum-equ.formal: For the perturbed FLRW gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) in conformal Newtonian gauge, $\hb^{-1}(e_\tau) = a(1 + \psi)\,e_\tau$, $\hb^{-1}(e_i) = a(1 - \phi)\,e_i$ at linear order, whose derived metric in the source's signature $(-,+,+,+)$ is $ds^{2} = a^{2}[-(1 + 2\psi)d\tau^{2} + (1 - 2\phi)dx^{2}]$, the covariant conservation of the stress-energy map under $D$, $\dot T(\dot D) = 0$ (in components $\nabla_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu} = 0$), gives a pressureless component of velocity divergence $\theta$ and anisotropic stress $\sigma$ the momentum equation $\theta' = -\mathcal{H}\theta + k^{2}\psi - k^{2}\sigma$, and the traceless part of the field equations of the gravitational field gives $k^{2}(\phi - \psi) = 12\pi G a^{2}\sum_{i}(\rho_{i} + p_{i})\sigma_{i}$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[eqs.~(30), (23d)]{MaBertschinger1995}.
dark-matter.imported-linear-momentum-equ.technical: For the perturbed FLRW gravitational field on flat spacetime in conformal Newtonian gauge, whose derived metric is $ds^{2} = a^{2}[-(1 + 2\psi)d\tau^{2} + (1 - 2\phi)dx^{2}]$, covariant conservation of the stress tensor gives a pressureless component with velocity divergence $\theta$ and anisotropic stress $\sigma$ the momentum equation $\theta' = -\mathcal{H}\theta + k^{2}\psi - k^{2}\sigma$. The traceless part of the field equations ties the difference of the two potentials to the total anisotropic stress, $k^{2}(\phi - \psi) = 12\pi G a^{2}\sum_{i}(\rho_{i} + p_{i})\sigma_{i}$. These are the standard linear-perturbation equations of Ma and Bertschinger.
dark-matter.imported-linear-momentum-equ.lay: These are the standard textbook equations for how small ripples in the early universe's matter move and how they disturb the gravitational field. One says how a component's flow speeds up or slows down under gravity and its own internal stresses; the other says that sideways stresses make the two kinds of gravitational potential differ.

imported_from.citation: C.-P. Ma and E. Bertschinger, Cosmological perturbation theory in the synchronous and conformal Newtonian gauges, Astrophys. J. 455, 7 (1995).

dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-p.formal:
Dark matter produced from the Standard-Model plasma by massless graviton exchange has rate per volume
\[
R(T) \;=\; \frac{\alpha\,T^{8}}{\bar{M}_{P}^{4}}, \qquad \bar{M}_{P} = 2.435 \times 10^{18}\ \mathrm{GeV},
\]
the reduced Planck mass $\bar{M}_{P} = M_{P}/\sqrt{8\pi}$ ($M_{P}$ the non-reduced mass), with $\alpha = 1.9 \times 10^{-4}$, $1.1 \times 10^{-3}$, $2.3 \times 10^{-3}$ for one scalar, one fermion and one vector \emph{produced} species respectively, the sum over the Standard-Model bath being inside the coefficient, weighted as $4|\mathcal{M}^{0}|^{2} + 45|\mathcal{M}^{1/2}|^{2} + 12|\mathcal{M}^{1}|^{2}$ over its scalar, Weyl-fermion and vector degrees. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Bernal2018}, Eq.~(31), $R^{0}(T) = (3997\pi^{3}/663552000)\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$ for the scalar case (the source writes $M_{P}$ for the reduced mass $\bar{M}_{P}$), and Table I, the massless-graviton limit of that paper's massive spin-2 mediator. Imported at assembly level: whether the fermion coefficient is per Weyl or per Dirac species is carried as a bracket; the factor between counting particles and pairs, and the mean energy per quantum, are absorbed into a factor of at most $2^{1/4}$ on the temperature ratio below.

\emph{Flag (10 November 2026): a process the series does not hold.} In its source the rate is computed from the exchange of a quantum of a spin-2 field between the plasma and the produced species. The series holds no quantum of the gravitational field: gravity here is the classical gauge field of Gauge Theory Gravity (conventions, section ``Gravity and the graviton''). The Fact is therefore an import from outside the series' own content, and every result that uses it holds conditionally on the rate. It is not known whether the classical gauge field sourced by matter gives this rate, another rate or none; that is open problem op.graviton-rate-as-classical-field-process. No number above is changed by this flag.
dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-p.technical: Matter produced from the Standard-Model plasma by massless graviton exchange is created at a rate per volume $R(T) = \alpha\,T^{8}/\bar{M}_{P}^{4}$, with $\bar{M}_{P} = 2.435 \times 10^{18}$ GeV the reduced Planck mass. The coefficient is $\alpha = 1.9 \times 10^{-4}$, $1.1 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2.3 \times 10^{-3}$ for one produced scalar, fermion and vector species, the sum over the Standard-Model bath already inside it. The result is the massless limit of a massive spin-2 mediator calculation, imported at assembly level: whether the fermion coefficient is per Weyl or per Dirac species is carried as a bracket, and the particle-versus-pair factor and the mean energy per quantum are absorbed into a factor of at most $2^{1/4}$ on the temperature ratio. Flag: the source computes the rate from the exchange of a quantum of a spin-2 field, and the series holds no quantum of the gravitational field, which in it is the classical gauge field of Gauge Theory Gravity; results that use this rate hold conditionally on it, and deriving it as a process of the classical field sourced by matter, or showing that it vanishes, is open problem op.graviton-rate-as-classical-field-process.
dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-p.lay: Even matter that feels no force but gravity is produced in a hot early universe, because ordinary particles colliding can occasionally create it through gravity. This imported result gives the rate, which rises very steeply with temperature, for producing scalar, fermion and vector particles. It is the input that fixes how warm gravity alone can make the hidden worlds. A caution: the calculation it is taken from treats gravity as carried by particles, gravitons, and in this collection gravity is a classical field with no such particle. Whether the classical field produces matter at the same rate, at a different one or not at all has not been worked out, so everything in the collection that uses this rate holds only if the rate does.

imported_from.citation: N. Bernal, M. Dutra, Y. Mambrini, K. Olive, M. Peloso, and M. Pierre, Spin-2 portal dark matter, Phys. Rev. D 97 (2018), 115020.

dark-matter.imported-schwinger-discharge.formal: A charged hole whose horizon field exceeds $E_{c} = m_{e}^{2}c^{3}/e\hbar$ discharges by pair creation, faster than it evaporates, toward $Q_{c} = 4\pi\varepsilon_{0}E_{c}r_{+}^{2}$, into the lightest charged carrier (for the mirror, the mirror electron). $Q_{c}/Q_{\mathrm{ext}} \propto M$ reaches one at about $1.3 \times 10^{5}$ solar masses (at one solar mass $Q_{c} \approx 1.3 \times 10^{15}$ C, $7.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of extremal, with $E_{c} = 1.32 \times 10^{18}$ V/m), so below that mass discharge returns the Gauss-law charge and above it does not limit it. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Gibbons1975, HiscockWeems1990}, from the record (the charged exterior is outside the Hawking paper's scope).
dark-matter.imported-schwinger-discharge.technical: A charged black hole whose horizon field exceeds the Schwinger field $E_{c} = m_{e}^{2}c^{3}/e\hbar$ loses charge by pair creation faster than it evaporates, down to $Q_{c} = 4\pi\varepsilon_{0}E_{c}r_{+}^{2}$, into the lightest charged carrier (for the mirror, the mirror electron). Since $Q_{c}/Q_{\mathrm{ext}} \propto M$ reaches one at about $1.3 \times 10^{5}$ solar masses, below that mass discharge brings the charge down to the Gauss-law value and above it does not limit the charge.
dark-matter.imported-schwinger-discharge.lay: A black hole with a strong enough electric charge pulls electron-positron pairs out of empty space and sheds charge quickly. For holes lighter than about a hundred thousand Suns this caps the charge they can keep; for heavier ones the cap is above the largest charge possible and does nothing. In the mirror world the same happens with mirror electrons.

imported_from.citation: G. W. Gibbons, Vacuum polarization and the spontaneous loss of charge by black holes, Commun. Math. Phys. 44 (1975) 245--264.
W. A. Hiscock and L. D. Weems, Evolution of charged evaporating black holes, Phys. Rev. D 41 (1990) 1142--1151.

dark-matter.mirror-share-assembled.formal:
Under Premises \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}, \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} and \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise} (the former Premise P4, democracy of the asymmetry, retired as a postulate, being a theorem for the mirror, clause (iii)), the Standard-Model paper's Hypothesis (S) as carried in Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}, and the input list of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain}, the mirror tower contributes exactly one visible share:
\[
f_{2} \;=\; \underbrace{\frac{\epsilon_{2}}{\epsilon_{6}}}_{\text{P2}}\cdot\;\underbrace{\frac{n_{2}}{n_{6}}}_{\text{derived}}\;\cdot\;\underbrace{\frac{m_{2}}{m_{6}}}_{\text{derived, given the common ceiling coupling}} \;=\; 1\cdot 1\cdot 1 \;=\; 1, \qquad \Omega_{\mathrm{mirror}} \;=\; \Omega_{b},
\]
exactly on the proton-only branch and to half a percent on the burning branch (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i)). The three factors are stated separately because they have three standings, and the exposure of the share is the weakest of them.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The mode ratio: derived, on no premise of this paper.)} $n_{2} = n_{6}$, the same state space.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The mass ratio: derived, given the common ceiling coupling.)} $m_{2} = m_{6}$ up to the two sectors' composition, the common ceiling and coupling being Premise \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise} along the reversal orbit (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}, scoped to sector labels, does not reach a coupling).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The asymmetry ratio: premised on P2.)} $\epsilon_{2} = \epsilon_{6}$ by the audit along the same orbit (P1's orientation clause a weaker second route), under the premises Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v) states for it (the common $N$ of P1 and the charge reading of the stored asymmetry); the former P4 is that clause on the mirror and is not assumed.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(No temperature in it.)} The share is one anywhere in the interval of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(iii).
\end{enumerate}
dark-matter.mirror-share-assembled.technical:
Under the single frozen point, indifference and the common ceiling coupling, with Hypothesis (S) and the input list of the Standard-Model chain (the democracy of the asymmetry being discharged for the mirror, not assumed), the mirror tower's share factorises as $f_{2} = (\epsilon_{2}/\epsilon_{6})(n_{2}/n_{6})(m_{2}/m_{6}) = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = 1$, so $\Omega_{\mathrm{mirror}} = \Omega_{b}$, exactly on the proton-only branch and to half a percent on the burning branch. The three factors have three standings. The mode ratio $n_{2} = n_{6}$ is derived from the shared state space, on no premise of the dark-matter analysis. The mass ratio is derived given the common-ceiling-coupling premise, which supplies the common ceiling and coupling along the reversal orbit (indifference, scoped to sector labels, does not reach a coupling), up to the two sectors' composition. The asymmetry ratio $\epsilon_{2} = \epsilon_{6}$ is premised on indifference along the same orbit, which discharges the democracy premise for the mirror.

No temperature enters: the share is one anywhere in the allowed interval for the stored asymmetry. The exposure of the share is that of its weakest factor, the premised asymmetry ratio.
dark-matter.mirror-share-assembled.lay: The mirror world, our world with the roles of time and space reversed, contributes exactly as much matter as our ordinary matter (exactly on one branch of the analysis, to within half a percent on the other), given two of the paper's premises (a single frozen point and indifference between mirror towers; a third, that the oriented towers share one asymmetry, follows for the mirror and is not assumed), the assumption that the two worlds start with equal force strengths at one common highest scale (the common ceiling coupling), the Standard-Model inputs, and the assumption that the slots behave like the pairs (Hypothesis (S)). The three ingredients, how many kinds of particle there are, how heavy they are and how large the matter excess is, each come out equal, but on different footings: the first is derived outright, the second depends on the equal-strengths assumption, and the third is assumed through the indifference symmetry. The answer does not depend on how hot the mirror world is.

dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile.formal:
Write $m_{r} = c_{r}\Lambda_{r}$, with $\Lambda_{r}$ the confinement scale of tower $r$'s non-abelian sector and $c_{r}$ the constituent factor of its lightest charge-carrying composite.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The mirror.)} By Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), with the common ceiling and coupling of Premise \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise}, $\Lambda_{2} = \Lambda_{6}$ and $c_{2} = c_{6}$ exactly, hence $f_{2} = 1$ under P4, which Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v) discharges for the mirror, an isomorphism of theories rather than a one-loop statement. As a ratio of mass densities it is a ratio of mean mass per baryon: ours is about $936.7$ MeV after helium, a mirror burnt entirely to helium (the completion limit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}'s burning branch) gives $931.8$ MeV, so $f_{2}$ is $0.995$ in that limit and $1$ on the proton-only branch, a one-sided systematic of half a percent at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the two branches bracket the share where the mirror is helium or protons; at the gravitational floor the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons, a composition neither branch describes, and it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$ (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}); the half-percent bracket is established there and not at the floor.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Fragility.)} The equality is unstable to any departure from the copy. Suppose the two towers shared a ceiling $M$ and coupling but differed in light content by $\Delta b$ over the running range, with $b_{6} \leq 11$; then at one loop
\[
\ln\frac{\Lambda_{2}}{\Lambda_{6}} \;\geq\; \frac{\Delta b}{b_{6} + \Delta b}\,\ln\frac{M}{\Lambda_{6}}.
\]
One Dirac flavour is $\Delta b = 2/3$, which with $\Lambda_{6} = 0.3$ GeV moves the mirror share by a factor between $4.89$ (bottom of the ceiling range, $b_{6} = 11$) and $21.4$ (top, $b_{6} = 7$), past the observed $5.364$ everywhere except at the bottom of the range on the most conservative branch. A coupling departure $\delta = \alpha_{2}(M)^{-1} - \alpha_{6}(M)^{-1}$ at the ceiling with identical content moves $\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6}$ by $e^{-2\pi\delta/b}$, a factor $2.45$ per unit at $b = 7$, so the share stays within ten percent of one only for $|\delta| < 0.106$. So $f_{2} = 1$ is exact, protected by the common-ceiling-coupling premise (Premise \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise}), and fragile.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The odd towers.)} In three and five dimensions the gauge coupling is dimensionful and the confinement scale is set by the coupling itself ($\Lambda_{3} \sim g_{3}^{2}N$, $\Lambda_{5} \sim 1/g_{5}^{2}$), so nothing about $\Lambda_{1,7,3,5}$ follows without a rule the series does not derive (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}); the unit-ball rule of the section “The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule” constrains that rule, as shares per unit of our volume, without supplying it.
\end{enumerate}
Level: (i) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}; (ii) is one-loop arithmetic under its stated assumptions, flagged; (iii) is a scope statement.
dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile.technical:
Write $m_{r} = c_{r}\Lambda_{r}$, with $\Lambda_{r}$ the confinement scale and $c_{r}$ the constituent factor of the lightest charge-carrying composite. For the mirror, the copy theorem with the common-ceiling-coupling premise gives $\Lambda_{2} = \Lambda_{6}$ and $c_{2} = c_{6}$ exactly, so $f_{2} = 1$, the democracy of the asymmetry being discharged for the mirror by the copy theorem, an isomorphism of theories rather than a one-loop statement; as a ratio of mass densities it is $0.995$ for a mirror burnt entirely to helium and $1$ on the proton-only branch. The T14c note finds the mirror helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$ and neutron-rich at the gravitational floor (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}), so this bracket does not cover the floor.

The equality is fragile. If the two towers shared ceiling and coupling but differed in light content by $\Delta b$, then at one loop $\ln(\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6}) \ge \frac{\Delta b}{b_{6} + \Delta b}\ln(M/\Lambda_{6})$; one Dirac flavour moves the share by a factor between $4.89$ and $21.4$ across the ceiling range, valued in the ceiling proposition under Hypothesis (U). With identical content a ceiling difference $\delta$ in $\alpha^{-1}$ moves $\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6}$ by $e^{-2\pi\delta/b}$, so the share stays within ten percent of one only for $|\delta| < 0.106$: the share of one is exactly as strong as the premise that equates the ceiling couplings. For the odd towers the coupling is dimensionful and sets the confinement scale itself, so nothing about their $\Lambda$ follows without a coupling rule the series does not derive.
dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile.lay: The mirror world's matter weighs exactly as much as ours, because the mirror is an exact copy, with the same particles and the same force strengths at the start, and the copy theorem gives it the same matter excess, so the premise that the flag imprints one asymmetry on every tower (P4) is not needed for it. How exact that is depends on what the mirror's matter becomes; a later note (T14c) finds it mostly neutrons rather than helium at its coldest, a case this estimate does not cover. A rough one-loop estimate, over the ceiling range that rests on Hypothesis (U), shows that the equality is fragile: one extra kind of light quark or a slightly different starting strength of the strong force would change the mirror's share by large factors. For the odd-dimensional hidden worlds nothing of this kind can be said without a new rule.

proofs.main:
(i) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), given the common ceiling and coupling of Premise \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise}, with Premise P4 discharged for the mirror by that theorem's clause (v) as an equality of $B - L$, and with Hypothesis (equal conversion), which is not proved here (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(i), version 11). (ii): one loop,
\[
\alpha(\mu)^{-1} \;=\; \alpha(M)^{-1} - \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mu}^{M} b\,d\ln\mu'
\]
for an asymptotically free sector, with $\Lambda$ the scale at which $\alpha^{-1}$ vanishes. With equal $\alpha(M)^{-1}$ and $b_{2} - b_{6} \geq \Delta b$,
\[
\alpha_{2}(\mu)^{-1} \;\leq\; \alpha_{6}(\mu)^{-1} - \frac{\Delta b}{2\pi}\ln\frac{M}{\mu};
\]
at $\mu = \Lambda_{2}$ the left side vanishes, so
\[
\frac{\Delta b}{2\pi}\ln\frac{M}{\Lambda_{2}} \;\leq\; \alpha_{6}(\Lambda_{2})^{-1} \;\leq\; \frac{b_{6}^{\max}}{2\pi}\ln\frac{\Lambda_{2}}{\Lambda_{6}}.
\]
Writing $L = \ln(\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6})$ and $L_{0} = \ln(M/\Lambda_{6})$,
\[
b_{6}^{\max}L \;\geq\; \Delta b\,(L_{0} - L), \qquad\text{so}\qquad L \;\geq\; \frac{\Delta b\,L_{0}}{b_{6}^{\max} + \Delta b};
\]
the script checks the chain as exact rational algebra and evaluates the factors at both ends of the ceiling range, the two readings of Hypothesis (U) in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} ($L_{0} = 35.23$ and $27.79$; $7.49$, $21.4$ at the top and $4.89$, $11.2$ at the bottom for $\Delta b = 2/3$; $18.84$ for $\Delta b = 1$). The coupling sensitivity, the price of a departure from Premise \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise}, is $\Lambda = M e^{-2\pi/(b\alpha(M))}$ differentiated, $d\ln\Lambda/d(\alpha^{-1}) = -2\pi/b$. (iii) is dimensional analysis: $[g^{2}] = \text{mass}^{4-d}$, with the absence of a coupling rule from Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}.

dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one.technical:
Every input of the Standard-Model chain is invariant under the signature reversal $(p,q) \mapsto (q,p)$ that carries this tower's $(1,3)$ to the mirror's $(3,1)$: the complexified fibre is the same, both conformal spin groups are $SU(2,2)$ with the same representation on the conformal spinor space, Hypothesis (S) has no signature in it, and one-loop running depends on content alone. So the mirror's derived content copies ours: gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ with the same global form, generation, hypercharges and chirality halves, including a massless mirror photon and mirror neutrinos; the ground type ($\R$ for the mirror, $\HH$ here) never enters.

With equal light content the $\beta$-functions agree at every scale, so a common ceiling $M$ and a common coupling there give $\Lambda_{2} = \Lambda_{6}$ and $c_{2} = c_{6}$, and with the equal asymmetry per mode $f_{2} = 1$ up to the ratio of mean mass per baryon set by the two nuclear histories, so $\Omega_{\mathrm{mirror}} = \Omega_{b}$ to half a percent. The common ceiling and coupling are a premise of their own, the common-ceiling-coupling premise, along the reversal orbit only: indifference, scoped to sector labels and not states, does not reach a coupling, and the odd towers get no such premise. The asymmetry per mode is equal, $\epsilon_{2} = \epsilon_{6}$, by the indifference audit applied to the stored charge, which is a sector label given that the number $N$ is common to the towers (a clause of the single frozen point) and that $\epsilon$ is a datum of the descent and not of a tower's state (the charge reading, the registered stance, a hypothesis of this route), and, more weakly, by both towers being oriented by the one flag under the single frozen point. This is the mirror instance of the former democracy premise P4, retired as a postulate. The share of one rests on the single frozen point, indifference, the common ceiling coupling, the charge reading and the copy.

Caveat: the T14c note shows (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2}) that indifference at its version-1 reach also equates the energy the descent deposits per unit charge, giving $\xi = 1$ and $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} = 7.45$, which the record excludes; the cold mirror the paper carries is an exception to indifference at that reach. Indifference as scoped leaves $\xi$ free, and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent; the common-ceiling-coupling premise equates no state.
dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one.lay: Swapping which directions count as time and which as space turns our world into a mirror world, and this result shows that every ingredient used to derive our particle physics survives the swap. So the mirror world has its own copy of the Standard Model as the series derives it (under Hypothesis (S)), with mirror photons and mirror neutrinos. If the two worlds share one cutoff scale and start with equal force strengths there (an assumption of its own, the common ceiling coupling), and under the framework's premises of a single frozen point (P1) and indifference (P2), which give an equal matter excess once that excess is read as a quantity fixed at the origin and not by temperature, it also has the same particle masses and the same matter excess, so its matter equals our ordinary matter to within half a percent, the gap coming from the two worlds' nuclear histories. A later note (T14c) shows that the indifference principle, applied as widely as the paper first applied it, would also make the mirror world as hot as ours, which observations rule out; as now worded it leaves the mirror's temperature open, and a cold mirror then needs a birth out of equilibrium.

proofs.main:
The list of inputs is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain}, whose own lemmas (pair count, Segre) are statements about $V_{\C}$ and about tensor products of complex spaces. Invariance item by item.

Complexification: $\R^{2,4} \otimes \C = \R^{4,2} \otimes \C$ as quadratic spaces, there being no signature over $\C$. Even subalgebra: $e_{i} \mapsto e_{i}e_{n}$ ($i < n$) identifies $\Cl^{0}(p,q)$ with $\Cl(p, q-1)$ when $e_{n}^{2} = -1$; the script verifies the relations exactly for $(2,4)$ and $(4,2)$, and Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}'s computation gives $\Cl(2,3)$ and $\Cl(4,1)$ the same type, centre and module dimension, both $\Mat(4,\C)$. The spin group (even versors with $R\tilde{R} = 1$) and the invariant form $\bar{\psi}\varphi$ on $\Cl^{0}f$ are defined by the even subalgebra and the ambient reversion, which the reversal leaves unchanged, since $(p,q) \mapsto (q,p)$ changes the signs of vector squares and not the order of products. Under $e_{i} \mapsto e_{i}e_{n}$ the ambient reversion becomes Clifford conjugation of $\Cl(2,3)$, the antilinear involution a hermitian form needs, and the form so built has signature $(2,2)$: the spin group is $SU(2,2)$ in both cases, with the same representation on the conformal spinor space $\CS$, the minimal left ideal of the even algebra (likewise $\Cl^{0}(1,3) \cong \Cl(1,2)$ and $\Cl^{0}(3,1) \cong \Cl(3,0)$ are both $\Mat(2,\C)$, with the same Lorentz spin group and Weyl spinors).

Mass formula: $m^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ is the squared norm of $\pi^{1} \wedge \pi^{2}$ for Weyl spinors of the common $SL(2,\C)$. Segre and hypercharge: statements about $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ and mode counts. dark-matter.mode-counts-two-modules-whic.technical:
With the towers populated at a common rung height $k$ (one descent, Premise P1), tower $r$'s Fock module is $S_{r} \otimes \mathcal{F}_{k}$, with $\tfrac{1}{2}\dim_{\R} S_{r} \cdot 2^{k}$ fermionic modes. The rung factor does not depend on the residue: every populated representative has Witt index $\min(p,q) = 1$, so $\dim \mathcal{F}_{k} = 2^{k}$ in every tower. The ground factor does: counting both irreducible modules where the centre splits, as Premise P2 (indifference) requires, $\dim_{\R} S_{r}$ is $8, 4, 4, 4, 8, 16$ at $r = 6, 2, 1, 7, 3, 5$, so the five dark towers' weighting relative to this one is $\sum_{r \neq 6} n_{r}/n_{6} = 9/2$, or $13/4$ with one module each, and $10$ or $15/2$ in the opposite labelling convention.

That weighting depends on the convention and is not the count. The series' matter is the derived state space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3})$ of five conformal spinor modes, not the full Fock module, and the mirror's is identical to ours, so $n_{2} = n_{6}$. For the odd towers the state space would need the correspondence between points and conformal spinors in three and five dimensions, which is established only in four, so $n_{1,7,3,5}$ are fixed only up to the pair counts $2$ and $3$, and they do not enter the asymmetric count.
dark-matter.mode-counts-two-modules-whic.lay: Assume, as the paper's premises do, that all the hidden worlds came from one descent and so sit at a common height on the ladder (Premise P1), and that where there are two mirror-image versions of the basic module both are counted (the indifference premise P2). One can then count how many particle states each hidden world has from the raw algebra, but the answer depends on bookkeeping choices, such as which world's count is used as the yardstick. The matter the framework actually derives lives in a smaller, specific space of states, and for the mirror world that space is exactly the same as ours. For the odd-dimensional worlds the corresponding count is not yet available beyond a count of their pairs.

dark-matter.nesting.technical:
Algebraically, in $\Cl(1,4)$ the generators $e_{0}, \ldots, e_{3}$ satisfy the relations of $\Cl(1,3)$, and in $\Cl(1,3)$ the generators $e_{0}, e_{1}, e_{2}$ satisfy those of $\Cl(1,2)$: this world's algebra is the slice of the five-dimensional tower's with the fifth generator dropped, and the three-dimensional tower's is a slice of ours, the mirror chain being the same with signatures reversed.

Geometrically, with $H'$ the hyperplane $x_{4} = 0$, $\B^{4} \cap H' = \B^{3}$ and $\B^{3} \cap \{x_{3} = 0\} = \B^{2}$, so each unit ball of space is the equatorial section of the next; and $\Sph^{5} \cap \{x_{6} = 0\} = \Sph^{4}$, $\Sph^{4} \cap \{x_{5} = 0\} = \Sph^{3}$, so each spacetime sphere is the equator of the next. The balls carry the space dimension $D$ and the spheres the spacetime dimension $n = D + 1$.
dark-matter.nesting.lay: The hidden worlds fit inside one another like nested slices. Our world's algebra is what remains of a five-dimensional world's when one direction is dropped, and a three-dimensional world's is what remains of ours. The same holds for the geometry: our unit ball of space is the equator of the larger world's ball, and so on down the chain.

dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-.formal: Three facts bear on a rule relating an odd tower's gauge coupling to this tower's. (a) In a tower of dimension $d \neq 4$ the gauge coupling is dimensionful, $[g^{2}] = \mathrm{mass}^{4-d}$, so a comparison with this tower's dimensionless coupling needs a length, and in five dimensions that length is the size of the fifth direction, which the sheaf paper's wall construction does not fix \cite{ButlerT4}. (b) No gauge coupling value is derived anywhere in the series: the Standard-Model paper takes $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ from the record \cite[Fact 2.8, Prop.~6.1]{ButlerT12}. (c) The odd towers are inequivalent to this one as soldered algebras (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}) and lie off the reversal orbit, and neither premise that equates across towers reaches them: Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} equates sector labels, not couplings, and only along that orbit, and Premise \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise} equates the ceiling couplings of the two members of that orbit only (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv)).
dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-.technical:
Three facts bear on a rule relating an odd tower's gauge coupling to ours. In dimension $d \neq 4$ the coupling is dimensionful, $[g^{2}] = \mathrm{mass}^{4-d}$, so a comparison with our dimensionless coupling needs a length, and in five dimensions that length, the size of the fifth direction, is not fixed by the wall construction. No gauge coupling value is derived anywhere in the series; ours are taken from the record. And neither premise that equates across towers reaches the odd towers, which are inequivalent to this one as soldered algebras and lie off the reversal orbit: indifference equates sector labels, not couplings, along that orbit only, and the common-ceiling-coupling premise equates the couplings of the mirror and this tower only.

\emph{Remark (a reading, not proved).} Taken together, the three facts say that any rule relating an odd tower's coupling to ours would be a further premise, and the paper adopts none. This reading is an inventory of what the stored results supply, at structural level, not a theorem in the series' strict sense: a rule could still follow from a result the series does not yet contain.
dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-.lay: Saying how strong the forces are in an odd-dimensional hidden world, compared with ours, would need an extra rule, and three facts stand in the way of getting one from the series: the strength there carries units, so comparing it needs a length the theory does not fix; the series does not predict our own force strengths either; and the assumptions that treat worlds alike (indifference, P2, and the equal starting strengths of the mirror world) only link our world with its mirror image. The natural reading, that any such rule would be a new assumption, is stated as a remark, not proved.

dark-matter.odd-towers-populated.formal:
\emph{Premise (Pop), the population of the odd towers.} The descent deposited matter in each of the four odd towers: the two three-dimensional towers (residues $1$ and $7$) and the two five-dimensional towers (residues $3$ and $5$), at their representatives under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives}.

\emph{It is inferred from the number it helps fit.} Nothing in the series reaches the odd towers' population: Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} does not equate them with this tower, the series gives them algebras and not contents, and what the descent deposited in each belongs to the pre-descent theory. The only support is the record read inside the framework (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}): with the mirror's share exactly one, empty odd towers would give a dark-to-baryon ratio of $1$ against the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$, and the framework has no other dark candidate, so the observed remainder $4.364$ is the evidence that they hold matter. That remainder is the same number the unit-ball closed form, which sums over these four towers, is then compared with. The premise therefore adds no support to the fit that is independent of the fitted number.

\emph{Scope.} This tower is populated by observation and the mirror by the copy along the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}); neither is part of this premise. The premise says that the odd towers hold matter, not how much: the amount is Premises \claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum} to \claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction}. No result outside the fitted total depends on it: the mirror share, the superselection, the parity theorem and the arrow are the same if the odd towers are empty.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if the pre-descent theory, once written, deposits nothing in an odd tower, or if the dark matter is shown to be other than the towers' matter; without it the framework's ratio is $1$.
dark-matter.odd-towers-populated.technical: The unit-ball closed form sums over the mirror and the four odd towers, so it needs the odd towers to hold matter. Nothing in the series gives that: indifference does not reach them, and the series assigns them algebras, not contents. The stored support is an inference from the record: with the mirror's share one, empty odd towers would give a ratio of $1$ against the observed $5.364$, so the remainder $4.364$ is read as their matter. That remainder is also what the closed form is compared with, so the premise is inferred from the number it helps fit and adds no independent support. It was held as text (the population observation, and a presupposition of R2); this entry registers it as a premise so that the total shows it among its conditions.
dark-matter.odd-towers-populated.lay: The formula for the amount of dark matter assumes that four of the hidden sectors actually contain matter. The series has no argument for that except the measurement itself: if they were empty, the dark matter would equal the ordinary matter, and it is about five times larger. So the assumption is read off from the very number the formula is meant to account for, and cannot count as separate evidence for it. This entry records it as an assumption in its own right.
