dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs.formal:
\emph{The mirror tower.} Its relativistic content is a copy of ours, so at recombination its radiation is $\rho'_{\mathrm{rad}} = (T'/T_{\gamma})^{4}\,\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}$ with $T'$ the mirror photon temperature and the same internal thermal history; in neutrino units the visible radiation is
\[
\Neff^{\mathrm{tot}} \;=\; \frac{8}{7}\left(\frac{11}{4}\right)^{4/3} + 3.044 \;=\; 7.447, \qquad\text{so}\qquad \Delta\Neff^{\mathrm{mirror}} \;=\; 7.447\left(\frac{T'}{T_{\gamma}}\right)^{4},
\]
and the Planck cap requires $T'/T_{\gamma} < 0.448$ (three relativistic mirror neutrinos; if the heaviest is non-relativistic at recombination, true for $T'/T_{\gamma}$ below about $0.3$ at our masses, the coefficient is $6.43$ and the threshold $0.47$; the paper carries the conservative figure). A copy releases the same entropy as ours at the same epochs, so this ratio is the ratio \emph{seeded at the descent} (the copied history fails at the mirror's nucleosynthesis near the floor, where burning reheats its plasma by $3.0$ to $3.2$, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}; the bound is met on either reading, by eight orders or more up to the hot-deposit point estimate of that Proposition): route (a) below does not arise for the mirror, and the descent must have heated it to less than $0.448$ of the visible temperature, the standard requirement of mirror-matter cosmology \cite{FootMirror2004}. The structure meets it with one datum: after the descent the mirror is heated only through the shared metric (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), which puts its temperature at a floor of about three parts in ten thousand of ours at the top of the ceiling range (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii); $1.1 \times 10^{-3}$ even for a coefficient of ten, beyond the mirror's content), and above the floor the deposit sets it, near four parts in a thousand on the paper's estimate (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}). A cold mirror with our baryon number is what the framework predicts once that seeded temperature is taken as a free datum of the descent; by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} this is an exception to P2, which, applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), gives $T'/T_{\gamma} = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$, excluded by the cap above. This is an exception to P2 at its version-1 reach; P2 as scoped leaves $\xi$ free (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}), and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}).

\emph{The five-dimensional towers.} A massless abelian species surviving in tower $r$ at temperature $T_{r}$ with $g_{r}$ light polarisations contributes
\[
\Delta\Neff \;=\; g_{r}\,\frac{4}{7}\left(\frac{11}{4}\right)^{4/3}\left(\frac{T_{r}}{T_{\gamma}}\right)^{4} \;\approx\; 2.2\,g_{r}\left(\frac{T_{r}}{T_{\gamma}}\right)^{4}
\]
($g_{r} = 2$ for a four-dimensional photon or a five-dimensional zero mode, $3$ if a fifth component is light). The cap $\Delta\Neff \lesssim 0.3$ is met by one such species if and only if $T_{r}/T_{\gamma} \lesssim (0.3/2.2\,g_{r})^{1/4}$, that is, $0.51$ for $g_{r} = 2$ and $0.46$ for $g_{r} = 3$, and by several jointly if their sum is under the cap.

Three routes close a channel, none proved here. (a) The sector is colder than the photons by a factor of about two, as a sector decoupled and releasing less entropy than ours is: the visible entropy release from the GeV epoch to today heats the photons relative to such a sector by $(g_{*}(\mathrm{GeV})/g_{*}(\mathrm{now}))^{1/3} \approx 2.51$, giving $\Delta\Neff \approx 0.11$ per two-polarisation species, so the two five-dimensional towers sit at $0.22$ with two light polarisations each, under the cap, and at $0.33$ with three, over it; a sector decoupled since the descent is colder still. (b) The abelian factor is Higgsed by the tower's own condensate, whenever that condensate carries the charge (this tower's neutral condensate is the accident that leaves our photon massless). (c) The rung-level charges, or the intrinsic $U(1)$, are not gauged in that tower once its content is derived as this tower's was. Route (a) is a thermal-history computation, (b) and (c) content derivations; all three are successor problem (1).

Observation level; the stance $\Delta\Neff \approx 0$ is registered conditional on them and on the mirror's seeded temperature.
dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs.technical:
For the mirror tower, whose relativistic content copies ours, the radiation in neutrino units is $N_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{8}{7}\left(\frac{11}{4}\right)^{4/3} + 3.044 = 7.447$, so $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\mathrm{mirror}} = 7.447\,(T'/T_{\gamma})^{4}$ and the Planck cap requires $T'/T_{\gamma} < 0.448$, the standard requirement of mirror-matter cosmology. Since a copy releases entropy as ours does, this is the ratio seeded at the descent. After the descent the mirror is heated only through the shared metric, which puts it at a floor of about three parts in ten thousand of our temperature at the top of the ceiling range, with the deposit setting it near four parts in a thousand on the paper's estimate. Caveat (T14c): that cold mirror takes the seeded temperature as a free datum, an unstated exception to indifference, which applied with the copy theorem's reach gives $T'/T_{\gamma} = 1$ and $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} = 7.45$, over the cap (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2}). That is an exception to indifference at its version-1 reach; indifference as scoped (labels, not states) leaves $\xi$ free (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}), and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}).

For a massless abelian species in tower $r$ with $g_{r}$ light polarisations, $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 2.2\,g_{r}(T_{r}/T_{\gamma})^{4}$, so the cap $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} \lesssim 0.3$ needs $T_{r}/T_{\gamma} \lesssim 0.51$ for $g_{r} = 2$ and $0.46$ for $g_{r} = 3$. Three routes would close such a channel, none proved here: the sector is colder by the entropy-release factor of about $2.51$, its abelian factor is Higgsed by its own condensate, or its charges are not gauged. The stance $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 0$ is registered conditional on these routes and on the mirror's seeded temperature, at observation level.
dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs.lay: Hidden copies of ordinary matter would carry their own kinds of light, and the cosmic microwave background tightly limits how much extra light the early universe could hold. This result works out how cold each hidden sector must be to stay within that limit: a mirror copy of our world must be below about 45 per cent of our temperature, and on the paper's estimates, with the mirror heated after the descent only through gravity, it sits far below that; a later note (T14c) points out that this coldness is an unstated exception to the paper's indifference principle, which applied evenly would make the mirror as hot as our world. As the principle is now scoped, it applies to labels such as charges and not to temperatures, so it leaves the mirror's temperature free; a cold mirror then needs the descent to have left the towers out of equilibrium. For the five-dimensional sectors it lists three ways the problem could be avoided, none of them yet proved, so the expectation of no extra light is conditional on those routes and on the mirror's starting temperature, and is held at observation level.

dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeent.formal:
The Standard-Model paper left one absolute bit undetermined, the particle-antiparticle orientation, expected to be fixed by the charge-zero condition. The expectation is refuted by a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ covariance argument parallel to the trichotomy's rescaling one, on three premises: that CPT conjugation $C$ is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure and leaves every action functional $S_{\mu}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape} invariant, $S_{\mu}\circ C = S_{\mu}$, the gauge couplings included (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}; checked in the proof for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action; premised for the imported gauge sector and for structures later papers add); Hypothesis (S), under which the Standard-Model paper's chirality proposition, the source of the relative-versus-absolute split, is proved (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}); and that the orientation flag is a datum of each solution, the sign of its complex structure relative to the Fock module's unit planted by the descent and not part of the kinematic structure (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}; were it kinematic, the bit would be constant on every solution space, hence dynamically fixed within each of two isomorphic theories, and the conclusion below would fail). Here $C$ is the composite of grade involution, reversal and the flag conjugate, an anti-automorphism; acting on fields as a symmetry does (vectors by its vector part, connections through the induced Lie algebra automorphism), it is $\mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, with $\kappa$ complex conjugation, so it is antilinear (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}).

Anything the structures determine is conjugation-invariant, and the orientation is not. The charge-zero condition fixes all \emph{relative} structure \cite[Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT12}; under that reading the absolute bit is not kinematic, and since conjugation maps each solution space onto itself and exchanges the two orientations, the bit takes both values on every nonempty solution space: it is initial data in the sense of clause (I) of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, and so neither dynamically fixed nor a parameter of the laws (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaustive-three-are}). No exhaustiveness of the kinematic, dynamical and initial-data alternatives is used. It is the Witt flag of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}: the open orientation of the content derivation and the arrow of time are one choice, made once.

The descent measure carries two numbers and one bit. The neutrino sector supplies no orientation refutation condition: the identification of $\nu_{R}$ with the hypercharge-zero singlet at grade zero is flag-covariant (the conjugate flag exchanges the singlet grades zero and three), so no completion of the orientation could exclude it \cite{ButlerT15}.

This is the seventeenth refutation (the sixteenth is the neutrino paper's \cite[Prop.~4.1(1)]{ButlerT15}), in the pattern of the thirteenth and the trichotomy: what the framework cannot determine, it can prove it cannot determine, and locate.
dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeent.technical:
The particle-antiparticle orientation, the one absolute bit the Standard-Model derivation left open, is not fixed by the charge-zero condition. The argument rests on three premises: that the CPT composite of grade involution, reversal and flag conjugation is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure and leaves every action functional and its parameters, gauge couplings included, unchanged (checked for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action, premised for the imported gauge sector); Hypothesis (S); and that the orientation flag belongs to each solution rather than to the kinematic structure. The composite reverses products, and acting on fields as a symmetry it is the pseudoscalar rotor followed by complex conjugation, so the conjugation is antilinear, not real linear. Anything the structures determine is invariant under this $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ conjugation, while the orientation is exchanged by it.

So the charge-zero condition fixes all relative structure and leaves the absolute bit kinematically underdetermined. Because the conjugation leaves each action, and the value of its parameter, unchanged, it carries every solution to a solution of the same theory with the opposite orientation; the bit therefore varies within each solution space, which is what initial data means in the action paper's classification, and it is neither fixed by the dynamics nor a parameter of the laws. The earlier third premise, that kinematic, dynamical and initial data exhaust the possibilities, is not needed. The bit is the Witt flag, so that the orientation of the derived content and the arrow of time are one choice made once. The neutrino sector supplies no refutation condition, since identifying $\nu_{R}$ with the hypercharge-zero singlet is flag-covariant, the conjugate flag exchanging the singlet grades $0$ and $3$.
dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeent.lay: Our universe is made of matter rather than antimatter, and in this framework a single yes-or-no choice decides which is which. Assuming that the matter-antimatter symmetry (CPT) respects every structure of the theory, its laws included (checked for the core structures, assumed for the imported forces and later additions), that the slots behave like the pairs (Hypothesis (S)), and that the choice belongs to each possible universe rather than to the theory's fixed structure (all three stated as assumptions), this result shows that none of the framework's laws can make that choice: the symmetry turns any possible universe into another possible universe of the same theory with the choice reversed. So the choice differs between solutions of one and the same theory, which makes it a starting condition rather than a setting of the laws, and it is the same choice that sets the direction of time.

proofs.main:
CPT conjugation is the composition of grade involution, reversal, and the flag conjugate $v_{k} \leftrightarrow w_{k}$ (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) on each tower's Clifford bundle; the grade involution negates every vector, the timelike one included (the T; the spatial inversion is the P). Because of the reversal the composite is an anti-automorphism, and it acts on fields as a symmetry does (the convention stated in \claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}): on vectors by its vector part, and on a connection through the Lie algebra automorphism it induces, so that curvature is fixed. In that convention it acts on fields as $C = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, $\kappa$ complex conjugation: its vector part $-1$ is the rotor $I_{6}$, and the flag conjugate that preserves the frozen point's action is complex conjugation, which carries the flag $W$ to $\overline W$, in the other family (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}). So $C$ is antilinear. Structure by structure: the fibre metric is fixed by grade involution, reversal and the exchange of a null pair, which is an isometry of the completion's hyperbolic plane; the pairing on the Fock module sends the grade-$k$ state to the grade-$(3-k)$ state \cite[Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT12} (\claimref{standard-model.chirality-two-halves-spinor-module-conjugation}), which is exactly what the flag conjugate does; and the action is the frozen point's, built from the metric and the completion. The derived gauge sector (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain}) is CPT-even by the standard theorem for local Lorentz-invariant actions, but that theorem concerns the antiunitary CPT operator of quantum field theory; that $C$, antilinear and so of Wigner's antiunitary type, realises that operator is argued, not proved, so the gauge sector's CPT-evenness is imported and carried as a premise (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}).

So $C$ is an isomorphism of the kinematic data exchanging the flag's two orientations, and a quantity the structures determine would be fixed by it while the orientation is not. The last step reads the bit against Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape} directly. Let $S_{\mu}$ be the action functionals, $\mu$ the norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ of the frozen point together with whatever couplings the imported gauge sector carries, and $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$ their solution spaces. The premise's clause for the action says $S_{\mu} \circ C = S_{\mu}$ for every $\mu$, the gauge couplings included; for the norm this is visible directly, since $C$ sends the real vector $I$ to $-I$, so $Q(CI) = Q(I)$ and $C$ does not move $\mu$, and for the gauge couplings it is the premise. A critical point of a $C$-invariant functional is carried by the involution $C$ to a critical point of the same functional, so $C(\mathcal{S}_{\mu}) = \mathcal{S}_{\mu}$ for every $\mu$. Let $q = \pm 1$ be the orientation bit, a function of the solution (the descent plants its flag once, Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}, so $q$ is conserved). By the premise that the flag is a datum (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}), the sign of the flag's complex structure $J$ relative to the Fock module's unit $I_7$ (the central pseudoscalar of the odd extension, \claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}) is configuration data of each solution, planted by the descent on the three-pair structure, and not part of the kinematic structure: were it kinematic, the bit would be constant on every solution space of the theory carrying it, hence (D) there, and the two orientations would be two isomorphic theories rather than two solutions of one. Under that premise, $C$ exchanges the two orientations, $q(Cx) = -q(x)$. For every $\mu$ with $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$ nonempty, which holds for the $\mu$ of our universe, $q$ therefore takes both values on $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$, so it is not constant on $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$: $q$ is (I). By Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaustive-three-are} it is then neither (D) nor (P), each of which requires constancy on every $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$; and it is not (K), since $x$ and $Cx$ have isomorphic kinematic structures, $C$ being that isomorphism, while $q(Cx) \neq q(x)$. The step excludes a parameter of the laws for the bit directly, because a parameter of the laws is constant on each solution space and the bit is not; no exhaustiveness of the kinematic, dynamical and initial-data alternatives enters. The relative-versus-absolute split is the Standard-Model paper's chirality proposition, imported under Hypothesis (S) (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}); the flag-covariance of the $\nu_{R}$ identification is the exchange of the singlet grades, which the legacy script verifies on the three-pair Fock model. The script of this version tests the logical step and the frozen-point part of the action, not the premises: it applies $C = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$ explicitly, in Gaussian rational arithmetic, and confirms that on fixed rational data in the six-dimensional ambient space it is $-1$ on vectors, fixes the curvature bivector, and fixes the norms and the integrand $\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, that on complexified data it is antilinear and carries each of them to its complex conjugate (with controls in which negating $I$ alone, or a real-linear flag conjugate in place of $\kappa$, flips the integrand), that the flag conjugate, on the split real form, is an isometry of the three null pairs exchanging the two pure vacua $v_{1}v_{2}v_{3}$ and $w_{1}w_{2}w_{3}$, and, exhaustively on small finite theories, that a $C$-odd quantity on $C$-stable solution spaces is (I) and not (K), with a control in which dropping $C$-stability makes it (P).

dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point.formal:
The descent was one event freezing one $I$ and making one orientation choice: all towers couple to one metric and are oriented, where they can be, by the one Witt flag of that event (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}). The orientation clause is used only on the reversal orbit, where the identification of the flag across the two towers is canonical. \emph{Support:} \cite[Thm.~4.7]{ButlerT6}, \cite[Obs.~7.4]{ButlerT12}; the orientation clause is this paper's. Structural premise.

\emph{The three clauses and their status.} The premise is three statements, used separately.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(P1a)] \emph{(Metric.)} One frozen point: all towers couple to one metric. Status: a theorem up to a common normalisation wherever the Weyl tensor has no kernel vector, given that every tower's frozen point is parallel for one tractor connection (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-unique-where-weyl-has-no-kernel}); an independent choice on conformally flat regions, the de Sitter vacuum included (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.two-frozen-points-conformally-flat}). What stays postulated is the one tractor connection, the normalisation, and the clause on conformally flat regions. This is the clause read as the sourcing rule (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}), and the one most widely used.
\item[(P1b)] \emph{(Orientation.)} Where towers can be oriented they are oriented by the one Witt flag; used only on the reversal orbit. Status: substitutable. The sign of the mirror's asymmetry is fixed by this clause or by Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} applied to the orientation bit (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mirror-asymmetry-route-one}; Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)), so under P2 as scoped to labels the clause is redundant on the reading that the bit is a label (argued). The mirror's share is even in that sign, so the dark-to-baryon total needs the clause under neither route (argued).
\item[(P1c)] \emph{(Common $N$.)} The number $N$ is common to the towers. Status: postulated, with no derivation found; it is used by the charge reading of the stored asymmetry (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}; Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v), first route). Whether a second tower can carry its own frozen-point norm is undecided; the conformally flat counter-model of (P1a) suggests it can (argued).
\end{enumerate}
The clauses are kept in one entity; results that assume P1 use the clause their text names.

\emph{Note (which connection, 2026-11-11).} The ``one tractor connection'' of (P1a) is not named above, and the two theorems cited there are about the normal tractor connection, for which a tractor is parallel in the physical scale only on Einstein regions. Under Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point} (FS) the frozen point is parallel, with unit pairing with $X$, for the varied connection $A_{\rho}$ on every field, matter included. For that connection the status of (P1a) is given by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-unique-for-the-field-space-connection}: if every tower's frozen point is parallel for the one $A_{\rho}$ on a connected part of the invertible region that contains one point where $-(\mathcal{R} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\mathrm{id})$ has no kernel vector (any point with isotropic matter other than $w = -\tfrac13$; on Einstein regions the Weyl condition above), the frozen points agree up to constants $c_{r}$, and the independent choice is confined to a component that is de Sitter at that $\Lambda$, not to every conformally flat region. What stays postulated is unchanged: the one connection, and the normalisation $c_{r} = \pm 1$, to which the common $N$ of (P1c) is equivalent given one $G$; (FS) normalises one tractor and does not supply it. For the tower of reversed signature the connection can be shared up to the sign of the frozen point or the discrete element $\operatorname{Ad}(I_{4})$ (the Remark of that Theorem); whether that element bears on the orientation clause (P1b) is not examined. The premise is unchanged.

dark-matter.p2-indifference.formal:
The descent cannot instantiate uncaused distinctions \cite[Principle~5.4]{ButlerT8}, \cite[\S2]{ButlerT13}: it equates along symmetry orbits and never equates inequivalent components. The residues are inequivalent as soldered algebras (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}) except along the reversal $r \mapsto -r$ (exchanging $2 \leftrightarrow 6$, $1 \leftrightarrow 7$, $3 \leftrightarrow 5$, fixing $0$, $4$), so P2 equates along that orbit only; which of $2$, $6$ is visible is declared indexical. Structural premise.

\emph{Scope: labels, not states.} What P2 equates along the orbit are the sector labels the descent deposits, the superselection labels of the deposited algebra, such as the tower charge (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}); it does not equate thermal states within a selected sector, so it says nothing about the temperatures of the two members of a reversal pair. The deposited mode set is declared finite. In the boundary-mode model of a reversal pair (Hypothesis (B') of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}) this scope is well defined: on every finite window the tower charge is a sector label and the temperature ratio $\xi = \beta/\beta'$ is not, so P2 reaches the stored charge and leaves $\xi$ free; a temperature becomes a label, in the disjointness sense, only on an algebra with infinitely many modes in one frequency band, which the finiteness declaration excludes.
dark-matter.p2-indifference.technical:
The descent cannot instantiate uncaused distinctions: it equates components along symmetry orbits and never equates inequivalent ones. The residues are inequivalent as soldered algebras except along the reversal $r \mapsto -r$, which exchanges $2 \leftrightarrow 6$, $1 \leftrightarrow 7$, $3 \leftrightarrow 5$ and fixes $0$ and $4$, so the premise equates towers along that orbit only. Which of $2$ and $6$ is the visible tower is declared indexical.

The premise is scoped to labels, not states: it equates the superselection labels the descent deposits, such as the tower charge, and not the thermal state within a sector, and the deposited set of modes is declared finite. In the boundary-mode model of a reversal pair the charge is a label on every finite set of modes while the temperature is not, so under this scope P2 constrains the stored charge and leaves the mirror's temperature ratio free; only with infinitely many modes in a frequency band would the temperature become a label too, and the finiteness declaration rules that out.
dark-matter.p2-indifference.lay: This assumption says the birth of the universe treats alike only things that are genuinely alike. The only hidden sectors that count as alike are pairs related by a reflection, so only those pairs are forced to match. Which member of the matching pair we live in is simply a matter of where we stand. What must match are the sector's fixed labels, such as its stored charge, not how hot it is: the assumption leaves the temperature of the mirror sector open, and it takes the number of modes the birth deposits to be finite.

dark-matter.p5-boundary-modes-hold-entro.technical: The ascended boundary mode space at a black hole's singular locus stores and returns information, quantified by its deficit theorem, but not global charge. Gauss-law charges are returned tower by tower through discharge, while baryon number is returned by no hole in any tower. The imported Hawking flux already implies this here: a hole emits baryons only once $T_{\mathrm{H}} > m_{p}$, that is below $M = M_{\mathrm{Pl}}^{2}/8\pi m_{p} \approx 6 \times 10^{36}$ GeV, returning less than $10^{-20}$ of a solar-mass progenitor's baryons. dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-space.formal:
Matter of any tower crossing this tower's horizon meets the shared singular locus, which degenerates every tower's algebra, so each tower ascends its own ladder there, parallel boundary mode spaces at one wall. The fate of what fell in, for all towers and holes (clause (iii) limited in mass):

(i) \emph{Energy:} its rest energy joins the one metric (P1) and is returned democratically as Hawking radiation into every populated tower, in proportion to each tower's light degrees of freedom once the temperature exceeds their gaps, because barriers, transmission coefficients and occupancies belong to the exterior metric, which does not record which tower the mass came from; this is P1 with Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators} and the Hawking paper's greybody assembly under its interface premise, run tower by tower \cite[Assembly~5.4]{ButlerT7}. (ii) \emph{Information:} it ascends its own tower's boundary mode space and returns in its own tower's channel, at little entropy cost: a solar-mass hole's Bekenstein entropy is of order $10^{77}$ against its progenitor's $10^{58}$, so the singularity paper's deficit theorem and Page curve are untouched, tower by tower. (iii) \emph{Gauss-law charges,} for holes below about $1.3 \times 10^{5}$ solar masses, are returned per tower by that tower's own discharge (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-schwinger-discharge-charged-hole}), at a cost of order the charge times the lightest charged mass, negligible against $M$; above that mass discharge does not limit the charge, and whether a supermassive hole returns it is left open here; no other clause uses (iii).

(iv) \emph{Global charges} are not returned in any tower, ours included (P5): information is returned at little cost because Hawking quanta are soft, and charge would cost the hole's mass to return because its lightest carrier is a GeV proton against a nanokelvin $T_{\mathrm{H}}$. (v) \emph{No remnant:} the singularity paper's exhaustiveness clause, imported as Fact \claimref{singularity.rate-models-kinematic-inputs-l-u} at its level there, a premise.

The late-stage evaporation therefore dims the visible final burst by the ratio of the total light degrees of freedom to the visible ones, of order the tower count if the towers are comparable, a minor prediction for primordial-black-hole burst searches at observation level, unconditional on the charge regime since it follows from (i) alone. The charge-saturated case is clearest: a hole formed from mirror matter alone has $Q_{2}m_{2} = M$, and it does not return its charge, exactly as no astrophysical hole of this tower returns ours. The ascend-then-descend structure at the degenerate locus is imported from the singularity paper \cite{ButlerT5}.
dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-space.technical:
Matter of any tower crossing a horizon meets the one shared singular locus, where every tower's algebra degenerates and ascends its own ladder, giving parallel boundary mode spaces at one wall. Under P1 and the Hawking paper's greybody assembly under its interface premise, run tower by tower, (i) the rest energy joins the metric and is re-emitted democratically as Hawking radiation into every populated tower, in proportion to its light degrees of freedom; (ii) information returns in its own tower's channel at little entropy cost, since $S_{\mathrm{BH}} \sim 10^{77}$ for a solar mass against a progenitor's $10^{58}$; (iii) Gauss-law charges are returned by discharge for holes below about $1.3 \times 10^{5}$ solar masses, and above that the question is left open.

Under P5, (iv) global charges are returned in no tower, since the lightest carrier is a GeV proton against a nanokelvin $T_{\mathrm{H}}$; and (v) there is no remnant, by the imported exhaustiveness premise. A consequence at observation level, from (i) alone, is that the final burst of an evaporating hole is dimmed by the ratio of total to visible light degrees of freedom.
dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-space.lay: Matter from any hidden sector that falls into a black hole ends up at the same place inside. This result follows what becomes of it, on stated premises: that all sectors share one gravitational field (P1), that the Hawking paper's interface premise about how emitted radiation reaches distant observers holds, that the hole's boundary modes give back information but not conserved particle counts (P5), and the imported premise that nothing is left over at the end. Under these, its energy comes back as Hawking radiation shared among all the sectors, its information comes back within its own sector, and its count of particles such as protons is not returned. A side effect, at the level of observation, is that the last flash of a tiny evaporating black hole would be fainter than expected, because part of it goes into the hidden sectors.

proofs.main:
The shared locus: the metric is one (P1, \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}), so its degeneration locus is one, and at it each tower's Clifford bundle meets its own corank condition; the ascent is within-tower (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), so each tower's boundary mode space opens separately over the same wall. Superselection (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}) constrains frozen-phase local operators, not counts: a mirror star collapsing and the hole radiating into every tower involves no operator with matrix elements between residues, the rest energy going into the shared metric and the emitted quanta being pair-created from each tower's own vacuum by that metric, the one channel Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable} leaves open; the clause that the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold the superselected charge stays true and stays about the residue label.

(i) is the greybody assembly (\claimref{hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise}) applied per tower, with democracy following from the metric's insensitivity to the residue. (ii) is arithmetic the script brackets: $S_{\mathrm{BH}} = 4\pi G M^{2}/\hbar c$ at one solar mass against a few nats per baryon over $1.2 \times 10^{57}$ baryons, ratio of order $10^{-19}$. (iii) is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-schwinger-discharge-charged-hole}, with that Fact's mass range. (iv) is P5 (\claimref{dark-matter.p5-boundary-modes-hold-entropy-not}), whose arithmetic the script brackets: the mass at which $T_{\mathrm{H}} = m_{p}$, $M_{\mathrm{Pl}}^{2}/(8\pi m_{p})$, in GeV and in grams, the maximal number of baryons a hole of that mass can emit, $M/m_{p}$, against the $M_{\odot}/m_{p}$ swallowed, and their ratio, below $10^{-20}$. (v) is the imported clause (Fact \claimref{singularity.rate-models-kinematic-inputs-l-u}).

Three consequences hold without changing any other result: the entropy accounting closes under democracy because the Hawking quanta are soft; the count is untouched, mass in holes still gravitating; and Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}'s ``cannot be produced afterwards'' concerns production, holes being a permitted sink. The trichotomy for what fell in (exact charge return, democratic emission, no remnant) is decided by P5 against the first alternative, which would cost the Hawking paper's interface premise or the singularity paper's exhaustiveness. The dimming factor is greybody counting at observation level, the towers' degree-of-freedom counts not derived.

dark-matter.population-count-one-share-h.technical:
For an oriented residue write $f_{r} = \epsilon_{r}n_{r}m_{r}/(\epsilon_{6}n_{6}m_{6})$ for the tower factor. Under Premises P1 to P3 and the common ceiling coupling (the paper's P4 being used only on the mirror, where it is a clause of the copy theorem), with every tower's matter diluting as this one's, (i) the asymmetric dark matter is the mirror tower's alone, the odd towers carrying none and residues $0$ and $4$ being sterile, with $\Omega^{\mathrm{asym}}_{\mathrm{dark}}/\Omega_{b} = f_{2} = 1$ against the observed $\Omega_{c}/\Omega_{b} \approx 5.364 \pm 0.065$, the one holding to half a percent on the burning branch. (ii) The remainder, $4.364\,\Omega_{b}$ or $\Omega h^{2} = 0.0976 \pm 0.0012$, is not asymmetric relic: an odd tower's matter, if any, is a symmetric relic deposited by the descent and heated afterwards only through gravity, its density set by the sector's own dynamics.

(iii) The remainder is not derived: the series derives no rule relating an odd tower's dimensionful coupling to this tower's dimensionless one, and no premise that equates across towers reaches the odd towers. The profile is mirror baryons at the proton mass, cold and dissipative within their sector, together with symmetric odd-tower matter of undetermined mass, both coupling to us by gravity alone; null results in direct and indirect detection are registered as conditional stances, at observation level on the flagged premises.
dark-matter.population-count-one-share-h.lay: Astronomers find about 5.4 times as much dark matter as ordinary matter. Assuming the three premises P1 to P3 (a single frozen point, indifference and nearest-dimension representatives; a fourth, a matter excess shared evenly across the oriented towers, is needed only for the mirror, where it follows from the mirror being a copy) and that the mirror world starts with the same force strengths as ours (the common ceiling coupling), and that every hidden sector's matter thins out with cosmic expansion as ours does, this result accounts for one of those units: a mirror copy of ordinary matter holding the same amount as ours to within half a percent. The other 4.4 units are not explained here; they would have to be a different, symmetric kind of matter in the other hidden sectors, felt by us only through gravity. The account is held at observation level on those premises.

dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance.formal:
\emph{CPT covariance.} CPT conjugation is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure and leaves every action functional invariant (T14, Proposition 5.2, its first premise: ``checked in the proof for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action; premised for the imported gauge sector and for structures later papers add'').

\emph{The conjugation.} CPT conjugation $\phi$ is the composite of grade involution, reversal and the flag conjugate exchanging the two families of maximal isotropic subspaces (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}). Because of the reversal, $\phi$ is an anti-automorphism of the Clifford algebra.

\emph{Convention (field action).} $\phi$ acts on fields as a symmetry: on a vector field by its vector part, and on a connection $A$ through the Lie algebra automorphism it induces, $A \mapsto -\phi(A)$, so that curvature is carried by that automorphism. In this convention $\phi$ acts on fields as $C = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, with $\kappa$ complex conjugation on $\Cl(2,4) \otimes \C$: its vector part $-1$ is the rotor $I_{6}$ of the identity component, and the flag conjugate that preserves the frozen point's action is complex conjugation, a real-linear one reversing that action (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}). So CPT conjugation is antilinear on the complexified ambient and on the Fock module, of Wigner's antiunitary type (argued there, not proved).

\emph{Action clause.} For every action functional $S_{\mu}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, the gauge couplings among its parameters $\mu$ included, $S_{\mu} \circ C = S_{\mu}$; in particular $C$ does not move $\mu$.

\emph{What is checked and what is premised.} Checked: the fibre metric, the completion, the pairing on the Fock module, and the frozen point's action, which with every functional of real tensor fields invariant under constant $SO_{0}(2,4)$ satisfies the action clause in this convention by the cited result's clause (5). Premised: the imported gauge sector, spinor and fermion fields, and structures later papers add. For the gauge sector the standard CPT theorem for local Lorentz-invariant actions concerns the antiunitary CPT operator of quantum field theory, and this conjugation is not that operator (argued): it fixes every bivector of $\Cl(2,4)$ ($I_{6}$ commutes with the even algebra), so every conformal generator and in particular every translation, and it is antilinear, so on a Hilbert space that carries the translations it reverses their generator and with it the energy, whereas the CPT operator of quantum field theory reverses the translations and keeps the energy positive. The gauge sector's invariance under this conjugation is therefore not supplied by the CPT theorem; it ``is imported and carried as a premise''.
dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance.technical:
The premise is that CPT conjugation, the composite of grade involution, reversal and the flag conjugate on each tower's Clifford bundle, is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure of the framework and leaves every action functional, together with the values of its parameters, unchanged. The gauge couplings are among those parameters, so the clause is that conjugation maps every theory of the family onto itself, not merely that it fixes the frozen point's action.

The convention is stated because the composite is an anti-automorphism (reversal reverses products), and an anti-automorphism can be made to act on an action in more than one way. Here it acts as a symmetry acts on fields: vectors by its vector part, connections through the Lie algebra automorphism it induces, so curvature is fixed. In that convention the composite acts on fields as the pseudoscalar rotor $I_{6}$, a rotation of the identity component, followed by complex conjugation, and the flag conjugate compatible with an invariant action has to be complex conjugation. So the conjugation is antilinear, the type of Wigner's antiunitary symmetries, not the real linear map the dark-matter paper's wording describes.

The paper checks the premise for the fibre metric, the completion's hyperbolic plane, the pairing on the Fock module and the frozen point's action; in the convention the action clause also holds for every functional of real tensor fields invariant under constant conformal rotations. For the imported gauge sector, spinor and fermion fields, and any structure a later paper adds, it is assumed. Under it, anything the structures and laws determine is conjugation-invariant, which is the first step of the argument that the particle-antiparticle orientation is not determined by them.
dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance.lay: This is an assumption, partly checked: a particular symmetry that swaps matter with antimatter, reverses time and mirrors space is taken to leave every basic structure of the framework, and every one of its laws including the strengths of the forces, unchanged. Worked out exactly, the symmetry involves complex conjugation, the same kind of operation quantum field theory uses for this symmetry, rather than an ordinary linear swap. The series verifies the assumption for the geometric structures and for gravity, and assumes it for the imported description of the forces and of matter. It is the first premise behind the claim that the matter-antimatter orientation of the universe is a free choice rather than something the framework fixes.

dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum.formal:
\emph{The flag as datum.} The descent's flag $W$ (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) is the $+I_7$ eigenspace of an orthogonal complex structure $J$ on $\R^{2,4}$, extended to $\R^{2,4} \oplus I_7\R^{2,4}$, and its conjugate $\overline W$ is the $+I_7$ eigenspace of $-J$; here $I_7 = I_6e$, the central pseudoscalar of the odd extension $\Cl(3,4) = \Cl(2,4)_{\C}$, is the scalar unit of the complexification and of the Fock module (\claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}), and $J$ is a map on vectors, not an element identified with it (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}, clause (2)). The premise: the sign of $J$ relative to the unit $I_7$ of the Fock module is configuration data of each solution, planted by the descent, and not part of the kinematic structure. That is, in the terms of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, a configuration $x$ and the configuration with the opposite sign of $J$ have isomorphic kinematic structures and lie in the configuration space of the same family of action functionals $S_{\mu}$; the orientation bit $q(x) = \pm 1$ is a function of the configuration, not of the theory.

\emph{What it is for.} With CPT covariance (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}), whose conjugation exchanges the two signs, it places the orientation bit in clause (I) of the Definition, taking both values on every nonempty solution space, rather than in (K) or (D). It is used by \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation} and its restatements \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection} and \claimref{one-relation.record-chain-votes-measurement-without-collapse}. Without it the conclusion fails in the way those results state: were the sign kinematic, the bit would be constant on every solution space of the theory carrying it, and the two orientations would be two isomorphic theories rather than two solutions of one.

\emph{What would refute it.} A structure of the framework, or a term of one of its action functionals, that distinguishes $J$ from $-J$ relative to the Fock module's $I_7$ and is fixed by the descent's kinematics rather than chosen by a solution: for example a proof that the pairing on the Fock module, the completion or the frozen point's data carry a preferred sign of $J$. Such a result would make the orientation bit kinematic or dynamically fixed. No observation tests the premise directly; it is a modelling choice about where the bit lives.
dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum.technical:
The descent's Witt flag can be described as a choice of orthogonal complex structure $J$ on the six-dimensional conformal ambient: the flag is the $+I_7$ eigenspace of $J$, and the conjugate flag, in the other family, is the $+I_7$ eigenspace of $-J$, with $I_7$ the scalar unit of the complexification, the central pseudoscalar of $\Cl(3,4)$. The orientation bit is then the sign of $J$ relative to the unit $I_7$ of the Fock module on which the modes act.

The premise is that this sign belongs to each solution, planted once by the descent, and is not part of the kinematic structure of the theory. Two configurations differing only in that sign are kinematically isomorphic and are configurations of the same theory. CPT conjugation, which acts antilinearly and exchanges the two signs, then carries every solution to a solution of the same theory with the opposite bit, so the bit is initial data. This is what the seventeenth refutation and its two restatements in the one-relation paper need; if the sign were kinematic, each orientation would define its own theory, the bit would be fixed within each, and their conclusion would fail. The premise would be refuted by a structure or law of the framework that singles out one sign of $J$ from the kinematics alone. It is a modelling choice, not tested by any observation directly.
dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum.lay: The framework's origin event makes one yes-or-no choice, which fixes both which of matter and antimatter is which and the direction of time. This assumption says where that choice lives: it is a fact about our particular universe, set when the universe began, not a built-in feature of the theory's laws or structure. A different universe obeying the same laws could have made the opposite choice. Several results, including the claim that the choice is a starting condition rather than a setting of the laws, rest on this assumption. It would be shown wrong if some part of the theory's fixed structure were found to prefer one answer.

No tower is diluted away or into prominence relative to this one.
dark-matter.projection-every-towers-cont.technical:
Read Premise P1 as the sourcing rule: a tower contributes to the one four-dimensional metric its energy per unit of shared three-volume, its content taken homogeneous along every direction it has. Suppose any extra directions either co-expand with the scale factor $a$ or are static, and a missing shared direction (in the three-dimensional towers) is filled by a comoving family of sheets, one per unit comoving length. Then the projected density of non-relativistic matter dilutes as $a^{-3}$ and that of radiation as $a^{-4}$, exactly as in this tower.

In the co-expanding case the density per $D$-volume goes as $a^{-D}$ for matter and $a^{-(D+1)}$ for radiation, and integrating over $e = D - 3$ extra directions of length proportional to $a$ restores $a^{e}$. A single sheet of fixed thickness would instead give $a^{-2}$ and $a^{-3}$, violating the rule's homogeneity clause. No tower is diluted away or into prominence relative to this one.
dark-matter.projection-every-towers-cont.lay: Hidden sectors with more or fewer dimensions than ours might thin out at a different rate as the universe expands, which would make them fade away or come to dominate. This result shows that, under the paper's rule for how such sectors feed gravity (its reading of Premise P1, one shared metric), provided any extra directions either grow with ours or stay fixed in size, and with a sector that lacks one of our directions counted as a family of evenly spaced sheets, their matter and radiation thin out exactly as ours do. Their share relative to ordinary matter therefore stays fixed over cosmic time.

proofs.main:
Let the tower have $D$ spatial directions, $D - 3 = e \geq 0$ of them extra. Co-expanding case: number density per unit $D$-volume scales as $a^{-D}$, and a massless quantum's energy as $a^{-1}$, so the densities per $D$-volume are $a^{-D}$ (matter) and $a^{-(D+1)}$ (radiation); the extra directions have length proportional to $a$, so integrating over them multiplies by $a^{e}$, giving $a^{-3}$ and $a^{-4}$. Static case: the extra directions have fixed length, number density per $D$-volume scales as $a^{-3}$, a massless quantum with no momentum along the static directions redshifts as $a^{-1}$, and integration over the fixed length changes no power: $a^{-3}$ and $a^{-4}$ again (a quantum with momentum along a static direction keeps that momentum and behaves as a massive four-dimensional mode, hence as matter).

For $e < 0$, the three-dimensional towers, the missing shared direction is filled as the hypothesis states, by a comoving family of sheets: the density per unit two-volume within a sheet scales as $a^{-2}$ (matter) or $a^{-3}$ (radiation), and the number of sheets per unit proper length along the missing direction as $a^{-1}$, giving $a^{-3}$ and $a^{-4}$.

The other reading, a single sheet of fixed proper thickness, violates the homogeneity clause of the rule (\claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}, read as the sourcing rule) and would give $a^{-2}$ and $a^{-3}$, under which the three-dimensional towers would grow relative to everything else; it is named because two of the four odd towers are exactly these. The exponent arithmetic is script-checked as a function of the rule (expanding directions, static extra directions, sheet families) for $D = 2, 3, 4$.

dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-dir.formal:
In the sourcing rule, a tower's matter counts through exactly one cell radius of each direction its neighbour lacks, on one side: a five-dimensional tower's matter through one radius of its extra direction, and a three-dimensional tower's sheets stacked one radius apart along the direction it lacks. the section “The thickness: a contact mechanism” gives a mechanism that returns this value and costs it.

\emph{The unit.} The cell radius of the premise is each tower's own cell radius, the Wigner-Seitz radius of that tower's own filling (the convention of the thickness $c\,d_{b}$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}). Under R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}) every tower has the same cell radius, so R2 also supplies R3's unit: it enters the total twice, as a number density and as this unit, and stays a premise of the total. The other reading, in which the thickness is one fixed length common to all towers and independent of their filling, is not adopted; the reduction of R1 and R2 to equal mass per unit ball (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r2-and-d-only-as-mass-per-unit-ball}) holds only in that reading.

Within the sourcing rule, a tower's matter counts through exactly one cell radius of each direction its neighbour lacks, on one side: a five-dimensional tower's matter through one radius of its extra direction, and a three-dimensional tower's sheets stacked one radius apart along the direction it lacks. A contact mechanism returns this value, at a stated cost, without deriving it.

The unit is each tower's own cell radius. Under R2 that radius is common to all towers, so R2 also supplies R3's unit and stays a premise of the total. dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem.formal:
The cosmic microwave background caps extra relativistic energy at $\Delta\Neff \lesssim 0.3$ \cite{Planck2018}, and one massless photon-like species (two polarisations) at the visible temperature contributes $\Delta\Neff = (8/7)(11/4)^{4/3} \approx 4.4$, so five democratically filled sectors with such photons would contribute of order twenty. The audit proceeds tower by tower, at two levels fixed by Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can} and Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries}: the \emph{ground} level, where the type decides whether the tower's spinors carry an intrinsic $U(1)$ (exactly at the complex member of each odd pair, $r = 3, 7$ in the paper's convention), and the \emph{rung} level, where every flagged tower carries abelian charges from its ladder pairs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The mirror tower, $r = 2$.)} Open, by theorem: the mirror's derived content is a copy of ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so it has a massless mirror photon and three light mirror neutrinos. The ground level is closed for the real member of the pair $\{2, 6\}$ (intrinsic group $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$, Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(i); which member depends on the labelling convention, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}) and irrelevant, since the content is not at that level. This is the mirror-matter situation of the literature, costed in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}.
\item \emph{(The three-dimensional towers, $r = 1, 7$.)} Closed at both levels: vector-like (no chirality in odd dimension), so Dirac masses are unforbidden and generic; with no massless charged matter left, each compact $U(1)$ in three dimensions, the intrinsic one of the complex member of $\{1, 7\}$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii)) and the rung-level ones of both, leaves no massless photon. The paper states that every such $U(1)$ confines by monopoles \cite{Polyakov1977}; with the half-integral bare Chern-Simons level that the parity anomaly forces (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.anomalies}(i)), that holds in the confining phase (C) only, and in phase (T) the photon is instead topologically massive (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases}); both phases close the channel. The non-abelian factors confine.
\item \emph{(The five-dimensional towers, $r = 3, 5$.)} Open at both levels: the complex member of the pair $\{3, 5\}$ carries an intrinsic $U(1)$ by theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii); which member depends on the convention), both carry rung-level ones, no Polyakov mechanism exists in five dimensions, and by Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} a surviving photon dilutes as $a^{-4}$, exactly as ours.
\item \emph{(The Goldstone exposure.)} Confining dark sectors with chiral breaking could leave massless dark pions. The framework supplies its own gap: any tower's accidental global symmetries are broken by its own tower's higher rungs (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), so the Goldstones are pseudo-Goldstones with masses of order $\Lambda_{\mathrm{conf}}^{2}/M_{\mathrm{rung}}$, the existence input a theorem and the mass estimate dimensional analysis.
\end{enumerate}
Conclusion: the three-dimensional towers are closed by theorem plus Polyakov confinement or, in phase (T), topological mass; the mirror tower is open by theorem, with a known relativistic content, and closes only if it is cold, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$; that is an exception at P2's version-1 reach, P2 as scoped leaving $\xi$ free, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}, and the cold mirror then needing a non-equilibrium descent, Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}); the five-dimensional towers are open with a content this paper does not derive. By the section “Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows” (proved given the imported rate) every dark tower's temperature is bounded below by gravitational heating at a few parts in ten thousand of the visible temperature at the top of the ceiling range, and above by whatever energy the descent deposited, which the $\Neff$ cap limits to $0.448$ for the mirror and the paper's hot-deposit estimate puts near $4 \times 10^{-3}$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}); across that interval both the mirror's channel and the five-dimensional towers' close by eight orders or more (twelve at the floor; the one case below eight is a nine-vector tower at the hot end, at $7.4$). $\Delta\Neff \approx 0$ is therefore a conditional stance, conditional on the open channels closing by one of the routes of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs} and on the deposit being no hotter than the estimate; so registered, and stated with that cost.

On self-interaction: in the three-dimensional towers it is at composite strength if their matter is the confined charged matter the closure leaves, which the series does not establish (the section “The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy”); in the five-dimensional ones it is undetermined; and for the mirror the composite figure is the wrong one, since mirror matter recombines at a visible temperature of order a keV (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}) and enters structure formation as neutral mirror atoms, with an elastic cross-section per mass of order $2 \times 10^{8}$ (hydrogen) or $5 \times 10^{7}$ (helium) $\mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$, and as a plasma once ionised inside a halo: collisional and dissipative like our gas, tested by the collisional-fraction and dark-disk bounds of refutation item 6. The rung-breaking scale of channel (4) is valued in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success}.
dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem.technical:
The microwave background caps extra relativistic energy at $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} \lesssim 0.3$, while one two-polarisation photon-like species at the visible temperature contributes $\frac{8}{7}\left(\frac{11}{4}\right)^{4/3} \approx 4.4$. The audit runs tower by tower at the ground level, where an intrinsic $U(1)$ sits exactly at the complex member of each odd pair, and at the rung level, where every flagged tower carries abelian ladder charges. The mirror tower is open by theorem, its content copying ours; the three-dimensional towers are closed at both levels, since Dirac masses are unforbidden and each compact $U(1)$ then either confines by Polyakov's monopole mechanism or, in the topologically massive phase that the forced half-integral Chern-Simons level allows, has a gapped photon (the T14c note, Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases}, which corrects the paper's "every compact $U(1)$ confines" to phase (C)); the five-dimensional towers are open, a surviving photon diluting as $a^{-4}$; and any dark Goldstones are lifted by higher rungs to masses of order $\Lambda_{\mathrm{conf}}^{2}/M_{\mathrm{rung}}$, the rung scale being the ceiling proposition's, valued under Hypothesis (U).

Every dark tower's temperature lies between the gravitational heating floor, a few parts in ten thousand of ours at the top of the ceiling range, and the deposit, estimated near $4 \times 10^{-3}$; across that interval the open channels close by eight orders or more. So $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 0$ is a conditional stance, conditional on the open channels closing by one of the listed routes and on the deposit being no hotter than the estimate. Caveat (T14c): a mirror that cold is an unstated exception to indifference, which applied with the copy theorem's reach gives $\xi = 1$ and $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} = 7.45$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2}). That is an exception to indifference at its version-1 reach; indifference as scoped (labels, not states) leaves $\xi$ free (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}), and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}).
dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem.lay: Each hidden sector could carry its own kind of light, and observations rule out much extra light in the early universe. This audit checks every sector: the three-dimensional ones lose their light either through a known confinement effect or, as a later note (T14c) shows for one of their two possible phases, because the force carrier gains a mass, while the mirror and five-dimensional ones could keep theirs. Any leftover massless particles in the confining sectors pick up small masses from those sectors' higher rungs, at a scale set under Hypothesis (U). The open sectors would still be harmless if they started out no hotter than the framework's estimate and their light is removed by one of the listed routes, for instance by their being cold enough; so the stance of no detectable extra radiation holds only under those conditions. The same later note points out that a cold mirror is an unstated exception to the paper's indifference principle. As the principle is now scoped, it applies to labels such as charges and not to temperatures, so it leaves the mirror's temperature free; a cold mirror then needs the descent to have left the towers out of equilibrium.

dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-nee.formal:
Let a pressureless component respond to the gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; the perturbed FLRW field in the conformal Newtonian gauge of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-linear-momentum-equation-traceless-field}, potentials $\psi$, $\phi$) at a fraction $g$ of the full strength, $\theta' = -\mathcal{H}\theta + g\,k^{2}\psi$. Then (i) it carries the anisotropic stress $\sigma = (1 - g)\psi$, and no other value; (ii) that stress enters the field equations, so that with the other components' stresses $\Sigma$,
\[
\psi \;=\; \frac{\phi - 12\pi G a^{2}\Sigma/k^{2}}{1 + 12\pi G a^{2}\rho\,(1 - g)/k^{2}} .
\]
For a three-dimensional tower whose sheets are held fixed, $g = \sin^{2}\theta$ for a wavevector at angle $\theta$ to the missing direction (script: $k_{\perp}^{2}/k^{2}$), $\tfrac{2}{3}$ averaged over orientations, and the stress of (i) is that of a medium holding the sheets in place. The series supplies no such medium: nothing in Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} or in the towers' content gives the sheet family a rigidity along its normal, and the sourcing rule couples the sheets' matter to the one gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ like any other. Hence, on the series as written, the sheets are displaced along their normal by the potential gradient, $g = 1$, and the three-dimensional towers respond to gravity in full at linear order.
dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-nee.technical:
Let a pressureless component respond to the gravitational field at a fraction $g$ of full strength, $\theta' = -\mathcal{H}\theta + g\,k^{2}\psi$. By the linear momentum equation it then carries the anisotropic stress $\sigma = (1 - g)\psi$ and no other value, and that stress enters the traceless field equation, giving $\psi = (\phi - 12\pi G a^{2}\Sigma/k^{2})/(1 + 12\pi G a^{2}\rho(1 - g)/k^{2})$.

For a three-dimensional tower whose sheets are held fixed, $g = \sin^{2}\theta$ at angle $\theta$ to the missing direction, $\frac{2}{3}$ on average, and the stress is that of a medium holding the sheets in place. The series supplies no such medium, so on the series as written the sheets are displaced along their normal by the potential gradient, $g = 1$, and the three-dimensional towers respond to gravity in full at linear order.
dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-nee.lay: Matter in a sector with fewer dimensions than ours might be expected to feel only part of gravity's pull. This result shows that a reduced response would need something physically holding that matter in place, and nothing in the framework does so. So, on the theory as it stands, the matter moves freely and responds to gravity in full, like ordinary dark matter, at least for small disturbances (at linear order).

dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-t.formal:
By exact superselection the towers interact only through the shared metric (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), so after the descent a dark tower can be heated only gravitationally; what the descent itself deposited in it (its charge, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, with whatever energy the deposit carried) is a datum, not a computation. Let the descent reheat this tower to $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ and let tower $r$, with $g_{d}$ light degrees of freedom that thermalise among themselves, be heated by graviton-mediated production from the visible plasma at rate per volume $\Gamma = c\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$, with $c$ the sum of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}'s per-species coefficients over the tower's light content. Then the produced comoving yield is
\[
Y \;=\; \frac{c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}}{3\,\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3}}, \qquad \kappa_{s} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi^{2}g_{*}}{90}}\;\frac{2\pi^{2}}{45}\,g_{s} \;=\; 145.3 \ \text{at } g_{*} = g_{s} = 100,
\]
its energy fraction at production is $4Y$, and the temperature ratio it alone would give is
\[
\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} \;=\; \Big(4Y\,\frac{g_{*}}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4} \;=\; 9.6 \times 10^{-4}\; c^{1/4}\Big(\frac{16}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4}\Big(\frac{T_{\mathrm{desc}}}{6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{GeV}}\Big)^{3/4}
\]
for $g_{*} = g_{s} = 100$ at the reheating. This is a floor: the tower's bath cannot be colder, and it is hotter by whatever energy the deposit carried. The ratio thereafter evolves through the two sectors' separate entropy conservation, by
\[
\left(\frac{g_{d}^{\mathrm{seed}}}{g_{d}}\right)^{1/3}\left(\frac{g_{s}}{g_{s}^{\mathrm{seed}}}\right)^{1/3}
\]
at any later epoch. Two inputs are not fixed by the formula: $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$, the ceiling of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} or below it, so that across that range the floor spans a factor $(3.5 \times 10^{11}/6 \times 10^{14})^{3/4}$, about $4 \times 10^{-3}$ ($3.75 \times 10^{-3}$), the body quoting the top and saying so; and the deposit's energy, which sets the actual ratio above the floor.
dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-t.technical:
Since superselection leaves the shared metric as the only channel, a dark tower can be heated after the descent only gravitationally. If the descent reheats this tower to $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ and tower $r$, with $g_{d}$ light degrees of freedom that thermalise among themselves, is heated by graviton-mediated production at rate $\Gamma = c\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$, the comoving yield is $Y = c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}/(3\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3})$ with $\kappa_{s} = 145.3$ at $g_{*} = g_{s} = 100$. The temperature ratio this alone gives is
$\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} = (4Y g_{*}/g_{d})^{1/4} = 9.6 \times 10^{-4}\,c^{1/4}(16/g_{d})^{1/4}(T_{\mathrm{desc}}/6 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV})^{3/4}$.

This is a floor: the tower is hotter by whatever energy the descent deposited. Thereafter the ratio evolves through the two sectors' separate entropy conservation, and across the range of reheating temperatures up to the ceiling the floor spans a factor of about $4 \times 10^{-3}$. The result is proved given the imported rate and the standard thermal history.
dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-t.lay: Even if the hidden sectors started completely cold, the hot ordinary matter of the early universe would warm them slightly through gravity, the only contact left between the sectors. Taking the standard rate for this gravitational production, and assuming each hidden sector's light particles share their heat among themselves, this result calculates that minimum warmth: about a thousandth of our temperature or less, depending on how hot the early universe became. The real temperature could be higher if the universe's birth heated the hidden sectors directly.

proofs.main:
With $dt = -dT/(HT)$,
\[
H \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{\pi^{2}g_{*}}{90}}\;\frac{T^{2}}{M_{P}}, \qquad s \;=\; \frac{2\pi^{2}}{45}\,g_{s}T^{3},
\]
in the reduced-mass convention the rate is quoted in (the familiar $1.66\sqrt{g_{*}}\,T^{2}/M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ with the non-reduced $M_{\mathrm{Pl}} = 1.22 \times 10^{19}$ GeV is the same rate, $1.66 = \sqrt{8\pi}\sqrt{\pi^{2}/90}$), the Boltzmann equation $\dot{n} + 3Hn = \Gamma$, gravitational production being the only source (by \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), for the comoving yield $Y = n/s$ reads
\[
\frac{dY}{dT} \;=\; -\frac{\Gamma}{HTs} \;=\; -\frac{c\,T^{2}}{\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3}},
\]

dark-matter.single-ideal-at-residues-zer.formal:
\emph{Premise (SI), the single-ideal clause.} At the reversal-fixed residues $0$ and $4$ a constituent lies in one chiral spinor ideal, and its mass is read through the reversion pairing on that ideal (the pairing reading of mass), not through the total momentum of Premise \claimref{dark-tower-matter.h1-momentum} (the momentum reading). The reversion pairing on one ideal vanishes identically exactly at these residues (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.reversion-pairing-vanishes-residues-zero-four}), so under the premise the towers of residues $0$ and $4$ hold no massive matter and do not enter the dark-to-baryon count.

\emph{Where it comes from.} This is clause (vi) of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}, a costed clause of the constituent definition, registered here as a premise in that clause's words. It was chosen knowing that the unit-ball fit needs it: the closed form $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi)$ sums over the mirror and the four odd towers only.

\emph{What it costs.} With residue $4$ populated the ratio is about $6.16$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}), and with both chiral ideals admitted at residues $0$ and $4$ about $8.254$, against the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$.

\emph{Support, and its limits.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.invariant-forms-on-spinor-ideal-factor-through-reversion} every spin-invariant bilinear form on a single spinor ideal is a linear functional of the reversion pairing, so at these residues no other pairing could carry a mass term: the premise chooses between the pairing reading and the momentum reading, not among pairings. In the lowest-causal window a single ideal is also what anomaly freedom gives at $(1,1)$, and at $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$ under the reading (G6) that a tower's own gauge fields live on its full six-dimensional space (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residues-zero-four-real-chirality-anomaly}); (G6) is recorded as a general reading and was itself chosen knowing that the fit needs residue $4$ empty. Neither supplies the premise: the series does not derive the pairing reading at these residues.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if the series' own structure gives matter at residue $0$ or $4$ a mass (the momentum reading there, or a second ideal), in which case the closed form's total moves to the values above; it becomes a theorem if the pairing reading is derived.

dark-matter.sourcing-rule-forced-not-cho.formal: (i) The field equations of a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), Einstein's equations for its derived metric, $\mathcal{G}(a) = -8\pi G\, T(a)$ in the store's sign (in components $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G\,T_{\mu\nu}$), are sourced by a local energy density and never by a total; the only covariant four-dimensional stress-energy map obtainable from matter homogeneous along a direction the metric does not see is its integral over that direction, $\rho_{4} = \rho_{5}L$, which is Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} read from the field equations. (ii) It passes the three standard tests. Continuity for dust in a product metric $a(t)^{2}dx^{2} + b(t)^{2}dy^{2}$ (the derived metric of the diagonal field $\hb^{-1}(e_x) = a\,e_x$, $\hb^{-1}(e_y) = b\,e_y$ on flat $\R^{1,4}$, the $d$-dimensional clause of the definition) gives $\rho_{5} \propto 1/(a^{3}b)$, so with $L \propto b$ the projected density $\rho_{5}L$ dilutes as $a^{-3}$ for a co-expanding and a static fifth direction alike, as the lemma states. Kaluza-Klein reduction over a metric fifth direction of size $L$ gives $G_{4} = G_{5}/L$ with $\rho_{4} = \rho_{5}L$, so $G_{4}\rho_{4} = G_{5}\rho_{5}$ is independent of $L$ for the bulk tower and the share $\rho_{5}L/\rho_{\mathrm{us}}$ is the same however Newton's constant is defined. And the projected stress-energy of five-dimensional dust comoving with our slice is four-dimensional dust, a quantum with momentum along the fifth direction appearing as a heavier particle at rest, by $Q(p) = m^{2} + p_{5}^{2}$ for its four-momentum $p$.

dark-matter.status-rule.formal:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The relation was found by solving the relation displayed with \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall} for the observed value, not predicted.
\item[(ii)] Among all expressions $1 + 2a + 2b$ with $a$ and $b$ ratios of the eight measures $V_{2}$ to $V_{5}$ and $|\Sph^{1}|$ to $|\Sph^{4}|$ ($3136$ expressions), $54$ lie within one standard deviation of $5.364$, taking $14$ distinct values, and $85$ within two; neighbouring targets give comparable counts ($43$ at $5.322$, $33$ at $5.24$). The closed form is one of fourteen equally simple candidates in the error bar (script). The mechanism of the section “The thickness: a contact mechanism” adds a discrete look-elsewhere of the same kind: of the clause combinations the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3} lists, only the chosen one reaches the observed value, and the clauses were chosen with it known.
\item[(iii)] The ball and sphere forms of Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not} are one relation. The exchanged assignment and the clock reflection give the same total as the other root of $T(c) = 5.364$, with the three- and five-dimensional shares exchanged; none of them is independent evidence for the total, and the exchanged assignment is not physically consistent and differs from the rule in composition (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not}).
\item[(iv)] The relation rests on R1, R2 and R3, none supplied by the series; the contact mechanism explains R3's value and does not derive it, and the de Sitter reading, which replaces R2 by democracy and fixes the unit, gives thickness $\tfrac{3\pi}{8}$ or $\tfrac{\pi}{4}$ and totals of $5.000$, $5.667$ or $4.333$, none within four standard deviations.
\item[(v)] The comparison is with one Planck column; the others give $5.322$ to $5.376$, and the ACT DR6 combination gives about $5.22$, below the floor of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(ii). If that lower value holds, no thickness in the family fits.
\item[(vi)] The relation needs residues $0$ and $4$ empty: with residue $4$ populated the ratio is about $6.16$ (\claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}), and with both chiral ideals admitted at residues $0$ and $4$ the total is about $8.254$. With one spinor ideal the emptiness of residues $0$ and $4$ is equivalent to the pairing reading of mass in dimensions $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, where the reversion pairing on one ideal vanishes identically (\claimref{synthesis.reversion-pairing-vanishes-residues-zero-four}); in the lowest-causal window it is also what anomaly freedom of a single ideal gives at $(1,1)$, and at $(1,5)$, $(5,1)$ under the reading (G6) that a tower's own gauge fields live on its full six-dimensional space and act on its constituents (\claimref{synthesis.residues-zero-four-real-chirality-anomaly}). The series adopts the single chiral ideal at residues $0$ and $4$ with the pairing reading of mass as a costed clause of the constituent definition, chosen knowing that the unit-ball fit needs it, and records (G6) as the general reading of where a tower's own gauge fields live, not as a postulate. The clause is part of what the relation rests on, beside R1 to R3. \emph{Note.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.invariant-forms-on-spinor-ideal-factor-through-reversion}, every spin-invariant bilinear form on a single spinor ideal is a linear functional of the reversion pairing, so at residues $0$ and $4$ no other pairing exists that could carry a mass term: the clause chooses between the pairing reading and the momentum reading of mass, not among pairings. It remains a clause chosen with the fit known. \emph{Note (register, 2026-11-10).} The clause is now a registered premise, \claimref{dark-matter.single-ideal-at-residues-zero-and-four}, and so is the population of the odd towers, \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated}, which is inferred from the number the relation fits; the stored statements of the total assume both.
\item[(vii)] \emph{(Note, 2026-11-10: the two readings are alternatives.)} The de Sitter reading of (iv) and the unit-ball reading cannot be held together: Premise D with R1 and R2 forces one quantum per de Sitter ball (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass}, note; argued). D is the premise of the de Sitter reading only and is not counted with R1 to R3. R3's unit is each tower's own cell radius, so R2 also supplies the one length of the relation.
\end{enumerate}
The relation is fitted: a closed form, a consistent mechanism inside the sourcing rule, and one length, fixed by R3 at one cell radius and returned by a contact mechanism on four clauses of its own. Its tier is observation level on R1 to R3 and on the costed clause (vi), and it supersedes nothing in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}: the mirror's share stays derived and the odd towers' shares stay underived, now with one candidate value each and its price stated.

So it is recorded as a fitted relation at observation level, not a prediction.
