dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-.formal:
Under the classification of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, with $\epsilon$ initial data of the descent, inherited rather than generated, and the number $N$ common to the towers under P1 ($N = M_{P}/H$, which fixes a count of registered units, about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, without being it: Observation \claimref{standard-model.largeness-number-universes-boundary-modes}; the light rays number $2\pi N^{2}/(c\ln 2)$ for $c$ boundary-mode arrays per light ray (\claimref{synthesis.the-residue-requires-two-arrays-per-unit-on-average-and-fixes-no-grouping}(iii)), and $c$ depends on the tower's content, a five-dimensional field counting one array set per Kaluza-Klein level, equivalently one per resolution cell of the extra direction, so the common count is that of registered units, not of light rays or of boundary modes; the argument uses only that $N$ is common):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Charge.)} The asymmetry stored in an oriented tower is the charge $Q = \epsilon N$, fixed by the descent's data and independent of the tower's temperature; it is not a thermal number $n - \bar{n} \propto g\,\mu T^{2}$. So the mirror share $f_{2} = 1$ holds at any mirror temperature: a cold mirror carries the same baryon charge as this tower in the same number of baryons, with negligible mirror radiation.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Origin.)} The charge is the descent's and cannot be produced afterwards: the one channel superselection leaves open, gravitational production from the visible plasma (the section “Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows”), yields $1.8$ to $2.7 \times 10^{-15}$ mirror quanta per unit entropy at the ceiling reheating against the $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy that our baryon number requires, more than four orders too few even counting every produced quantum as a baryon. Black holes are a sink for $Q$, not a source (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(iv), under P5): a mass-preserving rearrangement that erodes each tower's free baryon count and moves no share.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Temperature.)} Taken as a free datum of the descent, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$, which the record excludes; that is an exception at P2's version-1 reach, P2 as scoped leaving $\xi$ free, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}, and the cold mirror then needing a non-equilibrium descent, Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}), the mirror's temperature ratio $\xi = T'/T$ is bounded below by the gravitational floor, $\xi$ between $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ at the ceiling reheating (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii), the bracket the species-counting ambiguity; four parts in a thousand of this at the bottom of the ceiling range), and above by the $\Neff$ cap at $0.448$; a deposit of each unit of baryon number with energy of order the reheating temperature puts it at $\xi \approx 4 \times 10^{-3}$. The paper carries the whole interval. With $\eta = n_{B}/n_{\gamma} = 6.1 \times 10^{-10}$ here and equal baryon number,
\[
\eta' \;=\; \frac{\eta}{\xi^{3}}
\]
runs from $19$ to $26$ at the floor down to about $0.008$ at the hot deposit, crossing one at $\xi = \eta^{1/3} = 8.5 \times 10^{-4}$: at least $10^{7}$ times ours throughout, with $\Delta\Neff$ eight orders or more below the cap.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The two readings.)} The thermal reading would give $f_{2} \sim \xi_{2}^{3}$ instead, at most $0.090$ under the $\Neff$ cap ($0.448^{3}$) and $10^{-7}$ or less anywhere between the floor and the hot deposit; the two readings cannot both hold, and the paper's own classification decides for the charge.
\end{enumerate}
Level: the classification is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-trichotomy-descents-data}'s; the incompatibility is arithmetic. The mirror's nucleosynthesis, which is not a copy of ours and on which the burning branch of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) and the composition caveat of refutation item 6 rest, follows the proof, at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the proof's thermal up-down ratio at freeze-out fails at the floor, where the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons; it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$, an interval containing the hot-deposit estimate (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}). dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exa.formal:
By Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} and the acoustic programme (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupling}, the series' acoustic no-go, at its mixed level: within the s-wave current algebra, with the sphere step conditional on the Indifference premise and the thermal state on premise (Q)), matter in a neighbouring tower gravitates on this metric and does nothing else observable at first order: dark by structural necessity, at that level. Stability is then not suppressed but exact, in three steps, the first of which is proved given the sector decomposition of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The tower charge $r$ is superselected in the frozen phase: frozen-phase operators are built from the one soldering and preserve its signature (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}), so portal matrix elements between residues vanish identically away from walls.
\item The walls are unreachable: singular loci ascend within-tower, since the completion adjoins exactly $(1,1)$ and preserves the residue (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), while the mod-8 shadow walls that separate residues are displaced successively away from the physical region, by the wall-sequence theorem of the sheaf paper \cite[\S5]{ButlerT4}, under that theorem's hypotheses (a compact base and good couplings at every stage), carried here.
\item Therefore the only inter-tower event in the universe's history is the descent itself: the towers communicated once, at the origin, and have been in absolute mutual darkness but for weight ever since. The singular locus of a black hole is an inter-tower event for energy, as it already was for weight, and never for the residue of any quantum: energy crosses at the wall, the residue does not (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}).
\end{enumerate}
One residue is flagged at observation level: dark-tower matter crossing this tower's horizons carries superselected charge the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold, which routes it into the tower-wise run of the singularity paper's ascend-then-descend structure \cite{ButlerT5}; the computation of that routing, with the mass range of its Gauss-law clause, is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

Stability is then exact, in three steps: (1) given the sector decomposition, frozen-phase operators are built from one soldering and preserve its signature, so portal matrix elements between residues vanish away from walls and the tower charge $r$ is superselected; (2) the walls are unreachable, since singular loci ascend within a tower preserving the residue and the mod-$8$ shadow walls are displaced successively away from the physical region, under the wall-sequence theorem's hypotheses of a compact base and good couplings; (3) hence the only inter-tower event is the descent itself.

A black hole's singular locus is inter-tower for energy, as it already was for weight, but never for the residue of any quantum. Dark-tower matter crossing our horizons carries superselected charge that the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold, a residue flagged at observation level.

Given how the sectors are split, and provided the sheaf paper's conditions for its walls hold (a compact base and well-behaved couplings), this result argues that no process can change a particle's tower, so dark matter of this kind never decays; energy can still pass between the towers through gravity. dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-.formal:
If the fifth direction carried the metric, gravity would fall as the inverse cube on scales below its extent $L$. The two extents the series has are the baryon spacing and the de Sitter radius,
\[
d_{b} \;=\; \left(\frac{3}{4\pi n_{b}}\right)^{1/3} \;\approx\; 0.98\ \mathrm{m}, \qquad \ell \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{3}{\Lambda}} \;\approx\; 10^{26}\ \mathrm{m},
\]
with $n_{b} = 0.25\ \mathrm{m}^{-3}$ from $\Omega_{b}h^{2} = 0.02237$ (script: $d_{b}$ bracketed in $(0.95, 1.02)$ m). Both exceed the bound of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inverse-square-law-short-range} by more than four orders of magnitude. So the four-dimensional reading of P1 is forced by experiment, not chosen; the reductions of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-reductions}, which needed a metric fifth direction to be well posed, describe a setting that is itself excluded; and the thickness in R3 can never be measured or computed gravitationally, since gravity does not see the direction it lives in. Only the tower's own dynamics, its cell size, can set it, so R3 is correctly a statement counted in the tower's own cells; and for the projected density $\rho_{5}L$ to be finite the fifth direction must be compact or the matter localised within $L$ by those dynamics, which the series does not supply. That the count is one radius is R3; the contact mechanism of the section “The thickness: a contact mechanism” returns it, and gravity cannot. The comparison with $d_{b}$ takes today's baryon spacing as the extent, which assumes that the hidden direction co-expands with the shared ones. With R2 and R3 read as deposit clauses and a static hidden direction, the counted thickness today is the deposit-epoch cell radius, below $2.4 \times 10^{-10}$ m for any descent above $1$ MeV, more than $10^{5}$ times under the bound (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.unit-ball-clauses-hold-at-one-epoch-unless-hidden-direction-co-expands}(iv)); for that length the comparison above gives no exclusion, and the experimental argument rests on the co-expanding reading and on $\ell$.

\emph{Note (evaporation, argued).} Black holes reach where gravity does not. Under the interface premise a populated five-dimensional tower radiates through its Kaluza-Klein levels, whose number below a hole's temperature grows linearly with the extent $L_{f}$ of the fifth direction (\claimref{synthesis.five-dimensional-tower-kaluza-klein-channels-steepen-burst}(i)). If a massless five-dimensional species exists, an open fifth direction therefore makes every hole's emission infinite, so observed black-hole lifetimes exclude the branch above in which the direction is open and the matter is localised within $L$ by its dynamics, for any species free to move along the whole direction; the compact branch remains. And under the static deposit reading the extent is finite and small, and the break $E_{b} \propto 1/L_{f}$ of the burst's primary high-energy tail (\claimref{synthesis.five-dimensional-tower-kaluza-klein-channels-steepen-burst}(iii), (iv)) measures it, so the thickness, which gravity cannot see, is in principle observable through evaporation ($L_{f}$ is at least the counted thickness, and equal to it when the matter fills the fifth direction).

dark-matter.total-function-thickness.technical:
Let the five-dimensional towers' matter count through a length $c\,d_{b}$ of the extra direction and the three-dimensional towers' sheets be stacked $c\,d_{b}$ apart, assuming R1, R2 and the sourcing rule otherwise unchanged, with the mirror share one and, under P2, equal shares within each odd pair. Then $T(c) = \Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}/\Omega_{b} = 1 + \frac{8}{3c} + \frac{16c}{3\pi}$, which satisfies $T(c) = T(\pi/2c)$ and has a single minimum $T_{*} = 1 + 2\sqrt{128/9\pi} = 5.2554$ at $c_{*} = \sqrt{\pi/2}$, $1.7\sigma$ below the observed value.

$T(c) = 5.3643$ exactly at $c = 1$ and $c = \frac{\pi}{2}$, the two roots of one quadratic with product $\frac{\pi}{2}$. Against $5.364 \pm 0.065$ the allowed thicknesses are $c \in [0.943, 1.086]$ or $c \in [1.447, 1.667]$ at one standard deviation, and $[0.898, 1.750]$ at two; the three-dimensional fraction of dark matter is $8/(3c\,T(c))$, about $50\%$ at $c = 1$.

proofs.main:
Per unit of our three-volume (by Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}), with the common quantum mass of \claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum} and one quantum per unit ball of \claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}, the three densities are
\[
\rho_{5\mathrm{D}} = \frac{m\,c}{V_{4}\,d_{b}^{3}}, \qquad
\rho_{3\mathrm{D}} = \frac{m}{c\,V_{2}\,d_{b}^{3}}, \qquad
\rho_{\mathrm{us}} = \frac{m}{V_{3}\,d_{b}^{3}},
\]
so the shares are
\[
f_{3\mathrm{D}} = \frac{V_{3}}{c\,V_{2}} = \frac{4}{3c}, \qquad f_{5\mathrm{D}} = \frac{c\,V_{3}}{V_{4}} = \frac{8c}{3\pi},
\]
and the sum, with the mirror's share $1$ from Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent} and two towers of each odd dimension (populated by Premise \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated}, the towers of residues $0$ and $4$ adding nothing by Premise \claimref{dark-matter.single-ideal-at-residues-zero-and-four}), with equal shares within each odd pair (by \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}), is the relation displayed with \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}. (i) Substitute. (ii) $T$ is of the form $1 + \frac{A}{c} + Bc$ with $A = \frac{8}{3}$ and $B = \frac{16}{3\pi}$; by the arithmetic-geometric inequality
\[
\frac{A}{c} + Bc \;\geq\; 2\sqrt{AB}, \qquad \text{with equality at } c = \sqrt{\frac{A}{B}} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}} .
\]
(iii) $T(c) = T(1)$ is the quadratic
\[
Bc^{2} - \bigl(T(1) - 1\bigr)c + A = 0, \qquad c_{1}c_{2} = \frac{A}{B} = \frac{\pi}{2};
\]
$c = 1$ is a root by construction and $\frac{\pi}{2}$ is the other. (iv) and (v) are evaluation. The script checks (i) as an identity in $\pi$ for rational $c$, brackets $T_{\ast}$ and the window endpoints by rational bounds on $\pi$ and on the square root, and evaluates the fractions.

dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-c.formal:
The residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$ is invariant along every tower: the eight parallel towers are the eight residues, their parallelism derived rather than described. Call a signature $(p,q)$ \emph{causal} if $\min(p,q) = 1$: exactly one direction of the minority sign, the timelike one, whichever sign convention carries time. Labelling this world $(1,3)$, residue $6$, fixes the convention time $=$ plus, and the mirror residue $2$ reads $(3,1)$; under the opposite convention the two labels swap and the causal sort is unchanged, but every attribution of a Clifford type to a member of the reversal pair passes to the other member, since $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\mathbb{H})$ and $\Cl(3,1) \cong \Mat(4,\R)$ are not isomorphic. That attribution is fixed by a labelling convention Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} declares indexical, and is so read below. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Census; proved.)} Every residue contains causal signatures once the dimension is free: the lowest are $(1,1)$ at $r = 0$, $(2,1)$ at $r = 1$, $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, $(4,1)$ at $r = 3$, $(1,5)$ or $(5,1)$ at $r = 4$, $(1,4)$ at $r = 5$, $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, $(1,2)$ at $r = 7$. The residue alone therefore sorts nothing; a representative must be chosen.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The sort under P3; proved given the premise.)} Under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} the representatives are $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, this world; $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, a mirror Minkowski with real (Majorana-type) spinors; $(2,2)$ at $r = 0$, two times; $(4,0)$ or $(0,4)$ at $r = 4$, none; $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$ at $r = 1, 7$, three-dimensional; $(4,1)$ and $(1,4)$ at $r = 3, 5$, five-dimensional. Exactly two are sterile, $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ (a figure of the original), and they are the fixed points of the mirror map $r \mapsto -r$: under P3 the towers without a single time are the towers that are their own mirrors.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sensitivity; proved.)} The sterile set is a function of the window. With any dimension up to five allowed, only $r = 4$ is sterile ($(1,1)$ is a causal signature for $r = 0$); with dimensions three to six, only $r = 0$ ($(1,5)$ is one for $r = 4$); with the upper bound removed, nothing is ($(1,9)$ is one for $r = 0$ at ten); and the literal lowest-dimensional representative of every residue, with no lower bound, is definite for $r = 6$ itself, namely $(0,2)$: without a lower bound the criterion would sterilise this world.
\end{enumerate}
Six admit matter: this one and five dark. Which of the six the descent populated is a further question, answered for the mirror by P2 and for the odd towers only by the record (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). Structural level given P3; the two-time exclusion at $r = 0$ imports the standard instability of two-time dynamics, flagged, and the flag does not remove it (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}).
dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-c.technical:
The $(1,1)$ ascent adjoins one positive and one negative direction, so the residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$ is constant along every tower and the eight parallel towers are the eight residues. Call $(p,q)$ causal if $\min(p,q) = 1$. Since $(1,s)$ has residue $1 - s$, every residue contains causal signatures once the dimension is free, so the residue alone sorts nothing and a representative must be chosen. Under premise P3 (nearest-dimension representatives) the representatives are $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, $(2,2)$ at $r = 0$, $(4,0)$ or $(0,4)$ at $r = 4$, $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$ at $r = 1, 7$, and $(4,1)$ and $(1,4)$ at $r = 3, 5$. Exactly $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ are sterile, and they are the fixed points of the mirror map $r \mapsto -r$.

Which member of the reversal pair $\{6, 2\}$ is this world depends on the sign convention for time, and the convention matters for types because $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\HH)$ and $\Cl(3,1) \cong \Mat(4,\R)$ are not isomorphic; premise P2 declares the convention indexical. The sterile set is a function of the dimension window: other windows sterilise only $r = 4$, only $r = 0$, or nothing, and with no lower bound the criterion would sterilise this world's residue. Six towers admit matter, this one and five dark; the exclusion of $r = 0$ imports the standard instability of two-time dynamics.

dark-matter.two-reductions.formal:
In the setting of $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\; ds_{4}^{2}, \qquad \theta \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$, read in five-dimensional Gauge Theory Gravity (the $d$-dimensional clause of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}): the warped product $\ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\,ds_{4}^{2}$ is the derived metric of the gravitational field on flat $\R^{4,1}$, in the signature $(-,+,+,+,+)$ of $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\; ds_{4}^{2}, \qquad \theta \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$ (in the store's sign the derived metric is its negative), with $\hb^{-1}(e_\theta) = \ell\,e_\theta$ and $\hb^{-1}(a) = \cos\theta\,\hb_{4}^{-1}(a)$ on the four-dimensional directions, and the five-dimensional Einstein-Hilbert action is $\int \det(\hb)^{-1}\,\mathcal{R}\,d^{5}x$ (sign as in $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\; ds_{4}^{2}, \qquad \theta \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (Zero mode.) Integrating the five-dimensional Einstein-Hilbert and matter actions over $\theta$, the gravitational term, the bulk dust and the equatorial sheet acquire the factors
\[
\ell\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos^{2}\theta\,d\theta = \frac{\pi\ell}{2}, \qquad
\ell\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos^{4}\theta\,d\theta = \frac{3\pi\ell}{8}, \qquad 1,
\]
so $G_{4} = \frac{2G_{5}}{\pi\ell}$. Newton's constant cancels in the ratio, and the five-dimensional tower's effective thickness is
\[
L_{\mathrm{eff}} \;=\; \frac{3\pi}{8}\,\ell \;=\; \frac{V_{4}}{V_{3}}\,\ell .
\]
\item[(ii)] (Local projection.) For dust comoving with the slice, $T_{ab}n^{a}n^{b} = 0$ and $T = -\rho_{5}$, so the bulk term of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-induced-equations-hypersurface} contributes on the slice the energy density
\[
\frac{2\kappa_{5}^{2}}{3}\left(\rho_{5} - \frac{\rho_{5}}{4}\right) \;=\; \frac{\kappa_{5}^{2}\,\rho_{5}}{2} .
\]
With the $G_{4}$ of (i) this is an effective thickness $L_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\pi}{4}\,\ell$.
\item[(iii)] (The sheets.) A comoving family of three-dimensional sheets carrying total mass $M_{\mathrm{tot}}$ over our $\Sph^{4}$ of radius $\ell$, each at the three-dimensional tower's own density $\frac{M_{\mathrm{tot}}}{|\Sph^{3}|\,\ell^{3}}$, has spacing
\[
s \;=\; \frac{|\Sph^{4}|}{|\Sph^{3}|}\,\ell \;=\; \frac{4}{3}\,\ell
\]
along the polar arc.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, under D: (i) with (iii) gives every share $1$ and the total $5.000$; (ii) with (iii) gives $4.333$; (i) with sheets one radius apart gives $5.667$; (ii) with sheets one radius apart gives $5.000$ again (the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.two-reductions}). The rule's $L_{\mathrm{eff}} = \ell$ is produced by neither reduction. \emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The closed four-sphere of radius $\ell$ over which the sheet family of (iii) is counted is global and is not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region are in Gauge Theory Gravity, and that four-sphere is read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.
dark-matter.two-reductions.technical:
The fifth direction of a five-dimensional tower is promoted to a metric direction, writing $\dS_{5}$ of radius $\ell$ as the warped product $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\,ds_{4}^{2}$ with our world at the equator, in five-dimensional Gauge Theory Gravity the derived metric of a gravitational field on flat $\R^{4,1}$, in the signature $(-,+,+,+,+)$ of the warped product, and a four-dimensional Friedmann equation is extracted in two ways. Zero-mode integration over $\theta$ gives the gravitational, bulk and equatorial factors $\pi\ell/2$, $3\pi\ell/8$ and $1$, so $G_{4} = 2G_{5}/(\pi\ell)$ and the effective thickness is $L_{\mathrm{eff}} = \tfrac{3\pi}{8}\ell = \tfrac{V_{4}}{V_{3}}\ell$. Local projection with the imported induced-equation term gives the energy density $\kappa_{5}^{2}\rho_{5}/2$ for comoving dust, an effective thickness $\tfrac{\pi}{4}\ell$. A comoving family of three-dimensional sheets, each at that tower's own density, has spacing $s = \tfrac{4}{3}\ell$ along the polar arc. The integrals are Wallis's. The four-sphere over which the sheets are counted is closed, so that count is read beyond one flat chart, on several charts of flat spacetime glued by gauge transformations.

Under premise D (every populated tower carries the same total mass) the combinations give totals $5.000$ (zero mode with those sheets), $4.333$ (projection with those sheets), $5.667$ (zero mode, sheets one radius apart) and $5.000$ (projection, sheets one radius apart). Neither reduction produces the unit-ball rule's $L_{\mathrm{eff}} = \ell$. Both reductions need the fifth direction to carry the metric, a setting that short-range tests of Newton's law exclude (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity}); the numbers are computations in that excluded setting, kept for comparison.
dark-matter.two-reductions.lay: If the hidden fifth direction of a five-dimensional dark tower is treated as a real direction of space, there are two textbook ways to work out how its matter would look from our four-dimensional world. This result computes both, together with the spacing of the sheets of a three-dimensional tower. Assuming each tower carries the same total mass, the resulting dark-to-ordinary ratios lie between about 4.3 and 5.7, and neither method gives the thickness that the paper's unit-ball rule uses. Both methods need gravity to reach into the fifth direction, which laboratory tests rule out, so these are comparisons, not physical predictions.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric below is the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat $\R^{4,1}$, in the signature $(-,+,+,+,+)$ of $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\; ds_{4}^{2}, \qquad \theta \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$, and its index expressions are readings of $D$ and of the field strength through Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}.

The integrals are Wallis's. Foliating $\Sph^{n+1}$ by latitude $\phi$, the latitude sphere is an $\Sph^{n}$ of radius $\cos\phi$, so
\[
|\Sph^{n+1}| \;=\; |\Sph^{n}|\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos^{n}\phi\,d\phi, \qquad \int\cos^{n} \;=\; \frac{n-1}{n}\int\cos^{n-2}, \qquad \int\cos^{0} = \pi, \quad \int\cos^{1} = 2,
\]

dark-matter.two-roots-are-chord-arc-quar.formal: In the sphere form of the rule, represent the five-dimensional tower's spacetime by a sphere of radius $R$ with our spacetime as its equator. The region between the equator and one pole has extent $R$ along the polar axis (the chord) and $\tfrac{\pi R}{2}$ along the surface (the arc). With $R = d_{b}$: counting the tower's matter per unit chord over that region is the unit-ball rule, $c = 1$; counting it per unit arc is the exchanged assignment, $c = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$; and the two totals agree because Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(i) exchanges them, while their compositions differ (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not}). R2 selects the chord: its cells are unit balls of the tower's flat space, whose measure along the added direction is the radius. Between the equator and both poles the values are $c = 2$ and $c = \pi$, giving $5.729$ and $7.182$, both excluded.

dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower.technical:
For an irreducible real module of $\Cl(p,q)$, the commutant $D$ and the number of inequivalent irreducible modules depend only on the residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$, because $\Cl(p+1,q+1) \cong \Mat(2, \Cl(p,q))$ preserves both: $D = \R$ at $r = 0, 2$ (one module) and $r = 1$ (two); $D = \C$ at $r = 3, 7$ (one); $D = \HH$ at $r = 4, 6$ (one) and $r = 5$ (two). The intrinsic group is the unit group of $D$: $\Z_{2}$, $U(1)$ or $Sp(1)$.

For the P3 representatives, in the labelling convention in which this world is $(1,3)$, the mirror $r = 2$ and the fork $r = 0$ have real spinors with intrinsic group $\Z_{2}$, so no continuous charge commutes with their ground Clifford action; $r = 3$ and $r = 7$ have complex spinors and exactly one intrinsic abelian charge each; this world and $r = 4, 5$ are quaternionic, with $Sp(1)$ and no distinguished $U(1)$. At $r = 1, 5$ the two modules differ by the sign of the central volume element, which at $r = 3, 7$ acts as the complex unit. Under the opposite convention the attributions within each pair $\{r, -r\}$ swap. The intrinsic group bounds a tower's internal symmetry from below; it is not the whole of it.
dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower.lay: Each tower's basic algebra decides what kind of numbers its matter states naturally use: real numbers, complex numbers or quaternions. That choice depends only on the tower's label, and it fixes which continuous symmetries a tower carries before any further structure is added. For the representatives the paper uses, and in its labelling convention (the opposite convention swaps the two members of each mirror pair), the mirror tower comes out with real spinors and no built-in continuous charge, two of the odd towers with exactly one built-in charge each, and our own world with quaternionic spinors.

proofs.main:
$\Cl(p,q)$ is semisimple, so it is $\Mat(m, D)$ or $\Mat(m, D) \oplus \Mat(m, D)$, and the commutant of an irreducible module is $D$. The centre is $\R$ when $n = p + q$ is even and $\R[\omega]$ when $n$ is odd, $\omega = e_{1} \cdots e_{n}$ the volume element, with $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}(-1)^{q}$; so two components ($\omega^{2} = +1$) or a complex centre ($\omega^{2} = -1$) according to $n$ and $q$, which depend on $r$ as stated. For the division algebra, Lounesto's construction gives a primitive idempotent
\[
f \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{k}\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(1 + e_{T_{i}}\bigr)
\]
from a maximal set of $k$ commuting basis blades squaring to $+1$ generating a group of order $2^{k}$, and then $f\,\Cl(p,q)\,f \cong D$, of real dimension $1$, $2$ or $4$. Bott periodicity in the form $\Cl(p+1, q+1) \cong \Mat(2, \Cl(p,q))$ (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}) preserves $D$ and the component count, so both depend on the residue alone; the dependence within one period is the classical table (Cartan, Bott), recomputed here: the script builds every $\Cl(p,q)$ of dimension at most five in \texttt{GA.py}, computes the centre by exact linear algebra, finds a primitive idempotent by exhaustive search over blade sets and computes $\dim_{\R} f\,\Cl(p,q)\,f$ by exact rank, agreeing with the table on all twenty signatures and on the eight P3 representatives. The intrinsic group is the unit group of $D$: $\{\pm 1\}$, $U(1)$, $Sp(1)$. (i) to (iv) read off the table, in the labelling convention of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}; the two-sphere in (iii) is the set of imaginary unit quaternions.

The classical classification of real Clifford algebras is carried in the store by the imported external ingredients \claimref{rule2.imported-classification-centre-type-c-external}.

dark-matter.unit-ball-rule.formal:
Under R1 to R3, with the four odd towers populated (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated}) and residues $0$ and $4$ empty (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.single-ideal-at-residues-zero-and-four}), the share of a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions is $f = \tfrac{V_{3}}{V_{D}}$, and
\[
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; V_{3}\sum_{\text{dark }r}\frac{1}{V_{D_{r}}}
\;=\; \frac{V_{3}}{V_{3}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{4}}
\;=\; 1 + \frac{8}{3} + \frac{16}{3\pi} \;=\; \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \;=\; 5.36432\ldots
\]
against the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$. The agreement is built in, not predicted: the relation was found by solving for the observed value, and its clauses were chosen with it known, and the closed form is one of fourteen equally simple candidates within the error bar (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}).

\emph{What the total rests on.} On the stored dependence edges the past cone of this closed form holds these postulates of the dark-matter subject: R1, R2 and R3; P1 (\claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}), through the sourcing rule in which the shares are read (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}); P2 and P3, through the census of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}; and the two conditions registered as premises on 10 November 2026, the single-ideal clause \claimref{dark-matter.single-ideal-at-residues-zero-and-four} and the population of the odd towers \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated}. R2 enters twice, as the number density and as the unit of R3's thickness, which is each tower's own cell radius. The democracy premise (\claimref{dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass}) is not among them: it belongs to the de Sitter reading. The total remains a fit. The mirror's share of one is derived separately (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}), so the closed form fixes two shares, $\tfrac{4}{3}$ and $\tfrac{8}{3\pi}$, against one measured number, the remainder $4.36 \pm 0.07$. Chosen with that number known, by the store's own record: the relation was found by solving for the observed value (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(i)); the clauses of the contact mechanism that returns R3's value were chosen with it known (the same, (ii)); the single-ideal clause was chosen knowing that the fit needs it (the same, (vi)); and the population of the odd towers is inferred from the remainder itself (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). P1, P2 and P3 belong to the paper's earlier sections, written before the rule was proposed (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.setting-dark-matter-ratio-unit-ball}).
dark-matter.unit-ball-rule.technical:
Under premises R1 (equal mass per quantum), R2 (one quantum per unit ball of a tower's own space) and R3 (one cell per unshared direction), a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions has number density $1/V_{D}$ and so contributes a share $f = V_{3}/V_{D}$ of our matter per unit of our volume, with $V_{n}$ the volume of the unit $n$-ball. Summing over the five dark towers at their nearest-dimension representatives (the four odd ones taken as populated and residues $0$ and $4$ as empty, two conditions now registered as premises), the mirror with $D = 3$, two three-dimensional towers with $D = 2$ and two five-dimensional towers with $D = 4$, gives
$$\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} = 1 + \frac{8}{3} + \frac{16}{3\pi} = \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} = 5.36432\ldots,$$
against the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$. The agreement is a fit, not a prediction: the relation was found by solving for the observed value, its clauses chosen with it known, and it is one of fourteen equally simple values in the error bar (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}).

What the total rests on, on the stored edges: R1, R2 (twice: the density, and the unit of R3's thickness), R3, P1 through the sourcing rule, P2 and P3 through the census, the single-ideal clause and the population of the odd towers; not the democracy premise. It remains a fit: two shares, $4/3$ and $8/(3\pi)$, against one measured remainder, with the relation found by solving for the value, the contact clauses and the single-ideal clause chosen with it known, and the population of the odd towers inferred from the remainder itself.
dark-matter.unit-ball-rule.lay: This rule assigns every dark tower one particle of a common mass per unit-sized ball of its own space, and compares that density with ours. Towers with fewer or more spatial dimensions then contribute different amounts, fixed by the volumes of balls in two, three and four dimensions. Under its three premises, together with the assumptions that the four odd hidden sectors hold matter and that two further sectors hold none, the rule gives a dark-to-ordinary matter ratio of about 5.364, the observed value. The formula sets two shares against one measured number, and the assumption that the four sectors are filled is itself read off from that number; but the relation was found by solving for that value, and many equally simple formulas land inside the measurement's error, so the agreement is a fit rather than a prediction.

proofs.main:
The dark towers are the five of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(ii): the mirror, two three-dimensional and two five-dimensional. dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated.formal: The census says which towers can hold matter; it does not say which the descent filled, and the two are at different levels. This tower is populated by observation. The mirror is populated by P2: residues $6$ and $2$ are equivalent under signature reversal, so a descent that filled one filled the other, at the same asymmetry (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)); this is the one case in which population is derived. The four odd towers are reached by nothing in the series: P2 does not equate them with this tower, the tower paper gives them algebras and not contents, and what the descent deposited in each is the pre-descent theory's, successor problem (2). What supports their population is the record read inside the framework: with the mirror's share exactly one, an empty set of odd towers would make the ratio $1$ against the observed $5.364$, and the framework has no other dark candidate, so, granted the framework, the observed remainder is the evidence that the odd towers hold matter. That is an inference at observation level, not a count, and it is what the unit-ball rule presupposes when it sums over six towers (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}); since 10 November 2026 it is registered as a premise of the total, \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated}, with the statement that it is inferred from the number the rule fits. Nothing derived in this paper depends on the odd towers being populated: the mirror share, the superselection, the parity theorem and the arrow are the same if they are empty, and refutation item 6 says so.

dark-matter.which-towers-can-carry-arrow.formal:
The descent's orientation, and with it the asymmetry the flag sets in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, is undefined in the odd residues: $1, 3, 5, 7$ cannot be oriented and carry no asymmetry, whatever their content or window. It is defined in the even residues at their P3 representatives, all four-dimensional. Of those, $6$ and $2$ have one time, $4$ has none, and $0$ has two; so the towers that are both oriented and causal are this one and the mirror.

The two-time fork therefore leads to an \emph{oriented} tower: $(2,2)$ has ambient $\R^{3,3}$, $\mathrm{Spin}(3,3) \cong SL(4,\R)$, real four-component conformal spinors (real twistors: a minimal left ideal of $\Cl^+(3,3)$, whose pseudoscalar squares to $+1$, so there is no complex unit), three pairs, mass beginning at two by
\[
\det(\pi^{1}\tilde\pi^{1T} + \pi^{2}\tilde\pi^{2T}) \;=\; \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\br{\tilde\pi^{1}\tilde\pi^{2}}, \qquad \br{\pi\rho} = \pi_{1}\rho_{2} - \pi_{2}\rho_{1},
\]
for the two real spinor parts of $\mathrm{Spin}(2,2) \cong SL(2,\R) \times SL(2,\R)$, and the Standard-Model gauge algebra by that paper's Proposition 4.3 in dimension four \cite[Prop.~4.3]{ButlerT12}, whose two conditionalities (mass-begins-at-two in dimension $n \neq 4$ as a hypothesis, and the identification of the gauge algebra with the automorphisms of minimal massive compositeness) it carries: a Kleinian copy of the Standard Model. Its share would be one only on two equalities the paper cannot supply off this tower's reversal orbit: the asymmetry per mode (P4, a premise on the fork) and the ceiling coupling, which Premise \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise} equates for the mirror alone, along the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}(c)). The two-time instability import keeps the fork closed.

dark-tower-matter.adjoint-norm.technical:
In a causal tower with time direction $e_t$, the adjoint $x^\dagger = e_t\rev{x}e_t^{-1}$ satisfies $e_Ke_K^\dagger = Q(e_t)^{|K|}$ on every basis blade, so on the even algebra $\langle xx^\dagger\rangle_0$ is the sum of the squares of the coordinates of $x$. The idempotent $f$ is self-adjoint, and on the corner algebra $f\Cl^0(V)f$, which is $\R$, $\C$ or $\HH$, the adjoint is the standard conjugation: $x^\dagger x = xx^\dagger = N(x)f$ with $N(x) = 2\langle xx^\dagger\rangle_0 \geq 0$, zero only at $x = 0$.

Right multiplication by a corner element scales the momentum by its norm: $j(\psi x) = N(x)\,j(\psi)$ for every $\psi$ in the spinor ideal $S$.
dark-tower-matter.adjoint-norm.lay: In each tower with a time direction, the numbers a constituent carries (real, complex or quaternionic) come with a conjugation built from reversal and the time direction. This lemma shows that this conjugation is the usual one, so every nonzero number has a positive size. Multiplying a constituent's spinor by such a number multiplies its momentum by that size.

proofs.main:
\textit{(i) The blades.}\enspace Every direction other than $e_{t}$ has square $-Q(e_{t})$. There are two cases.

If $t \notin K$, moving $e_{t}$ through the $|K|$ vectors of $\rev{e_{K}}$ costs one sign each, and a blade times its reverse is the product of its squares:
\[
e_{K}^{\dagger} = e_{t}\rev{e_{K}}e_{t}^{-1} = (-1)^{|K|}\rev{e_{K}}, \qquad e_{K}\rev{e_{K}} = \bigl(-Q(e_{t})\bigr)^{|K|},
\]
so $e_{K}e_{K}^{\dagger} = (-1)^{|K|}\bigl(-Q(e_{t})\bigr)^{|K|} = Q(e_{t})^{|K|}$.

If $e_{K} = e_{t}e_{K'}$, then $\rev{e_{K}} = \rev{e_{K'}}e_{t}$, and
\begin{align*}
e_{K}^{\dagger} &= e_{t}\rev{e_{K'}} = (-1)^{|K'|}\,\rev{e_{K'}}\,e_{t}, \\
e_{K}e_{K}^{\dagger} &= (-1)^{|K'|}\,e_{t}\bigl(e_{K'}\rev{e_{K'}}\bigr)e_{t} = (-1)^{|K'|}\bigl(-Q(e_{t})\bigr)^{|K'|}\,Q(e_{t}) = Q(e_{t})^{|K|}.
\end{align*}
For $K \neq L$, $e_{K}e_{L}^{\dagger}$ is a multiple of $e_{K \triangle L}$, which has no scalar part. Hence for even $x = \sum_{K}x_{K}e_{K}$,
\[
\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0} \;=\; \sum_{K,L}x_{K}x_{L}\,\ip{e_{K}e_{L}^{\dagger}}_{0} \;=\; \sum_{K}x_{K}^{2} \qquad \text{(check B0)}.
\]



\emph{(ii) The corner and its conjugation.}  With $f = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + e_{t}e_{a})$ and $\rev{(e_{t}e_{a})} = e_{a}e_{t}$,
\[
f^{\dagger} = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(1 + e_{t}\,e_{a}e_{t}\,e_{t}^{-1}\bigr) = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + e_{t}e_{a}) = f.
\]
The corner $\F = f\Cl^{0}f$ is a division algebra $\R$, $\C$ or $\HH$ with unit $f$ (Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}(iii)). It is closed under $\dagger$, since $(fxf)^{\dagger} = fx^{\dagger}f$, and $\dagger$ is an anti-involution of it with $\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0} > 0$ for $x \neq 0$ by (i).

The standard conjugation is the only anti-involution with that positivity. Every other candidate has an element with $xx^{\dagger} = -f$, whose scalar part is $-\tfrac{1}{2}$:
\begin{itemize}
\item on $\C$ the other candidate is the identity, and a unit square root $x$ of $-f$ gives $xx^{\dagger} = xx = -f$;
\item on $\HH$ every other anti-involution is $x \mapsto u\bar{x}u^{-1}$ for a unit imaginary $u$, and a unit imaginary $v$ anticommuting with $u$ gives $v\,u\bar{v}u^{-1} = v^{2} = -f$.
\end{itemize}
So $\dagger$ is the standard conjugation, and
\[
x^{\dagger}x \;=\; xx^{\dagger} \;=\; N(x)\,f
\]
with $N$ the standard norm; the script verifies this as a polynomial identity in $x$'s coordinates (check B1). Taking scalar parts, with $\ip{f}_{0} = \tfrac{1}{2}$,
\[
\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0} \;=\; N(x)\,\ip{f}_{0} \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,N(x),
\]
which is positive definite by (i), since $x$ is even (B3).



\emph{(iii) The norm law.}  By the definition of the adjoint, $e_{t}\rev{x} = x^{\dagger}e_{t}$, and $\psi f = \psi$ for $\psi \in S$. So
\begin{align*}
\psi x\,e_{t}\,\rev{(\psi x)} &= \psi\,\bigl(x e_{t}\rev{x}\bigr)\,\rev{\psi} \\
&= \psi\,\bigl(xx^{\dagger}\bigr)\,e_{t}\rev{\psi} \\
&= N(x)\,\psi f\,e_{t}\rev{\psi} \\
&= N(x)\,\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi},
\end{align*}
and the grade-one part is $j(\psi x) = N(x)\,j(\psi)$ (B2).

dark-tower-matter.anomalies.technical:
In the three-dimensional towers each abelian factor $U(1)_\pm$ couples to exactly one unit-charge two-component fermion, which shifts its Chern-Simons level by $\tfrac12\,\mathrm{sign}(m)$ (the parity anomaly). Integrality of the effective level then forces the bare levels into $\mathbb{Z} + \tfrac12$, never zero, so the gauge sector breaks parity.

In the five-dimensional towers, in units $q' = 3Y$, the species $U, D, E, N$ (the content found under Hypothesis (S)) have $\sum q'^3 = -6$ and $\sum q' = 0$ with multiplicities, and the induced abelian cubic Chern-Simons coefficient $\tfrac12\sum \mathrm{sign}(m)\,q'^3$ is an integer for every choice of mass signs. The $SU(3)$ and mixed levels are not analysed.
dark-tower-matter.anomalies.lay: Each charged particle in a three-dimensional tower shifts a topological term in its force by half a unit, and consistency then requires that term never to vanish, so these towers' forces distinguish left from right. In the five-dimensional towers the corresponding abelian term is a whole number for any choice of mass signs, for the particle content found there under the slot hypothesis. The non-abelian terms are not examined.

proofs.main:
\textit{(i)}\enspace With bare level $k$ and one unit-charge fermion of mass $m$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content}(i)), the effective level is, by Fact \claimref{rule2.imported-parity-anomaly},
\[
k_{\mathrm{eff}} \;=\; k + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{sign}(m) \;\in\; \mathbb{Z} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad k \in \mathbb{Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \qquad \text{(G1, G2)},
\]
and no half-integer is zero, so a parity-odd Chern-Simons term is always present.



\emph{(ii)}  In units $q' = 3Y$ the species of Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-content} carry $q' = 2, -1, -3, 0$ for $U, D, E, N$, with colour multiplicity $3$ for $U$ and $D$. So
\begin{align*}
\sum q'^{3} &= 3(2)^{3} + 3(-1)^{3} + (-3)^{3} + 0 = 24 - 3 - 27 = -6, \\
\sum q' &= 3(2) + 3(-1) + (-3) + 0 = 0 \qquad \text{(G3)}.
\end{align*}
In the induced coefficient $\tfrac{1}{2}\sum \mathrm{sign}(m)\,q'^{3}$ (Fact \claimref{rule2.imported-five-dimensional-chern-simons-shift}) the terms of $U$ and $N$ are the integers $\pm 12$ and $0$, and those of $D$ and $E$ are $\pm\tfrac{3}{2}$ and $\pm\tfrac{27}{2}$, whose sum is an integer for each choice of signs.

dark-tower-matter.constituents-field.formal:
In tower $r$ the fields $\F(T)$ and $\F(S)$ are equal, and equal to the division algebra of residue $r + 1$:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccccccc@{}}
\toprule
$r$ & $6$ & $2$ & $1$ & $7$ & $3$ & $5$ & $0$ & $4$ \\
tower & $(1,3)$ & $(3,1)$ & $(2,1)$ & $(1,2)$ & $(4,1)$ & $(1,4)$ & $(2,2)$ & $(4,0)$, $(0,4)$ \\
conformal & $(2,4)$ & $(4,2)$ & $(3,2)$ & $(2,3)$ & $(5,2)$ & $(2,5)$ & $(3,3)$ & $(5,1)$, $(1,5)$ \\
field & $\C$ & $\C$ & $\R$ & $\R$ & $\HH$ & $\HH$ & $\R$ & $\HH$ \\
$\dim_{\R} T$, $\dim_{\R} S$ & $8, 4$ & $8, 4$ & $4, 2$ & $4, 2$ & $16, 8$ & $16, 8$ & $4, 2$ & $8, 4$ \\

In particular the field is not a function of the conformal pseudoscalar's square: $Q(\omega) = -1$ at $r = 7$ (field $\R$) and at $r = 3$ (field $\HH$).
dark-tower-matter.constituents-field.technical:
For a tower $V = \R^{p,q}$ of residue $r = p - q \bmod 8$, the commutant of the spin action on the constituent ideal $T = \Cl^0(\hatV)\hf$ of the conformal algebra and the commutant on the spinor ideal $S = \Cl^0(V)f$ are equal, and both are the division algebra of residue $r + 1$, since $\Cl^0(p,q) \cong \Cl(p,q-1)$ shifts the residue by one. The field is $\C$ at $r = 6, 2$, $\R$ at $r = 1, 7, 0$ and $\HH$ at $r = 3, 5, 4$, with the ideal dimensions of the table.

The field is not a function of the square of the conformal pseudoscalar: $Q(\omega) = -1$ both at $r = 7$, with field $\R$, and at $r = 3$, with field $\HH$.
dark-tower-matter.constituents-field.lay: Each of the eight towers has its own kind of number for its basic constituents: real numbers, complex numbers or quaternions. This theorem reads off which from the classification of real Clifford algebras: complex for our tower and its mirror, real for the three-dimensional towers and one sterile tower, quaternionic for the five-dimensional towers and the other sterile tower. The answer is the same in the larger conformal algebra and in the tower itself.

proofs.main:
\textit{The two even algebras.}\enspace By Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}(i),
\begin{align*}
\Cl^{0}(\hatV) &= \Cl^{0}(p+1, q+1) \cong \Cl(p+1, q), \\
\Cl^{0}(V) &= \Cl^{0}(p, q) \cong \Cl(p, q-1),
\end{align*}
and both have residue $(p+1) - q = p - (q-1) = r + 1$. The one tower with $q = 0$ is $(4,0)$: there $\Cl^{0}(4,0) \cong \Cl(0,3)$, of residue $-3 \equiv 5 = r + 1$, and $(0,4)$ gives the same algebra.



\emph{The commutant.}  By Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}(ii) each algebra is a matrix algebra over the division algebra $D(r+1)$, or a sum of two copies of one, and by Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}(iii) the commutant of a minimal left ideal is $D(r+1)$. Reading $D$ off for each tower:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
r & 6 & 2 & 1 & 7 & 3 & 5 & 0 & 4 \\
r + 1 & 7 & 3 & 2 & 0 & 4 & 6 & 1 & 5 \\ \hline
D(r+1) & \C & \C & \R & \R & \HH & \HH & \R & \HH
\end{array}
\]



\emph{Checks.}  The script computes every commutant from scratch on exact matrix representations of the ideals and classifies it (checks A1, A2), with the dimensions (A3) and the pseudoscalars (A4, A5).

dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-conte.formal:
In the towers $r = 3, 5$, under (S) the state space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{1} \oplus \C^{3})$ has sixteen states. With $Y = s - k/3$ ($s$ the slot occupation, $k$ the number of occupied pairs), the complement $(s,k) \mapsto (1-s, 3-k)$ negates $Y$ and conjugates colour, so the sixteen are eight species-states and their conjugates, four vector-like Dirac species:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccl@{}}
\toprule
species & colour & $Y$ & states $(s,k)$ \\
\midrule
$U$ & $3$ & $2/3$ & $(1,1)$, conjugate $(0,2)$ \\
$D$ & $3$ & $-1/3$ & $(0,1)$, conjugate $(1,2)$ \\
$E$ & $1$ & $-1$ & $(0,3)$, conjugate $(1,0)$ \\
$N$ & $1$ & $0$ & $(0,0)$, $(1,3)$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
These are the electric charges of one of our generations with the weak doublet removed. Through the section $B \mapsto ((\det B)^{-1}, B)$ the centre of $U(3)$ acts on $(s,k)$ by $\lambda^{k - 3s} = \lambda^{-3Y}$, so $3Y$ is an integer with $3Y + k \equiv 0 \pmod 3$, $k$ being the triality: the lattice of $U(3)$, satisfied automatically; the neutral species $N$ is the empty state and the full row of Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.neutral-row}. Without (S) the content is one Dirac colour triplet of $Y = 2/3$. There is no chirality and every species has a gauge-invariant bare mass.
dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-conte.technical:
In the towers $r = 3, 5$, under Hypothesis (S) the state space $\Lambda^\bullet(\C^1 \oplus \C^3)$ of the one slot and the three pairs has sixteen states. With $Y = s - k/3$ for slot occupation $s$ and pair number $k$, the complement $(s,k) \mapsto (1-s, 3-k)$ negates $Y$ and conjugates colour, giving four vector-like Dirac species: $U$ (colour $3$, $Y = 2/3$), $D$ ($3$, $-1/3$), $E$ ($1$, $-1$) and the neutral $N$ ($1$, $0$), the electric charges of one of our generations with the weak doublet removed.

Through the section $B \mapsto ((\det B)^{-1}, B)$ the centre of $U(3)$ acts by $\lambda^{-3Y}$, so $3Y$ is an integer with $3Y + k \equiv 0 \pmod 3$, satisfied automatically. Without (S) the content is one Dirac colour triplet of $Y = 2/3$. There is no chirality, and every species has a gauge-invariant bare mass.
dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-conte.lay: Assuming the slot hypothesis, which treats a constituent's slot as a quantum mode like its pairs, a five-dimensional tower's matter comes in four kinds: two coloured quark-like species of charge two thirds and minus one third, a charged lepton-like species and a neutral one. These are the charges of one family of our matter with the weak-force partners missing. Without the hypothesis only one coloured species remains, and in either case each species can have a mass without any Higgs-like field.

proofs.main:
The state space under (S) (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.hypothesis-s-slot-statistics}) has
\[
\dim \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{4} \;=\; \sum_{s=0}^{1}\sum_{k=0}^{3}\binom{3}{k} \;=\; 2 \cdot 8 \;=\; 16
\]
states, the $\binom{3}{k}$ states at pair number $k$ forming the $1, 3, \bar{3}, 1$ of the $SU(3)$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras}(ii). The complement negates $Y$:
\[
Y(1 - s, 3 - k) \;=\; (1 - s) - \frac{3 - k}{3} \;=\; -\Bigl(s - \frac{k}{3}\Bigr) \;=\; -Y(s, k),
\]
and the remaining weights are arithmetic (F3, F4). The masses are as in Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content}(iv).

dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-tower.formal:
Decimal, with imports as stated. With the fifth direction one cell radius deep and co-expanding (R3; \cite[Rem.~7.9, Rem.~7.14]{ButlerT14}):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $LT$ runs from about $390$ (at $g_{s} = 106.75$) to $1170$ today: the Kaluza-Klein spacing is always below $T/120$, so the towers are five-dimensional at the visible temperature and at their matter's mass scale (K5); at T14's small dark temperatures the dark bath itself is only a few Kaluza-Klein levels deep.
\item[(ii)] Five-dimensional gauge theory is infrared free; reducing to four dimensions gives a confinement scale below $\pi/L$ by a factor smaller than $e^{-250}$ even at strong coupling (K7), and the $1/r^{2}$ potential binds nothing unless the theory is within a factor of about eight of strong coupling at the quark mass (supplementary \file{D5C}, H3; \cite{CLP2000}). There are no dark hadrons and no dark atoms.
\item[(iii)] With the Kaluza-Klein tower populated, $\Delta\Neff < 0.3$ needs $T_{D}/T_{\gamma} < 0.085$ for the nine vectors of $\uu(3)$ ($0.13$ for one photon), not the $0.46$ to $0.51$ of T14's zero-mode formula \cite[Prop.~6.3]{ButlerT14}; a sector decoupled at a GeV would give about $670$ (K6). T14's own temperature estimates meet the corrected bound by orders.
\item[(iv)] Two-body scattering is collisionless by geometry, $\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}/m = \sigma_{5}/(Lm) < 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$ even for charged and coloured species (supplementary \file{D5C}, H9).
\item[(v)] With no boundary term in the series the gauge field's natural condition at the ends of the fifth direction keeps a four-dimensional zero mode, so beyond about a metre the charged species form a neutral dark plasma. Published plasma-instability limits \cite{SSS2024, PIC2024}, rescaled to a GeV, lie six to ten orders below the coupling a freeze-out relic needs and about two to five orders below a deposit at a natural five-dimensional coupling (supplementary \file{D5C}, Section 14, and \file{CHECK\_COS}). Whether such instabilities transfer bulk momentum in a merger is not established \cite{Lasenby2020}: an exposure, not an exclusion.
\item[(vi)] If the neutral species $N$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-content}) carries R2's count as a deposit and the charged species annihilate at weak coupling, the tower carries no long-range charge and is collisionless whatever the zero modes do. Under Premise \claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule} this branch is open to both five-dimensional towers.
\end{enumerate}
The relic is a symmetric gas of free spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ dark quarks and leptons, or of $N$ alone. The lightest species is stable by fermion parity, the lightest quark and lepton by species numbers broken only at the rung scale.
dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-tower.technical:
Decimal estimates with imported physics, taking the fifth direction one cell radius deep and co-expanding (premise R3). (i) $LT$ runs from about $390$ to $1170$, so the Kaluza-Klein spacing stays below $T/120$ and the towers are five-dimensional at the visible temperature and at their matter's mass scale, while at small dark temperatures the dark bath is only a few levels deep. (ii) Five-dimensional gauge theory is infrared free: the reduced confinement scale lies below $\pi/L$ by a factor smaller than $e^{-250}$ even at strong coupling, and the $1/r^2$ potential binds nothing unless the theory is within about a factor eight of strong coupling, so there are no dark hadrons or atoms. (iii) With the Kaluza-Klein tower populated, $\Delta\Neff < 0.3$ needs $T_D/T_\gamma < 0.085$ for the nine vectors of $\uu(3)$, not the zero-mode $0.46$ to $0.51$; a sector decoupled at a GeV would give about $670$.

(iv) Two-body scattering is collisionless by geometry, $\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}/m < 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm^2\,g^{-1}}$. (v) With no boundary term a four-dimensional zero mode survives and the charged species form a neutral dark plasma, an exposure to plasma-instability limits, not an exclusion. (vi) If the neutral species $N$ carries R2's count and the charged species annihilate at weak coupling, the tower is collisionless; under Premise U this branch is open to both towers. The relic is a symmetric gas of free spin-$\tfrac12$ species, or of $N$ alone.
dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-tower.lay: Assuming, with premise R3, that the extra direction is about one particle spacing deep and grows with the universe, these decimal estimates describe what the five-dimensional towers' matter does. Their forces never confine, so there are no dark nuclei or atoms; their radiation is small enough for the temperatures the dark-matter paper estimates; and their particles barely scatter. Their charged particles could form a dark plasma, a possible weakness, unless only the neutral species survives in the needed numbers, a branch open to both towers under the transposition rule.

dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras.technical:
Under H2 (the gauge algebra is the automorphism algebra of the minimal massive hierarchy) and Premise U: in the three-dimensional towers $r = 1, 7$ mass begins at two real constituents of two real pairs, so the hierarchy is $\R^2 \otimes \R^2$. Its automorphisms $A \otimes B$ with $A, B \in O(2)$ form $(O(2) \times O(2))/\mathbb{Z}_2$, the kernel being $\{(1,1), (-1,-1)\}$: the gauge algebra is the abelian $\so(2) \oplus \so(2)$, of dimension two, with identity component $U(1)_+ \times U(1)_-$.

In the five-dimensional towers $r = 3, 5$ mass begins at one constituent whose three pairs are complex, with the unit that builds the third pair, so the hierarchy is $\C^1 \otimes \C^3$. Its automorphisms form $(U(1) \times U(3))/U(1) \cong U(3)$, and the gauge algebra is $\uu(3) = \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$, of dimension nine.
dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras.lay: Assuming that a tower's forces are the symmetries of its smallest composite that can have mass, as in the Standard-Model paper, and a rule for carrying that construction to other towers, this theorem finds the forces of the odd towers. The three-dimensional towers get two independent forces like electromagnetism. The five-dimensional towers get a colour force like our strong force together with one force like electromagnetism, nine force carriers in all.

proofs.main:
\textit{(i) The two factors.}\enspace The constituent count is two (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(i)) and the field is $\R$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}), so by U2 (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule}) the slot group is $O(2)$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.ladder}). The pairs are real (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.pairs}(i)), and by U2 their group is the orthogonal group of the real pair space, again $O(2)$.

The norm clause of U2 matters here. Without it, the pair mixings preserving the canonical relations alone would be $GL(2,\R)$, acting by $B$ on the $w_{i}$ and by $B^{-T}$ on the $v_{i}$. That is the mechanism of Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.kleinian-algebra}, where the sterile tower has no time direction and so no adjoint.



\emph{(i) The kernel.}  An automorphism of $\R^{2} \otimes \R^{2}$ respecting both factors is $A \otimes B$, and
\[
A \otimes B = 1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A = \lambda 1, \;\; B = \lambda^{-1}1,
\]
with $\lambda$ real and orthogonal, so $\lambda = \pm 1$. The kernel $\{(1,1), (-1,-1)\}$ is discrete, no generator is lost, and the algebra is $\so(2) \oplus \so(2)$ (the gauge algebra by \claimref{dark-tower-matter.h2-identification}; checks E1, E2).



\emph{(i) The charges.}  Write $s$ and $p$ for the weights of the slot and pair rotations. The element $(-1, -1)$ acts as $(-1)^{s + p}$, so the group's representations are those with $s + p$ even, on which
\[
q_{\pm} = \frac{s \pm p}{2}
\]
are the integral charges of $U(1)_{\pm}$ (F2).



\emph{(ii) The slot.}  The constituent count is one (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(ii)). The slot group of one constituent is $Sp(1)$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.ladder}), acting on the spinor part through H1 (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.h1-momentum})'s identification of the two fields. The pair unit of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.third-pairs-unit-five-dimensions} lies in that field, and only the circle it generates commutes with the pair algebra, so the slot is one complex line with group $U(1)$.



\emph{(ii) The pairs and the kernel.}  By U2 the three complex pairs carry $U(3)$. The action $(\lambda, B) \mapsto \lambda B$ has the common scalar as its kernel, as in T12's proof of its Theorem 4.1, so the group is
\[
\frac{U(1) \times U(3)}{U(1)} \;\cong\; U(3)
\]
(E3; the control $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3} \mapsto 12$ is E4).

dark-tower-matter.h1-momentum.formal:
A constituent has a spinor part $\psi$ in the tower's spinor ideal $S$ (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-tower-matter.ideals-fields-momentum}), carried by a map $T \to S$ that intertwines the action of the tower's spin group, so that the field of $T$ acts on $S$ through it; its momentum is the vector part of $\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi}$. In dimension four this is T12's Fact 2.1 in the even algebra; in dimensions three and five it is a premise.

\emph{Note (what of H1 is forced).} In the causal towers of dimension three to five the quadratic vectors of one constituent's spinor part that are covariant under the connected spin group form one real line, spanned by this momentum (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.constituent-momentum-is-the-unique-spin-covariant-quadratic-vector-on-the-spinor-ideal}). So, given a spinor part and a momentum that is quadratic and covariant, the formula is forced up to a real factor. H1 is weakened by that result, not retired: what stays premised in dimensions three and five is that a constituent has a spinor part in $S$ carried by an intertwining map, that its momentum is a quadratic covariant vector of it, the normalisation, and the additivity of momenta over constituents, which covariance does not force.
dark-tower-matter.h1-momentum.technical:
H1 takes a constituent to carry a spinor part $\psi$ in the tower's spinor ideal $S$, through a map from the conformal constituent ideal $T$ to $S$ that intertwines the action of the tower's spin group, so that the field of $T$ acts on $S$ through it; its momentum is the vector part $\langle \psi e_t\rev{\psi}\rangle_1$. In dimension four this is the Standard-Model paper's statement written in the even algebra; in dimensions three and five it is a premise, not a theorem.

Note: given a spinor part and a quadratic, spin-covariant momentum, the formula is forced up to a real factor in the causal towers of dimension three to five (the constituent-momentum uniqueness result). H1 is weakened, not retired: the spinor part, quadraticity and covariance, the normalisation and additivity over constituents stay premised.
dark-tower-matter.h1-momentum.lay: This is an assumption, not a result: a constituent's motion is read from a spinor in the tower's own algebra, linked to the constituent in the larger conformal algebra in a way that respects the tower's rotations. In our four-dimensional world this is already established; in three and five dimensions it is assumed. A later result shows that the formula itself is not a free choice: once the motion is read from such a spinor in a way that respects rotations and boosts, it is the only possibility up to an overall factor. What remains assumed is that the spinor exists, that the reading has that form, and that motions of several constituents add.

dark-tower-matter.hypothesis-s-slot-stat.formal: The constituent slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs, so that the composite's state space is the exterior algebra of slot and pair modes \cite[Sec.~5]{ButlerT12}. Used only where stated.
dark-tower-matter.hypothesis-s-slot-stat.technical: Hypothesis (S) takes the constituent slots of a tower's composite to be fermionic modes on the same footing as its ladder pairs, so the composite's state space is the exterior algebra of the slot and pair modes. It is the Standard-Model paper's slot hypothesis carried from our tower to every tower, without that paper's chirality clause, and it is used only where a result says so. In the three-dimensional towers the slot-level states it produces are not representations of the global form (the kernel of the action on the hierarchy is discrete there), as \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.why-s-fails-three-dimensions-not} records.
dark-tower-matter.hypothesis-s-slot-stat.lay: This is an assumption, not a result: the places a composite's constituents occupy are treated as quantum modes of the same kind as their internal pairs. Our own tower's particle physics uses the same assumption; here it is carried to the dark towers, and only the results that state it rely on it.

dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-stru.formal: (i) For $q \geq 1$, $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \cong \Cl(p,q-1)$, by $e_{a} \mapsto e_{a}e_{n}$ with $Q(e_{n}) = -1$; for $p \geq 1$, $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \cong \Cl(q, p-1)$. (ii) $\Cl(p,q)$ is a matrix algebra over $D \in \{\R, \C, \HH\}$, or a sum of two, with $D$ fixed by $p - q \bmod 8$: $\R$ at $0, 1, 2$; $\C$ at $3, 7$; $\HH$ at $4, 5, 6$. (iii) A minimal left ideal $Af$ of a simple or semisimple algebra $A$, $f$ a primitive idempotent, has commutant $\mathrm{End}_{A}(Af) \cong (fAf)^{\mathrm{op}}$, a division algebra (Schur), acting by right multiplication. Sources: \cite{Chevalley1954, Lounesto2001, LawsonMichelsohn1989}.
dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-stru.technical: Three classical facts. (i) For $q \geq 1$, $\Cl^0(p,q) \cong \Cl(p,q-1)$ by $e_a \mapsto e_ae_n$ with $Q(e_n) = -1$, and for $p \geq 1$, $\Cl^0(p,q) \cong \Cl(q,p-1)$. (ii) $\Cl(p,q)$ is a matrix algebra over $D \in \{\R, \C, \HH\}$, or a sum of two, with $D$ fixed by $p - q \bmod 8$: $\R$ at $0, 1, 2$, $\C$ at $3, 7$, $\HH$ at $4, 5, 6$. (iii) A minimal left ideal $Af$ of a simple or semisimple algebra $A$, with $f$ a primitive idempotent, has commutant $(fAf)^{\mathrm{op}}$, a division algebra by Schur's lemma, acting by right multiplication.
dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-stru.lay: These are textbook facts about Clifford algebras, the algebras of directions that underlie the series. They say how the even part of such an algebra matches a smaller algebra, which kind of number (real, complex or quaternionic) each algebra is built over according to its signature, and that the symmetries of its basic spinor spaces form a number system of that kind.

dark-tower-matter.imported-cluster-simul.formal: In the idealised Bullet-like merger runs of T14b \cite[Obs.~7.1, Table~3]{ButlerT14b}: (i) with only the mirror colliding ($18.6$ percent of the dark matter, as gas) the subcluster keeps a separate lensing peak on its galaxies and a mass-to-light change of $0.82$ against the observed $0.84 \pm 0.07$; (ii) with the mirror gas and one three-dimensional tower's share of colliding fluid ($43.5$ percent colliding) the subcluster dissolves, and with more it dissolves too; (iii) with the mirror collisionless and $24.9$ or $31.6$ percent of colliding fluid, the subcluster keeps a weaker peak but only $0.55$ or $0.44$ of its central mass: the colliding fluid alone costs about half of it. In (i) the subcluster's own mass is $0.57$ of the cold-dark-matter run's, but mass and light leave together and the mass-to-light change, the quantity the observational bound is inferred from, is consistent. No run lies between $18.6$ and $24.9$ percent colliding. The colliding components there are fluids.

dark-tower-matter.ladder.formal: Let $\F = f\Cl^{0}(V)f$ act on $S$ on the right and on $S^{n}$ by $\psi'_{i} = \sum_{k}\psi_{k}U_{ki}$ for $U \in M_{n}(\F)$. Then $U$ preserves the total momentum of every $n$-tuple if and only if $UU^{\dagger} = 1$, where $(U^{\dagger})_{ik} = (U_{ki})^{\dagger}$. The momentum-preserving group is $O(n)$, $U(n)$ or $Sp(n)$ as $\F = \R$, $\C$, $\HH$: $O(n)$ in the three-dimensional towers, $U(n)$ in this tower and the mirror, $Sp(n)$ in the five-dimensional towers.
dark-tower-matter.ladder.technical:
Let the corner field $\F = f\Cl^0(V)f$ act on the spinor ideal $S$ on the right and on $n$-tuples by $\psi'_i = \sum_k \psi_kU_{ki}$ with $U \in M_n(\F)$. Then $U$ preserves the total momentum of every $n$-tuple if and only if $UU^\dagger = 1$, with $(U^\dagger)_{ik} = (U_{ki})^\dagger$: by the norm law, preserving momentum is preserving the positive form $\sum_k N(a_k)$ on $\F^n$.

So the momentum-preserving group is $O(n)$, $U(n)$ or $Sp(n)$ as $\F$ is $\R$, $\C$ or $\HH$: $O(n)$ in the three-dimensional towers, $U(n)$ in this tower and the mirror, and $Sp(n)$ in the five-dimensional towers.
dark-tower-matter.ladder.lay: Several constituents can be mixed into one another using the tower's own kind of number. This theorem shows that the mixings that keep their total momentum are exactly the unitary ones for that kind of number: rotations for real numbers, unitary matrices for complex numbers, and their quaternionic analogue for quaternions.

proofs.main:
\textit{Unitary mixings preserve the momentum.}\enspace Using $e_{t}\rev{y} = y^{\dagger}e_{t}$ on each entry of $U$,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{i}\psi'_{i}e_{t}\rev{\psi'_{i}} &= \sum_{i}\sum_{k,l}\psi_{k}U_{ki}\,e_{t}\,\rev{U_{li}}\,\rev{\psi_{l}} \\
&= \sum_{k,l}\psi_{k}\Bigl(\sum_{i}U_{ki}U_{li}^{\dagger}\Bigr)e_{t}\rev{\psi_{l}}.
\end{align*}
If $UU^{\dagger} = 1$, that is $\sum_{i}U_{ki}U_{li}^{\dagger} = \delta_{kl}f$, the right-hand side is $\sum_{k}\psi_{k}e_{t}\rev{\psi_{k}}$.



\emph{Only unitary mixings do.}  Take $\psi_{k} = \psi a_{k}$ for one $\psi \in S$ with $j(\psi) \neq 0$ and a row $a = (a_{k}) \in \F^{n}$. Then $\psi'_{i} = \psi\,(aU)_{i}$, and Lemma \claimref{dark-tower-matter.adjoint-norm}(iii) gives the total momenta before and after as
\[
P = \Bigl(\sum_{k}N(a_{k})\Bigr)\,j(\psi), \qquad P' = \Bigl(\sum_{i}N\bigl((aU)_{i}\bigr)\Bigr)\,j(\psi).
\]
Their equality for every $a$ says that $U$ preserves the positive definite form $\sum_{k}N(a_{k})$ on $\F^{n}$, whose polarisation is the standard $\F$-Hermitian form; so $UU^{\dagger} = 1$.



\emph{The groups.}  The isometry groups of the standard forms over $\R$, $\C$, $\HH$ are $O(n)$, $U(n)$, $Sp(n)$, and Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field} assigns the fields. The script checks an $\F$-unitary mixing in every causal tower as a polynomial identity (C1) and exhibits a non-unitary mixing that changes the total momentum (C2).

dark-tower-matter.mirror-against-record.formal: On every branch the mirror recombines early (at a visible temperature of $0.04$ to $3$ keV) and is cold dark matter for the microwave background and large-scale structure, and in galaxies it is a collisional gas that cools by bremsstrahlung in a few gigayears, settles partly and forms stars. Against the Gaia thin-disk bounds \cite{Widmark2021} and Roux and Cline's limit $\Omega_{b'} \lesssim 0.8\,\Omega_{b}$ \cite{RouxCline2020}, only the helium interval has room: there T14b's Galaxy models pass at the Sun only with helium-star feedback \cite[Obs.~9.1]{ButlerT14b}, and Roux and Cline's limit, which covers the whole helium interval, is exceeded by a factor $1.24$. Nothing in the construction lowers the mirror's share below $0.995$ or changes its microphysics without a further exception to P2: the copy is exact and the tension T14 records stands. (The cold mirror itself is an exception to P2 at its version-1 reach; P2 as scoped leaves $\xi$ free, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}, and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent, Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}.) Observation level, on imported galaxy modelling.
dark-tower-matter.mirror-against-record.technical:
Observation level, on imported galaxy modelling. On every branch the mirror recombines early, at a visible temperature of $0.04$ to $3$ keV, and is cold dark matter for the microwave background and large-scale structure; in galaxies it is a collisional gas that cools by bremsstrahlung in a few gigayears, settles partly and forms stars. Against the Gaia thin-disk bounds and Roux and Cline's limit $\Omega_{b'} \lesssim 0.8\,\Omega_b$ only the helium interval has room: there the Galaxy models pass at the Sun only with helium-star feedback, and Roux and Cline's limit, which covers the whole helium interval, is exceeded by a factor $1.24$.

Nothing in the construction lowers the mirror's share below $0.995$ or changes its microphysics without a further exception to P2: the copy is exact, and the tension the dark-matter paper records stands. The cold mirror itself is an exception to P2 at its version-1 reach only; P2 as scoped leaves $\xi$ free, and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent.
dark-tower-matter.mirror-against-record.lay: At the level of observation, and relying on imported models of galaxies, the mirror tower behaves like ordinary cold dark matter on cosmic scales but like gas inside galaxies, where it cools, settles and forms stars. Observations of our Galaxy's disk and of mirror-matter cosmology leave room only if the mirror is mostly helium, and even then one published limit is exceeded by about a quarter. The construction offers no way to shrink the mirror's share.

dark-tower-matter.mirror-algebra.technical: The linear map $e_K \mapsto (-1)^{|K|/2}e_K$ on even basis blades is an algebra isomorphism from the even algebra of a signature onto the even algebra of the reversed signature, with every $Q(e_a)$ negated; in particular $\Cl^0(3,1) \cong \Cl^0(1,3)$ and $\Cl^0(4,2) \cong \Cl^0(2,4)$. It carries the mirror's pseudoscalar $I_4'$ to $+I_4$ and its conformal pseudoscalar $I_6'$ to $-I_6$. The full algebras differ: $\Cl(1,3)$ has quaternionic irreducible modules and $\Cl(3,1)$ real ones.
dark-tower-matter.mirror-algebra.lay: The mirror tower has the opposite signature to ours, with the signs of space and time swapped in its metric. This theorem gives an explicit sign rule that identifies the even part of its algebra, where spinors and rotations live, with ours, using real numbers only. Under it the mirror's spacetime volume element matches ours while its conformal one comes out reversed, and the full algebras, which include vectors, still differ.

proofs.main:
\textit{(i) The product rule.}\enspace Write $Q$ for the squares of the first signature and $Q' = -Q$ for those of the second. For even blades $e_{K}$, $e_{L}$,
\[
e_{K}e_{L} \;=\; \sigma \prod_{c \in K \cap L}Q(e_{c})\;e_{K \triangle L},
\]
with $\sigma$ the reordering sign, which does not depend on the squares; the same holds in the second algebra with $Q'$ in place of $Q$.



\emph{(i) The map respects it.}  Let $\varphi(e_{K}) = (-1)^{|K|/2}e_{K}$, and use $|K \triangle L| = |K| + |L| - 2|K \cap L|$ and $\prod_{c}Q'(e_{c}) = (-1)^{|K \cap L|}\prod_{c}Q(e_{c})$. Then
\begin{align*}
\varphi(e_{K}e_{L}) &= \sigma\prod_{c}Q(e_{c})\,(-1)^{|K \triangle L|/2}\,e_{K \triangle L}
= (-1)^{\frac{|K|+|L|}{2}}(-1)^{|K \cap L|}\,\sigma\prod_{c}Q(e_{c})\,e_{K \triangle L}, \\
\varphi(e_{K})\,\varphi(e_{L}) &= (-1)^{\frac{|K|+|L|}{2}}\,\sigma\prod_{c}Q'(e_{c})\,e_{K \triangle L}
= (-1)^{\frac{|K|+|L|}{2}}(-1)^{|K \cap L|}\,\sigma\prod_{c}Q(e_{c})\,e_{K \triangle L}.
\end{align*}
The two agree. The script checks every pair of basis blades in both cases (I1).



\emph{(ii)}  On the pseudoscalars,
\[
\varphi(I_{4}') = (-1)^{4/2}\,I_{4} = +I_{4}, \qquad \varphi(I_{6}') = (-1)^{6/2}\,I_{6} = -I_{6} \qquad \text{(I2)}.
\]



\emph{(iii)}  The commutants are $\HH$ and $\R$ (I3; Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}).

dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition.formal:
Decimal. Supplementary scripts: the mirror's (folder \file{MIR}, checks D1, D2 and E0 to E7) and the cosmology check's (folder \file{CHECK\_COS}). T14 carries $\xi$ from the gravitational floor ($2.8$ to $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ at the top of the ceiling range) to the $\Neff$ cap ($0.448$), with a hot-deposit estimate near $4 \times 10^{-3}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] At the floor the mirror is charge-dominated and degenerate from the moment it is seeded: the Fermi energy its deposited baryon number must carry exceeds the floor's thermal deposit by $49$ to $84$, and at its weak freeze-out the quark chemical potential is $18$ to $23$ times its temperature. Beta equilibrium persists into the hadron phase, and for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$ (our tower's sphaleron value $L/B = -51/28$, or zero) the mirror ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons. Its endpoint is cold, dense, neutron-rich matter; the composition after decay and capture needs a dense-matter network and is not computed here.
\item[(ii)] Between $\xi \approx 3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$, an interval containing T14's hot-deposit estimate, the mirror is helium ($Y' = 0.94$ to $1.00$).
\item[(iii)] Above that interval the helium fraction falls ($Y' = 0.85$ at $\xi = 0.1$) and towards the cap the mirror is hydrogen-rich ($Y' = 0.58$ at $\xi = 0.448$).
\end{enumerate}
T14 does not print a mirror $\eta'$ at freeze-out; its floor value $19$ to $26$ is the late-time ratio, and the thermal up-down ratio T14 assumes there is inconsistent with its own $\eta' > 1$.

(ii) For $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$ the mirror is helium, $Y' = 0.94$ to $1.00$. dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition.lay: The mirror tower copies our physics, so what its matter becomes depends mainly on how hot it was compared with our world. These decimal estimates show that if it was as cold as gravity alone allows, it ends as dense neutron-rich matter; if it was moderately warm, it is almost pure helium; and if it was near the radiation limit, it is mostly hydrogen. The coldest case is not followed to its final composition.

dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2.formal: T14 applies P2 along the reversal orbit to equate the ceiling coupling and the asymmetry per mode, both data of the descent \cite[Thm.~4.3(iv), (v)]{ButlerT14}. The energy the descent deposits per unit charge is a datum of the same kind, and P2 declares which of $2$, $6$ is visible to be indexical. Applied with the same reach, P2 gives $\xi = T'/T = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = \tfrac{8}{7}(\tfrac{11}{4})^{4/3} + 3.044 = 7.45$ at recombination, excluded by a factor of about $25$. T14's mirror, cold from the gravitational floor upward \cite[Prop.~4.6, Prop.~A.2]{ButlerT14}, is therefore an exception to P2 that T14 neither states nor costs. It is an exception at P2's version-1 reach, the reach T14 used; P2 as scoped (version 2) leaves $\xi$ free (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}), and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}). Assembly level.

dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2.lay: The dark-matter paper uses an indifference principle, P2, to argue that the mirror tower and ours received equal shares of certain initial quantities. This assembly-level argument shows that applying the same principle to the energy each tower received would make the mirror as hot as our world, adding far more radiation than observations allow. So the cold mirror the paper relies on is an unstated exception to its own principle as first stated. As the principle is now scoped, it applies to labels such as charges and not to temperatures, so it leaves the mirror's temperature free; a cold mirror then needs the descent to have left the towers out of equilibrium.

proofs.main:
