synthesis.constituent-momentum-is-the-un.formal:
Let $V$ be a causal tower of dimension $n \in \{3, 4, 5\}$, that is $\R^{2,1}$, $\R^{1,2}$, $\R^{1,3}$, $\R^{3,1}$, $\R^{4,1}$ or $\R^{1,4}$, with $e_{t}$, $f$, the spinor ideal $S = \Cl^{0}(V)f$ and the momentum $j(\psi) = \langle \psi e_{t}\rev{\psi}\rangle_{1}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-tower-matter.ideals-fields-momentum}. The bivectors $B$ of $\Cl(V)$ act on $S$ by $\psi \mapsto B\psi$ and on $V$ by $v \mapsto Bv - vB$. Covariance here is under the Lie algebra of bivectors, hence under the connected group the rotors generate; no reflection is imposed, the bivectors act on $S$ from the left only (the right action of the field of $S$ is not imposed), and $\beta$ below is real-bilinear. Call a map $\mu : S \to V$ a \emph{spin-covariant quadratic vector} if $\mu(\psi) = \beta(\psi, \psi)$ for a symmetric $\R$-bilinear $\beta : S \times S \to V$ with
\[
\beta(B\psi, \phi) + \beta(\psi, B\phi) \;=\; B\,\beta(\psi, \phi) - \beta(\psi, \phi)\,B
\]
for every bivector $B$ and all $\psi, \phi \in S$; and call a quadratic form $S \to \R$ \emph{spin-invariant} if its symmetric bilinear form satisfies the same equation with right-hand side zero.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Uniqueness for one constituent; proved, by an exact rank computation in each of the six towers.)} The spin-covariant quadratic vectors on $S$ form a real line, spanned by $j$: $j$ is the only one up to a real factor. That the symmetric square of a spinor module contains the vector once in these dimensions is classical spinor algebra; what is done here is to place it on the series' spinor ideals.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The projection; proved.)} For $n = 3$ and $n = 4$, $\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi}$ is a vector for every $\psi \in S$, so the projection $\langle\,\cdot\,\rangle_{1}$ in $j$ removes nothing, and $S$ carries no nonzero spin-invariant quadratic form. For $n = 5$,
\[
\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi} \;=\; j(\psi) + s(\psi)\,I,
\]
with $I$ the pseudoscalar of $\Cl(V)$, which is central, and $s$ a nonzero quadratic form on $S$; the spin-invariant quadratic forms on $S$ are the real multiples of $s$. These counts (none for $n = 3, 4$, one line for $n = 5$) agree with \claimref{synthesis.invariant-forms-on-spinor-ideal-factor-through-reversion}(iii), which is not used here.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Mass in dimension five; proved.)} For $n = 5$ and every $\psi \in S$, with $y = \psi e_{t}\rev{\psi}$,
\[
y^{2} = 2\,s(\psi)\,I\,y, \qquad Q(j(\psi)) = s(\psi)^{2}\,I^{2}, \qquad m^{2}\bigl(j(\psi)\bigr) = Q(e_{t})\,Q(j(\psi)) = s(\psi)^{2},
\]
and $2\,s(\psi)^{2} = \langle x x^{\dagger}\rangle_{0}$ for $x = \rev{\psi}\psi$, the single-constituent law of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(ii), of which this clause is a restatement in terms of $s$. So in the five-dimensional towers the mass of one constituent is the square of the central part that the projection in $j$ removes, and the constituent is massless exactly where $s(\psi) = 0$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What covariance does not fix; proved in the six towers.)} The spin-covariant real bilinear maps $S \times S \to V$, with no symmetry imposed, form a space of dimension $1$, $2$, $4$ for $n = 3, 4, 5$, the real dimension of the field of $S$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}). On $S \oplus S$, two constituents, a spin-covariant quadratic vector is a multiple of $j(\psi_{1})$, a multiple of $j(\psi_{2})$ and such a bilinear map of $(\psi_{1}, \psi_{2})$, so the space has dimension $3$, $4$, $6$, larger than the plane spanned by the two single momenta (for $n = 3, 4$ also computed directly on $S \oplus S$). The total momentum $j(\psi_{1}) + j(\psi_{2})$ of the Definition is one point of it. The cross terms are odd under $\psi_{2} \mapsto -\psi_{2}$ and the two single momenta are even, so covariance together with invariance under a change of sign of one constituent leaves $a\,j(\psi_{1}) + b\,j(\psi_{2})$: that momenta add is then the absence of a cross term together with equal weights $a = b$, clauses of the Definition that covariance does not supply.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Reading for Premise H1; argued.)} In dimensions three and five the momentum clause of Premise \claimref{dark-tower-matter.h1-momentum} is, by (i), equivalent to the weaker statement that a constituent's momentum is a nonzero spin-covariant (connected group) real-quadratic function of its spinor part with values in $V$, together with a real factor: a positive factor multiplies every mass of the tower by one constant and a negative one exchanges the two time orientations. The formula is therefore not an independent choice. What remains assumed in H1 is that a constituent has a spinor part in $S$ (the intertwining map), that its momentum is quadratic in that part and covariant, and, from the Definition, that momenta add. In dimension three the premise's formula has the form of the four-dimensional one with nothing removed; in dimension five it removes the central part $s\,I$, which by (iii) carries the whole single-constituent mass.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.constituent-momentum-is-the-un.technical: Premise H1 of the dark-tower paper takes a constituent's momentum, in the towers of dimension three and five, to be the vector part of $\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi}$ for its spinor part $\psi$, as in dimension four. This result asks how much of that is a choice, in the six causal towers of dimension three to five. Requiring only that the momentum be a vector depending quadratically on $\psi$ and transforming with it under the spin algebra leaves, by an exact computation in each tower, a single candidate up to a real factor, and it is the premise's $j$; covariance is under the connected spin group only (no reflections) and the dependence is real-quadratic. This is a standard fact of spinor algebra, placed here on the series' ideals. In dimensions three and four the product $\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi}$ is already a vector, so the projection removes nothing. In dimension five it has a second part, a multiple $s$ of the central pseudoscalar; $s$ is the only spin-invariant quadratic form on the spinor ideal (in agreement with the stored classification of invariant forms, which is not used), and the squared mass of a single constituent equals $s^{2}$, which restates the stored single-constituent mass law. For two constituents covariance allows cross terms beside the two single momenta, as many as the real dimension of the ideal's field, so the covariant quadratic vectors of two constituents form spaces of dimension three, four and six in dimensions three, four and five; requiring also invariance under a change of sign of one constituent removes the cross terms and leaves the two weights, so the additivity of momenta is a separate clause. Under these conditions the formula of H1 is forced once momentum is assumed quadratic and covariant; the existence of the spinor part, quadraticity, covariance and additivity remain assumed.
synthesis.constituent-momentum-is-the-un.lay: One of the assumptions behind the series' account of matter in the hidden worlds of three and five dimensions is a formula for the momentum of a basic constituent, copied from our four-dimensional world. This result shows that, in the six such worlds with one time direction, the formula is not a free choice: if momentum is to be an arrow in spacetime built from two copies of the constituent's internal state, and to turn when the state is turned, there is only one such formula up to an overall factor. Here "turn" means continuous rotations and boosts only, not mirror reflections, and this is a standard fact about spinors, placed here in the series' algebra. In five dimensions the same construction also produces a single extra number, and the mass of a lone constituent is exactly the square of that number. What is still assumed is that constituents have such an internal state at all, that momentum is built from two copies of it, and that the momenta of several constituents simply add: for two constituents the same requirement allows extra mixed terms, in three, four and five dimensions alike, so it does not single out the plain sum.

synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r.formal:
\emph{Setting and conditions.} Assume the representatives of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives}, so that the towers that admit matter have space dimension $D_{r} = 3$ for this world ($r = 6$) and the mirror ($r = 2$), $D_{r} = 2$ for $r = 1, 7$ and $D_{r} = 4$ for $r = 3, 5$; assume, as the stored total does, that all six are populated (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}) and that residues $0$ and $4$ are empty (the single-ideal clause, Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(vi)); and assume the stored sourcing rule (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}, which rests on Premise P1, \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}). A \emph{filling} gives each populated tower a quantum mass $m_{r} > 0$ and a number $\nu_{r} > 0$ of quanta per unit volume of its own space. Fix one length $d$, common to all towers and independent of the filling. With the sourcing rule read through a length $\lambda d$ of the extra direction of a five-dimensional tower and with a three-dimensional tower's sheets $\mu d$ apart, the shares and the total are
\[
f_{r} \;=\; \frac{m_{r}\nu_{r}}{m_{6}\nu_{6}} \times
\begin{cases} \lambda d & D_{r} = 4, \\ 1 & D_{r} = 3, \\ 1/(\mu d) & D_{r} = 2, \end{cases}
\qquad
T \;=\; \sum_{r \neq 6} f_{r} .
\]
Premise R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}) is $m_{r} = m$ for all $r$; R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}) is $\nu_{r} V_{D_{r}} d^{D_{r}} = 1$, with $V_{D}$ the volume of the unit ball $\B^{D}$. \emph{Reading of R3.} R3 (\claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction}) says ``one cell radius''. It is read here as $\lambda = \mu = 1$ in the fixed length $d$, not in each tower's own cell radius $a_{r}$, defined by $\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}a_{r}^{D_{r}} = 1$. Under R2 the two readings coincide ($a_{r} = d$); they differ as soon as R2 is varied. Premise R3 as now stated chooses the second, each tower's own cell radius (the Status paragraph below); clause (i) is a statement about the first. Write $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$, \emph{equal mass per ball of radius $d$}, for the statement that $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}}$ takes one value on all populated towers.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(One density law; proved, under the fixed-length reading of R3.)} R1 and R2 together imply $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$. Under $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ and R3 so read, $f_{r} = V_{3}/V_{D_{r}}$ and $T = (11\pi + 16)/3\pi$, the total of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}; with the thicknesses free, $T = 1 + 8/3\mu + 16\lambda/3\pi$, as in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}. $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ implies neither R1 nor R2: for positive numbers $s_{r}$ that are constant on the reversal orbits, with $s_{2} = s_{6} = 1$ and $s_{1} = s_{7}$, $s_{3} = s_{5}$ not both $1$, the filling $m_{r} = s_{r}m$, $\nu_{r} = 1/(s_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}})$ satisfies $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$, violates R1 and R2, and has every share and the total unchanged. It leaves the mirror pair as the population count has it and keeps every equality along the reversal orbits, so it is a model of P1, P2, P3, the common ceiling coupling and R3 in the fixed-length reading (argued for P2: the model equates along the orbits whatever counts as a sector label). So, under that reading, every share depends on R1 and R2 only through $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$. \emph{Under the other reading this fails.} If the thickness is one own cell radius $a_{r}$, then
\[
f_{r} \;=\; \frac{m_{r}}{m_{6}}\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{D_{r}}}\,\Bigl(\frac{a_{6}}{a_{r}}\Bigr)^{3},
\]
which $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ does not fix: with $s_{3} = s_{5} = 16$ and $s_{r} = 1$ elsewhere, $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ holds and the total is $11/3 + 32/3\pi \approx 7.06$. On that reading R2 is used twice, once in the density and once to supply R3's unit, and the shares depend on $m_{r}/a_{r}^{3}$. The stored results that use R1 or R2 separately (the common mass and the cell radius in the cluster bound, R2's number density in the odd towers' population and survival) are not statements of the total.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Democracy of the total mass; proved, given the reading of the stored sphere form.)} Read a tower's mass per unit measure of its Euclidean de Sitter sphere $\Sph^{D_{r}+1}$ as its mass per unit volume of its space divided by one length common to all towers, as the stored sphere form does. Then the total mass of tower $r$ on the sphere of radius $\ell$ is a common factor times $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}\ell^{D_{r}}$, by $|\Sph^{D+1}| = 2\pi V_{D}$. Hence the democracy premise (\claimref{dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass}) is $(\mathrm{E}_{\ell})$, the same kind of law at the de Sitter radius, and with the thickness $\ell$ it gives the same shares (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}). The law and the thickness are tied through one length: $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ with thickness $d'$ gives $V_{3}/V_{D_{r}} \times (d'/d)^{D_{r}-3}$. $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ and $(\mathrm{E}_{\ell})$ are different statements for $d \neq \ell$ and neither implies the other: under R1 and R2 in the length $d$ the total masses on the spheres are in the ratio $(\ell/d)^{D_{r}}$, unequal across dimensions, and the democracy premise leaves $m_{r}$ and $\nu_{r}$ separately free.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The mirror's term is obtained twice; the premise sets are audited.)} At $D_{r} = 3$, $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ gives $f_{2} = 1$ through the sourcing rule. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(i) gives $f_{2} = 1$ from Premises P1, P2, the common ceiling coupling and the copy of content, with P4 discharged for the mirror, and without R1, R2 or R3. The two derivations share P1 (through the sourcing rule), P2 and P3 among the subject's postulates; the first does not have P4 or the common ceiling coupling under it, the second not R1, R2 or R3. So restricted to the reversal pair $\{2, 6\}$, $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ is a consequence of the population count, and it is a premise only on the four odd towers. The two agree exactly on the proton-only branch; on the burning branch of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) the population count gives $f_{2} = 931.8/936.7 \approx 0.9948$ (the stored $0.995$), so R1 read as equal mean mass per baryon fails there by about one part in two hundred and the total is smaller by about $1/200$; both values lie within one standard deviation ($0.065$) of the record's $5.364$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What still moves the total; proved.)} With $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ kept: thicknesses $(\lambda, \mu) = (2, 1)$ and $(1, 2)$ give $11/3 + 32/3\pi$ and $7/3 + 16/3\pi$, each more than five standard deviations from the record; one quantum per cube of side $2d$ in place of the ball, with thickness one side, gives exactly $5$, more than five standard deviations below; a three-dimensional tower read at $D_{r} = 4$ gives $7/3 + 8/\pi$. So R3, the shape of the cell and the dimensions of P3 are each used.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Count; audited on the stored dependence edges and a text search.)} Among the twenty-three postulates of the dark-matter subject: the past cone of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule} contains five on its stored edges, P2, P3, R1, R2, R3, and six with P1, which enters through the sourcing rule that the proposition's proof uses and its edges do not record. The past cone of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}, which takes the mirror's term from the population count, contains seven, P1, P2, P3, P4, R1, R2 and the common ceiling coupling, and eight with R3 as the choice $\lambda = \mu = 1$; the restatements \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-unit-ball-rule} and \claimref{simulations.imported-unit-ball-rule-family} have the same five and eight. A third stored statement of the same total, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}, has the democracy premise and R3. The union over these stored statements of the total is nine; fourteen of the twenty-three lie under none of them. Of the fourteen, four lie under stored results that vary the conditions of the total: P5 (\claimref{synthesis.no-rule-p2-licenses-gives-the-thickness-of-r3}), H1 (\claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}), and H1, H2 and Premise U (\claimref{synthesis.bott-shifted-model-leaves-the-odd-towers-dimension-free}); the remaining ten (CPT covariance, the flag as datum, Hypothesis (S) carried to every tower, the six modelling premises of the cluster simulations and the registered asymmetry) lie under no stored result whose text contains the value $5.364$ or its closed form. The statements of the total were found by that text pattern, which misses statements by reference (the third above was added by hand), so ``under none'' is audited on the search, not proved. The cones also contain postulates of other subjects: under the closed form the four foundation premises (\claimref{synthesis.premise-the-bit}, \claimref{synthesis.premise-minimal-non-commutativity}, \claimref{synthesis.premise-superposition-over-the-integers}, \claimref{synthesis.continuum-completion-premise}); the population-count route adds \claimref{dark-matter.hyp-u-equal-rank-one-eigenvalues} (subject neutrinos), \claimref{scrambling.indifference-structural-premise-series}, \claimref{sheaf.tameness}, \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} and \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}. Three conditions of the closed form are held as text and not as edges: the sourcing rule with P1, the single-ideal clause and the population of the odd towers. By (i) to (iii), under the fixed-length reading, the subject's premises of the total reduce to: P1 for the sourcing rule; P3 for the dimensions; $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ on the four odd towers; R3; and for the mirror's term either $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ on the reversal pair or P2 and the common ceiling coupling. The total remains a fit: $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ and R3 fix the two odd shares $4/3$ and $8/3\pi$ against one measured number.
\end{enumerate}

synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r.technical:
The stored total of dark to baryonic matter is a sum of shares, each the ratio of a tower's mass density, read per unit of this world's volume by the sourcing rule (which rests on P1), to ours. Assume the counted thickness of R3 is one fixed length common to all towers, the length in which the cell of R2 is measured, and not each tower's own cell radius; under R2 the two are the same, and the store's wording, one cell radius, does not say which is meant when R2 is varied. Under that reading a share sees R1 (equal quantum masses) and R2 (one quantum per unit ball) only through their product, equal mass per ball of that radius: a filling in which the odd towers' quanta are heavier by a factor and rarer by the same factor violates both and has the same shares. Under the other reading the statement fails: the same kind of filling, with the five-dimensional towers' quanta sixteen times heavier and rarer, moves the total to about $7.06$. The democracy premise, equal total mass on each tower's de Sitter sphere, is the same kind of law at the de Sitter radius, by $|\Sph^{D+1}| = 2\pi V_{D}$ and given the stored reading of the sphere form; with the thickness equal to that radius it gives the same shares, and neither law implies the other. The mirror's share of one is obtained twice: from the density law at dimension three, and from the population count under P1, P2 and the common ceiling coupling; the two share P1, P2 and P3 among the subject's premises. On the burning branch the second gives about $0.995$, so they disagree there by about half a percent, inside the error bar. The thickness, the ball shape of the cell and the dimensions of P3 each move the total when changed. On the stored dependence edges, five of the subject's twenty-three postulates lie under the closed form (six with P1, held for it as text), eight under the total with the mirror's term taken from the population count, and the democracy premise with R3 under a third stored statement; fourteen lie under no stored statement of the total found by the search, four of them under results that vary its conditions. The cones also hold the four foundation premises and five postulates of other subjects, and the closed form assumes, as text, that the odd towers are populated and that residues $0$ and $4$ are empty. The total remains a fit.

synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r.lay: The series fits the measured ratio of dark matter to ordinary matter, 5.364, with a rule built on several assumptions. This result sorts out which assumptions the number uses. Two of them, that all hidden worlds have quanta of the same mass and that each holds one quantum per unit ball, matter for the number only through their product, the mass per unit ball, as long as the counted thickness is a fixed common length; if the thickness is instead each world's own spacing, this is no longer true and the same change of filling moves the number to about 7. A third assumption, equal total mass in every world, is the same kind of law with a cosmic unit of length, and gives the same shares given the stored reading of it. The share of the mirror world is derived twice, by two routes that agree to within about half a percent. Of the twenty-three assumptions filed under dark matter, at most eight stand under the number on either route, besides the series' foundation premises and five assumptions filed elsewhere, and assuming also that the hidden worlds are populated as the rule supposes. Under all of this the ratio is still fitted, not predicted: two shares are chosen and one number is matched. The series does not adopt that reading: it takes the counted thickness to be each world's own spacing, so the statement above holds only in a reading the series does not use.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} The shares of the Setting are the sourcing rule of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} (a five-dimensional tower's density times the length of its extra direction; a sheet family's density per unit area over the spacing), divided by this world's density. Throughout (i) the thickness is $\lambda d$, $\mu d$ in the fixed length $d$. Under R1 and R2, $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}} = m$ for every $r$, which is $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$. Under $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ with common value $\kappa$, $m_{r}\nu_{r} = \kappa/(V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}})$, so
\[
f_{r} \;=\; \frac{V_{3}\,d^{3}}{V_{D_{r}}\,d^{D_{r}}} \times \bigl(\lambda d,\; 1,\; 1/(\mu d)\bigr)
\;=\; \frac{V_{3}}{V_{D_{r}}} \times \bigl(\lambda,\; 1,\; 1/\mu\bigr)
\]
for $D_{r} = 4, 3, 2$: the unit $d$ and the value $\kappa$ cancel. With $V_{2} = \pi$, $V_{3} = 4\pi/3$, $V_{4} = \pi^{2}/2$ the shares are $4/3\mu$, $1$, $8\lambda/3\pi$, and the sum over the mirror and the two towers of each odd dimension is $1 + 8/3\mu + 16\lambda/3\pi$, which at $\lambda = \mu = 1$ is $(11\pi + 16)/3\pi$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}; with $\lambda = \mu = c$ it is the function of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}). For the rescaled filling, $m_{r}\nu_{r} = m/(V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}})$ whatever the $s_{r}$, so $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ holds with $\kappa = m$ and each $f_{r}$ is as before, while $m_{r} = s_{r}m$ is not constant and $\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}} = 1/s_{r} \neq 1$ on an odd pair. Since, with the thickness a fixed length, $f_{r}$ is a function of the products $m_{r}\nu_{r}$ alone, no share separates R1 and R2 from $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$. The model against the other premises: $s_{2} = s_{6} = 1$ leaves the reversal pair's masses, densities and stored charge as they were, so the population count's equalities ($m_{2} = m_{6}$, $\epsilon_{2} = \epsilon_{6}$) hold; $s_{1} = s_{7}$ and $s_{3} = s_{5}$ keep every quantity equal along the reversal orbits, which is all P2 can ask whatever counts as a sector label; P1, P3 and the common ceiling coupling do not mention the odd towers' fillings; P4 is void on the odd residues. \emph{The other reading.} A tower's own cell radius is $a_{r}$ with $\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}a_{r}^{D_{r}} = 1$. With thickness $a_{r}$, a five-dimensional tower's density per unit of our volume is $m_{r}\nu_{r}a_{r} = m_{r}/(V_{4}a_{r}^{3})$ and a three-dimensional tower's is $m_{r}\nu_{r}/a_{r} = m_{r}/(V_{2}a_{r}^{3})$, against ours $m_{6}/(V_{3}a_{6}^{3})$, which is the displayed formula. In the rescaled filling $a_{r} = s_{r}^{1/D_{r}}d$, so $f_{r} = s_{r}^{1 - 3/D_{r}}\,V_{3}/V_{D_{r}}$: with $s_{3} = s_{5} = 16$ the five-dimensional shares double, $a_{r} = 2d$, and $T = 1 + 8/3 + 32/3\pi = 11/3 + 32/3\pi$. (Check 1: two rescalings constant on reversal orbits keep every share in the fixed-length reading; rescaling the mass without the number density moves the total; in the own-radius reading the same fillings give $11/3 + 32/3\pi$ and $17/9 + 32/3\pi$.)

\emph{(ii).} Let $\sigma_{r} = m_{r}\nu_{r}/(2\pi L)$ be the mass per unit $(D_{r}+1)$-measure, with one length $L$ for all towers (the stored sphere form reads one quantum per unit ball as one quantum per unit sphere, the factor $2\pi$ cancelling; any common $L$ serves). The total mass on the sphere of radius $\ell$ is
\[
M_{r} \;=\; \sigma_{r}\,|\Sph^{D_{r}+1}|\,\ell^{D_{r}+1} \;=\; \frac{\ell}{L}\; m_{r}\nu_{r}\,V_{D_{r}}\,\ell^{D_{r}},
\]
using $|\Sph^{D+1}| = 2\pi V_{D}$, which follows from the recursions $V_{D} = (2\pi/D)V_{D-2}$ and $|\Sph^{n}| = (2\pi/(n-1))|\Sph^{n-2}|$ with $V_{0} = 1$, $V_{1} = 2$, $|\Sph^{1}| = 2\pi$, $|\Sph^{2}| = 4\pi$ by induction on $D$. So $M_{r}$ is the same for all populated towers exactly when $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}\ell^{D_{r}}$ is, which is $(\mathrm{E}_{\ell})$. By (i) the shares under $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ with thickness $d$ are the same for every $d$, and with thickness $d'$ each acquires the factor $(d'/d)^{D_{r}-3}$, which is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}'s agreement of the two forms. Under R1 and R2 in the unit $d$, $M_{r} = (\ell/L)\,m\,(\ell/d)^{D_{r}}$, which takes three different values on $D_{r} = 2, 3, 4$ unless $\ell = d$; and the democracy premise constrains only the products $m_{r}\nu_{r}$. (Check 2: the identity for $D = 0$ to $8$ from the two recursions; equal masses at $\ell = d$, the ratios $(\ell/d)^{D+1}$ of the check's normalisation $L = d$ otherwise.)

\emph{(iii).} At $D_{r} = 3$ the share under $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ is $V_{3}/V_{3} = 1$. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(i) states $f_{2} = \epsilon_{2}n_{2}m_{2}/\epsilon_{6}n_{6}m_{6} = 1$ in its own notation, a ratio of mass densities in two three-dimensional spaces, which is $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ on the pair $\{2, 6\}$ whatever $d$. Its premises are those it names. The first derivation reads the share through the sourcing rule, which rests on P1, so the two share P1, P2 and P3 among the subject's postulates; that the stored cone of the closed form contains neither P4 nor the common ceiling coupling, and that of the population count none of R1, R2 and R3, was read from the stored dependence edges (clause (v)). On the burning branch Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) gives mean masses per baryon $936.7$ and $931.8$ MeV at equal number densities, a ratio $9318/9367 \approx 0.9948$ which it rounds to $0.995$, so $m_{2} \neq m_{6}$ there and the total with that term is smaller by $49/9367$, between $1/200$ and $1/190$. With $3.14159265358 < \pi < 3.14159265359$ both totals lie in $(5.359, 5.365)$, inside $5.364 \pm 0.065$. (Check 3.)

\emph{(iv).} Substitute in the formula of (i): $(\lambda, \mu) = (2, 1)$ gives $1 + 8/3 + 32/3\pi \approx 7.06$ and $(1, 2)$ gives $1 + 4/3 + 16/3\pi \approx 4.03$. For cubic cells of side $2d$, $m_{r}\nu_{r} = m/(2d)^{D_{r}}$, and with thickness $2d$ each odd share is $(2d)^{3}/(2d)^{D_{r}} \times (2d)^{D_{r}-3} = 1$, so $T = 5$, the value the stored note \claimref{note.dark-matter.setting-what-rule-costs} records for cubic cells. A tower with $D_{r} = 2$ read at $D_{r} = 4$ exchanges a term $4/3$ for $8/3\pi$. (Check 4.)

\emph{(v).} The cones were computed from the built graph of the store at the pinned versions, following uses, assumes, founded\_on, specialises and derived\_from edges, and intersected with the list of entities of status postulate and subject dark-matter; the postulates of other subjects in the same cones are listed in the statement. The stored statements of the total and the results that vary it were found by a pattern search of every claim's text for the value $5.364$, $5.3643$ and the closed form (thirteen entities, two of them conjectured observations and one a postulate, with empty cones); Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}, which states the total by reference, was added by hand, and its cone holds the democracy premise and R3. The cone of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} is P1 alone; Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule} has no edge to it, though its proof and R3 are phrased in the sourcing rule, which is why P1 is counted as text for the closed form. The union over the three routes is P1, P2, P3, P4, R1, R2, R3, the common ceiling coupling and the democracy premise. The fourteen outside it are P5, CPT covariance, the flag as datum, H1, H2, Hypothesis (S) carried to every tower, Premise U, the six modelling premises of the cluster simulations and the registered asymmetry. The reduction is (i) to (iii).

\emph{Premises.} The shares are defined by the stored sourcing rule, which is a reading of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} (its metric clause). The sum over the mirror and the four odd towers uses that the odd towers hold matter (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated}) and that residues $0$ and $4$ add nothing (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.single-ideal-at-residues-zero-and-four}); both are conditions of the stored closed form, named in the Setting and in (v).

synthesis.dimmed-burst-time-rescaled-cop.formal:
Let a black hole of the one metric evaporate in the regime where every populated tower's light species are lighter than its temperature, so that the emission coefficients are constant. Write $\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$ for this tower's coefficient in the mass-loss law, $\Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}$ for the gravitational sector's, $\Psi_{\mathrm{odd}}$ for the odd towers', $\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}$ for the total, $g = \Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}/\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$, $o = \Psi_{\mathrm{odd}}/\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$, and let the standard expectation be the hole with this tower and gravitons only, total coefficient $\Psi_{0} = \Psi_{\mathrm{vis}} + \Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}$. Put $D = \Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}/\Psi_{0}$. Let $\tau$ be the hole's remaining lifetime and $N(E;\tau)$ the number of visible quanta per unit energy emitted in its last $\tau$, $N_{0}$ its standard value.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Every channel's flux per unit energy depends on $M$ and $E$ only through $ME$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise}), so $dM/dt = -\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}/M^{2}$ and $M(\tau)^{3} = 3\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}\tau$; at fixed $M$ the visible power is the same as in the standard case (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(i)).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Time rescaling.)} For any visible emission $h(E, M)$ per unit time, secondaries included, the same function in every tower configuration because the exterior metric does not record which tower the mass came from,
\[
N(E;\tau) \;=\; \frac{1}{D}\, N_{0}(E;D\tau):
\]
the visible burst of the last $\tau$ is the standard burst of the last $D\tau$, divided by $D$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Three dimming laws.)} Consequently, at fixed remaining lifetime: the visible energy emitted in the last $\tau$ is $D^{-2/3}$ times its standard value; the hole's temperature is $D^{-1/3}$ times its standard value; and for primary emission, whose flux depends on $E$ and $M$ only through $ME$, the high-energy tail $N(E;\tau) \to C\,E^{-3}/(\Psi_{0}D)$ for $E\,M(\tau)$ large, which does not depend on $\tau$, is $1/D$ times its standard value. Only this primary tail, and the visible fraction of the power at fixed mass, are dimmed by the full ratio.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Floor.)} The mirror's light content copies ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so $D = (2 + g + o)/(1 + g) = 2 + (o - g)/(1 + g)$: $D \ge 2$ if and only if $o \ge g$, and with $o = 0$, $D = 2 - g/(1 + g)$. The factors of (iii) are $D$, $D^{2/3}$ and $D^{1/3}$.
\end{enumerate}
The odd towers enter only through $o$; the burst prediction needs their emission coefficients and no other property of them.

\emph{Scope note.} A populated five-dimensional tower never meets the hypothesis of constant coefficients at every mass: under the interface premise its Kaluza-Klein levels are emission channels of the shared exterior, the mass-loss law gains a term $B/M^{3}$ with $B$ proportional to the fifth direction's extent, and the time-rescaled copy (ii), with the laws (iii) drawn from it, holds for such a tower only for masses well above the crossover mass $M_{\times} = B/A$ of \claimref{synthesis.five-dimensional-tower-kaluza-klein-channels-steepen-burst}(ii); below it $M^{4} = 4B\tau$ and the primary high-energy tail steepens from $E^{-3}$ to $E^{-4}$ above a break.
synthesis.dimmed-burst-time-rescaled-cop.technical:
In the regime where every tower's light species are lighter than the hole's temperature, the greybody-inherited flux makes the mass-loss law $dM/dt = -\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}/M^{2}$. Against the standard expectation, this tower plus gravitons, the total is larger by $D = (2 + g + o)/(1 + g)$, with $g$ and $o$ the gravitational and odd-tower coefficients relative to this tower's and the mirror counted as a copy. The visible emission at a given mass is the same function as in the standard case, so a hole with dark towers passes through the same masses, and emits the same visible spectrum at each, but $D$ times faster: the visible burst of its last $\tau$ is the standard burst of the last $D\tau$, divided by $D$.

Three laws follow at fixed time before the end: the visible energy is dimmed by $D^{2/3}$, the temperature lowered by $D^{1/3}$, and the high-energy tail of the primary spectrum, independent of $\tau$ and falling as $E^{-3}$, dimmed by the full $D$. $D$ is at least $2$ exactly when the odd towers emit at least as much as the gravitational sector, and is $2 - g/(1 + g)$ if they emit nothing.

Scope: if a five-dimensional tower is populated, its Kaluza-Klein levels (under the interface premise) add a term $B/M^{3}$ to the mass-loss law, so these laws hold only for masses well above the crossover mass $M_{\times}$ of \claimref{synthesis.five-dimensional-tower-kaluza-klein-channels-steepen-burst}; below it the remaining lifetime is $M^{4}/(4B)$ and the primary tail steepens to $E^{-4}$.
synthesis.dimmed-burst-time-rescaled-cop.lay: The series predicts that the last explosive moments of a small evaporating black hole should be fainter than usual, because the hole also radiates into hidden worlds. This result says exactly how. The hidden worlds make the hole lose mass faster, so it runs through the same sequence of temperatures in less time. As a result, a telescope watching the final seconds sees the light of a longer stretch of the ordinary burst, squeezed and divided. The very high energy light emitted directly by the hole is dimmed by the full factor (about two from the mirror world alone), but the total light in the final seconds is dimmed less, by that factor to the power two thirds, and the burst looks cooler at a given time before its end.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} By Theorem \claimref{hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise} the flux in each channel is $\frac{1}{2\pi}\Gamma_{s\ell m}(E)\,n_{\pm}(E)$ at $\TH = 1/(8\pi M)$. For the Schwarzschild exterior the transmission coefficients depend on $E$ only through $ME$ (the barriers scale with $M$), and $E/\TH = 8\pi ME$, so each channel's flux per unit energy is $\phi(ME)$ for a function $\phi$ fixed by the channel. The power is then $P(M) = \int E\,\phi(ME)\,dE = M^{-2}\int x\,\phi(x)\,dx$ (substituting $x = ME$), and summing over the channels of every populated tower, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(i) all radiate from the one exterior in proportion to their light degrees of freedom once the temperature exceeds their gaps, gives $dM/dt = -\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}/M^{2}$ with constant $\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}$ in the stated regime. Integrating to the end of the evaporation, $M(\tau)^{3} = 3\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}\tau$, and at fixed $M$ this tower's power $\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}/M^{2}$ is the same as in the standard case. The check verifies the $M^{-2}$ law exactly for polynomial flux shapes of compact support in $ME$.

\emph{(ii).} Let $M_{\Psi}(t)$ be the mass at remaining lifetime $t$ when the total coefficient is $\Psi$, so $M_{\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}}(t)^{3} = 3\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}t = 3\Psi_{0}(Dt) = M_{\Psi_{0}}(Dt)^{3}$. The visible emission per unit time at mass $M$ is a function $h(E, M)$ of the exterior and of this tower's content only: Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(i) states that barriers, transmission coefficients and occupancies do not record which tower the mass came from, and the same holds for the visible secondaries, which are this tower's physics at energy $E$. Hence
\[
N(E;\tau) = \int_{0}^{\tau} h\bigl(E, M_{\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}}(t)\bigr)\,dt = \int_{0}^{\tau} h\bigl(E, M_{\Psi_{0}}(Dt)\bigr)\,dt = \frac{1}{D}\int_{0}^{D\tau} h\bigl(E, M_{\Psi_{0}}(s)\bigr)\,ds = \frac{1}{D}N_{0}(E;D\tau),
\]
with $s = Dt$. The check verifies the identity exactly for emission functions polynomial in $M^{3}$, both with the baseline $\Psi_{0} = \Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$ and with a graviton term in it, and confirms that the plain ratio $N_{0}(E;\tau)/D$ differs from it.

\emph{(iii).} The visible energy emitted in the last $\tau$ is the visible share of the remaining mass, $(\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}/\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}})M_{\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}}(\tau) = D^{-2/3}(\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}/\Psi_{0})M_{\Psi_{0}}(\tau)$, $D^{-2/3}$ times the standard value. The temperature is $1/(8\pi M_{\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}}(\tau)) = D^{-1/3}/(8\pi M_{\Psi_{0}}(\tau))$. For the primary visible flux, $h(E, M) = \phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(ME)$ by (i); with $dt = M^{2}dM/\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}$,
\[
N(E;\tau) = \frac{1}{\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}}\int_{0}^{M(\tau)}\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(ME)\,M^{2}\,dM = \frac{1}{\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}E^{3}}\int_{0}^{EM(\tau)}\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(x)\,x^{2}\,dx,
\]
which for $EM(\tau)$ large tends to $C E^{-3}/\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}} = C E^{-3}/(D\Psi_{0})$ with $C = \int_{0}^{\infty}\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(x)x^{2}\,dx$, finite since the occupancies fall exponentially in $x$, and independent of $\tau$: the tail is $1/D$ times the standard tail. Secondaries obey the exact rescaling (ii) but not this tail law, which needs $h$ to depend on $E$ and $M$ only through $ME$. The check verifies the cube relations exactly and the $\tau$-independence of the tail for a flux shape of compact support. At fixed $M$ the visible power is unchanged and the visible fraction of the total is $1/D$ of its standard value, so the full ratio applies to that fraction and to the primary tail, and not to quantities measured at fixed time before the end.

\emph{(iv).} By Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(i) and (iii) the mirror's light content, and hence its emission coefficient, equals this tower's, so $\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}} = 2\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}} + \Psi_{\mathrm{odd}} + \Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}$ and $D = (2 + g + o)/(1 + g) = 2 + (o - g)/(1 + g)$, which is at least $2$ exactly when $o \ge g$; with $o = 0$ it is $2 - g/(1 + g)$, just below $2$ since $g$ is small for the standard-model content (of order a percent or less, from the literature, cited from memory). The odd towers' content (Propositions \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content} and \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-content}) enters only through $o$, whose value needs the emission of lower- and higher-dimensional fields from the one exterior, which is not derived here.

\emph{Numerical reading (not part of the check).} Burst searches compare the photon fluence of the final $\tau$, for $\tau$ between a fraction of a second and a few hundred seconds, with the standard expectation; their energy band lies near the temperature of the last seconds (a few TeV and above for a hole of the standard-model content, from the literature, cited from memory), where neither the tail law nor the energy law is exact. At $D = 2$ the fluence there is dimmed by a factor between $2^{2/3} \approx 1.59$ and $2$ (computed), and for Euclidean, background-free counting the sensitive volume, which scales as the fluence to the power $3/2$, falls by a factor between $2$ and $2^{3/2} \approx 2.83$; so a rate limit derived for undimmed bursts weakens by that factor.

synthesis.field-strength-heat-kernel-coe.formal:
Under H1, H2 and U (the towers' gauge algebras), (S) where stated, the covariant gauge and the indefinite-form premise of the stored rule, and reading each tower's gauge field as dynamical in its own dimension: let a tower of dimension $d \in \{3, 4, 5\}$ have the algebra $\Cl(p,q)$, $p + q = d$, of its signature ($\Cl(2,1)$, $\Cl(1,2)$; $\Cl(1,3)$, $\Cl(3,1)$; $\Cl(4,1)$, $\Cl(1,4)$), and for a bivector $F$ put $X = -2\langle F^{2}\rangle_{0}$ and, for a representation in which $F$ acts by $M(F)$, the spin weight $s = 4\,\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{tr}\,M(F)^{2}/X$ of \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces}: $M(F)a = a\cdot F$ on vectors and $M(F)\psi = \tfrac12F\psi$ on a left ideal with $n_{c}$ complex components. The stored rule assigns to a field with $n$ components, statistics $\sigma$ and determinant weight $w$ the number $c = \tfrac13\sigma w(n + 6s)$ per unit index, the trace of the flat coefficient $\tfrac1{12}\Omega_{\mu\nu}\Omega^{\mu\nu} + \tfrac12E^{2}$ of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-heat-kernel-coefficients-and-background-field-gauge}(i), which is stated in every dimension.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Spin weights; proved.)} In each of the six algebras $s = -4$ on vectors and $s = -n_{c}/2$ on a left ideal of $n_{c}$ complex components ($n_{c} = 2$ in dimension three, $4$ for a Dirac ideal in four and five). In $\Cl(2,1)$ the ideal's commutant is $\mathrm{span}\{P, w\}$ with $w^{2} = +P$ and contains no unit of square $-1$: there $n_{c}$ means half the real dimension, the complex unit being the $\so(2)$ charge and not an element of the tower's algebra; the weight, a real trace, is unaffected.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The rule in dimension $d$; proved, given the Fact.)} A gauge vector with its ghosts has $c = \tfrac16(d - 24) - \tfrac13 = \tfrac16(d - 26)$ per unit adjoint Casimir, a spinor of $n_{c}$ components $c = n_{c}/3$ per unit index, a complex scalar $\tfrac13$: at $d = 4$ the stored $-\tfrac{11}{3}$, $\tfrac23$, $\tfrac43$; at $d = 3$, $-\tfrac{23}{6}$ and $\tfrac23$; at $d = 5$, $-\tfrac72$ and $\tfrac43$. In the expansion of the Fact this coefficient multiplies $t^{(4-d)/2}$: a logarithm of the cut-off at $d = 4$ only (clause (ii) of the Fact is stated there only), a term finite at short proper time at $d = 3$ and a power of the cut-off at $d = 5$; the squared coupling has mass dimension $4 - d$. So $c$ is a one-loop running coefficient at $d = 4$ and a heat-kernel number, with no regulator-independent meaning as a beta coefficient, at $d = 3$ and $5$. In three dimensions the determinant of the squared Dirac operator is the modulus of the fermion determinant only; its parity-odd phase is the induced Chern-Simons level that the stored phases result uses, and it is not part of $c$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The table on the stored content; computed.)} With the algebras of \claimref{synthesis.gauge-algebra-by-tower} and the content of \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content} and \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-content}: in the three-dimensional towers each $\so(2)$ factor has $c = \tfrac23$ (one unit-charge two-component fermion, no vector term); in the five-dimensional towers the colour factor has $c = 3\cdot(-\tfrac72) + 2\cdot\tfrac43\cdot\tfrac12 = -\tfrac{55}{6}$ under (S) (triplets $U$, $D$) and $-\tfrac{59}{6}$ without (S), and the abelian factor $\tfrac43\sum\dim\cdot Y^{2} = \tfrac{32}{9}$ under (S) and $\tfrac{16}{9}$ without, in the normalisation $Y = s - k/3$ of the stored content. Read in four dimensions, one copy of the five-dimensional content has $b_{3} = -\tfrac{29}{3}$ under (S), the colour coefficient of one generation, and $-\tfrac{31}{3}$ without, against the stored $-7$ of the visible sector at three generations, which three copies of the (S) content would equal; the number of copies is not stored.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What follows and what does not; argued, consistent with the stored obstructions, to which it adds the coefficients.)} This clause concerns the odd towers; the mirror tower's coefficients and scale are the visible ones, ratio $1$, under the common-ceiling premise (\claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), (iv)), which does not reach the odd towers. The store already records that off $d = 4$ the coupling is dimensionful with no fixed length, that no coupling value is derived and that no premise equates couplings across to the odd towers (\claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}); that the three-dimensional towers are abelian with a dimensionful coupling, no transmutation and bare masses, and that nothing confines in five dimensions (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.r1-has-no-mechanism-odd-towers}); and that the five-dimensional gauge theory is infrared free, its reduction to four dimensions with the fifth direction one cell radius deep giving a confinement scale below $\pi/L$ by more than $e^{-250}$ (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}(ii)). In the three-dimensional towers the stored phases are decided by the effective Chern-Simons level, not by the sign of $c$ (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases}), and the only scales are the dimensionful coupling (the topological mass $e^{2}/2\pi$ of the stored phases) and the free bare masses. The numbers of (iii) are consistent with these: under a different hypothesis, a common dimensionless coupling $\alpha_{0}$ at a common scale with massless content, which no stored statement supplies, the four-dimensional reading would give at one loop $\ln(\Lambda_{5}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{vis}}) = (2\pi/\alpha_{0})(\tfrac17 - \tfrac{3}{29}) = (2\pi/\alpha_{0})\tfrac{8}{203}$; this is a different hypothesis from that of the stored reduction (under R3) and does not contradict its verdict. No scale ratio for an odd tower follows from the store.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.field-strength-heat-kernel-coe.technical: The series derives the one-loop running of the visible gauge couplings from traces of the squared spin generator in the spacetime algebra, and derives a gauge algebra and matter content for each dark tower, but had not put the two together. The spin traces turn out to be the same in the three- and five-dimensional towers' algebras as in four dimensions, so the same rule yields a number per field in every dimension; for a gauge vector with ghosts it is $(d - 26)/6$. That number governs logarithmic running only in four dimensions. In three dimensions the coupling carries a mass dimension and the stored analysis already decides confinement by a topological level; in five the coupling has inverse mass dimension and the one-loop term is a power of the cut-off. A table is given for the stored content, with the four-dimensional reading of the five-dimensional content beside it, and the inputs a confinement-scale ratio would need are listed: none is in the store except for the mirror tower, where the ratio is one.
synthesis.field-strength-heat-kernel-coe.lay: The strong force gets stronger at long distances, which is why quarks are confined, and the series can compute that trend for our own sector from the algebra of spacetime. The dark sectors of the series live on towers of other dimensions with their own forces, so one can ask whether those forces confine too and at what scale. The same algebraic calculation goes through in three and five dimensions and gives definite numbers. But only in four dimensions do those numbers describe a force that changes slowly with distance; in three and five dimensions the strength of a force has a built-in length scale and the numbers do not settle the question. For the mirror copy of our own sector the answer is already known: it behaves exactly like ours. For the odd-dimensional towers, a confinement scale would need information the series does not contain. The numbers hold under the series' premises for what the towers contain, and where stated under the slot-module hypothesis.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} On vectors $M(F)a = a\cdot F = \tfrac12(aF - Fa)$ is the map with matrix $F^{\mu}{}_{\nu}$, antisymmetric with respect to the metric, so $\mathrm{tr}\,M(F)^{2} = F^{\mu}{}_{\nu}F^{\nu}{}_{\mu} = -F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}$, and with the normalisation $\langle F^{2}\rangle_{0} = -X/2$ of \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces} this is $-X$: $s = -4$ in every signature and dimension. On a left ideal $AP$, $P$ an idempotent, the real trace of left multiplication by $x$ is the trace over the whole algebra of $y \mapsto xyP$, which is $\sum_{b}\langle b^{-1}xbP\rangle_{0}$ over the blades $b$. For a blade $x$ the sum $\sum_{b}b^{-1}xb$ is $2^{d}x$ if $x$ is central and $0$ otherwise (each generator either commutes or anticommutes with $x$, and a non-central blade anticommutes with half of the blades). $F^{2} = \langle F^{2}\rangle_{0} + \langle F^{2}\rangle_{4}$, and blades of grade four are not central for $d \le 5$; so the real trace of $\tfrac14F^{2}$ on $AP$ is $\tfrac14\langle F^{2}\rangle_{0}$ times the real dimension $2n_{c}$, its complex trace $\tfrac14 n_{c}\langle F^{2}\rangle_{0} = -n_{c}X/8$, and $s = -n_{c}/2$. In $\Cl(2,1)$, with $P = \tfrac12(1 + e_{0}e_{2})$, the commutant $PAP$ of the ideal is spanned by $P$ and $w = IP$, $I$ the central pseudoscalar of square $+1$, so $w^{2} = P$ (checked). The check evaluates both traces on a generic rational bivector in each algebra, with ideals of $n_{c} = 2$ complex components in dimension three and $4$ in four and five.

\emph{(ii).} By clause (iii) of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-heat-kernel-coefficients-and-background-field-gauge} the quantum gauge field is a real boson on the vector index ($\sigma = 1$, $w = \tfrac12$, $n = d$, $s = -4$): $\tfrac13\cdot\tfrac12(d - 24)$; its ghosts are a complex scalar of opposite statistics ($\sigma = -1$, $w = 1$, $n = 1$, $s = 0$): $-\tfrac13$; the squared Dirac operator has $\sigma = -1$, $w = \tfrac12$, $n = n_{c}$, $s = -n_{c}/2$: $-\tfrac16(n_{c} - 3n_{c}) = n_{c}/3$. By clause (i) of the Fact the flat local part of $a_{4}$ in dimension $n$ is $(4\pi)^{-n/2}\int\mathrm{tr}(\tfrac12E^{2} + \tfrac1{12}\Omega^{2})$ and enters $\mathrm{Tr}\,e^{-tD}$ with $t^{(4-n)/2}$; the proper-time integral $\int dt\,t^{-1}t^{(4-n)/2}$ is logarithmic at its lower end only for $n = 4$, converges there for $n = 3$ and diverges as a power for $n = 5$. The gauge field has mass dimension $(d - 2)/2$ with the coupling in the covariant derivative, so the squared coupling has dimension $4 - d$.

\emph{(iii).} Three dimensions: by \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content}(i) each factor couples to one two-component fermion of unit charge; an abelian factor has no adjoint Casimir. Five dimensions: by \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-content} the species under (S) are $U$ $(3, \tfrac23)$, $D$ $(3, -\tfrac13)$, $E$ $(1, -1)$, $N$ $(1, 0)$, four-component Dirac fields, and without (S) one triplet of $Y = \tfrac23$; $C_{2} = 3$ and $T = \tfrac12$ on the triplet (clause (3) of the spin-trace result); $\sum\dim\cdot Y^{2} = \tfrac43 + \tfrac13 + 1 = \tfrac83$. The four-dimensional reading replaces $-\tfrac72$ by $-\tfrac{11}{3}$: $-11 + \tfrac43 = -\tfrac{29}{3}$. The algebras are those of \claimref{synthesis.gauge-algebra-by-tower}.

\emph{(iv).} Stored statements: \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows} (dimensionful coupling off four dimensions, no coupling value, no premise reaching the odd towers), \claimref{dark-tower-matter.r1-has-no-mechanism-odd-towers} and \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}(ii) (the stored reduction and its scale); \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), (iv) for the mirror and for the scope of the common-coupling premise; \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases} for the phases of the three-dimensional towers. The one-loop relation $\Lambda = \mu_{0}\exp(2\pi/(b\,\alpha_{0}))$ for $b < 0$ gives the displayed difference with $b = -7$ and $-\tfrac{29}{3}$. The clause is a reading: it lists what a ratio would need and finds none of it stored.

synthesis.five-dimensional-tower-kaluza-.formal:
Let the two five-dimensional towers be populated, with their fields on the one metric's exterior times a fifth direction of extent $L_{f}$ that the metric does not see (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.sourcing-rule-forced-not-chosen}: a quantum with momentum $p_{5}$ along it appears as a four-dimensional quantum of mass $|p_{5}|$), and with the natural condition at the ends that keeps a zero mode (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}(v)), or with the fifth direction closed; $L_{f}$ is at least the counted thickness of R3, and equal to it when the matter fills the fifth direction. Let a black hole of the one metric, of mass $M$ and temperature $\TH = 1/(8\pi M)$, evaporate under the interface premise of Theorem \claimref{hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Level sum.)} The Kaluza-Klein levels have masses $\mu_{k} = k\pi/L_{f}$, $k \ge 0$ (or $2\pi|k|/L_{f}$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, closed), and the number of levels of mass at most $\mu$ differs from $L_{f}\mu/\pi$ by at most one. Each level of each species $s$ is a channel of the exterior whose power is $M^{-2}\psi_{s}(M\mu)$, with $\psi_{s}$ of bounded variation. The tower's coefficient in the mass-loss law is therefore
\[
\Psi_{5}(M) \;=\; \frac{L_{f}}{\pi M}\sum_{s} I_{s} + R(M), \qquad I_{s} = \int_{0}^{\infty}\psi_{s}(y)\,dy > 0, \qquad |R(M)| \le \sum_{s}\mathrm{TV}(\psi_{s}),
\]
so that $-M^{2}\,dM/dt = A(M) + B/M$ with $B = \sum_{\text{5D towers}}(L_{f}/\pi)\sum_{s}I_{s} > 0$ and $A(M)$ bounded: this tower, the mirror, the gravitational sector, the three-dimensional towers (taken bounded) and the remainders $R$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Mass-time law.)} With $A_{+}$ an upper bound of $A$ and $V = \sum\mathrm{TV}(\psi_{s})$ over both towers, the remaining lifetime obeys $M^{4}/(4(B + A_{+}M)) \le \tau \le M^{4}/(4(B - VM))$ for $M < B/V$, so $M(\tau)^{4} = 4B\tau\,(1 + O(M/M_{\times}))$ below the crossover mass $M_{\times} = B/A$, against $M(\tau)^{3} = 3\Psi\tau$ for constant coefficients. The constant-coefficient regime of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.dimmed-burst-time-rescaled-copy} holds for a populated five-dimensional tower only for $M \gg M_{\times}$; below it no constant $D$ makes the burst a time-rescaled copy of the standard one.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Tail.)} For primary visible emission $\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(ME)$ with $x^{3}\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(x)$ integrable, the visible quanta per unit energy emitted in the last $\tau$ obey $E^{4}N(E;\tau) \to C_{3}/B$ as $E \to \infty$, for every $\tau > 0$, with $C_{k} = \int_{0}^{\infty}\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(x)x^{k}\,dx$, against $E^{3}N(E;\tau) \to C_{2}/\Psi$ for constant coefficients. For constant $A$ and a hole far above $M_{\times}$ at the start, $N(E) = E^{-3}\int_{0}^{\infty}\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(x)\,x^{3}\,dx/(Ax + BE)$: the time-integrated tail falls as $E^{-3}$ below and as $E^{-4}$ above a break at $E_{b} = (A/B)(C_{3}/C_{2})$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What the break measures.)} $E_{b}$ and the crossover temperature $T_{\times} = 1/(8\pi M_{\times}) = A/(8\pi B)$ are inversely proportional to $L_{f}$, with a coefficient fixed by the towers' contents and the exterior's transmission coefficients. The extent of the fifth direction, which gravity cannot measure (Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity}), sets the evaporation spectrum.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.five-dimensional-tower-kaluza-.technical: A five-dimensional tower's fields live on the shared exterior times a fifth direction the metric does not see, so each field is a ladder of four-dimensional fields of masses spaced by $\pi/L_{f}$, the Kaluza-Klein levels the store already counts in the cosmological bath. Under the interface premise each level is an emission channel of the shared exterior, and its power depends on the hole's mass only through $M\mu$ and the scaling $M^{-2}$. Summing the levels, whose number below a given mass grows linearly with $L_{f}$, gives a coefficient $(L_{f}/\pi M)\sum I_{s}$ plus a bounded remainder: the mass-loss law gains a term $B/M^{3}$. Below the crossover mass $M_{\times} = B/A$ that term dominates, the remaining lifetime is $M^{4}/(4B)$ instead of $M^{3}/(3\Psi)$, and the time-rescaling law of the dimmed burst no longer applies. The primary high-energy tail integrated over the burst steepens from $E^{-3}$ to $E^{-4}$ above a break energy inversely proportional to $L_{f}$, so the burst spectrum measures the extent of the fifth direction, which gravity cannot.
synthesis.five-dimensional-tower-kaluza-.lay: On the standard assumption that a black hole's radiation is fed by its horizon in every channel, a hidden world with an extra space direction can absorb the radiation of a small black hole in many more ways than ours can, because each kind of particle in it comes in a whole ladder of versions, one for each way of vibrating across the extra direction. The hotter the hole, the more rungs of the ladder it can reach, so as the hole shrinks and heats up it pours more and more of its energy into that world. Its final stage then runs differently from the standard picture: it loses mass on a faster schedule, and the very energetic light it sends us falls off more steeply with energy above a certain break. Where the break sits depends on the size of the extra direction, which gravity alone could never reveal.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} On flat $\R^{4,1}$ the five-dimensional tower's fields meet the gravitational gauge fields only on the shared directions: $\hb^{-1}(e_{5}) = e_{5}$ and the rotation gauge field has no component along or into $e_{5}$, since the metric does not see the fifth direction (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.sourcing-rule-forced-not-chosen}(i)). The vector derivative splits as the gauged four-dimensional part plus $e_{5}\partial_{5}$, the exterior is the same for every value of the fifth coordinate, and a field with dependence $\cos(\mu y)$ or $e^{I_4\mu y}$ along $e_{5}$ (the field theory's unit $I_4$, acting on the right) is a four-dimensional field of mass $\mu$ on the one metric's exterior, which is the relation $p^{\mu}p_{\mu} = m^{2} + p_{5}^{2}$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.sourcing-rule-forced-not-chosen}(ii). The horizon seen by these fields is the hole's horizon times the whole fifth direction: no part of the fifth direction lies outside it, because nothing in the exterior depends on the fifth coordinate. This is the reading Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}(i), (iii) already uses when it counts the Kaluza-Klein levels as light degrees of freedom of the bath. A hole localised in the fifth direction, with each level coupling through an overlap of order $r_{\mathrm{h}}/L_{f}$, would need the fifth direction to carry the metric, which Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity} excludes; that reading is not available here.

\emph{(i).} With the natural condition at the ends the modes along the fifth direction are $\cos(k\pi y/L_{f})$, $k \ge 0$, masses $k\pi/L_{f}$; on a closed fifth direction of length $L_{f}$ they are $e^{2\pi I_4 k y/L_{f}}$, masses $2\pi|k|/L_{f}$, doubly degenerate above zero. In both cases the counting function $\mathcal{N}(\mu)$ (levels of mass at most $\mu$) satisfies $\mathcal{N}(\mu) - L_{f}\mu/\pi \in [-1, 1]$. By Theorem \claimref{hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise}, each level of each species is an exterior channel whose flux per unit energy is $(1/2\pi)\sum_{\ell}(2\ell+1)\Gamma_{s\ell}(\omega;\mu)\,n_{\pm}(\omega/\TH)$; the barrier of a field of mass $\mu$ on the Schwarzschild exterior scales with $M$, so $\Gamma$ depends on $M\omega$ and $M\mu$ only, and $\omega/\TH = 8\pi M\omega$. The power in the level is therefore $M^{-2}\psi_{s}(M\mu)$ with $\psi_{s}(y) = \int x\,\phi_{s}(x, y)\,dx$, positive, and falling as $e^{-8\pi y}$ for large $y$ because a quantum of energy $\omega \ge \mu$ is Boltzmann suppressed; it is of bounded variation. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(i) says the same thing at the level of counting: the hole's energy is returned to each tower in proportion to its light degrees of freedom once the temperature exceeds their gaps, and the gaps of a five-dimensional tower are the level spacing $\pi/L_{f}$. Summing over levels as a Stieltjes integral and integrating by parts against $e(\mu) = \mathcal{N}(\mu) - L_{f}\mu/\pi$, which vanishes below zero and satisfies $|e| \le 1$,
\[
\sum_{k}\psi_{s}(M\mu_{k}) = \int_{0^{-}}^{\infty}\psi_{s}(M\mu)\,d\mathcal{N}(\mu) = \frac{L_{f}}{\pi M}\int_{0}^{\infty}\psi_{s}(y)\,dy - \int_{0^{-}}^{\infty} e(\mu)\,d\psi_{s}(M\mu),
\]
and the last term is bounded by $\mathrm{TV}(\psi_{s})$. Multiplying by $M^{-2}$ and summing over species and over the two towers gives (i). The check verifies the inequality $|hS(h) - \int\psi| \le h\,\mathrm{TV}(\psi)$, $h = \pi M/L_{f}$, exactly for both level sets on monotone and non-monotone polynomial shapes, with exact expected sums, and the counting bounds.

\emph{(ii).} Write $\Psi(M) = A(M) + \Psi_{5}(M)$ for the total, so $|dM/dt| = \Psi(M)/M^{2}$ and $M\Psi(M) \in [B - VM,\ B + A_{+}M]$ by (i), $A_{+}$ bounding the remaining coefficients (this tower and the mirror, constant once their light species are below $\TH$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.dimmed-burst-time-rescaled-copy}(i)); the gravitational sector; the three-dimensional towers, taken bounded; and $V$). The remaining lifetime is $\tau(M) = \int_{0}^{M} m^{3}\,dm/(m\Psi(m))$, and the integrand lies between $m^{3}/(B + A_{+}M)$ and $m^{3}/(B - VM)$ on $[0, M]$, which integrate to the stated bounds; so $4B\tau/M^{4} \in [B/(B + A_{+}M),\ B/(B - VM)]$, which tends to one as $M \to 0$. For constant $A$ and no remainder, $\tau(M) = \int_{0}^{M}m^{3}\,dm/(Am + B)$ lies between $M^{3}/(3A) - BM^{2}/(2A^{2})$ and $M^{3}/(3A)$, the constant-coefficient law above $M_{\times} = B/A$. If a constant $D$ made the burst a time-rescaled copy, $M(\tau)^{3}/\tau$ would be constant; under the pure law $M^{4} = 4B\tau$ it is $(4B)^{3/4}\tau^{-1/4}$. The check verifies the integrand bounds at sample points, the exact integrals of the bounding polynomials, the squeeze, the pure law on fourth powers and three different values of the would-be $D$.

\emph{(iii).} The primary visible flux depends on $E$ and $M$ only through $ME$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.dimmed-burst-time-rescaled-copy}(i)), and $dt = M^{3}dM/(M\Psi(M))$, so with $x = EM$
\[
E^{4}N(E;\tau) = \int_{0}^{EM(\tau)}\frac{\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(x)\,x^{3}}{(x/E)\,\Psi(x/E)}\,dx .
\]
For each fixed $x$ the denominator tends to $B$ as $E \to \infty$. On $x \le BE/(2V)$ it is at least $B/2$, so the integrand is dominated by $2x^{3}\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}(x)/B$; on $x > BE/(2V)$ the denominator is at least $(x/E)\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$ and that part is at most $E\int_{BE/2V}^{\infty}x^{2}\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}\,dx/\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$, which tends to zero since $\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}$ falls exponentially. Dominated convergence gives $E^{4}N \to C_{3}/B$. With constant coefficients the same substitution gives $E^{3}N \to C_{2}/\Psi$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.dimmed-burst-time-rescaled-copy}(iii)). For constant $A$ and $M(\tau) \to \infty$ the integral is exactly $E^{-3}\int\phi_{\mathrm{vis}}x^{3}\,dx/(Ax + BE)$, whose two asymptotes $C_{2}/(AE^{3})$ and $C_{3}/(BE^{4})$ cross at $E_{b} = (A/B)(C_{3}/C_{2})$. For the mixed law $M\Psi(M) = AM + B$ and a flux shape supported on $[\tfrac12, 1]$ ($C_{2} = 23/1920$, $C_{3} = 3/320$) the check computes exact brackets of $N(E)$ itself (bounding the denominator on subintervals, or the factor $1/(1 + B/(AM))$ on the support, and integrating the polynomial numerators exactly), shows $E^{4}N$ closing on $C_{3}/B$ at high energy and $E^{3}N$ on $C_{2}/A$ at low energy, with the wrong constants excluded, brackets $N(2E)/N(E)$ near $1/16$ above the break and near $1/8$ below it, and verifies the two pure laws exactly.

\emph{(iv).} $B$ is linear in $L_{f}$ with coefficient $\sum_{s}I_{s}/\pi$ per tower, and $A$ does not involve $L_{f}$, so $M_{\times}$, $T_{\times}$ and $E_{b}$ scale as $L_{f}$, $1/L_{f}$ and $1/L_{f}$.

\emph{Numerical reading (argued; not part of the check).} In the geometric-optics limit $\sum_{\ell}(2\ell+1)\Gamma \approx (\omega^{2} - \mu^{2})\,b_{c}(v)^{2}$, with the critical impact parameter of a massive particle of speed $v$ on the Schwarzschild exterior, $b_{c}^{2} = M^{2}\bigl(8v^{4} + 20v^{2} - 1 + (1 + 8v^{2})^{3/2}\bigr)/(2v^{4})$ (cited from memory; it gives $27M^{2}$ at $v = 1$ and angular momentum $4\mu M$ as $v \to 0$, both standard). Numerical integration (work script, floating point) gives a level sum of about $1.07\,L_{f}\TH$ zero-mode equivalents per bosonic degree of freedom and $1.15\,L_{f}\TH$ per fermionic one. So $T_{\times}$ is of order $1/L_{f}$, times the ratio of this tower's and the mirror's light degrees of freedom to the five-dimensional towers'. Under co-expansion of the fifth direction $L_{f}$ is at least the baryon spacing, about $0.98$ m, so $1/L_{f} \le 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$ eV and every hole hotter than that (below about $10^{29}$ g) is below the crossover: at $\TH = 10$ MeV the visible fraction of the power is of order $10^{-14}$, and the lifetime of a hole of initial mass $M_{0} \ll M_{\times}$ is $(3/4)(M_{0}/M_{\times})$ times its constant-coefficient value. With a static fifth direction and R2, R3 as deposit clauses, $L_{f}$ is the deposit-epoch cell radius, $L_{f}T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ between about $390$ and $1170$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}(i)), so $T_{\times}$ is of order $T_{\mathrm{desc}}/10^{3}$: about a keV for a descent at an MeV, beyond any burst search for a descent near the rung scale. The three-dimensional towers enter $A$ differently: their fields live on sheets, and under the interface premise only a sheet that meets the horizon has near-horizon channels, so a hole far smaller than the sheet spacing receives their emission only through the sheets it holds; whether a hole keeps the sheets that crossed it at formation is a question of sheet dynamics the series does not settle (argued; not used above).

\emph{Which mode space the channels are counted in (argued; not part of the check).} The channels of (i) are emission channels: exterior channels of the one metric's horizon, one per level, species, partial wave and energy, each with its near-horizon occupancy, as the interface premise counts them; they are radiated light degrees of freedom. They are not identified here with arrays of the horizon's boundary-mode space, and nothing above depends on such an identification: levels with $\mu \gg \TH$ are Boltzmann suppressed, so only the set of about $L_{f}\TH$ levels below the temperature radiates, and the results do not depend on the ultraviolet extent of the level count. If the boundary modes of a five-dimensional field are counted one array set per Kaluza-Klein level (equivalently, by the counting function of (i), one per resolution cell of the fifth direction; the two are one count, not a choice), then the count about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$ that the common number $N$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number} fixes is a count of light rays (one array each), the arrays per ray depend on the tower's content as they already do among four-dimensional towers, and a horizon entropy summed over towers would be extensive in $L_{f}$; neither is used here.
