synthesis.mirror-asymmetry-route-one.formal:
Let $\Phi : (\sigma, \mu, \rho) \mapsto (\sigma, \mu, -\rho)$ be the scale-independent map from this tower's tractor fibre, metric $h$ of signature $(2,4)$, to the mirror's, metric $h'$ of signature $(4,2)$, with $h'(\Phi X, \Phi Y) = -h(X, Y)$ (the proof of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}), extended to $V_{\C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\Phi$ carries every Witt pair $(W, W')$ of $(V_{\C}, h)$ to the Witt pair $(\Phi W, \Phi W')$ of $(V_{\C}, h')$, with $\Phi W = W$ when $W$ is spanned by the $\sigma$-direction and vectors of $\mu_{\C}$. On the Fock modules, $\Lambda\Phi : \Lambda W' \to \Lambda \Phi W'$ intertwines the creation operators, intertwines the annihilation operators up to the sign $-1$ that the reversed form puts on every contraction, and intertwines every mode number operator exactly, the two signs cancelling. So $\Phi$ carries the Fock grade $k$ to grade $k$, particles to particles, and the asymmetry per mode of this tower, measured against $W$, to the mirror's measured against $\Phi W$, with sign $+1$. The composite $\Phi \circ C$ with the flag conjugate $C : v_{j} \leftrightarrow w_{j}$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation} is a second anti-isometry, carrying $W$ to $\Phi W'$, in the other family (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}), and the asymmetry with sign $-1$.
\item[(ii)] Hence the first route of clause (v) of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}, the audit along the reversal orbit, gives $\epsilon_{2} = +\epsilon_{6}$ exactly when the mirror is oriented by $\Phi W$, and $\epsilon_{2} = -\epsilon_{6}$ if by $\Phi W'$. Which holds is a discrete datum of the same kind as the orientation itself: conjugation of the mirror's kinematic data alone, an automorphism under the first premise of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation}, exchanges the two, so no kinematic or dynamical result fixes it. It is fixed by the orientation clause of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} or by Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} applied to that discrete datum; route one therefore needs an orientation input of route two's kind: P1's orientation clause, or P2 applied to the bit.
\item[(iii)] Route one applies Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} to a continuous datum of the descent along the reversal orbit, the reach at which Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} obtains $\xi = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$, excluded. So route one stands only under a scoping of P2 that separates the asymmetry per mode from the energy deposited per unit charge. Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} at version 2 states one: it equates labels, not states, so it reaches the stored charge $Q = \epsilon N$; in the boundary-mode model of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not} that scoping leaves the temperature free on every finite window, and on the full algebra exactly when the Powers-Stormer sum of its (iii) converges, and route one stands at that scope. When infinitely many boundary modes share a frequency band the same scoping reaches $\xi$ and gives $\xi = 1$, and route one does not stand there.
\end{enumerate}
Under P2 at version 2 clause (v) has both routes: route two by the orientation clause of P1, and route one by the audit with P2 as scoped, which equates along the orbit the labels of the descent, among them the stored asymmetry $Q = \epsilon N$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(i)) and the orientation bit of (ii), and not the temperature ratio where (iii) leaves it free (on finite windows, or when that sum converges). The claim that the audit stands with P2 at its version-1 reach does not survive Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2}.
synthesis.mirror-asymmetry-route-one.technical: The mirror tower is this tower's tractor geometry with the metric's sign reversed, and the two are related by one canonical map that flips the sign of the form. That map keeps every maximal isotropic subspace isotropic, so it carries this tower's Witt flag to a flag of the mirror; on the Fock modules it keeps creation operators, flips the sign of annihilation operators, and so keeps every number operator and the Fock grade. Particles go to particles, and the asymmetry per mode is carried with its sign. Composing with the flag conjugate gives a second sign-reversing map that exchanges particles and antiparticles. The audit route to the equality of the two towers' asymmetries therefore needs the mirror to be oriented by the image of this tower's flag, a discrete datum that no structure fixes, as in the seventeenth refutation; it is supplied by the single-flag clause of P1 or by P2 applied to that bit. The audit route also applies P2 to a continuous datum of the descent along the reversal orbit, exactly the reach that a later note shows forces the mirror to the photon temperature and is excluded by the effective number of neutrino species. P2 at version 2 is scoped in exactly that way, to labels such as the stored charge and not to states such as the temperature. In the boundary-mode model that scoping leaves the temperature free on every finite window, and on the infinite mode algebra only when the Powers-Stormer sum converges; with infinitely many modes in one frequency band it reaches the temperature again and gives the excluded hot mirror. So the clause has both routes, under P1's orientation clause, or by the audit under P2 as scoped, the second only where the deposited mode set is effectively finite.
synthesis.mirror-asymmetry-route-one.lay: The dark-matter paper argues that the mirror world has the same small excess of matter over antimatter as ours, by two routes. One route says nature would not make an unexplained difference between the two worlds. This result checks the step that route skipped: the natural map between the two worlds does send matter to matter, not to antimatter, so if the worlds are matched by it an excess equal in size is also equal in sign. But whether the mirror is matched to us that way is itself a choice nothing fixes, the same kind of choice as which of matter and antimatter we call matter, so the route needs an assumption about orientation after all. And the same reasoning, applied to the mirror's temperature, gives a hot mirror that observations exclude, so the route also needs a reason to apply the rule to the excess and not to the heat. The rule as the framework now states it supplies that reason: it applies to labels, such as the excess, and not to states, such as the heat. That works only if the hidden sector's relevant modes are effectively finite in number; with infinitely many modes at similar energies the heat becomes a label too, and the route fails again.

proofs.main:
\emph{Step 1 (the map on the flag).} The proof of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe} gives $\Phi$ and $h'(\Phi X, \Phi Y) = -h(X, Y)$; a linear map with this property sends $h$-isotropic subspaces to $h'$-isotropic ones of the same dimension and keeps the pairing $W \times W' \to \C$ nondegenerate, so $(\Phi W, \Phi W')$ is a Witt pair of $h'$, and $\dim(\Phi W_{1} \cap \Phi W_{2}) = \dim(W_{1} \cap W_{2})$ for any two maximal isotropic subspaces, so the family relation is kept. In a Witt basis $n_{a}, p_{1}, p_{2} \mid n_{b}, q_{1}, q_{2}$ with $n_{a}$ the $\sigma$-direction, $n_{b}$ the $\rho$-direction and $p_{i}, q_{i} \in \mu_{\C}$, $\Phi$ is $\mathrm{diag}(1,1,1,-1,1,1)$, so $\Phi W = W$ and $\Phi W' = W'$ as subspaces.

\emph{Step 2 (the Fock modules).} Let $c(v) = v \wedge$ for $v \in W'$ and $c(w) = 2\iota_{h(w, \cdot)}$ for $w \in W$, so that $c(x)^{2} = h(x,x)$; likewise $c'$ for $h'$. Then $c'(\Phi v)\,\Lambda\Phi = \Lambda\Phi\,c(v)$ and, because $h'(\Phi w, \Phi v) = -h(w, v)$, $c'(\Phi w)\,\Lambda\Phi = -\Lambda\Phi\,c(w)$. The mode number operator is $N_{j} = c(v_{j})c(w_{j})/2h(w_{j}, v_{j})$, and for the mirror $N'_{j} = c'(\Phi v_{j})c'(\Phi w_{j})/2h'(\Phi w_{j}, \Phi v_{j})$; the sign of the product and the sign of the normalisation cancel, so $N'_{j}\,\Lambda\Phi = \Lambda\Phi\,N_{j}$, and the grade $\sum_{j} N_{j}$ is intertwined. The particle-antiparticle labelling is the grade pairing $k \leftrightarrow 3 - k$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation}, so it is carried with sign $+1$, and so is any asymmetry measured against the flag. The flag conjugate $C$ exchanges $v_{j}$ and $w_{j}$; it is an isometry of $h$, $\Phi \circ C$ is an anti-isometry carrying $W$ onto $\Phi W'$, and $W$, $W'$ lie in opposite families since they meet in $0$ and $m = 3$ is odd (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}); so $\Phi \circ C$ carries grade $k$ to grade $3 - k$ and the asymmetry with sign $-1$. The check verifies all of this in exact rational arithmetic on the Witt basis, with the signatures $(2,4)$ and $(4,2)$ of the real forms.

\emph{Step 3 (route one needs the orientation).} Clause (v) of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one} equates the two towers' asymmetries along the reversal orbit. Measured against each tower's own flag, the equation reads $\epsilon_{2} = +\epsilon_{6}$ if the mirror's flag is $\Phi W$ and $-\epsilon_{6}$ if it is $\Phi W'$, by Step 2. Applying the flag conjugate to the mirror's Clifford bundle alone is, under the first premise of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation} (conjugation is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure), an automorphism of the two towers' joint kinematic data, the towers sharing only the metric, which it fixes; it exchanges the two assignments. By that proposition's covariance argument, no kinematic or dynamical result fixes the assignment, and it is supplied by a premise: P1's orientation clause, or P2 read as refusing a per-tower orientation, the reading the P1 attack note gives it.

\emph{Step 4 (the reach).} Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} applies P2, at the reach clause (v) uses (a difference of two continuous data of one reversal orbit is an uncaused distinction), to the temperature ratio, a datum of the descent of the same kind, and obtains $\xi = 1$, $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$, excluded. Route one at that reach therefore yields an excluded consequence alongside its intended one; it can be kept only with a scoping of P2 that separates the two data, which P2 at version 2 states (labels, not states; the stored charge is a label and, in the boundary-mode model of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}, the temperature is not on any finite window, nor on the full algebra when the Powers-Stormer sum of its (iii) converges), and at that scope route one stands; when infinitely many boundary modes share a frequency band that theorem's scoping reaches $\xi$ and gives $\xi = 1$, and route one does not stand there. synthesis.mirror-extensions-causal-conve.formal:
Write the mirror of a signature $(p,q)$ as $(q,p)$, the reversal $g \mapsto -g$. Call T14's convention (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}) the \emph{causal reading}: in a causal signature, $\min(p,q) = 1$, the time direction is the one generator of the minority sign, so this world $(1,3)$ has time $+$ and the mirror $(3,1)$ has time $-$. That Proposition's phrase "time $=$ plus" labels this world, whose minority sign is plus, and agrees with the causal reading there; the two readings differ only on the mirror. Call the convention of Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}, time $+$ in both towers, the \emph{uniform reading}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For $n = p + q$ odd, the central volume elements satisfy $\omega^{2}(q,p) = -\omega^{2}(p,q)$: reversal exchanges the doubled and the complexified types, and residue $r$ with $-r$.
\item[(ii)] In the causal reading the four extensions are: this world $+$ space $= \Cl(1,4)$, doubled, $r = 5$; this world $+$ time $= \Cl(2,3)$, complexified, $r = 7$; mirror $+$ time $= \Cl(3,2)$, doubled, $r = 1$; mirror $+$ space $= \Cl(4,1)$, complexified, $r = 3$. For each kind $X$, mirror $+ X$ is the reversal of this world $+ X$, so the pairs $(5,3)$ and $(7,1)$ are reversal pairs and the extension maps commute with $r \mapsto -r$. The convention-free statement is: in both towers a generator of square $-1$ doubles the shadow and a generator of square $+1$ complexifies it. In the causal reading this world's space and the mirror's time double, and this world's time and the mirror's space complexify.
\item[(iii)] In the uniform reading the same four algebras are labelled with mirror $+$ space $= \Cl(3,2)$ and mirror $+$ time $= \Cl(4,1)$; the pairs of like kind have residues $(5,1)$ and $(7,3)$, which are not reversal pairs, and the mirror $(3,1)$, still causal ($\min(p,q) = 1$), has three time directions and one space direction, which conflicts with Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}'s reading of the minority direction as time.
\item[(iv)] At the even residues $2$ and $6$ the obstructed one-dimensional extension is the one by a generator of square $-1$ (Theorem \claimref{rule2.where-obstruction-sits-commuting-square}(a)). At residue $6$ that generator is spacelike, so this world leaves residue $6$ into the obstruction through its Kaluza-Klein direction, as Corollary \claimref{rule2.which-residues-obstruct-which-way} states. At residue $2$, in the causal reading, it is timelike: the mirror's Kaluza-Klein direction gives $\Cl(4,1)$, complexified, simple, residue $3$, with no obstruction, and the mirror's obstructed extension is a second time direction, $\Cl(3,2)$ at residue $1$. The sentence of that corollary on the mirror residue $2$ holds for the extension by a generator of square $-1$, which is the mirror's Kaluza-Klein direction only in the uniform reading.
\item[(v)] In de Sitter the direction that the frozen point's complement adds (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}(i)) has the space sign of each world in the causal reading: it is space for both towers, doubling ours to $\Cl(1,4)$ and complexifying the mirror's to $\Cl(4,1)$. The uniform reading labels the mirror's $\Cl(4,1)$ as an extension by time.
\end{enumerate}
T14's nesting (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(i), the mirror chain being ours with the signatures reversed) and the Rule 2 plane (Proposition \claimref{rule2.rule-2-plane}(ii), $\Cl(3,1)$ from $\Cl(2,1)$ by a third spatial direction of square $+1$) use the causal reading. The Rule 2 note is therefore internally mixed: its plane result uses the causal reading, while Theorem \claimref{rule2.where-obstruction-sits-commuting-square} names $\Cl(p,q{+}1)$ spacelike and $\Cl(p{+}1,q)$ timelike, which is the uniform reading for the mirror.
synthesis.mirror-extensions-causal-conve.technical:
Two conventions meet in the dark sector. T14 calls a signature causal when it has exactly one direction of the minority sign and reads that direction as time, so the mirror $(3,1)$ has its single time of square $-1$ and three spatial directions of square $+1$. T14's phrase "time $=$ plus" labels this world, where plus is the minority sign, so it agrees with this reading. T14a's Corollary 2.4, and the Rule 2 note in its naming of spacelike and timelike extensions, instead call the plus sign time in both towers; the Rule 2 note's own plane result uses T14's reading, so that note is internally mixed. The four algebras $\Cl(1,4)$, $\Cl(2,3)$, $\Cl(3,2)$, $\Cl(4,1)$ and their residues $5, 7, 1, 3$ do not depend on the convention; their names do.

In T14's causal reading the mirror's extension by space is $\Cl(4,1)$, residue $3$, complexified, and its extension by time is $\Cl(3,2)$, residue $1$, doubled. Each of the mirror's extensions is then the metric reversal of ours of the same kind, so the residues pair as $5 \leftrightarrow 3$ and $7 \leftrightarrow 1$ and the extension maps commute with $r \mapsto -r$. Reversal in odd dimension flips the square of the central volume element, so the reversal of a doubled algebra is complexified: the rule that holds in both towers is that a generator of square $-1$ doubles and one of square $+1$ complexifies. T14a's sentence "in both towers the time generator complexifies and the space generator doubles" is true in its uniform reading, under which the mirror, still a signature with one minority direction, has three times; in the causal reading it holds for this world only, and for the mirror the roles are exchanged.

The consequence a reader meets is in the Rule 2 note: its corollary that the physical lineage leaves residue $6$ only through a spacelike Kaluza-Klein direction, and that "the same holds at the mirror residue 2". In the causal reading the mirror's spacelike extra direction gives the complexified $\Cl(4,1)$, which is not obstructed; the mirror's obstructed extension is a second time. The tower and its mirror therefore differ in which physical extension carries the Rule 2 obstruction, a difference the copy theorem does not see because it runs through even subalgebras. T14a's own de Sitter result already fits the causal reading: the added direction is spacelike for both towers, doubling ours and complexifying the mirror's. T14's nesting and the unit-ball rule's space dimensions (three for the mirror, two and four for the odd towers) also presuppose it; in the uniform reading the mirror and the residue $1$ and $3$ representatives would each have one spatial direction.
synthesis.mirror-extensions-causal-conve.lay: The series pairs our spacetime with a mirror world whose geometry has the opposite overall sign. Two papers describe the mirror's possible extra dimensions with opposite naming rules: one calls the plus sign "time" in both worlds, which would give the mirror three time directions; the other calls the single odd-one-out direction "time" in each world. The algebras are the same either way, but the names are not. This result shows that the second naming is the one under which our world and the mirror match each other step for step, and that the rest of the dark-matter work already uses it. Under it, an extra space dimension splits our algebra into two copies but makes the mirror's complex, so the obstruction that our world meets through an extra space dimension, the mirror meets through a second time instead.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} By Lemma \claimref{odd-extensions.volume-element-odd-dimension}, for $n$ odd $\omega$ is central and $\omega^{2}(p,q) = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2 + q}$. Then $\omega^{2}(q,p)/\omega^{2}(p,q) = (-1)^{p - q} = (-1)^{n} = -1$. The residue of $(q,p)$ is $q - p \equiv -(p - q) \pmod 8$. By Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(i) and (ii), $\omega^{2} = +1$ is the doubled type and $\omega^{2} = -1$ the complexified type, so reversal exchanges them.

\emph{(ii)} In the causal reading the time sign of $(1,3)$ is $+$ and of $(3,1)$ is $-$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}: the timelike direction is the one of the minority sign). Adjoining a generator of the time sign gives $(2,3)$ and $(3,2)$; adjoining one of the other sign gives $(1,4)$ and $(4,1)$. The residues are $7, 1, 5, 3$. Lemma \claimref{odd-extensions.volume-element-odd-dimension} at $n = 5$ gives $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{q}$: $+1$ for $(1,4)$ and $(3,2)$, $-1$ for $(2,3)$ and $(4,1)$, and Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification} gives the types. Reversing $(1,4)$ gives $(4,1)$ and reversing $(2,3)$ gives $(3,2)$, so mirror $+ X$ is the reversal of this world $+ X$ for $X$ = space and time; $5 + 3 \equiv 7 + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod 8$. Both shadows have $q$ odd; adjoining a generator of square $-1$ makes $q$ even and $\omega^{2} = +1$, adjoining one of square $+1$ leaves $q$ odd and $\omega^{2} = -1$, in either tower. This is the computation in the proof of Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}, whose algebras and residues are unchanged; only the labels of the mirror's two rows are exchanged.

\emph{(iii)} In the uniform reading the mirror's space generator has square $-1$, giving $(3,2)$ at residue $1$, and its time generator square $+1$, giving $(4,1)$ at residue $3$, as Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair} lists. Then $5 + 1 \equiv 6$ and $7 + 3 \equiv 2 \pmod 8$, neither $0$, and the mirror's extension of each kind is not the reversal of ours. With time the plus sign, $(3,1)$ has three time directions. It still has $\min(p,q) = 1$, so it is causal by the Proposition's definition; what the uniform reading contradicts is that Proposition's reading of the single minority direction as the timelike one.

\emph{(iv)} Theorem \claimref{rule2.where-obstruction-sits-commuting-square}(a): for $n$ even and $p - q \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ the obstructed extension is $A_{s} = \Cl(p, q{+}1)$, the one by a generator of square $-1$, and the extension by a generator of square $+1$ has complex type. Both $(1,3)$ and $(3,1)$ have $p - q \equiv 2 \pmod 4$. For $(1,3)$ the square $-1$ generator is spacelike in either reading, giving $\Cl(1,4)$ at residue $5$, which is Corollary \claimref{rule2.which-residues-obstruct-which-way}. For $(3,1)$ in the causal reading the square $-1$ generator is timelike: the obstructed extension $\Cl(3,2)$ is a second time direction, and the spacelike extension is $\Cl(4,1)$, of complex type, simple, residue $3$. The corollary's sentence on residue $2$ is therefore a statement about the extension by a generator of square $-1$, the theorem's $A_{s}$; it names the mirror's Kaluza-Klein direction only in the uniform reading.

\emph{(v)} By Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}(i), for $\Lambda > 0$ our $I^{\perp}$ is $(1,4)$ and the mirror's, its reversal, is $(4,1)$; the added unit vector $e_{V}$ has $Q(e_{V}) = -1$ in ours and $Q(e_{V}) = +1$ in the mirror's. In the causal reading these are the space signs of the two towers, so both add a spatial direction; the types are those of (ii). In the uniform reading the mirror's $Q(e_{V}) = +1$ is the time sign.

\emph{The convention of T14 and of the Rule 2 plane.}  Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(i) builds the residue-five tower as this world plus a fifth spatial generator and states that the mirror chain is the same with the signatures reversed, which is the causal reading of (ii). Proposition \claimref{rule2.rule-2-plane}(ii) reads $\Cl(3,1)$ as $\Cl(2,1)$ plus a third spatial direction with $\nu^{2} = +1$, the plane's time $e_{t}$ having square $-1$: again the minority sign carries time. Theorem \claimref{rule2.where-obstruction-sits-commuting-square} instead names $A_{s} = \Cl(p,q{+}1)$ spacelike for every $(p,q)$, which for the mirror is the uniform reading, so the Rule 2 note uses both. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}'s phrase "time $=$ plus" labels this world $(1,3)$, where plus is the minority sign, and does not conflict with the causal reading.

The check recomputes $\omega^{2}$ and the centrality of $\omega$ for every signature of odd dimension up to nine, the central idempotents of the doubled cases, the table of (ii) and its failure under the uniform reading, the obstructed extension for every even signature up to dimension eight, and the de Sitter vector on rational instances of the frozen point in the conformal-model form $I = n_{\infty} + (\Lambda/6)\,n_{0}$, in the tractor signatures $(2,4)$ and $(4,2)$, reading each world's space sign as the majority sign of its Lorentz frame rather than from the convention being tested.

synthesis.mirror-temperature-measures-de.formal:
Assume Premise \claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy} ($T_{\mathrm{desc}} \leq \alpha$), with $\alpha \leq 10^{13}$ GeV at either end of Hypothesis (U) (Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.branch-m-3}), the charge reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, and the mirror's copied content (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}). Write $\xi = T'/T$ and $Y_{B} = n_{B}/s = 8.7 \times 10^{-11}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The floor drops out.)} The gravitational floor has $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}}^{4} \propto T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature}), so from its values at $6 \times 10^{14}$ GeV (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}) it is below $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$ for the mirror, more than $200$ times below the lower edge $\xi = 3 \times 10^{-3}$ of the interval in which the mirror is helium (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}(ii)); for a nine-vector five-dimensional tower it is below $1.7 \times 10^{-5}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The deposit law.)} Let the descent deposit in the mirror an energy $\varepsilon\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ per unit of its charge, and assume that the deposit is thermalised at once among the mirror's light content, that $g' = g = 106.75$ at the deposit ($T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ above the electroweak scale), and that neither tower receives entropy afterwards beyond its own copied history, which then preserves the ratio (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}). Then
\[
\xi^{4} \;=\; \tfrac{4}{3}\,Y_{B}\,\varepsilon \;+\; \xi_{\mathrm{floor}}^{4},
\]
with no other dependence on $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$. This tower holds $\tfrac{3}{4}T_{\mathrm{desc}}/Y_{B} = 8.6 \times 10^{9}\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ per unit charge, so $\xi^{4}$ is, up to the floor, the ratio of the two towers' deposits per unit charge; equal deposits give $\xi = 1$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The window.)} The $\Neff$ cap $\xi < 0.448$ gives $\varepsilon < 3.5 \times 10^{8}$; T14's hot deposit, $\varepsilon = 3$, gives $\xi = 4.3 \times 10^{-3}$; and the mirror is helium, $3 \times 10^{-3} \leq \xi \leq 2 \times 10^{-2}$, exactly when $0.70 \leq \varepsilon \leq 1.4 \times 10^{3}$. Below $\varepsilon \approx 0.7$ the mirror is colder than the helium interval, down to the floor of (i).
\end{enumerate}
So under (R) the mirror's temperature fixes the deposit per unit charge in units of the reheating temperature and says nothing about the reheating temperature itself. (R) only removes the floor: at the ceiling $T_{\mathrm{desc}} = 6 \times 10^{14}$ GeV the mirror's floor changes $\xi^{4}$ at the helium edge by less than $1.3 \times 10^{-4}$ of its value, so (ii) and (iii) hold to that accuracy without (R).
synthesis.mirror-temperature-measures-de.technical: Under Premise (R), which keeps the descent's reheating temperature below about $10^{13}$ GeV, the gravitational heating of the dark towers is negligible: it leaves the mirror below $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$ of the visible temperature, more than two hundred times colder than the interval $3 \times 10^{-3} \leq \xi \leq 2 \times 10^{-2}$ in which the mirror burns to helium. The mirror's temperature is then set by the energy the descent deposited per unit of its charge. Writing that energy as $\varepsilon T_{\mathrm{desc}}$, and assuming the deposit thermalises at once with the mirror's copied light content and no later entropy injection, the reheating temperature cancels: $\xi^{4} = \tfrac43 Y_{B}\varepsilon$ with $Y_{B} = 8.7 \times 10^{-11}$. The dark-radiation cap allows $\varepsilon$ up to $3.5 \times 10^{8}$; a helium mirror needs $\varepsilon$ between $0.70$ and $1.4 \times 10^{3}$, which contains T14's hot deposit $\varepsilon = 3$. Without (R) the same law holds to about one part in ten thousand in $\xi^{4}$ at the helium edge.
synthesis.mirror-temperature-measures-de.lay: The descent that started the universe left each family of worlds with a stored charge. If the descent happened below the temperature that the series' neutrino paper assumes, then gravity afterwards heated the mirror world by a negligible amount, so the mirror's temperature today records only how much energy the descent put into it per unit of charge. Measured in units of the descent's own temperature, that energy is the one number that matters: if the mirror world burned its matter to helium, as one of the series' scenarios needs, it lies between about 0.7 and 1400; the limit on extra radiation only caps it near 350 million. The descent's temperature itself drops out and is left unconstrained by the mirror.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature} gives $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} = (4Y g_{*}/g_{d})^{1/4}$ with $Y = c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}/(3\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3})$, so $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}}^{4}$ is proportional to $T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}$ at fixed content. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity} gives $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} \leq 3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ for the mirror (the top of its counting bracket) and $3.5 \times 10^{-4}$ for the nine-vector tower, at $T_{\mathrm{desc}} = 6 \times 10^{14}$ GeV. Premise \claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy} caps $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ at $\alpha$, which Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.branch-m-3} places near $9 \times 10^{12}$ GeV at the top of Hypothesis (U) and near $5.1 \times 10^{9}$ GeV at its bottom; the check uses $10^{13}$ GeV, above both. Then $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}}^{4} \leq (3.2 \times 10^{-4})^{4}(10^{13}/6 \times 10^{14})^{3}$, which is below $(1.5 \times 10^{-5})^{4}$, and $200^{4}\xi_{\mathrm{floor}}^{4} < (3 \times 10^{-3})^{4}$. For the nine-vector tower the same scaling gives a floor below $1.7 \times 10^{-5}$, between $184$ and $185$ times below $3 \times 10^{-3}$; the helium interval is the mirror's, so this comparison is recorded only as a bound on that tower's floor. Without (R), at $T_{\mathrm{desc}} = 6 \times 10^{14}$ GeV, the mirror's floor is at most $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ and $(3.2 \times 10^{-4}/3 \times 10^{-3})^{4}$ lies between $1.2$ and $1.3 \times 10^{-4}$, so the floor changes $\xi^{4}$ at the helium edge by less than $1.3 \times 10^{-4}$ of its value. The helium interval is Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}(ii).

\emph{(ii)} By Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(i) the mirror holds the same charge as this tower, $n'_{B} = n_{B} = Y_{B}s$, independent of its temperature. A deposit $\varepsilon T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ per unit charge, thermalised, gives $\rho' = \varepsilon T_{\mathrm{desc}}Y_{B}s$, with $s = \tfrac{2\pi^{2}}{45}gT_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}$ and $\rho = \tfrac{\pi^{2}}{30}gT_{\mathrm{desc}}^{4}$; with the mirror's light content a copy of ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), $g' = g = 106.75$ above the electroweak scale, and $\xi^{4} = \rho'/\rho = \varepsilon Y_{B}\cdot\tfrac{2/45}{1/30} = \tfrac43 Y_{B}\varepsilon$, the factor $\pi^{2}$ and $T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{4}$ cancelling. Energies add, so the floor's contribution adds to $\xi^{4}$. After the descent each tower conserves its own entropy, and a copy releases the same entropy at the same epochs, so the ratio seeded at the descent is the ratio at recombination (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}). This tower's energy per unit charge at reheating is $\rho/n_{B} = \tfrac34 T_{\mathrm{desc}}/Y_{B}$, and $\tfrac43 Y_{B}\cdot\tfrac34/Y_{B} = 1$: equal deposits per unit charge give $\xi = 1$, the value Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} finds P2 would impose and the record excludes.

\emph{(iii)} Inverting, $\varepsilon = \xi^{4}/(\tfrac43 Y_{B})$ up to the floor, which by (i) changes $\xi^{4}$ by less than $10^{-8}$ of $(3 \times 10^{-3})^{4}$. The cap $\xi < 0.448$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs} gives $\varepsilon < 3.48 \times 10^{8}$; the helium interval gives $0.698 < \varepsilon_{\min} < 0.70$ and $1379 < \varepsilon_{\max} < 1380$; T14's hot deposit (energy of order the reheating temperature, $3T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ per unit charge, the identity of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(iii)) gives $\xi^{4} = 4Y_{B}$, $\xi = 4.3 \times 10^{-3}$, inside the helium interval. All the arithmetic is exact over the rationals in the check. What is not claimed: that the deposit is thermalised at once (a non-thermal deposit changes the composition analysis, not the energy bookkeeping of (ii)), that the mirror must be helium, or any value of $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ below the cap.

synthesis.no-rule-p2-licenses-gives-the-.formal:
Let the five-dimensional towers' matter count through $\lambda$ cell radii of their extra direction and the three-dimensional towers' sheets be stacked $\mu$ cell radii apart ($\lambda, \mu > 0$, common within each reversal pair), with Premises \claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}, \claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball} and the sourcing rule as stored; Premise \claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction} is $\lambda = \mu = 1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Independence; proved.)} Every premise of the unit-ball relation other than R3 (F1 to F4, P1, P2, P3, R1, R2, the costed single-ideal clause and the imports) holds for every $(\lambda, \mu)$: R2's densities in each tower's own space, R1's common mass, every sector label the descent deposits (residues, orientability, the stored charge $\epsilon N$ of the oriented pair and zero for the odd towers) and P2's equalities along reversal orbits are the same for all of them. The other postulates of the cone do not name the thickness and hold alike: T14's (U) (rank-one eigenvalues at the ceiling), P4 (one asymmetry per mode on oriented towers), P5 (what boundary modes return), the interface premise (I), (P), (Q), (R), the rate inputs (L, U), the slot-module hypothesis (this tower's composites), the common-ceiling premise (the reversal pair), the indifference premise and tameness. The dark-to-baryon ratio is
\[
T(\lambda, \mu) \;=\; 1 + \frac{8}{3\mu} + \frac{16\lambda}{3\pi},
\]
increasing in $\lambda$, decreasing in $\mu$, and taking every value above $1$; on the diagonal it is $T(c)$ of \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}, and $T(1,1) = (11\pi + 16)/3\pi$. As scoped, Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} reaches labels and not states, so it licenses no rule on fillings at all.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The rules P2 licenses on the orbit reading; proved, given the definition.)} P2 as stored licenses no filling rule, by (i); this clause concerns its orbit extension. Call a deposit rule licensed by P2 if every equality it imposes between fillings of two towers equates objects in one orbit of the symmetries of the deposited structure: members of one reversal orbit, or objects common to all towers, as the rungs of the one wall (\claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}) or the light rays of the common count $N$ (\claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}); this is P2's text (it equates along symmetry orbits and never equates inequivalent components) with the extension under which the stored rule of equal filling per rung of the shared wall is licensed. A tower's own cells are balls of its own space, of dimension $2$, $3$ or $4$, and balls of different dimension are not isometric, so no licensed rule equates a three- or five-dimensional tower's filling per own cell with this tower's: R2 and R3 together are democracy in cells that P2 does not relate. A licensed cross-tower rule fills a common object equally in every tower, so each odd tower's share is $1$, or $1/\epsilon$ with $0 < \epsilon \le 1$ under the charge reading, where this tower's baryons are the asymmetric excess $\epsilon$ of the common count and the odd towers carry none. R3's five-dimensional share is $8/3\pi \in (\tfrac56, \tfrac89)$, below one, so no licensed rule gives it, for any $\epsilon$; equivalently the licensed thicknesses are $\lambda = 3\pi/8$ or $3\pi/8\epsilon$, both above $\tfrac98$, never $1$. (The three-dimensional share $\tfrac43$ would be $1/\epsilon$ only at $\epsilon = \tfrac34$.) An annihilation stage would multiply the odd shares by a survival fraction, a dynamical quantity the series cannot fix, having no coupling rule for the odd towers (\claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Cost.)} The thickness is a recorded input, R3 stays a premise, and $5.364$ remains a fit; the three-dimensional fraction $8/(3\mu T)$, $49.7\%$ at R3, rests on it too. The licensed rules do not exclude the observed total: with the charge branch for all four odd towers $T = 1 + 4/\epsilon$, which is $5.364$ at $\epsilon = 1000/1091 \approx 0.917$, and $\epsilon$ is free initial data of the descent (\claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(i)); a licensed rule with that $\epsilon$ reproduces the total with shares other than R3's, so the fit is moved from R3 to $\epsilon$, not removed. Equal filling gives $T = 5$.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.no-rule-p2-licenses-gives-the-.technical: The unit-ball relation counts a five-dimensional tower's matter through one cell radius of its extra direction and stacks a three-dimensional tower's sheets one cell radius apart (R3). Let those two lengths be free, $\lambda$ and $\mu$ cell radii, equal within each mirror-related pair as P2 requires. Nothing else in the premises changes: the densities in each tower's own space, the common mass, and every sector label are the same, so every value of the dark-to-baryon ratio above one is reached by some pair, and R3's value is one point. P2 as stored reaches labels and licenses no filling rule at all. Its orbit reading allows only equalities between objects that a symmetry relates: two members of a reversal pair, or objects all towers share, such as the rungs of the one wall or the light rays of the common count. A five-dimensional tower's cells are four-balls and ours are three-balls, which no symmetry relates, so P2 can only equate fillings of shared objects. That gives every odd tower the same count as ours (share one, total $5.000$) or, if our baryons are only the small asymmetric excess $\epsilon$ of the common count, share $1/\epsilon$, at least one. R3 needs the five-dimensional share $8/3\pi \approx 0.85$, below one, so no such rule gives it. Such a rule can still reach the observed total, with all four odd shares $1/\epsilon$ and $\epsilon \approx 0.92$, which moves the fit from the thickness to $\epsilon$.
synthesis.no-rule-p2-licenses-gives-the-.lay: The series' fit of the amount of dark matter depends on how thick, in its own units, the matter of the five-dimensional and three-dimensional hidden worlds counts. The fit sets that thickness to one unit. This result shows that nothing else in the theory fixes it: any thickness is compatible with every other assumption, and gives a different total. The theory's indifference principle, as stated, says nothing about how worlds are filled; on the natural reading that extends it to fillings, it could only make different worlds fill shared objects equally, which gives each hidden world at least as much matter as ours, never the slightly smaller share the fit's rule needs for the five-dimensional worlds. Such a filling can still match the observed total, but only by choosing another free number of the theory to fit it. So the observed ratio of dark to ordinary matter remains something the theory fits, not something it predicts.

proofs.main:
\emph{Shares.} By Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} a tower's matter acts on this one per unit of the shared three-volume. With R2 the number density in a tower's own space is $1/V_{D}$ in the common cell unit and with R1 the mass per quantum is common, so, as in the proof of \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}, a five-dimensional tower counted through $\lambda$ cell radii has $\rho_{5} = m\lambda/V_{4}$ and a three-dimensional tower with sheets $\mu$ apart has $\rho_{3} = m/(\mu V_{2})$, against $\rho_{\mathrm{us}} = m/V_{3}$. The shares are $f_{5} = \lambda V_{3}/V_{4} = 8\lambda/3\pi$ and $f_{3} = V_{3}/(\mu V_{2}) = 4/3\mu$, the mirror's is $1$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}), and with two towers of each odd dimension $T(\lambda,\mu) = 1 + 8/3\mu + 16\lambda/3\pi$. On $\lambda = \mu = c$ this is $T(c)$ of \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}; the check confirms the agreement at three values of $c$.

(i) \emph{Premise by premise.} The postulates of the cone at the pinned versions are F1 to F4, P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, R1, R2, R3, T14's (U), the interface premise (I), (P), (Q), (R), the rate inputs (L, U), the slot-module hypothesis, the common-ceiling premise, the indifference premise and tameness; besides R3, those that the argument below does not treat concern eigenvalues at the ceiling ((U)), the asymmetry per mode of oriented towers (P4), what boundary modes return (P5), channel occupancies (I), the boundary-mode state ((P), (Q), (R), (L, U)), this tower's composites (slot module), the reversal pair's couplings (common ceiling), distinctions in constructions (indifference) and degenerations (tameness), and none names a counted thickness. R3 is the only premise that names the counted thickness: R2 fixes the density in the tower's own space and a common cell radius, R1 the mass, the sourcing rule the projection, and none of these contains $\lambda$ or $\mu$. F1 to F4, P3, the costed clause and the imports concern algebras and signatures, which the family does not touch. P1 concerns the one frozen point, the one metric and the orientation of the reversal pair $\{2, 6\}$. P2 (\claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}) equates the sector labels the descent deposits, along reversal orbits only; the labels are the residues, orientability and the tower charge, which is $\epsilon N$ for the oriented pair and zero for the odd towers, which carry no asymmetry (\claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}), all independent of $(\lambda, \mu)$, and the family keeps $\lambda$ and $\mu$ common within each orbit, so P2's equalities hold (the check confirms equal shares and mirrored residues within the three orbits at two members of the family, and lists the labels). So every premise but R3 holds at every $(\lambda, \mu)$. $T$ is affine in $\lambda$ with slope $16/3\pi > 0$ and decreasing in $\mu$; as $\lambda \to 0$ and $\mu \to \infty$ it tends to $1$ and it is unbounded in $\lambda$, so by continuity it takes every value above $1$. The check brackets $T(1,1) \in (5.36, 5.37)$ and $T(2, \tfrac12) \in (9.7, 9.8)$ with $\tfrac{333}{106} < \pi < \tfrac{355}{113}$, and the monotonicity and limits at sample points with $3 < \pi < \tfrac{16}{5}$. Since P2 as scoped reaches labels, which do not vary, it imposes nothing on $(\lambda,\mu)$.

(ii) P2 at its pinned version is scoped to labels, not states (\claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}), so as stored it licenses no filling rule, as (i) records; this clause concerns the orbit extension defined in the statement, the reading under which the stored rule of equal filling per rung of the shared wall counts as licensed. \emph{Orbits of cells.} The space of a tower is the span of its generators other than the single time; its Gram matrix (computed with \texttt{GA.py} for the six populated representatives) is definite of rank $3$ for this world and the mirror, $2$ for the three-dimensional pair and $4$ for the five-dimensional pair. An isometry preserves dimension, so a unit ball of rank $4$ or $2$ is not carried to one of rank $3$ by any symmetry, while the members of each reversal orbit have equal rank. Hence a licensed rule equates per-cell fillings only within a reversal orbit, and every licensed equality between an odd tower and this one is between fillings of objects common to all towers. \emph{Common objects.} Let $O$ be such a set, with density $n_{O}$ per unit of the shared three-volume, the same for every tower because the objects are shared. A licensed rule fills each object of $O$ with the same number $k$ of quanta in every tower it equates, so an odd tower holds $kn_{O}$ quanta per unit three-volume. If this tower's baryons are the deposited count, its density is also $kn_{O}$ and the share is $1$. Under the charge reading of \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number} this tower's baryons are the asymmetric excess, $\epsilon kn_{O}$ with $0 < \epsilon \le 1$ (an excess cannot exceed the count), while an odd tower, with no asymmetry and no annihilation rule, keeps $kn_{O}$, so its share is $1/\epsilon \ge 1$. Equating with a second set $O'$ in place of $O$ gives the same two values, and a rule that equated a filling of $O$ with one of a different set $O'$ would relate objects in different orbits. So the licensed shares are $1$ and $1/\epsilon$. With $3 < \pi < \tfrac{16}{5}$, $8/3\pi \in (\tfrac56, \tfrac89)$, strictly below $1$, hence below every licensed share for every $\epsilon$; the licensed thicknesses solve $8\lambda/3\pi \in \{1, 1/\epsilon\}$, $\lambda = 3\pi/8 \in (\tfrac98, \tfrac65)$ or $3\pi/8\epsilon \ge 3\pi/8$, so never $\lambda = 1$. For the three-dimensional pair $4/3\mu = 1/\epsilon$ at $\mu = 1$ needs $\epsilon = \tfrac34$, which is why the five-dimensional share is the one that decides. With an annihilation stage the odd share would be $s/\epsilon$ for a survival fraction $s$; $s$ is fixed by the odd towers' couplings, and the series has no rule relating those to this tower's (\claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}), so no licensed rule supplies $s = 8\epsilon/3\pi$. The common objects named in the statement are the rungs of the one wall, at which every tower ascends its own ladder (\claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}), and the light rays of the common count $N$ (\claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}); the argument uses only that they are shared.

(iii) By (i) the thickness is undetermined by the premises other than R3, and by (ii) the licensed rules do not reach R3's value; R3 therefore enters the unit-ball relation as an input, and the closed form $(11\pi + 16)/3\pi$ is the value at that input, a fit. The three-dimensional fraction $2f_{3}/T = 8/(3\mu T)$ inherits the same dependence. \emph{The observed total on the licensed rules.} With the charge branch for all four odd towers each odd share is $1/\epsilon$ and $T = 1 + 4/\epsilon$; $T = 5.364$ gives $\epsilon = 4/4.364 = 1000/1091 \in (0.916, 0.917)$ (checked), and $\epsilon$ is initial data of the descent, free in the store (\claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(i)). So a licensed rule reproduces the observed total with every odd share $1091/1000$ rather than R3's $4/3$ and $8/3\pi$: the fit moves from R3 to $\epsilon$ and is not removed. Equal filling ($T = 5$) does not reach it.

synthesis.oriented-causal-towers-mirror-.technical: Orientation of a tower, in the sense of the Witt flag, is the condition that the two halves of a Witt pair of its complexified conformal ambient lie in opposite families, which holds exactly when the tower dimension $n$ is divisible by four. Causality is $\min(p,q) = 1$. In dimension $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$, $n \ge 4$, the only causal signatures are $(1, n-1)$ and $(n-1, 1)$, of residues $\pm(n-2)$, and $n - 2 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ makes these $2$ and $6$ modulo $8$ whatever $n$ is. So orientation and causality together select the mirror pair $\{2, 6\}$ in every window, not only at the dimension-four representatives of Premise P3. The two self-mirror even residues $0$ and $4$ never host an oriented causal tower, and their pseudoscalars always square to $+1$, so they never carry a pseudoscalar unit. The selected pair always does: tower and conformal pseudoscalars square to $-1$, the tower one commutes with the ascended plane as the field theory's $I_{4}$ does, and the spacelike one-dimensional extension of either member is the type-C obstruction of the root paper.
synthesis.oriented-causal-towers-mirror-.lay: The series sorts its eight towers by a number from zero to seven. Two properties matter for whether a tower can hold matter like ours: whether it has a single direction of time, and whether its spinors carry an orientation bit that can record a matter-antimatter asymmetry. The dark-matter paper found that only our tower and its mirror have both, but only after assuming every tower lives in four dimensions. This result removes that assumption: in any number of dimensions, having both properties forces the tower number to be 2 or 6, our tower and its mirror, and those two always come with a built-in imaginary unit, while towers 0 and 4 never do.

proofs.main:
\emph{Orientation.} By Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion} the conformal ambient of a representative of signature $(p,q)$ has signature $(p+1, q+1)$ and dimension $n + 2$. If $n$ is odd the ambient dimension is odd and Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities} gives a single family, so no Witt pair lies in opposite families and the tower is not oriented. If $n$ is even the ambient has dimension $2m$ with $m = (n+2)/2$, and by part (iii) of that proposition a Witt pair lies in opposite families exactly when $m$ is odd, that is $n + 2 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, that is $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$. So a tower is oriented if and only if $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$, and in particular $n$ is even, and so is $r$, since $p - q \equiv p + q \pmod 2$.

\emph{(i).} Let the tower be oriented and causal. Causality, $\min(p,q) = 1$, needs $n \ge 2$, and with $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ this gives $n \ge 4$. Then the signatures of dimension $n$ with $\min(p,q) = 1$ are $(1, n-1)$ and $(n-1, 1)$, which are distinct because $n - 1 \ge 3 > 1$; there are exactly two. Their residues are $1 - (n-1) = 2 - n$ and $(n-1) - 1 = n - 2$. From $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$, $n - 2 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, so $n - 2 \equiv 2$ or $6 \pmod 8$, and $2 - n = -(n-2)$ is then $6$ or $2$ respectively: the two residues are $\{2, 6\}$ as a set, and they are exchanged by $r \mapsto -r$. Every oriented causal tower is one of these two, so has residue $2$ or $6$.

\emph{(ii).} Modulo $8$ the map $r \mapsto -r$ fixes exactly $0$ and $4$ ($2r \equiv 0 \pmod 8$ iff $r \equiv 0 \pmod 4$), and by (i) neither is the residue of an oriented causal tower, in any dimension. For any signature with $r \equiv 0$ or $4 \pmod 8$, $p - q \equiv 0 \pmod 4$, so Lemma \claimref{transport.sign} gives $\omega^{2} = +1$. An element squaring to $+1$ is not an imaginary unit, so no tower of these residues has a pseudoscalar imaginary unit. Here $n \equiv r \pmod 2$ is even, so $\omega$ has even grade; a frame vector $e_{i}$ anticommutes with the $n - 1$ other factors of $\omega = e_{1} \cdots e_{n}$ and commutes with itself, so $e_{i}\omega = (-1)^{n-1}\omega e_{i}$, and for $n$ even every vector anticommutes with $\omega$; hence every product of two vectors commutes with $\omega$, and $\omega$ is central in the even subalgebra. With $\omega^{2} = 1$, $\bigl(\tfrac12(1 \pm \omega)\bigr)^{2} = \tfrac14(2 \pm 2\omega) = \tfrac12(1 \pm \omega)$, the two idempotents are central in the even subalgebra, sum to $1$ and multiply to $\tfrac14(1 - \omega^{2}) = 0$: chirality is a splitting into two real ideals. (For $n = 0$, the signature $(0,0)$, $\omega = 1$ and the splitting is trivial, $1 = 1 + 0$; for $n \ge 2$ both idempotents are nonzero, since $\omega \notin \R$.)

\emph{(iii).} An oriented causal tower has $r = \pm(n - 2) \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, so Lemma \claimref{transport.sign} gives $\omega_{n}^{2} = -1$. The conformal ambient $(p+1, q+1)$ has the same $p - q$, so the same lemma gives $\omega_{n+2}^{2} = -1$. Since $n$ is even, $\omega_{n}$ anticommutes with each of the tower's vectors (the argument of (ii)) and is central in the even subalgebra. A vector of the ascended plane is orthogonal to all $n$ factors of $\omega_{n}$ and anticommutes with each, an even number of sign changes, so it commutes with $\omega_{n}$. These are the properties Proposition \claimref{field-theory.where-each-lives} records for $I_{4}$, which at $n = 4$, $(p,q) = (1,3)$, is $\omega_{4}$ itself: $I_{4}$ spans the centre of $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ with $1$, and $[I_{4}, E] = 0$ for the ascended plane's bivector $E$. Finally $p - q \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ and $n$ is even, so by Theorem \claimref{rule2.where-obstruction-sits-commuting-square}(a) the spacelike extension $\Cl(p, q+1)$ carries the type-C obstruction. Its volume element $\omega_{n+1}$ has odd grade $n + 1$, so it commutes with every vector and is central, and $p - (q+1) = r - 1 \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ gives $\omega_{n+1}^{2} = +1$ by Lemma \claimref{transport.sign}; so $\tfrac12(1 \pm \omega_{n+1})$ are central idempotents, nonzero because $\omega_{n+1} \notin \R$, summing to $1$, and they are the two ideals of the obstructed extension.

\emph{The consequence.} The argument of (i) used only $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ and $\min(p,q) = 1$ and made no choice of dimension, so it holds for every representative of every residue. An odd residue has $n$ odd and is never oriented; residues $0$ and $4$ are excluded by (ii); so in every window the oriented causal towers have residues $2$ and $6$ only, which is the conclusion Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-can-carry-arrow} reached at the four-dimensional representatives of Premise P3, now without that premise.

The check computes, for every signature of dimension at most $10$, the family bit from $m = (n+2)/2$, causality, the residue and $\omega^{2}$ from the blade product, and confirms (i) and (ii) by enumeration; for the oriented causal signatures of dimensions $4$ and $8$ it verifies in exact arithmetic that $\omega_{n}$ anticommutes with every tower vector, commutes with both ascended generators and every bivector, that $\omega_{n+2}^{2} = -1$, and that in $\Cl(p, q+1)$ the volume element is central with square $+1$.

synthesis.pati-salam-monopoles-bound-des.formal:
Work on the chain of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector}: the $(10,1,3)$ vev breaks $G = SU(4) \times SU(2)_{L} \times SU(2)_{R}$ directly to the Standard Model group $H$ at $M_{I} = 1.95 \times 10^{10}$ GeV (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}), with $v_{R} = M_{I}/g_{R} = 4.15 \times 10^{10}$ GeV, and assume (D): no inflationary stage follows the descent and entropy is conserved after it (the history of Conjecture \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}, taken here as a hypothesis). Assume (K): wherever the broken phase forms by a causal process (a thermal transition at $T_{c}$, or a deposit at $T_{d}$ whose vacuum orientation is uncorrelated beyond the Hubble length), at least one monopole forms per Hubble volume $H^{-3}$ with probability $p \ge \tfrac{1}{10}$, with $g_{*} \ge 106.75$ there; and take as premises the literature inputs (a) to (e) of the proof, which are not imported in the store and are cited from memory: (a) $\pi_{2}(G/H) \cong \pi_{1}(H)$ for simply connected $G$, with stable monopoles for each class; (b) the Kibble-Preskill causal estimate underlying (K); (c) Preskill's annihilation floor; (d) the MACRO flux limit $\mathcal{F} < 1.4 \times 10^{-16}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ sr$^{-1}$, applied to galactic monopoles with speed $\beta \ge 7 \times 10^{-4}$; (e) high-temperature symmetry restoration, with its known exceptions. The statements below are proved given (a) to (e).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Monopoles exist.)} The hypercharge $Y = T_{3R} + \tfrac12(B - L)$ is traceless on the $4$ and on the $SU(2)_{R}$ doublet, so it generates a circle in the simply connected $G$ commuting with $SU(3) \times SU(2)_{L}$; it gives the Standard Model hypercharges on the $(4,2,1) \oplus (\bar 4,1,2)$ and closes first at period $6$. Hence $\pi_{2}(G/H) = \pi_{1}(H) \supseteq \mathbb{Z}$: the breaking leaves stable monopoles, of mass $M_{M} \approx 4\pi v_{R}/g_{R} > 10^{12}$ GeV.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The causal minimum against the flux limit.)} The minimum of (K) at temperature $T$ is $n_{M}/s \ge p\,(\pi^{2}g_{*}/1440)^{1/2}(T/M_{P})^{3}$ ($M_{P}$ the reduced Planck mass), not diluted afterwards under (D); at $T = v_{R}$ it exceeds $3.6 \times 10^{-25}$, while the flux limit allows at most $3.7 \times 10^{-26}$ today, a factor above $12$. The minimum exceeds the limit for every $T \ge 0.48\,v_{R} = 2.0 \times 10^{10}$ GeV and every $\beta \ge 10^{-4}$, and not at $T = 0.3\,v_{R}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Neither annihilation nor closure decides it.)} Preskill's annihilation floor, $n_{M}/s \sim 10^{-10}(M_{M}/10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV}) > 10^{-12}$, lies far above the causal minimum, so annihilation cannot bring $n_{M}/s$ below it; closure ($\Omega h^{2} < 0.12$) allows up to $3.9 \times 10^{-22}$ and is not the binding constraint.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The seeding origin.)} The seeding condition of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.seeding-remainder-excludes-perturbative-pati-salam}, $c\,T_{d}^{4} \ge A/2$ with $A^{1/4} = 1.217 \times 10^{12}$ GeV and $c = 0.312$, needs $T_{d} > 1.36 \times 10^{12}$ GeV $> 32\,v_{R}$, so unless the symmetry is not restored at high temperature the transition happens in the descended phase, and by (ii) the seeding origin is excluded on the chain unless $T_{c} < 0.48\,v_{R}$ or the monopoles are removed after they form by a temporary breaking of electromagnetism that confines them in flux tubes (the Langacker-Pi mechanism, from memory), which needs a stage of the descended phase the chain does not contain. This holds whether or not Premise (R) (\claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy}) and perturbative couplings hold. Seeding with $T_{d}$ below $2.0 \times 10^{10}$ GeV needs $c > 6.8 \times 10^{6}$, about $3 \times 10^{9}$ vector species.
\item[(v)] \emph{(The deposit clause.)} A descent below $T_{c}$ that deposits the broken phase with an orientation uncorrelated beyond its Hubble length gives the same minimum at $T_{d}$, so it is excluded for $T_{d} \ge 2.0 \times 10^{10}$ GeV. A deposit aligned beyond its Hubble length escapes, and such correlations are available in principle: a deposit correlated by the frozen point's stabiliser reaches the length $|x_{d}|$ of the descent slice in the frozen point's chart, about four present Hubble radii (filed alongside, synthesis.frozen-point-geometry-reads-descent-as-vacuum, whose obstruction concerns the spectrum of $\zeta$, not the vacuum orientation).
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, on the chain the reheating temperature of the descent is below $2.0 \times 10^{10}$ GeV, or the transition is cold ($T_{c} < 0.48\,v_{R}$), or the symmetry is not restored at high temperature with a deposit aligned beyond the descent's Hubble length, or the monopoles are removed by a Langacker-Pi stage; of the three premises that the stored seeding result finds incompatible, the seeding origin is the one that also fails on its own.
synthesis.pati-salam-monopoles-bound-des.technical:
On the stored chain, the Majorana element's vev breaks Pati-Salam straight to the Standard Model at about $2 \times 10^{10}$ GeV. Because the hypercharge is a circle inside the simply connected Pati-Salam group, the breaking leaves stable magnetic monopoles, of mass above $10^{12}$ GeV. In the series' history the descent is at the origin and nothing inflates afterwards, so monopoles formed after the descent are never diluted.

The literature inputs used here (the topology of the breaking, the causal estimate, the annihilation floor, the MACRO limit and high-temperature restoration) are premises cited from memory, not yet imported. Causality fixes a minimum: where the broken phase forms with an orientation that is uncorrelated beyond the Hubble length, at least about one monopole in ten Hubble volumes survives, which gives $n_{M}/s \ge p\sqrt{\pi^{2}g_{*}/1440}\,(T/M_{P})^{3}$. At $T = v_{R}$ this is above $3.6 \times 10^{-25}$; the MACRO flux limit allows at most $3.7 \times 10^{-26}$ for galactic monopoles. Annihilation cannot help, because it acts only above a floor near $10^{-12}$, and closure is not the binding constraint. The minimum stays above the limit for every formation temperature above $0.48\,v_{R}$, about $2 \times 10^{10}$ GeV.

The seeding origin of the odd-tower remainder needs a descent hotter than $1.36 \times 10^{12}$ GeV, thirty-two times $v_{R}$. The bath then restores Pati-Salam, and the breaking happens afterwards in the descended phase; its monopoles exceed the flux limit unless the transition is cold, below $0.48\,v_{R}$. That holds whatever one decides about Premise (R) and perturbative couplings, so among the three premises the stored seeding result cannot reconcile, the seeding origin is the one with an independent obstruction. The escapes are a cold transition, high-temperature non-restoration with a deposit aligned beyond the descent's Hubble length, a temporary breaking of electromagnetism that confines and annihilates the monopoles (the Langacker-Pi mechanism), or a chain other than the stored one. An aligned deposit is available in principle: a deposit correlated by the frozen point's stabiliser reaches about four present Hubble radii on the descent slice (filed alongside, synthesis.frozen-point-geometry-reads-descent-as-vacuum). A cooler descent that deposits the broken phase with an uncorrelated orientation meets the same bound at its own temperature.
synthesis.pati-salam-monopoles-bound-des.lay: The theory's particle physics breaks a larger symmetry down to the familiar one at about twenty billion times the proton mass in energy units. Symmetry breaking of this kind leaves behind magnetic monopoles, isolated magnetic charges, wherever separate regions of the early universe chose their broken state independently. Without a later period of rapid expansion to thin them out, causality guarantees a minimum number of them. Underground detectors have looked for passing monopoles and found none, which caps their number below that minimum unless the breaking happened in a cool universe. One proposed origin for part of the dark matter needs the universe to start far hotter than that, so it would produce too many monopoles, whatever else is assumed, unless the breaking happens in an unusual way or the monopoles are removed later.

proofs.main:
Units $\hbar = c = k_{B} = 1$ except where cm and s are written; $3 < \pi < 22/7$ wherever $\pi$ enters a bound; $M_{P} = 2.435 \times 10^{18}$ GeV is the reduced Planck mass.

\emph{Literature inputs: premises of the statement, not imported in the store, cited from memory (to be imported as Facts).} (a) For a simply connected group $G$ broken to $H$, $\pi_{2}(G/H) \cong \pi_{1}(H)$ (the exact homotopy sequence of $H \to G \to G/H$), and every element of $\pi_{2}(G/H)$ is carried by a finite-energy 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole; for Pati-Salam broken to the Standard Model the lightest monopole carries two Dirac units (Lazarides, Magg and Shafi 1980). (b) The Kibble mechanism with Preskill's estimate: a broken phase formed with an orientation uncorrelated beyond a length $\xi \le H^{-1}$ leaves at least about $p \approx \tfrac{1}{10}$ monopole per $\xi^{3}$ (Kibble 1976, Preskill 1979); (K) uses only $\xi \le H^{-1}$, which causality enforces, and $p \ge \tfrac{1}{10}$. (c) Preskill's annihilation: monopole-antimonopole annihilation in the plasma reduces $n_{M}/s$ only to a floor of about $10^{-10}(M_{M}/10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV})$ and acts only above it. (d) The MACRO final flux limit for slow and fast monopoles, $\mathcal{F} < 1.4 \times 10^{-16}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ sr$^{-1}$ over $4 \times 10^{-5} \lesssim \beta < 1$ (MACRO Collaboration 2002); galactic monopoles move at least at the halo's virial speed, $\beta \ge 7 \times 10^{-4}$, and light ones are accelerated by the galactic field to larger $\beta$, where the IceCube limits are stronger still. (e) High-temperature symmetry restoration, with its known exceptions for negative cross-couplings (Weinberg 1974; Dvali, Melfo and Senjanovic 1995). Not a premise but a listed escape: the Langacker-Pi mechanism (Langacker and Pi 1980), in which a temporary breaking of electromagnetism at intermediate temperatures confines monopoles and antimonopoles in flux tubes and annihilates them; it needs an additional stage of the descended phase that the stored chain does not contain.

(i) In the series' language $G = SU(4) \times SU(2)_{L} \times SU(2)_{R} \cong \mathrm{Spin}(6) \times \mathrm{Spin}(4)$, the even Clifford group of the slot module that the rung parity leaves after the first breaking (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}), is simply connected. On the $4$ of $SU(4)$, $\tfrac12(B - L) = \operatorname{diag}(\tfrac16, \tfrac16, \tfrac16, -\tfrac12)$, traceless; $T_{3R} = \pm\tfrac12$ on the $SU(2)_{R}$ doublet, traceless; so $Y = T_{3R} + \tfrac12(B - L)$ lies in the semisimple Lie algebra of $G$ and $t \mapsto \exp(2\pi tY)$ (the phase unit realised as a unit bivector) is a closed one-parameter subgroup. On the $(4,2,1)$ it gives $\tfrac16$ and $-\tfrac12$, and on the conjugates of the $(\bar 4,1,2)$ it gives $-\tfrac23, \tfrac13, 0, 1$: the Standard Model hypercharges (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pati-salam-representation-theory-survival}), with least common period $6$. It commutes with $SU(3) \times SU(2)_{L}$, so $H$ contains a central circle and $\pi_{1}(H) \supseteq \mathbb{Z}$; by (a) the breaking at $M_{I}$ leaves stable monopoles. Their mass is of order $4\pi v_{R}/g_{R}$, above $10^{12}$ GeV with $g_{R} = 0.469$ and $v_{R} = M_{I}/g_{R} \in (4.15, 4.16) \times 10^{10}$ GeV (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector}).

(ii) In the radiation-dominated descended phase $H = \pi\sqrt{g_{*}/90}\,T^{2}/M_{P}$ and $s = (2\pi^{2}/45)g_{*}T^{3}$, so (K) gives $n_{M}/s \ge pH^{3}/s$, and $(pH^{3}/s)^{2} = p^{2}\pi^{6}(g_{*}/90)^{3}(T/M_{P})^{6}/((2\pi^{2}/45)^{2}g_{*}^{2}) = p^{2}\pi^{2}g_{*}(T/M_{P})^{6}/1440$ (the constant $45^{2}/(4 \cdot 90^{3}) = 1/1440$ is checked). The bound is increasing in $g_{*}$, so $g_{*} \ge 106.75$ makes it conservative. Under (D) there is no inflationary stage after the descent and entropy is conserved, so $n_{M}/s$ is today's value. Today $s_{0} = (2\pi^{2}/45)g_{s}(T_{0})T_{0}^{3}$ with $T_{0} = 2.7255$ K (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-planck-2018-lcdm-parameters}), $k_{B}T_{0}/\hbar c = 11.90$ cm$^{-1}$, $s_{0} = 2891$ cm$^{-3}$ (checked between $2600$ and $3200$ with the $\pi$ brackets). An isotropic flux $\mathcal{F}$ of monopoles of speed $\beta$ has $n_{M} = 4\pi\mathcal{F}/(\beta c)$, so (d) gives $n_{M}/s_{0} < 4\pi\mathcal{F}/(\beta c\,s_{0}) < 3.7 \times 10^{-26}$ at $\beta = 7 \times 10^{-4}$ (the cosmic average; clustering in the halo would only raise the local density and strengthen the bound). At $T = v_{R}$ the causal minimum exceeds $3.6 \times 10^{-25}$, more than $12$ times the limit with $\pi$ bracketed adversely on both sides (the check pins $100\,(\text{minimum}/\text{maximum})^{2}$ to the integer part $16341$). Since the minimum scales as $T^{3}$, it exceeds the limit for every $T \ge 0.48\,v_{R}$ (checked at $0.48\,v_{R}$), and the check confirms it does not at $0.3\,v_{R}$ with the brackets reversed, so the threshold lies in $(0.3, 0.48)\,v_{R}$; the check pins its sixth power, $(T_{*}/v_{R})^{6}$, to integer parts $6119 \times 10^{-6}$ and $4217 \times 10^{-6}$ with the two bracketings, that is $T_{*} \in (0.40, 0.43)\,v_{R}$ ($0.409\,v_{R} = 1.70 \times 10^{10}$ GeV at the central value of $\pi$). At $T = v_{R}$ it exceeds the limit for every $\beta \ge 10^{-4}$.

(iii) With $M_{M} > 4 \cdot 3 \cdot v_{R}/g_{R} > 10^{12}$ GeV, Preskill's floor is above $10^{-12}$, more than $10^{10}$ times the causal minimum, so annihilation leaves $n_{M}/s \ge \min(\text{initial}, \text{floor})$, which is at least the causal minimum. Closure, $\Omega_{M}h^{2} = M_{M}(n_{M}/s)s_{0}/(\rho_{c}/h^{2}) < 0.12$ with $\rho_{c}/h^{2} = 1.0537 \times 10^{-5}$ GeV cm$^{-3}$, allows $n_{M}/s$ up to $3.9 \times 10^{-22}$ at $M_{M} = 1.1 \times 10^{12}$ GeV, above the minimum, so the flux limit, not closure, is the constraint.

(iv) By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.seeding-remainder-excludes-perturbative-pati-salam}, the seeding origin needs $c\,T_{d}^{4} \ge A/2$; with the odd towers' vectors, $c = 0.312$, $T_{d}^{4} \ge A/(2c)$ gives $T_{d} \in (1.36, 1.38) \times 10^{12}$ GeV at the threshold, above $32\,v_{R}$. Gauge interactions thermalise the bath at these temperatures, and unless (e)'s exception applies the Pati-Salam symmetry is restored, so the broken phase forms again at $T_{c}$ in the descended phase, a causal process covered by (K): by (ii) the result is excluded unless $T_{c} < 0.48\,v_{R}$ or a Langacker-Pi stage removes the monopoles after they form. No step uses Premise (R) (\claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy}) or a bound on the couplings; the stored incompatibility of those two with the seeding origin is therefore not the only obstruction to it. For the seeding temperature to lie below $2.0 \times 10^{10}$ GeV, where (ii) no longer bites, the coefficient would have to exceed $A/(2(2.0 \times 10^{10})^{4}) > 6.8 \times 10^{6}$, more than $2.9 \times 10^{9}$ vectors at the imported per-vector coefficient $2.3 \times 10^{-3}$.

(v) If $T_{d} < T_{c}$, the descent deposits the broken phase directly. If its vacuum orientation is uncorrelated beyond the descent's Hubble length, (K) applies at $T_{d}$ with the same function, so $T_{d} \ge 0.48\,v_{R}$ is excluded. Only a deposit aligned beyond its Hubble length escapes, the same pre-metric correlation that Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb} finds the primordial spectrum would need. Such correlations are available in principle: a deposit correlated by the frozen point's stabiliser depends on the descent slice only through separations relative to $|x_{d}|$, about four present Hubble radii (filed alongside, synthesis.frozen-point-geometry-reads-descent-as-vacuum); its obstruction concerns the spectrum of $\zeta$, not the orientation of the broken vacuum, so it does not close this escape.

\emph{Scope.} The chain's $M_{I}$ and $g_{R}$ are the stored record-level values; a different chain (for example a two-step breaking through $U(1)_{B-L}$, or a much higher $M_{I}$ off the chain) moves the threshold with $v_{R}$. The transition temperature $T_{c}$ is not computed (the store has no Pati-Salam potential); $T_{c}/v_{R} < 0.48$ needs a Higgs quartic small against the gauge coupling. The literature inputs (a) to (e) are from memory and should be imported.

Numerical values (float, not evidence): $s_{0} = 2891.3$ cm$^{-3}$; causal minimum at $v_{R}$, $4.23 \times 10^{-25}$; flux maximum at $\beta = 7 \times 10^{-4}$, $2.90 \times 10^{-26}$; ratio $14.6$; threshold $1.70 \times 10^{10}$ GeV; threshold speed at $T = v_{R}$, $\beta = 4.8 \times 10^{-5}$; $M_{M} \approx 1.1 \times 10^{12}$ GeV.

The check verifies the constant $1/1440$, the hypercharge assignments, tracelessness and period, the phase unit in $\Cl(2,4)$, the bounds on $v_{R}$ and $s_{0}$, the causal minimum against the flux limit with the threshold bracketed in $(0.3, 0.48)\,v_{R}$, the annihilation floor and closure comparison, and the seeding temperature and coefficient.
