synthesis.residues-zero-four-real-chiral.formal:
Use the spinor ideal $S = \Cl^{0}(V)f$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-tower-matter.ideals-fields-momentum}, one ideal per tower, with $f = \tfrac12(1 + e_{t}e_{a})$ at $(1,1)$ and $f = \tfrac14(1 + e_{t}e_{a})(1 + cI)$, $c = \pm 1$, at $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$, $I$ the pseudoscalar of $V$; the single ideal is the series' costed clause for residues $0$ and $4$, chosen with the fit known. Call a causal tower \emph{really chiral} if $I^{2} = +1$ and $I$ is central in $\Cl^{0}(V)$. Let a tower share with this one its time and up to three space directions, as in the sourcing rule (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}). Write (A) for the local-anomaly theorem and the two-dimensional covariant anomaly form, imported from the literature and not in the store; clauses (ii) to (iv) are conditional on (A).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Every window; proved.)} A causal tower is really chiral if and only if its dimension is $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, if and only if its residue is $0$ or $4$ (the splitting is that of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.oriented-causal-towers-mirror-pair-every-window}(ii); its form for the single ideal is the lemma of the result filed alongside, synthesis.reversion-pairing-vanishes-residues-zero-four). There $S$ is an eigenspace of left multiplication by $I$ with a real eigenvalue ($+1$ at $(1,1)$, $c$ at $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$), the two eigenvalues give non-isomorphic $\Cl^{0}(V)$-modules, and any conjugation keeps the eigenvalue.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Anomaly forms; computed, conditional on (A).)} The pure rotation-gauge anomaly form of one chiral spin-$\tfrac12$ field in dimension $n$ is the degree-$(n+2)$ part of $\hat{A} = \prod_{i}(x_{i}/2)/\sinh(x_{i}/2)$, nonzero exactly when $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$: $-p_{1}/24$ for $n = 2$, $(7p_{1}^{2} - 4p_{2})/5760$ for $n = 6$. The pure-gauge part is $\mathrm{tr}_{R}\,F^{(n+2)/2}/((n+2)/2)!$, an even power exactly when $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$. In a really chiral tower the single-ideal content and its conjugates have one chirality, so these forms add: the rotation-gauge part is $N$ times that of one field and the gauge part is positive on every nonzero element of a gauge algebra acting nontrivially. Gauge vectors are not chiral, and the content has no gravitino and no two-form field, so nothing cancels them.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Residue $0$, lowest-causal window.)} At $(1,1)$, $I = e_{t}e_{a}$ is the bivector of the tower's own plane, both of whose directions are shared; on the sourcing rule's reading the tower's matter lives on planes of this tower's spacetime and meets the field of the one metric induced on them. Such fields have non-constant scalar curvature: in conformal time, $R = -2\eta^{-4}$ (radiation era) and $R = -4\eta^{-6}$ (matter era) on a coordinate plane of a spatially flat expanding field, and $R = 4M/r^{3}$ on the $t$-$r$ plane of the Schwarzschild field (de Sitter's $R = 2H^{2}$ is constant). Where $R$ varies the anomaly makes the covariant divergence of the stress nonzero, so single-ideal tower matter of residue $0$ at $(1,1)$, massive or massless, has no conserved rotation-covariant stress and cannot source the field equations, whose left side is divergence-free identically (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.sourcing-rule-forced-not-chosen}). The clause concerns the tower's single-ideal matter only: content with equal chiral weight on the two sheets of an edge has $c_{L} = c_{R}$ and no anomaly.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Residue $4$, lowest-causal window.)} At $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$, on $S$ the pseudoscalar $I_{4}$ of the four shared directions equals $-cJ$, $J$ the unit bivector of the two unshared directions, $J^{2} = -1$ (here $J$ is the unshared-plane bivector, not the unit $J = e_2e_3$ of the conventions' unit principle). The one metric rotates only shared directions (the unshared ones are not gravitational, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity}), and in four dimensions the rotation-gauge anomaly form vanishes, so the one metric's field meets no obstruction at residue $4$. Under (G6), the reading that the tower's own gauge fields are fields on its six-dimensional space and act nontrivially on its constituents, the gauge part of (ii) is nonzero and single-ideal matter of residue $4$ is anomalous. Without (G6) nothing here empties residue $4$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, in the lowest-causal window and given (A), the single-ideal clause empties residue $0$ through the one metric alone and residue $4$ through (G6). At higher causal members of residue $0$, such as $(1,9)$ and $(9,1)$, only four directions are shared and, as in (iv), the one metric meets no obstruction; at the non-causal representatives of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} nothing here applies. The result filed alongside shows that with one ideal the emptiness of residues $0$ and $4$ holds under the pairing reading of mass and fails at residue $4$ under the momentum reading; under (G6), (iv) closes that escape at residue $4$. If both ideals are admitted at $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, the content of residues $0$ and $4$ is vector-like and anomaly-free.
synthesis.residues-zero-four-real-chiral.technical:
Take the single spinor ideal in every causal tower. For a causal signature of even dimension $n$ the pseudoscalar squares to $+1$ exactly when $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, which is exactly residues $0$ and $4$ in every window; there the single ideal is one of two non-isomorphic chiral modules and a constituent and its conjugate have the same chirality. Granting the imported anomaly theorems, dimension $2 \bmod 4$ is also exactly where local anomalies of one chirality exist and cannot cancel: the rotation-gauge form is the degree-$(n+2)$ part of the $\hat{A}$ genus, nonzero only in those dimensions, and the pure-gauge form is an even power of the field strength, positive on any nontrivially acting algebra, with no two-form field in the content to cancel it.

In the lowest-causal window, at residue $0$, in dimension two, both directions are shared, the one metric induces fields of varying curvature on the tower's planes (the radiation and matter eras of an expanding field, the Schwarzschild $t$-$r$ plane), and the anomaly makes the stress of single-ideal tower matter non-conserved, so that matter cannot be a source of the field equations; content with equal weight on both sheets of an edge is not affected. At residue $4$ the shared pseudoscalar equals the unshared-plane rotation on the ideal, so against the one metric the content is four-dimensional and meets no gravitational obstruction; it is anomalous only under (G6), the reading that the tower's own gauge fields live on its six-dimensional space and act on its constituents, a reading chosen knowing that the unit-ball fit needs residue $4$ empty. Higher causal members of residue $0$ share only four directions and meet no obstruction from the one metric.
synthesis.residues-zero-four-real-chiral.lay: The dark-matter paper leaves two of its eight families of worlds empty by assumption. In every possible number of dimensions, these two families are exactly the ones in which matter of a single handedness keeps its handedness when matter is swapped for antimatter. Granting standard results of quantum theory that are not yet recorded in the series, a world built from one handedness of matter then has broken bookkeeping of energy or of charge that its other particles cannot repair. If the family's matter has one handedness, as the series' definition says, and lives on two-dimensional slices of our spacetime, as the series' rule for how hidden matter feeds gravity implies, then in the smallest member of the first family this breakdown happens in the ordinary gravitational field of our universe, and that member is empty of matter and of radiation. In the smallest six-dimensional member of the second family it happens only through that world's own forces, and only if those forces spread through all six of its dimensions, an assumption chosen knowing that the paper's dark-matter count needs this family empty. If both handednesses are allowed, both families could hold matter.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} The equivalence of real chirality with $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ and with residues $0$ and $4$ among causal signatures is Theorem \claimref{synthesis.oriented-causal-towers-mirror-pair-every-window}(ii) and (iii) (with Lemma \claimref{transport.sign} for the sign of $I^{2}$): causal signatures of even dimension $n$ have residue $\pm(n-2) \pmod 8$, so $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ gives $r \in \{0, 4\}$ with $I^{2} = +1$ and $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ gives $r \in \{2, 6\}$ with $I^{2} = -1$, and for even $n$ the pseudoscalar is central in $\Cl^{0}(V)$; for odd $n$, $\Cl^{0}(V)$ is central simple. The form of the splitting on a single ideal, that reversion exchanges the two chiral projectors exactly when $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, is the lemma of the result filed alongside (synthesis.reversion-pairing-vanishes-residues-zero-four), and is not reproved here. What is added is the eigenvalue on the ideals of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field} and of the lowest-causal content result (\claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}). At $(1,1)$, $I = e_{t}e_{a}$, so $If = \tfrac12(I + I^{2}) = f$ and $I\psi = Iaf = aIf = \psi$ for $\psi = af$, $a \in \Cl^{0}(V)$. At $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$, $I(1 + cI) = c(1 + cI)$ gives $If = cf$ and, $I$ being central in $\Cl^{0}(V)$, $I\psi = c\psi$ on $S$. A $\Cl^{0}(V)$-module map commutes with the central element $I$, so it preserves its eigenvalue: the ideals with $c = 1$ and $c = -1$ are not isomorphic, and the same holds at $(1,1)$ for $f$ and $1 - f$. Any conjugation of the constituent field acts on $S$ by right multiplication or by a real-linear map commuting with the action of $\Cl^{0}(V)$, so it keeps a real eigenvalue of $I$: in a really chiral tower a constituent and its conjugate have the same chirality. At residues $2$ and $6$, $I^{2} = -1$, $I$ has no real eigenvector, and chirality is the splitting of the complexification $S \oplus I_{W}S$ into the $\pm I_{W}$ eigenspaces of the complex structure $I$, where $I_{W} = Ie$ is the central pseudoscalar of the odd extension $W = V \oplus \R e$, $Q(e) = -I^{2} = +1$, which commutes with $I$ and with the whole action (\claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}); a conjugation, $I_{W} \mapsto -I_{W}$, reverses it. $I_{W}$ and $I$ are different elements and are not identified. The check enumerates every causal signature with $n \le 14$ and builds $S$ at $(1,1)$, $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$.

\emph{(ii).} With $y = x^{2}$, $(x/2)/\sinh(x/2) = 1/\sum_{k} (y/4)^{k}/(2k+1)! = 1 - y/24 + 7y^{2}/5760 - 31y^{3}/967680 + 127y^{4}/154828800 + \cdots$; the product over the Chern roots, rewritten in the elementary symmetric functions $p_{j}$ of the $y_{i}$, gives the degree-$4j$ parts $-p_{1}/24$, $(7p_{1}^{2} - 4p_{2})/5760$, $(-31p_{1}^{3} + 44p_{1}p_{2} - 16p_{3})/967680$ and $(381p_{1}^{4} - 904p_{1}^{2}p_{2} + 208p_{2}^{2} + 512p_{1}p_{3} - 192p_{4})/464486400$, all nonzero (the check expands the product exactly in four variables). The anomaly theorem, part of (A), imported from the literature, cited from memory and not in the store (Alvarez-Gaum\'e and Witten, 1984), states that the local rotation-gauge and gauge anomalies of a chiral spin-$\tfrac12$ field in dimension $n$ descend from the degree-$(n+2)$ part of $\hat{A}(R)\,\mathrm{ch}(F)$, with sign set by the chirality, and that a local anomaly is removable by a local counterterm if and only if that form vanishes. Pontryagin classes have degrees $4j$, so the pure rotation-gauge part vanishes for $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ and is the nonzero $\hat{A}_{(n+2)/4}$ for $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$. The pure-gauge part is $\mathrm{tr}_{R}F^{k}/k!$ with $k = (n+2)/2$, even exactly when $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$. For a Hermitian generator $X$ of the gauge algebra with real weights $\lambda_{i}$ on $R$, $\mathrm{tr}_{R}X^{k} = \sum_{i}\lambda_{i}^{k}$; for even $k$ the conjugate representation gives the same sum and the sum is positive whenever $X$ acts nontrivially, while for odd $k$ the conjugate gives the negative. By (i) every field of a really chiral tower's single-ideal content, conjugates included, has the same chirality, so the forms of the content are sums of terms of one sign: the rotation-gauge part is $N\hat{A}_{(n+2)/4}$ for $N$ field components counted in units of one chiral field, nonzero for $N \ge 1$, and the gauge part is positive on every nontrivially acting generator. Gauge vectors are not chiral and contribute nothing; the series has no gravitino, gravity being transport and not a quantised field, and the constituents' content contains no two-form field, self-dual or not; a Green-Schwarz term, which could cancel a factorising part, needs such a field, so no field of the content can cancel these forms. The series already treats such conditions as necessary for consistency (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, the four-dimensional case, where conjugation reverses chirality and the cubic sums can and do cancel).

\emph{(iii).} At $(1,1)$ both generators are shared, and under the sourcing rule (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}) the tower's matter sits in comoving copies of its plane in this tower's spacetime and moves in the field of the one metric. A coordinate plane $y = z = 0$ of a spatially flat expanding field $a(\eta)^{2}(-d\eta^{2} + dx^{2} + dy^{2} + dz^{2})$ is the fixed set of two reflections, hence totally geodesic, with induced field $a^{2}(-d\eta^{2} + dx^{2})$ and scalar curvature $R = 2(aa'' - a'^{2})/a^{4}$ (sign convention with de Sitter positive, which is also the store's sign for the scalar curvature, $\mathcal{R} = 4\Lambda$ on de Sitter). For $a = \eta$ (radiation) $R = -2\eta^{-4}$, for $a = \eta^{2}$ (matter) $R = -4\eta^{-6}$, both with nonzero $\partial_{\eta}R$; for $a = -1/(H\eta)$ (de Sitter) $R = 2H^{2}$. The $t$-$r$ plane of the Schwarzschild field, fixed by the reflections of the sphere, has field $-f\,dt^{2} + dr^{2}/f$, $f = 1 - 2M/r$, and $R = -f'' = 4M/r^{3}$, $\partial_{r}R = -12M/r^{4} \ne 0$. The check computes these exactly. The single ideal at $(1,1)$ is one-dimensional and real with $I = +1$, so $N$ constituent fields are $N$ real chiral fields of one sign, with gravitational anomaly coefficient $c_{L} - c_{R} = \pm N/2$ (one such field has central charge $\tfrac12$). The two-dimensional anomaly in covariant form, part of (A) (imported, cited from memory: Alvarez-Gaum\'e and Witten 1984 for the anomaly, Iso, Umetsu and Wilczek 2006 for the covariant form; Robinson and Wilczek 2005 used the consistent form), is $\nabla_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu} = \kappa\,(c_{L} - c_{R})\,\epsilon^{\nu\mu}\partial_{\mu}R$ with $\kappa = \pm 1/96\pi$ by convention, and by Bardeen and Zumino the local counterterm that restores conservation leaves an antisymmetric stress proportional to $R$, so no choice of counterterm gives a stress that is both conserved and rotation-covariant. On the plane fields above $\partial R \ne 0$, so the stress of single-ideal residue-$0$ matter, massive or massless, is not conserved. The field equations of the one metric equate a divergence-free side to the source (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.sourcing-rule-forced-not-chosen}), so such matter cannot be a source of them, and P1 makes every tower's matter a source. Inflow from another tower could cancel the anomaly only through a coupling between towers, and the towers interact only through the one metric (Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-towers-their-types}). The argument concerns the tower's single-ideal matter only. Content carried with equal chiral weight on the two sheets of an edge, as the horizon modes are when labelled by null direction (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.r-loc-needs-sheet-labelled-modes}(v)), has $c_{L} = c_{R}$ on the $t$-$r$ plane and no anomaly; nothing here constrains it. The argument also needs both directions of the tower to be shared, which holds at $(1,1)$ only: a higher causal member of residue $0$, $(1,9)$ or $(9,1)$, shares four directions, and against the one metric its content is four-dimensional as in (iv), with no rotation-gauge anomaly. With the content result that no number of single-ideal constituents at $(1,1)$ is massive (\claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}(ii)), residue $0$ at its lowest causal member holds neither single-ideal matter nor single-ideal radiation, given (A) and the sourcing reading.

\emph{(iv).} At $(1,5)$ the shared generators are $e_{0}, \ldots, e_{3}$ and the unshared $e_{4}, e_{5}$; at $(5,1)$ they are the time $e_{5}$ with $e_{0}, e_{1}, e_{2}$, and $e_{3}, e_{4}$. In both orderings $I = I_{4}J$ with $I_{4}$ the ordered product of the shared generators and $J$ that of the unshared ones, $I_{4}^{2} = J^{2} = -1$, and $I_{4}$, $J$ commute. On $S$, $I_{4}J\psi = c\psi$, so $I_{4}\psi = cJ^{-1}\psi = -cJ\psi$. Under the one metric, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity} is not a field along the unshared directions, the rotation gauge takes values in shared bivectors, all of which commute with $J$; the content is then four-dimensional spin-$\tfrac12$ whose complex chirality (the action of $I_{4}$) is tied to the eigenvalue of the ungauged rotation $J$. In four dimensions the rotation-gauge anomaly form vanishes by (ii), and $J$ is not a gauge generator, so no obstruction arises from the one metric's field. If instead the tower's own gauge fields are fields on its six-dimensional space and act nontrivially on its constituents (the reading (G6), chosen knowing that the unit-ball fit needs residue $4$ empty; the store treats the five-dimensional towers' gauge fields this way, Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}(i), (v), and the one rule's algebra acts on each constituent's pair factor, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gauge-algebra-by-tower}), then by (ii) with $n = 6$ the gauge part $\tfrac{1}{24}\sum\mathrm{tr}_{R}F^{4}$ is positive on every acting generator, so the content's anomaly does not vanish and single-ideal matter of residue $4$ is inconsistent. Neither (G6) nor the cited propositions enter (i) to (iii); without (G6), (i) and (ii) leave residue $4$ unobstructed. The result filed alongside finds that with one ideal residue $4$ escapes emptiness under the momentum reading of mass ($m^{2} = \tfrac14$ for two constituents); under (G6) that escape is closed, since the single-ideal constituents are then anomalous whatever reading of mass is taken.

\emph{Consequence.} The six residues $1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7$ meet no local anomaly from (ii): in odd dimension the forms have odd degree and vanish, and in dimension four the rotation-gauge part vanishes and the gauge part has odd power, so it can cancel within the content: a field and its conjugate of opposite chirality cancel identically, and the Standard Model content cancels by its hypercharges. So, in the lowest-causal window and given (A), under the single-ideal definition the anomaly conditions empty exactly residue $0$, using only the one metric and the sourcing reading, and residue $4$, using (G6). If both ideals are admitted at $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, the content contains each chirality with its conjugate in equal number, every form in (ii) cancels, and nothing here empties either residue; the content result then gives massive matter at $(1,1)$ as well.

synthesis.reversion-pairing-vanishes-res.formal:
Let a tower representative have signature $(p,q)$, $n = p + q$, residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$ and pseudoscalar $\omega$; call it causal when $\min(p,q) = 1$. Use the spinor ideal $S = \Cl^{0}(V)f$ and the momentum $j(\psi) = \ip{\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi}}_{1}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-tower-matter.ideals-fields-momentum}, with the chiral factor $\tfrac12(1 \pm \omega)$ in $f$ in dimension six as in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Every dimension; proved.)} The centre of $\Cl^{0}(V)$ is $\R$ for $n$ odd and $\R \oplus \R\omega$ for $n$ even. When $n$ is even and $\omega^{2} = +1$, $P_{\pm} = \tfrac12(1 \pm \omega)$ are central idempotents of $\Cl^{0}(V)$, and $\rev{P}_{\pm} = P_{\mp}$ exactly when $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$; in that case $\rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2} = 0$ for all $\psi_{1}, \psi_{2} \in \Cl^{0}(V)P_{+}$ (and likewise for $P_{-}$), so the reversion pairing vanishes identically on any spinor ideal of one chirality. A causal signature satisfies these conditions exactly when $r \in \{0, 4\}$, the two residues fixed by the reversal $r \mapsto -r$, in every dimension: its causal members have $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, while the causal members of residues $2$ and $6$ have $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ and $\omega^{2} = -1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Every dimension; proved.)} For a causal signature of any other residue $\Cl^{0}(V)$ is simple, and the reversion pairing on $S$ is not identically zero.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Computed, exact.)} At the nine causal signatures of dimensions two to six, for both chiralities in dimensions two and six, the pairing vanishes on all of $S \times S$ exactly at $(1,1)$, $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Computed, exact.)} Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(i) writes the mass of two constituents as $m^{2} = 2\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0}$ with $x = \rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}$ at $n = 3, 4$ (reproduced here on basis pairs), and (ii) there writes the one-constituent mass at $n = 5$ through $x = \rev{\psi}\psi$: in every populated causal tower mass is a function of the reversion pairing. At $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$ the pairing is zero while the momentum sum of two basis constituents has $m^{2} = \tfrac14$. The pair law therefore does not extend to dimension six, and the two readings of a massive composite (a nonvanishing pairing between constituents; a timelike total momentum) which coincide wherever the store proves them, separate exactly at residues $0$ and $4$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, with one spinor ideal per tower, the emptiness of residues $0$ and $4$ (the clause of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} that the unit-ball fit needs) holds at every causal representative, in every dimension, under the pairing reading, and fails at residue $4$ under the momentum reading; the choice between the two readings in dimensions $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ is what that clause carries. The flag bit cannot carry it: residues $0$, $4$ and the odd residues all lack the bit, and the odd residues have a nonvanishing pairing. Taking the pairing reading is a costed clause, chosen with the fit known (the unit-ball value is itself a fit, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}). Filed alongside, synthesis.residues-zero-four-real-chirality-anomaly cites (i) as its lemma; under its hypothesis (G6), that a residue-$4$ tower's own gauge fields live on its six-dimensional space, its anomaly result closes the momentum reading's escape at residue $4$.
synthesis.reversion-pairing-vanishes-res.technical:
In a tower of even dimension whose pseudoscalar squares to $+1$, the projectors $\tfrac12(1 \pm \omega)$ split the even subalgebra into two chirality blocks. When the dimension is $2 \bmod 4$ the reversion turns $\omega$ into $-\omega$ and so exchanges the two blocks; then $\rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}$ lands in the product of the two blocks, which is zero, for any two constituents of one chirality. Among the towers with one time direction this happens exactly at residues $0$ and $4$, the two residues fixed by the reversal, in every dimension; elsewhere the even subalgebra is simple and the pairing is not zero. An exact computation confirms it at the nine lowest causal signatures.

T14c's mass formulas in dimensions three, four and five express mass through this pairing. At $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$ the pairing is identically zero, but the total momentum of two constituents still has $m^{2} = \tfrac14$. So "mass carried by the pairing" and "mass as a timelike total momentum" agree wherever the series has proved them and disagree exactly at residues $0$ and $4$. With one spinor ideal per tower, the first reading empties residues $0$ and $4$ in every window, and the second leaves residue $4$ massive; the clause of P3 that the dark-matter fit needs is this choice, made with the fit known, and the flag bit cannot make it. Filed alongside, the anomaly result for these residues closes the momentum reading's escape at residue $4$ under the hypothesis that that tower's own gauge fields live on its six dimensions.
synthesis.reversion-pairing-vanishes-res.lay: The dark-matter paper needs two of its eight families of hidden worlds to be empty, and so far it has simply assumed that. This result finds that exactly those two families share a peculiar algebraic feature in every dimension: the quantity the series uses to pair two building blocks into a massive particle is identically zero there, while it is not zero in the six families that are supposed to hold matter. If mass is taken to come from that pairing, as in every case the series has proved (dimensions three to five), the two families are empty automatically; if instead mass is read off from the combined motion of the building blocks, one of them is not. The assumption is thereby turned into a precise choice between two definitions that agree everywhere else.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} For $n$ even every vector anticommutes with $\omega$, so every bivector, and hence every even element, commutes with it: $\omega$ is central in $\Cl^{0}(V)$. A basis blade $e_{B}$ commutes or anticommutes with each bivector $e_{i}e_{k}$, and distinct blades multiply a fixed blade to distinct blades, so the centre of $\Cl^{0}(V)$ is spanned by the even blades that commute with every bivector; these are $1$ alone for $n$ odd and $1, \omega$ for $n$ even (the check enumerates every signature with $n \le 8$). Since $\omega^{2} = e_{1}\cdots e_{n}e_{1}\cdots e_{n} = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}\prod_{i}e_{i}^{2} = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2 + q}$ and $\rev{\omega} = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}\omega$, for $n$ even and $\omega^{2} = 1$ the elements $P_{\pm} = \tfrac12(1 \pm \omega)$ are central idempotents with $P_{+}P_{-} = 0$, and $\rev{P}_{+} = P_{-}$ exactly when $n(n-1)/2$ is odd, that is $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$. Then for $\psi_{1}, \psi_{2} \in \Cl^{0}(V)P_{+}$, using $\psi_{i} = \psi_{i}P_{+}$, $\rev{\psi}_{1} = P_{-}\rev{\psi}_{1}$ and the centrality of $P_{-}$ on the even element $\rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}$,
\[
\rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2} \;=\; P_{-}\,\rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}\,P_{+} \;=\; \rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}\,P_{-}P_{+} \;=\; 0 .
\]
For a causal signature with $q = 1$ the residue is $n - 2$, and with $p = 1$ it is $2 - n$; either way $r \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ exactly when $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, and then the exponent $n(n-1)/2 + q$ is even (odd plus one for $q = 1$, odd plus $n - 1$ for $p = 1$), so $\omega^{2} = 1$. When $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ the same exponent is odd and $\omega^{2} = -1$, and the residue is $2$ or $6$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.oriented-causal-towers-mirror-pair-every-window}(i)). The check confirms the sign rules against the algebra for every signature with $n \le 8$ and applies them to the causal signatures for $n \le 64$. The fixed points of $r \mapsto -r$ modulo $8$ are $0$ and $4$. Residue, Morita class and division-ring type are constant along a tower (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}); the statement here is about every causal member, not only the lowest.

\emph{(ii)} For a causal signature of residue other than $0$ and $4$, either $n$ is odd and $\Cl^{0}(V)$ is a semisimple real algebra with centre $\R$, hence simple, or $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ and the centre is $\R \oplus \R\omega$ with $\omega^{2} = -1$, a field, so again $\Cl^{0}(V)$ is simple. Write $A = \Cl^{0}(V)$. With $\psi_{1} = f$ and $\psi_{2} = af$, $a \in A$, the pairing is $\rev{f}\,a\,f$. In a simple ring $AfA = A$, so $\rev{f}AfA = \rev{f}A \ni \rev{f} \ne 0$ and therefore $\rev{f}Af \ne 0$: the pairing is not identically zero on $S$.

\emph{(iii)} With the bases of $S$ built from Definition \claimref{obj.dark-tower-matter.ideals-fields-momentum} exactly as in the check of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content} (dimensions $1, 2, 2, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8, 8$ at $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(1,3)$, $(3,1)$, $(1,4)$, $(4,1)$, $(1,5)$, $(5,1)$), the check evaluates $\rev{s}_{i}s_{l}$ on every pair of basis elements; it is zero for all pairs exactly at $(1,1)$ (either ideal, $f$ or $1 - f$, which are $P_{\pm}$ there) and at $(1,5)$, $(5,1)$ for either chiral factor, and nonzero for some pair at the six other signatures. By bilinearity, vanishing on basis pairs is vanishing on $S \times S$.

\emph{(iv)} On every ordered pair of basis elements of $S$ at $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(1,3)$, $(3,1)$ the check confirms $m^{2}(j(s_{i}) + j(s_{l})) = 2\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0}$ with $x = \rev{s}_{i}s_{l}$ and $x^{\dagger} = e_{t}\rev{x}e_{t}^{-1}$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(i), whose proof is a polynomial identity), and counts the pairs with nonzero mass ($2$, $2$, $8$, $8$). At $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$, by (i), $x = 0$ for every pair, so the right-hand side is zero, while the momentum sum of the first two basis elements has $m^{2} = \tfrac14$, the value of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}(iii). Hence the identity fails in dimension six. In dimension five Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(ii) gives the one-constituent mass as $\tfrac12\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0}$ with $x = \rev{\psi}\psi$, so in each of the populated causal towers (dimensions three, four, five) the mass the store has proved is a function of the reversion pairing. The momentum reading at $(1,5)$ rests on Premise H1 extended to dimension six, as recorded in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}; part (iv) inherits that extension and parts (i) to (iii) do not use it.

\emph{The consequence.} With one spinor ideal per tower, a reading in which a composite is massive only through a nonvanishing pairing of its constituents gives no massive matter at any causal member of residues $0$ and $4$, in any dimension, by (i), and leaves the six other residues their pairing, by (ii); the momentum reading gives mass at $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}(iii)). The flag bit exists exactly at $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.oriented-causal-towers-mirror-pair-every-window}), so residues $0$, $4$ and every odd residue lack it; since the odd residues have a nonvanishing pairing by (ii) and are taken as populated, absence of the bit cannot be the reason for the emptiness of $0$ and $4$. The pairing reading is a costed clause, chosen with the fit known (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}). Filed alongside, synthesis.residues-zero-four-real-chirality-anomaly cites (i) as its lemma; under its hypothesis (G6), that the residue-$4$ tower's own gauge fields are fields on its six-dimensional space acting on its constituents, the anomaly of a single chiral ideal excludes residue-$4$ matter on either reading, which closes the momentum reading's escape there.

(Reading, parenthetical and from memory: in the field-theory language this is the statement that in dimensions $2 \bmod 4$ the Lorentz-invariant spinor bilinears pair opposite chiralities only, charge conjugation preserving chirality there, so a single-chirality field admits no mass term; the two-constituent momentum mass is then the invariant mass of a two-particle state of massless quanta, which any non-collinear pair has. The statement above does not rely on this reading.)

synthesis.seeding-remainder-excludes-per.formal:
Let the remainder $\Omega h^{2} = 0.0976 \pm 0.0012$, that is $4.364\,\Omega_{b}$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(ii)), consist of odd-tower relics of gravitational seeding with quanta no heavier than the bath, produced at the rate of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate} with summed coefficient $c$ over the produced light content, with the yield of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature} (the two antecedents of T14's seeding signpost, not asserted by T14). Then $c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{4} \ge A/2$ with $A^{1/4} = 1.217 \times 10^{12}$ GeV, the factor $2$ being the yield bracket of the imported rate. Assume Premise \claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy}, $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le \alpha = \min(\alpha, M_{3})$, of which only the consequence $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le M_{3}$ is used.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] On the chain of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector} with the $(15,2,2)$ at the record's central values, $M_{3} = f_{J}v_{R}$ with $v_{R} = 4.2 \times 10^{10}$ GeV. If $f_{J} \le 4\pi$, then $M_{3} < 5.35 \times 10^{11}$ GeV and the four conditions are jointly satisfiable only if $c > c^{*} = 13.49$, about $5900$ vector species at the imported per-vector coefficient. The four odd towers' gauge vectors (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gauge-algebra-by-tower}: $2 + 2 + 9 + 9$) give $c = 0.051$, and four towers each with the mirror's Standard-Model coefficient $0.078$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii)) give $0.312$; at these the seeding temperature exceeds the largest allowed $M_{3}$ by factors above $4.0$ and $2.5$. Satisfying the signpost on this chain at $c = 0.312$ needs $f_{J} > 32$, a Dirac mass $m_{D} > 8.2$ GeV against the perturbative cap $5.2$ GeV.
\item[(ii)] Without the chain, at the bottom end of Hypothesis (U) read at a common low scale (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success}), $M_{3} = m_{b}^{2}/m_{3} < 3.63 \times 10^{11}$ GeV and the conjunction needs $c > 63.7$.
\item[(iii)] The top end of (U) at a common low scale, $M_{3} = m_{t}^{2}/m_{3} > 5.8 \times 10^{14}$ GeV, satisfies the signpost for any $c \ge 0.051$ (the odd towers' vectors alone) even with $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le M_{3}/66$, and on the chain it needs $f_{J} > 4000\pi$. The clause with $M_{3}/66$ depends on that reading: read at the ceiling, both ends of (U) fall by about an order of magnitude and $(M_{3}/66)^{4} < A/(2c)$ at $c = 0.051$, while $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le M_{3}$ alone is still met.
\end{enumerate}
So under (R) the odd-tower remainder is a seeding relic only off the perturbative Pati-Salam branch and only at the top end of (U); on the perturbative chain, whose cap lies near the bottom end of (U), the remainder must come from the descent's deposit, or (R), or the seeding antecedents, fail. The margin in (i) at $c = 0.312$ survives an increase of $v_{R}$ by a factor up to $2.5$; the same chain at one loop (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.chain}(2)), $M_{I} = 3.2 \times 10^{11}$ GeV, exceeds that, so (i) holds at the two-loop record level only.
synthesis.seeding-remainder-excludes-per.technical:
Assume the remainder of the dark matter, $4.364$ times the baryons, consists of odd-tower relics produced gravitationally from the visible plasma, with quanta no heavier than the bath, which are the two antecedents of T14's seeding signpost. With the stored yield, the remainder then needs $c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{4} \ge A/2$ with $A^{1/4} = 1.217 \times 10^{12}$ GeV, where $c$ sums the imported production coefficients over the produced light species and the $2$ is the imported rate's yield bracket. Premise (R), assumed, gives $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le M_{3}$ in its weakest form.

On the Standard-Model paper's chain with the $(15,2,2)$, the heavy neutrino mass is $M_{3} = f_{J}v_{R}$ with $v_{R} = 4.2 \times 10^{10}$ GeV, so a perturbative $f_{J} \le 4\pi$ caps $M_{3}$ below $5.35 \times 10^{11}$ GeV. All four conditions then hold only if $c > 13.49$, about $5900$ vector species. The odd towers' gauge vectors give $c = 0.051$, and four towers with Standard-Model-sized content give $0.312$; at these the seeding temperature exceeds the cap by factors above $4$ and $2.5$, and meeting the signpost would need $f_{J} > 32$. At the bottom end of Hypothesis (U), with no chain input, $M_{3} < 3.63 \times 10^{11}$ GeV and the conjunction needs $c > 63.7$. At the top end of (U), read at a common low scale, the signpost is met, for content at least the odd towers' vectors, even with the fitted factor $66$ below $M_{3}$ (read at the ceiling, only without that factor), but on the chain that end needs $f_{J}$ above $10^{4}$.

So under (R) the odd towers' remainder can be a seeding relic only off the perturbative Pati-Salam branch, at the top end of (U); on the perturbative chain, whose cap lies near the bottom end of (U), it must come from the descent's deposit, or (R) or the seeding antecedents fail. The margin holds at the two-loop record level only; the one-loop intermediate scale of the same chain would dissolve it. A representative fit of the Standard-Model paper under Premise (EW) reaches the same conclusion without the perturbativity bound (filed alongside, synthesis.untuned-fit-caps-lightest-heavy-neutrino).
synthesis.seeding-remainder-excludes-per.lay: The series leaves open where the part of the dark matter not explained by the mirror world comes from. One suggestion in the dark-matter paper is that it was made by gravity alone from the hot early universe, which would need that early universe to have been at least about a trillion GeV hot. A separate assumption in the neutrino paper says the early universe never got hot enough to make the heavy neutrinos, and the Standard-Model paper's preferred unification route, with a reasonably sized coupling, puts those neutrinos below about half a trillion GeV. This result checks the arithmetic, assuming the leftover dark matter was made by gravity in that way and using the Standard-Model route's couplings as computed at two loops: the three cannot all hold for any plausible amount of hidden matter. Something has to give: the heavy neutrinos are heavier than that route allows, the early universe was hotter than the neutrino assumption allows, or the leftover dark matter was laid down directly at the universe's origin rather than made by gravity afterwards.

proofs.main:
\emph{The seeding requirement.} By Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature} a tower heated by graviton-mediated production at rate $c\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$ (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}) carries comoving yield $Y = c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}/(3\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3})$, $\kappa_{s} = 145.3$ at $g_{*} = g_{s} = 100$, $M_{P} = 2.435 \times 10^{18}$ GeV. Summing over the produced towers, $c$ is the summed coefficient over all produced light species. The provenance of the rate absorbs the particle-pair and mean-energy factors into at most $2^{1/4}$ on the temperature ratio $\xi \propto Y^{1/4}$, so at most a factor $2$ on $Y$; we allow $Y \le 2c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}/(3\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3})$. If the relics' mass is $m \le T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ (the bath condition of T14's signpost), their mass per unit entropy is at most $2c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{4}/(3\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3})$. The remainder is $(\Omega_{c}/\Omega_{b} - 1)$ times the baryon mass per unit entropy, $m_{p}\,\eta_{s}$ with $\eta_{s} = 8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ the baryons per unit entropy of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(iii) and $\Omega_{c}/\Omega_{b} - 1 = 4.364 \pm 0.065$ from Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}. Taking the lower ends, $4.299$ and $8.65 \times 10^{-11}$, and $m_{p} = 0.938272$ GeV, the requirement is $c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{4} \ge A/2$ with
\[
A = 3\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3}\,(4.299)(0.938272)(8.65 \times 10^{-11})\ \mathrm{GeV}, \qquad (1.217 \times 10^{12})^{4} < A < (1.218 \times 10^{12})^{4}\ \mathrm{GeV}^{4}.
\]
(With central inputs and no factor $2$ this is T14's signpost: $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \ge 1.22 \times 10^{12}\,c^{-1/4}$ GeV, above $2 \times 10^{12}$ GeV for $c \le 0.14$.)

\emph{Premise (R).} Premise \claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy} states $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le \alpha = \min(\alpha, M_{3})$, hence $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le M_{3}$, the hypothesis of the statement. We use only this; the branch value $\alpha \approx M_{3}/66$ of T15 is a fitted instance and would strengthen (i) and (ii) by $66^{4}$ in $c^{*}$.

\emph{(i)} Proposition \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector} gives, on the chain with the $(15,2,2)$ at central values, $v_{R} = 4.2 \times 10^{10}$ GeV and $m_{D}^{2} = m_{3}f_{J}v_{R}$; the seesaw $m_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/M_{3}$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} then reads $M_{3} = f_{J}v_{R}$, which is the statement of T15 Remark 4.7 that the Majorana matrix on this route is $v_{R}f$. With $v_{R} \le 4.25 \times 10^{10}$ (the rounding) and $f_{J} \le 4\pi < 4 \cdot 355/113$, $M_{3} < 5.35 \times 10^{11}$ GeV. The conjunction needs $A/(2c) \le T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{4} \le M_{3}^{4}$, so $c \ge c^{*} = A/(2M_{3}^{4})$, and exact evaluation gives $13.49 < c^{*} < 13.50$, more than $5800$ times the per-vector coefficient $2.3 \times 10^{-3}$. Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gauge-algebra-by-tower} gives the odd towers' gauge algebras of dimensions $2, 2, 9, 9$, so their vectors alone give $c = 22 \times 2.3 \times 10^{-3} = 0.0506$; Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii) gives $c \le 0.078$ for a Standard-Model content, and four such towers give $0.312$. At these values $A/(2c) > (4.04\,M_{3})^{4}$ and $> (2.56\,M_{3})^{4}$ respectively, and at $c = 0.312$, $T_{\mathrm{desc}} > 1.36 \times 10^{12}$ GeV. Meeting the signpost on the chain at $c = 0.312$ needs $f_{J} = M_{3}/v_{R} \ge T_{\mathrm{desc}}/v_{R} > 32$, and $m_{D}^{2} = m_{3}M_{3} \ge m_{3}T_{\mathrm{desc}} > (8.2\ \mathrm{GeV})^{2}$ with $m_{3} \ge 49.4$ meV, while $f_{J} \le 4\pi$ gives $m_{D}^{2} = m_{3}f_{J}v_{R} < (5.2\ \mathrm{GeV})^{2}$. Since the comparison is linear in $v_{R}^{4}$, the conclusion at $c = 0.312$ survives any $v_{R}$ below $2.56$ times the stored value; the same chain at one loop has $M_{I} = 3.2 \times 10^{11}$ GeV (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.chain}(2)), about seventeen times the two-loop value, so (i) is a two-loop record-level statement.

\emph{(ii)} Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} at its bottom end gives $M_{3} = m_{b}^{2}/m_{3}$; with $m_{b} \le 4.23$ GeV and $m_{3} \ge 49.4$ meV, $M_{3} < 3.63 \times 10^{11}$ GeV and $c^{*} = A/(2M_{3}^{4}) \in (63.7, 63.9)$.

\emph{(iii)} At the top end, $m_{t} \ge 172.28$ GeV and $m_{3} \le 50.5$ meV give $M_{3} > 5.8 \times 10^{14}$ GeV and $(M_{3}/66)^{4} > A/c$ already at the vectors' $c = 0.0506$ without the factor $2$, so the signpost is met; on the chain, $f_{J} = M_{3}/v_{R} > 4000\pi$. Read at the ceiling, with both ends of (U) lowered by a factor $10$, $M_{3}/10 > 5.8 \times 10^{13}$ GeV still satisfies $(M_{3}/10)^{4} > A/c$ at $c = 0.0506$, but $(M_{3}/660)^{4} < A/(2c)$ there (using $M_{3} < 6.1 \times 10^{14}$ GeV from $m_{t} \le 172.86$ GeV and $m_{3} \ge 49.4$ meV), so the clause with the factor $66$ holds only at the common low scale.

The check evaluates every inequality above in exact rational arithmetic, comparing fourth powers so that no root is taken, and recovers $\kappa_{s}$ from its formula and the stored $1.44$ GeV of the chain's Dirac mass at $f_{J} = 1$.

synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temp.formal:
\emph{Hypothesis (B').} The reversal pair carries the joint boundary-mode algebra, the CAR algebra over $\ell^{2}(J) \oplus \ell^{2}(J')$ (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics} for each tower), and the superselection of the tower charge (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}) is represented by taking as observables the elements invariant under each tower's charge rotation $a_{j} \mapsto e^{\theta e_{2}e_{3}}a_{j}$ ($j \in J$), $a'_{j} \mapsto e^{\theta' e_{2}e_{3}}a'_{j}$ ($j \in J'$), with $\theta, \theta'$ independent. Here the complex unit of the boundary modes is the transverse bivector $e_{2}e_{3}$, which commutes with the radial-plane modes and squares to $-1$, and their scalars are $\mathrm{span}\{1, e_{2}e_{3}\}$ (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}, where it is called $J$; it is written out here because $J$ names the mode set).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The charge is a sector label on windows.)} On every window $\mathfrak{A}_{F} \otimes \mathfrak{A}'_{F'}$ the observable algebra is the direct sum, over the joint charge values $(q, q')$, of the full matrix algebras of the joint charge eigenspaces; its centre is spanned by the joint charge projections, and window states of different charge are disjoint.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The temperature is not, on windows.)} Every product of Gibbs states of the two towers' boost clocks at inverse temperatures $\beta, \beta'$, equal or not, has invertible density and gives positive weight to every joint charge sector; so any two of them have the same central support, $1$, and no central projection of the observable window algebra separates two values of $\xi = \beta/\beta'$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The temperature on the full algebra.)} For the I-states $\omega_{\beta}$, $\omega_{\beta'}$ of one tower (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}) with $\beta \neq \beta'$, let $a_{j} = \sqrt{n_{j}n'_{j}} + \sqrt{(1 - n_{j})(1 - n'_{j})}$ be the Hellinger affinity of mode $j$; $a_{j} < 1$ for every mode of nonzero frequency, and $1 - a_{j} \le |n_{j} - n'_{j}|$. By the Powers-Stormer criterion the two states are quasi-equivalent if $\sum_{j}(1 - a_{j}) < \infty$ and disjoint otherwise. Hence if infinitely many frequencies $\omega_{j}$ lie in a compact subset of $(0, \infty)$ the two I-states are disjoint, and the temperature is a label of the full algebra in the disjointness sense, which on the full algebra is also the sense in which charge sectors are labels; if $\sum_{j}(n_{j} + n'_{j}) < \infty$ they are quasi-equivalent. The stored charge is a finite label (an eigenvalue of an element of the observable algebra) only on windows: a thermal state over infinitely many modes has no finite total charge, and there the charge too can be a label only in the disjointness sense, as a charge density. So the comparison of (i) with (iii) is between like and like exactly when the deposited mode set is finite, or when both are read as densities.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} The scoping first offered, without proof, in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.mirror-asymmetry-route-one} at its version 2, and stated by P2 at its version 2 (labels, not states), under which P2 equates the superselection labels of the descent and not the state within the selected sector, is well defined and leaves $\xi$ free on every finite window, and on the full algebra exactly when the sum in (iii) converges; when infinitely many boundary modes share a frequency band, the same scoping reaches $\xi$ and gives $\xi = 1$, the value Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent} reads as excluded under its hypothesis (M). Which case holds is decided by whether the deposited sector's mode set is finite, as the series' count of about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$ boundary modes for the cosmological horizon suggests (an observation-level count, not a premise here), or infinite, as the countable $J$ of the Definition allows. The scoping reaches the stored charge $Q = \epsilon N$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}), but not the ceiling coupling, which is not a charge.
synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temp.technical: The question is whether the mirror's temperature is the same kind of quantity as the stored asymmetry, so that one rule could equate the second and not the first. In the boundary-mode model the asymmetry is a superselected charge: on every finite set of modes the observables split into blocks labelled by the two towers' charges, and states of different charge can be told apart by a central element. The temperatures are not labels of that kind: thermal states of the pair at any two temperatures give weight to every block, so no central element distinguishes them; within one block the temperature is a property of the state. On the infinite algebra the situation changes when infinitely many modes have frequencies in a bounded band away from zero: then, by the Powers-Stormer criterion, thermal states at different temperatures are disjoint, and the temperature becomes a label as well, in the same disjointness sense in which a charge density is one there (a thermal state over infinitely many modes has no finite total charge). A rule of indifference applied to labels of the descent and not to states can therefore free the mirror's temperature if the deposited sector has finitely many modes, as the series' mode count suggests, and cannot if it has infinitely many in a band. Such a rule reaches the asymmetry but not the ceiling coupling.
synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temp.lay: The framework's prediction of no extra radiation needs the mirror copy of our matter to be cold, while its indifference principle treats our world and the mirror alike. One way out is to say that the principle equalises only fixed labels of each world, like a conserved charge, and not the state each world happens to be in, like its temperature. This result checks whether that distinction is real in the mathematical model the framework uses. For any finite number of modes it is: the charge labels separate blocks of the theory, and temperature does not. With infinitely many modes at similar frequencies it fails, because temperature then becomes a label too. So the way out works only if the relevant number of modes is finite, which is something the framework has to decide.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} Under (B') the joint algebra is the CAR algebra over $\ell^{2}(J) \oplus \ell^{2}(J')$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra} for its states), its windows are $\mathfrak{A}_{F} \otimes \mathfrak{A}'_{F'} \cong \End(\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{F}) \otimes \End(\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{F'})$ (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}), with scalars $\mathrm{span}\{1, e_{2}e_{3}\}$, $e_{2}e_{3}$ the boundary modes' complex unit, and the two charge rotations act on a window by conjugation with $e^{\theta e_{2}e_{3}Q_{F}}$ and $e^{\theta' e_{2}e_{3}Q'_{F'}}$, $Q_{F} = \sum_{j \in F}N_{j}$, $Q'_{F'} = \sum_{j \in F'}N'_{j}$. Representing the superselection of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable} by these invariants is the hypothesis (B'); the stored asymmetry is the eigenvalue of such a charge (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(i)).

(i) An element of $\End(\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{F})$ is invariant under conjugation by $e^{\theta e_{2}e_{3}Q_{F}}$ for all $\theta$ if and only if it commutes with $Q_{F}$, that is, if and only if it preserves each eigenspace $\Lambda^{q}\C^{F}$; so the invariant subalgebra is $\bigoplus_{q}\End(\Lambda^{q}\C^{F})$, a direct sum of full matrix algebras, whose centre is spanned by the eigenprojections $P_{q}$ of $Q_{F}$. The same holds for the mirror, and the observable window algebra, the tensor product of the two invariant subalgebras, is $\bigoplus_{q, q'}\End(\Lambda^{q}\C^{F} \otimes \Lambda^{q'}\C^{F'})$ with centre spanned by the $P_{q} \otimes P'_{q'}$. Two window states supported in different joint sectors are separated by the central projection of one of them, so they are disjoint. The check realises a window of two modes per tower in $\Cl(4,4)$, confirms the CAR relations, confirms that the charge projections are idempotent, sum to one, have ranks $4$, $8$, $4$ of $16$, and commute with every bilinear $a^{*}_{i}a_{j}$ of either tower, and computes the dimension of the algebra those bilinears generate as $36 = (1 + 4 + 1)^{2}$, the dimension of $\bigoplus_{q,q'}\End$ for sectors of dimensions $1, 2, 1$ in each tower; it also exhibits two states of different charge separated by a central projection.

(ii) For one-particle Hamiltonians $h$, $h'$ and inverse temperatures $\beta$, $\beta'$ the product of Gibbs states has density $\rho = \prod_{j \in F}(1 + (x_{j} - 1)N_{j}) \prod_{j \in F'}(1 + (x'_{j} - 1)N'_{j})$ up to normalisation, $x_{j} = e^{-\beta\omega_{j}}$, $x'_{j} = e^{-\beta'\omega'_{j}}$, all positive; its inverse is the same product with every $x$ replaced by $1/x$, so $\rho$ is invertible and the state is faithful. A faithful state gives every nonzero projection positive weight, in particular every $P_{q} \otimes P'_{q'}$, so its central support is $1$. Two states with the same central support are not separated by any central projection: if $Z$ is central with $\omega(Z) = 1$ then $\omega(1 - Z) = 0$, so $1 - Z = 0$ by faithfulness, and $\omega'(Z) = 1$ as well. On a finite-dimensional algebra this is quasi-equivalence. So within every joint sector the ratio $\xi$ is a parameter of the state and not of the sector. The check confirms $\rho\rho^{-1} = 1$ exactly, that all nine sector weights are positive and sum to one, and that the mirror's occupation is $x'/(1 + x')$ and differs from ours exactly when $x' \neq x$, for $x = \tfrac13$ and $x' \in \{\tfrac13, \tfrac{1}{50}, \tfrac27\}$.

(iii) The I-state at $\beta$ is the quasi-free state with diagonal symbol $n_{j} = (e^{\beta\omega_{j}} + 1)^{-1}$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}), gauge-invariant. The Powers-Stormer criterion (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness}(a)) states that two gauge-invariant quasi-free states with symbols $A$, $B$ are quasi-equivalent if and only if $A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}$ and $(1 - A)^{1/2} - (1 - B)^{1/2}$ are Hilbert-Schmidt, and that such states are factor states, so that they are disjoint whenever they are not quasi-equivalent. For diagonal symbols the sum of the two squared Hilbert-Schmidt norms is $\sum_{j}\bigl[(\sqrt{n_{j}} - \sqrt{n'_{j}})^{2} + (\sqrt{1 - n_{j}} - \sqrt{1 - n'_{j}})^{2}\bigr] = 2\sum_{j}(1 - a_{j})$, which gives the stated dichotomy. For a mode of frequency $\omega_{j} > 0$, $n_{j} \neq n'_{j}$ when $\beta \neq \beta'$, and $a_{j} < 1$: squaring, $a_{j}^{2} < 1$ is equivalent to $4n n'(1 - n)(1 - n') < (n + n' - 2nn')^{2}$, and directly, $a_{j}$ is the Bhattacharyya coefficient of two distinct probability vectors $(n, 1 - n)$ and $(n', 1 - n')$, which equals $1$ only when they coincide (Cauchy-Schwarz with equality only for proportional vectors). The bound $1 - a_{j} \le |n_{j} - n'_{j}|$ follows from $(\sqrt{p} - \sqrt{q})^{2} \le |\sqrt{p} - \sqrt{q}|(\sqrt{p} + \sqrt{q}) = |p - q|$ applied to both terms. Now $1 - a$ is a continuous, strictly positive function of $\omega$ on $(0, \infty)$ at fixed $\beta \neq \beta'$, so it is bounded below by some $c > 0$ on any compact subset; infinitely many frequencies in such a subset make $\sum_{j}(1 - a_{j}) \ge \sum c = \infty$, and the states are disjoint. If instead $\sum_{j}(n_{j} + n'_{j}) < \infty$, then $\sum_{j}(1 - a_{j}) \le \sum_{j}|n_{j} - n'_{j}| < \infty$ and they are quasi-equivalent. Disjoint factor states of the full algebra are separated by a central projection of the von Neumann algebra of their direct sum, so in the first case $\beta$ is a label in the disjointness sense. The same conclusion for KMS factor states whose induced von Neumann algebra is of type III is Takesaki's theorem (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness}(b)), the standard result behind (iii). The comparison with (i) needs care: there the charge is a label because it is the eigenvalue of a central element of a finite window algebra. On the full algebra $Q = \sum_{j}N_{j}$ is not an element of the observable C*-algebra, and a thermal I-state over infinitely many modes has no finite total charge; what can label such a state is a charge density, and only in the same disjointness sense (by the criterion above with $n_{j}$ shifted by a chemical potential). So the stored charge $Q = \epsilon N$ is a finite sector label of the deposited state exactly when the deposited mode set is finite, the same finiteness the reading below invokes for the temperature; with infinitely many modes both are labels in the disjointness sense, and a scope to labels reaches both. The check verifies, in exact rational arithmetic over a grid of seven Gibbs parameters $x = e^{-\beta\omega}$ in each argument, that $a^{2} < 1$ exactly when $x \neq x'$ (equality exactly on the diagonal), through the rational form above, and that $1 - a \le |n - n'|$, through the rational inequality $4nn'(1 - n)(1 - n') \ge \bigl((1 - |n - n'|)^{2} - nn' - (1 - n)(1 - n')\bigr)^{2}$ whenever the bracket is positive.

\emph{The reading.} Proposition \claimref{synthesis.mirror-asymmetry-route-one} first offered, at its version 2 and without proof, a scoping under which P2 equates the superselected charges of the descent, which the stored asymmetry is and the temperature ratio is not; P2 states it at its version 2 (labels, not states), and the Proposition now reads route one through it. By (i) and (ii) that distinction is a representation-theoretic one on every window: the stored charge selects a central projection, the temperature does not. By (iii) it survives the inductive limit exactly when the sum converges; when infinitely many boundary modes share a frequency band it does not, the temperature is then a label of the same kind as the charge, and a scoping to labels equates the two towers' temperatures, $\xi = 1$, which Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent} reads, under its hypothesis (M), as $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$, excluded. The series counts about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$ boundary modes for the cosmological horizon (at observation level, in the Standard-Model paper's largeness observation, not used as a premise here), a finite number, which places the series in the first case if that count bounds the deposited sector's modes; the Definition's countable $J$ does not decide it. The ceiling coupling of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv) is not a charge, so the scoping does not reach it; it reaches the asymmetry clause (v).

synthesis.two-frozen-points-conformally-.formal:
Let $U$ be a connected region of conformal Minkowski space with the flat scale $\eta$ of signature $(1,3)$, so that the tractor connection of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} is flat, with tractor form $\eta^{-1}(\mu,\mu) + 2\sigma\rho$ of signature $(2,4)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Frozen points.)} For constants $s, r \in \R$ and $m \in \R^{1,3}$, the tractor $I_{(s,m,r)} = (\sigma, d\sigma, r)$ with $\sigma = s + \eta(m, x) - \tfrac{r}{2}Q(x)$ is parallel, with constant norm $Q(I) = 2rs + Q(m)$; on the region $\sigma \neq 0$ its scale $\sigma^{-2}\eta$ is Einstein with $\Lambda = 3Q(I)$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Two frozen points, one $\Lambda$.)} Two such tractors $I_A, I_B$ of equal norm $\Lambda/3 \neq 0$ that are not proportional give, where $\sigma_A\sigma_B \neq 0$, two Einstein metrics $\sigma_A^{-2}\eta$ and $\sigma_B^{-2}\eta$ with the same $\Lambda$ in one conformal class that are not homothetic ($\sigma_A/\sigma_B$ is not constant). Example: $I_A = (1, 0, 1)$, $I_B = (1, (1,0,0,0), \tfrac12)$, $\Lambda = 6$, $\ip{I_A}{I_B} = \tfrac32$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Not a gauge copy.)} The ambient group $SO(2,4)$ has dimension $15$; the stabiliser of one non-null frozen point has dimension $10$, and that of an equal-norm pair spanning a nondegenerate plane has dimension $6$. Pairs of points of fixed norm form a ten-dimensional space with nine-dimensional orbits, so the pair has exactly one invariant, $\ip{I_A}{I_B}$, which no gauge transformation changes. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}, which makes every fluctuation of one pair $(I, V)$ a gauge transformation, does not reach it.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Stationarity.)} The tractor curvature $F$ vanishes on $U$, so a sum over towers $\sum_r Q(I_r)^{-1}\int \epsilon(I_r, V_r, F, F)$ of functionals in the three-argument form, with one shared connection, is stationary at this configuration under variations of the connection and of every $(I_r, V_r)$, whatever the frozen points are.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, on a region where the Weyl part of the field strength vanishes, and in particular on the de Sitter vacuum, the frozen-point geometry, the three-argument functional and the no-fluctuation proposition allow the towers to couple to different frozen points of one norm. The metric clause of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} is there an independent choice: it fixes the invariant by requiring $I_B = \pm I_A$.

\emph{Note (scope, 2026-11-11).} The statement is for the normal tractor connection. For the connection $A_{\rho}$ of Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point} (FS) the field strength is $-(\mathcal{R} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\mathrm{id})$, which vanishes on the de Sitter field at that $\Lambda$ and on no other isotropic field with matter, so for that connection the independent choice exists only on a component that is de Sitter at that $\Lambda$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-unique-for-the-field-space-connection}, clauses (iii) and (iv)).
synthesis.two-frozen-points-conformally-.technical: P1 says that every tower couples to one frozen point and so to one metric. This result tests whether that follows from the frozen-point geometry and the action. On a region where the Weyl part of the field strength vanishes (conformally flat derived metric), which includes the de Sitter vacuum, the tractor connection is flat and every constant tractor is parallel. Any two parallel tractors of the same norm give two Einstein metrics with the same cosmological constant in one conformal class, not related by a constant rescaling. The ambient group cannot carry one into the other while keeping the pair: the pair has one gauge invariant, their inner product. The configuration is stationary for a sum of the functional over towers, since every term of its first variation carries a factor of the vanishing curvature. So on the vacuum, the premises other than P1 allow towers with different frozen points of one norm, and the metric clause of P1 is an independent choice there. Where the Weyl tensor has no kernel vector, parallel tractors are multiples of one, and the question does not arise.
synthesis.two-frozen-points-conformally-.lay: One of the series' assumptions is that every hidden sector feels the same gravity, because the origin of the universe fixed one special reference point for everything. This result asks whether the rest of the theory forces that. In empty space with a cosmological constant it does not. There, two different reference points of the same strength can coexist, and each gives a perfectly good geometry with the same cosmological constant but a different notion of distance. No change of description turns one into the other. So in empty space the assumption is a real choice. Where there is matter and curvature of the right kind, the choice is forced.

synthesis.unit-ball-clauses-hold-at-one-.formal:
Work in the setting of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}: one shared scale factor $a$; a five-dimensional tower whose hidden direction has scale $b \propto a^{\beta}$ (the derived metric of the diagonal field $\hb^{-1}(e_{y}) = b\,e_{y}$, $\beta = 1$ co-expanding, $\beta = 0$ static), its quanta conserved and homogeneous along the hidden extent; a three-dimensional tower's sheets comoving, one per unit comoving length. Read R2 and R3 (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}) either as standing clauses, holding at every epoch with the current cell radii, or as deposit clauses, fixing the count once at the descent with the counted thickness thereafter comoving with $b$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The ratio of a three-dimensional tower's cell radius to ours is constant in time for every $\beta$; that of a five-dimensional tower goes as $a^{(\beta - 1)/4}$. So R2's common radius holds at more than one epoch exactly when $\beta = 1$.
\item[(ii)] With R3 standing, the five-dimensional towers' projected density goes as $a^{-3(3 + \beta)/4}$, an effective equation of state $w = (\beta - 1)/4$ read from the dilution exponent (no pressure is derived): dust exactly when $\beta = 1$, and $w = -\tfrac14$ for a static hidden direction, where the five-dimensional share grows as $(1 + z)^{3/4}$ toward the present, by a factor between $189$ and $190$ from $1 + z = 1090$ and between $1.68$ and $1.69$ from $1 + z = 2$. At the unit-ball value (itself a fit to the observed ratio, Propositions \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule} and \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}) these towers hold a fraction $16/(11\pi + 16)$, between $0.316$ and $0.317$, of the dark matter.
\item[(iii)] With R2 and R3 as deposit clauses the projected density is dust for every $\beta$ and the shares fixed at the descent persist.
\item[(iv)] For a static hidden direction under the deposit reading, the counted thickness today is the deposit-epoch cell radius, $d_{b,0}\,a_{\mathrm{dep}} \le d_{b,0}\,T_{0}/T_{\mathrm{desc}}$; for any descent above $1$ MeV it is below $2.4 \times 10^{-10}$ m, more than $10^{5}$ times under the $40$ micrometre bound of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inverse-square-law-short-range}. The step of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity} that takes today's baryon spacing $d_{b} \approx 0.98$ m as the extent holds under co-expansion; under a static hidden direction the relevant thickness is this deposit-epoch length.
\end{enumerate}
So R2 and R3 can be standing clauses only with a co-expanding hidden direction, a direction the four-dimensional metric does not see (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity}), so nothing in the sourcing rule makes it co-expand. Without that premise, R3 is a rule for the descent's deposit, as the open problem frames it, and its value is set at the deposit epoch.
synthesis.unit-ball-clauses-hold-at-one-.technical:
Follow each tower's cell radius through the expansion. A sheet tower's own two-dimensional density falls as $a^{-2}$, so its cell radius grows as $a$, like ours, and its sheets, comoving, stay one radius apart: for the three-dimensional towers R2 and R3 are automatically epoch-independent. A five-dimensional tower's own four-dimensional density falls as $(a^{3}b)^{-1}$; with the hidden scale $b \propto a^{\beta}$ its cell radius grows as $a^{(3+\beta)/4}$, so its ratio to ours is constant only for $\beta = 1$. If R3 is a standing clause, counting through the current cell radius, the projected density goes as $a^{-3(3+\beta)/4}$, an effective equation of state $w = (\beta - 1)/4$, which is $-\tfrac14$ for a static hidden direction: the five-dimensional share would grow by $(1+z)^{3/4}$, about $190$ since last scattering. If R2 and R3 fix the count at the deposit, everything dilutes as dust whatever $\beta$ is.

So either the hidden direction co-expands with ours, which the four-dimensional metric does not drive and which would be a further premise, or R2 and R3 are statements about the deposit epoch. In the second case the counted thickness today is the deposit-epoch cell radius, below $2.4 \times 10^{-10}$ m for any descent above $1$ MeV, so the argument that compares today's baryon spacing ($0.98$ m) with short-range tests of gravity applies only under co-expansion.
synthesis.unit-ball-clauses-hold-at-one-.lay: The dark-matter formula counts hidden matter in "cells" whose size is tied to the spacing of ordinary matter. This result follows those cells through the expansion of the universe. For the hidden sectors with fewer dimensions than ours the rule keeps working automatically. For those with an extra dimension it keeps working only if that extra dimension stretches exactly as ours does; if it does not stretch, then either that dark matter would thin out unlike ordinary matter, growing in relative amount by a factor of nearly two hundred since the early universe, which is not what is seen, or the rule describes only the moment the matter was laid down. In that second case the thickness in the formula is a microscopic length from the birth of the universe, not today's one metre.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} In the sourcing rule of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} a tower's content is homogeneous along every direction it has and contributes its energy per unit of shared three-volume. Take comoving numbers $N$ conserved. Our quanta have density $n_{b} \propto a^{-3}$ and cell radius $r_{b} = (V_{3}n_{b})^{-1/3} \propto a$. A three-dimensional tower's sheets contain two shared directions and are comoving, one per unit comoving length along the third; its own density is $n_{3} \propto a^{-2}$ and its cell radius $r_{3} = (V_{2}n_{3})^{-1/2} \propto a$. A five-dimensional tower with hidden scale $b \propto a^{\beta}$ has own density $n_{5} \propto (a^{3}b)^{-1}$ and cell radius $r_{5} = (V_{4}n_{5})^{-1/4} \propto a^{(3 + \beta)/4}$. The ball volumes are constants and drop out of every ratio of epochs.

\emph{(i)} The clauses are those of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}. $r_{3}/r_{b}$ is constant and $r_{5}/r_{b} \propto a^{(\beta - 1)/4}$. The check verifies $(r_{3}/r_{b})^{6} = n_{b}^{2}/n_{3}^{3}$ constant and $(r_{5}/r_{b})^{24} = n_{b}^{8}/n_{5}^{6} = a^{6(\beta - 1)}$ times its value at $a = 1$, at the scale factors $1, 2, 3, \tfrac72$ and $\beta \in \{0, \tfrac12, 1, 2\}$, and that only $\beta = 1$ gives a constant. R2 sets $r_{5} = r_{3} = r_{b}$ in one unit; at two epochs this needs $\beta = 1$. The sheet spacing is a comoving length, so it grows as $a$ like $r_{3}$, and R3's ``one radius apart'' is preserved for the three-dimensional towers whichever reading is taken.

\emph{(ii)} With R3 standing, a five-dimensional tower contributes $\rho = m\,n_{5}\,r_{5}$ per unit shared volume, so $\rho^{4} \propto n_{5}^{3} \propto a^{-3(3 + \beta)}$, that is $\rho \propto a^{-3(1 + w)}$ with $1 + w = (3 + \beta)/4$, an effective equation of state read from the dilution exponent; no pressure is derived. The check verifies $\rho^{8}a^{24(1 + w)}$ constant at the sample scale factors for each sample $\beta$, and that $\rho^{8}a^{24}$ (dust) is constant only for $\beta = 1$; the effective $w$ is $-\tfrac14, -\tfrac18, 0, \tfrac14$ at $\beta = 0, \tfrac12, 1, 2$. For $\beta = 0$ the ratio of this projected density to ours goes as $a^{-9/4}/a^{-3} = a^{3/4}$, so between $1 + z$ and today it changes by $(1 + z)^{3/4}$; the integer part of $(1090^{3})^{1/4}$ is $189$ and that of $100 \cdot 2^{3/4}$ is $168$. At the unit-ball value, itself a fit to the observed ratio (Propositions \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule} and \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}), the five-dimensional shares are $2 \cdot \tfrac{8}{3\pi}$ of the total $\tfrac{11}{3} + \tfrac{16}{3\pi}$, a fraction $\tfrac{16}{11\pi + 16}$, whose thousandths part is $316$ at both ends of $\tfrac{333}{106} < \pi < \tfrac{355}{113}$. (Observational reading, from memory and not used: the CMB and large-scale structure bound a dark-matter equation of state to $|w| \lesssim 10^{-3}$, and the dark-to-baryon ratio inferred at last scattering agrees with late-time cluster baryon fractions to about ten percent, so a component of a third of the dark matter with $w = -\tfrac14$ is excluded by orders of magnitude.)

\emph{(iii)} With R2 and R3 fixed at the deposit, the counted thickness is a fixed length along the hidden direction, $t \propto b$, and $\rho = m\,n_{5}\,t \propto a^{-3}$ for every $\beta$; the check verifies $\rho^{2}a^{6}$ constant for each sample $\beta$. This is the lemma's dilution, applied to the counted slab instead of the whole hidden extent.

\emph{(iv)} Under (iii) with $\beta = 0$, the counted thickness today equals its value at the deposit, which R3 set to the deposit-epoch cell radius, equal by R2 to ours then: $t_{0} = r_{b}(a_{\mathrm{dep}}) = d_{b,0}\,a_{\mathrm{dep}}$ with $a_{0} = 1$. Entropy conservation gives $a_{\mathrm{dep}} = (g_{s,0}/g_{s,\mathrm{dep}})^{1/3}\,T_{0}/T_{\mathrm{desc}} \le T_{0}/T_{\mathrm{desc}}$, since the entropy degrees of freedom do not increase toward the present. With $d_{b,0} < 1.02$ m (the bracket of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity}), $T_{0} = 2.7255$ K $< 2.35 \times 10^{-13}$ GeV and $T_{\mathrm{desc}} \ge 10^{-3}$ GeV, $t_{0} < 2.397 \times 10^{-10}$ m, and the $40$ micrometre bound of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inverse-square-law-short-range} exceeds it by a factor whose decimal order is $5$. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity} lists today's baryon spacing and the de Sitter radius as the extents the series has; under co-expansion today's counted thickness is indeed of order $d_{b,0}$ (the cell radius grows with $a$ from the deposit on), but with a static hidden direction it is $t_{0}$, which that comparison does not reach. Which towers are populated, R1 and the value of the thickness are not touched; the statement is about the consistency of R2 and R3 across epochs only.

(iii) deposit R3: dust for every beta
